questions.sample: Yes, when I'm tidying up or walking somewhere. I turn it off for English listening practice, though, because otherwise I end up following the wrong set of words.
questions.sampleZh: 会，比如收拾东西或者走路去什么地方的时候。不过练英语听力时我会关掉，不然听着听着，我的注意力就跑到歌词上了。

questions.en: Have you learned about music at school?
questions.zh: 你在学校学过音乐吗？
questions.sample: Yes, I had music classes at school, where we learned simple rhythms and sang together. I've never trained seriously, but I liked that everyone could join in.
questions.focusWording: Have you learned about music at school?
variants: Have you taken any music classes?
questions.sampleZh: 学过，学校有音乐课，我们学简单的节奏，也一起唱歌。我没受过系统训练，但我很喜欢每个人都能参与的感觉。

questions.en: Do you know how to play any musical instruments?
questions.zh: 你会演奏什么乐器吗？
questions.sample: Not properly, I'm afraid. I can follow a simple rhythm, but if you handed me an instrument, I'd need someone to show me where to start.
questions.focusWording: Do you know how to play any musical instruments?
questions.sampleZh: 老实说，不算会。我能跟上简单的节奏，但要是给我一件乐器，我还得找个人教教我该从哪儿开始。

questions.en: Do you think children should have music lessons at school?
questions.zh: 你觉得孩子应该在学校上音乐课吗？
questions.sample: Yes, I think they should get the chance. A music lesson can be enjoyable even for a child who will never perform, because making music together is fun in itself.
questions.focusWording: Do you think children should have music lessons at school?
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得应该给他们这个机会。即使一个孩子以后不会上台表演，也完全可以享受音乐课，因为和大家一起玩音乐本身就很好玩。

questions.en: Do you think it is easy to learn to play a musical instrument?
questions.zh: 你觉得学乐器容易吗？
questions.sample: Learning the first few notes might be easy, but getting a smooth sound takes patience. I'd find it much easier with someone there to correct small mistakes.
questions.focusWording: Do you think it is easy to learn to play a musical instrument?
questions.sampleZh: 学会头几个音可能不难，但要把声音奏得连贯顺畅，还是需要耐心。如果有人在旁边帮我纠正小错误，我会觉得容易得多。

questions.en: Do you think music can change how people feel?
questions.zh: 你觉得音乐能改变人的心情吗？
questions.sample: Definitely. A lively song can give me the energy to start a task, while something quieter helps me slow down after a noisy journey home.
questions.sampleZh: 当然。一首欢快的歌能让我打起精神开始做事，而在嘈杂的路上折腾一阵回家后，安静一点的音乐又能让我慢慢放松下来。

questions.en: Where do you hear music in your daily life, for example in a shopping centre?
questions.zh: 日常生活中，你会在哪些地方听到音乐（比如在商场）？
questions.sample: I hear it in cafés, shops and restaurants almost every day. Often I notice the music only when I recognise a song or when it's too loud for conversation.
questions.sampleZh: 我几乎每天都能在咖啡馆、商店或餐厅听到音乐。很多时候，只有听到熟悉的歌，或者音量大得影响聊天时，我才会特别注意它。

questions.en: Did you enjoy listening to music when you were a child?
questions.zh: 你小时候喜欢听音乐吗？
questions.sample: Yes, especially songs I could sing along to without understanding every word. Repeating a catchy chorus was much more fun than trying to remember all the verses.
questions.sampleZh: 喜欢，尤其是那些即使不懂每个词，也能跟着唱的歌。反复唱一段朗朗上口的副歌，比费劲记住每一段主歌有意思多了。

questions.en: Do you sometimes dislike music that you hear?
questions.zh: 你有时会不喜欢自己听到的音乐吗？
questions.sample: Yes, particularly if a shop plays the same loud song on repeat. Even a tune I normally enjoy can get annoying when I'm trying to talk to someone.
questions.sampleZh: 会，尤其是有些店把同一首歌开得很响，还一直循环播放。就算是我平时喜欢的曲子，想和人说话的时候听多了也会烦。

questions.en: How often do you go shopping?
questions.zh: 你多久购物一次？
questions.sample: I buy food a few times a week, but I shop for clothes much less often. When I go out with friends, we're more likely to come home with snacks.
questions.sampleZh: 我一周会买好几次吃的，买衣服的次数就少多了。和朋友出门逛，最后拎回家的往往还是零食。

questions.en: Do you prefer shopping online, or going to a shop?
questions.zh: 你更喜欢网购还是到商店买东西？
questions.sample: For familiar things I prefer shopping online. If I'm buying shoes, though, I'd rather go to a shop and walk around a little before paying.
questions.sampleZh: 买熟悉的东西时，我更喜欢网购。不过买鞋时我还是愿意去实体店，穿上走几步再付钱。

questions.en: Have you ever returned anything you bought online?
questions.zh: 你退过网购的东西吗？
questions.sample: Yes, I've returned clothes that didn't fit the way I expected. Since then I've paid more attention to measurements instead of relying on photos or a size label.
questions.sampleZh: 退过，有些衣服上身的效果和我预期的不一样。从那以后，我会更留意具体尺寸，不会只看照片或尺码标签。

questions.en: Do you like shopping?
questions.zh: 你喜欢购物吗？
questions.sample: I enjoy some kinds of shopping, especially browsing food markets. Looking for a particular cable or charger feels more like a job I want to finish quickly.
questions.sampleZh: 有些东西我挺喜欢逛的，尤其是卖吃的的市场。要是为了找某一款线缆或充电器，就更像一件想赶快完成的任务。

questions.en: Do you enjoy shopping in malls?
questions.zh: 你喜欢逛商场吗？
questions.sample: Sometimes, especially if a friend and I can have lunch there afterwards. I get tired of walking into similar clothing shops, so the food usually keeps me interested.
questions.focusWording: Do you enjoy shopping in malls?
questions.sampleZh: 有时喜欢，尤其是逛完还能和朋友在那儿吃午饭的时候。逛来逛去都是相似的服装店，我会觉得累，通常还是好吃的更能提起我的兴趣。

questions.en: What are the advantages of online shopping?
questions.zh: 网购有什么好处？
questions.sample: It's easy to compare several products without spending an afternoon travelling between shops. I also like being able to read a few reviews before I decide.
questions.focusWording: What are the advantages of online shopping?
questions.sampleZh: 比较几种商品很方便，不用把整个下午花在不同商店之间来回跑。我也喜欢在做决定之前先看看几条买家评价。

questions.en: What are the disadvantages of online shopping?
questions.zh: 网购有什么缺点？
questions.sample: You can't feel the material or try something on. A jacket can look great in a photo and still feel uncomfortable the moment you put it on.
questions.focusWording: What are the disadvantages of online shopping?
questions.sampleZh: 你摸不到材质，也不能试穿。一件外套照片上看起来很好，真穿到身上，可能马上就会觉得不舒服。

questions.en: Do you like to compare the prices in different shops?
questions.zh: 你喜欢比较不同商店的价格吗？
questions.sample: Yes, especially for an expensive purchase. I won't visit five shops to save a tiny amount, but a quick comparison helps me tell whether a discount is genuine.
questions.focusWording: Do you compare prices in different shops before buying something?
questions.sampleZh: 会，尤其是买比较贵的东西时。我不会为了省一点点钱跑五家店，不过简单比个价，有助于看出是不是真的有优惠。

questions.en: Have you ever returned something you bought that you weren't happy with?
questions.zh: 你有没有因为对买到的东西不满意而退货？
questions.sample: Yes, I once bought something that looked better in the pictures than in person. I returned it and learned to check the return policy before ordering.
questions.sampleZh: 有，有一次我买的东西照片比实物好看。我把它退了，也学会了下单前先看清退货政策。

questions.en: Do you wear different clothes at weekends and on weekdays?
questions.zh: 周末和工作日，你会穿不一样的衣服吗？
questions.sample: Yes, a little. I wear plain, practical clothes when I'm working in the shop, but at weekends I might try something brighter if I'm meeting a friend.
questions.focusWording: Do you wear different clothes on weekdays and weekends?
questions.sampleZh: 有一点不同。在店里上班时我穿得简单方便，周末如果约朋友见面，我可能会试试颜色更明亮的衣服。

questions.en: What colours of clothes do you like to wear?
questions.zh: 你喜欢什么颜色的衣服？
questions.sample: I like dark green and simple neutral colours. They're easy to match, so I don't have to spend ages deciding what to wear before leaving home.
questions.sampleZh: 我喜欢深绿色和一些简单的中性色。它们都很好搭，所以出门前不用花好长时间纠结穿什么。

questions.en: What kinds of clothes do you usually like to wear?
questions.zh: 你通常喜欢穿哪种衣服？
questions.sample: I like soft T-shirts, loose trousers and a light jacket. I can study in them, take a walk and go out to eat without changing my whole outfit.
questions.sampleZh: 我喜欢穿柔软的 T 恤、宽松的裤子，再加一件轻便外套。这样穿既可以学习、散步，也可以出门吃饭，不用整套换衣服。

questions.en: Do you prefer comfortable clothes or smart clothes?
questions.zh: 你更喜欢穿舒适的衣服，还是比较讲究得体的衣服？
questions.sample: Comfortable clothes win on most days. If I have an interview, I'll dress more smartly, but I still want to be able to sit and move comfortably.
questions.focusWording: Do you prefer comfortable clothes or smart clothes?
questions.sampleZh: 大多数时候我都会选舒服的衣服。如果要面试，我会穿得讲究些，不过我还是希望坐着和走动时都舒服。

questions.en: Do you like wearing T-shirts?
questions.zh: 你喜欢穿 T 恤吗？
questions.sample: Yes, I wear them quite often. A plain T-shirt is easy to match with jeans, and I can put a jacket over it if the weather changes.
questions.sampleZh: 穿，我还挺常穿的。素色 T 恤很好配牛仔裤，天气变了，也可以在外面套件外套。

questions.en: Do you spend a lot of time choosing clothes?
questions.zh: 你会花很多时间挑衣服吗？
questions.sample: Not usually. I tend to reach for combinations I already know work, and I'd rather spend the extra ten minutes having breakfast than comparing two similar tops.
questions.sampleZh: 一般不会。我通常会拿自己穿惯了、知道好搭的那几件。与其花十分钟对比两件差不多的上衣，我更愿意用这点时间吃早饭。

questions.en: Will your style of clothes change in the future?
questions.zh: 你觉得自己将来的穿衣风格会改变吗？
questions.sample: Probably a little. I'd like a few clothes that work both in the shop and at an exhibition, but I don't expect to give up comfortable shoes.
questions.focusWording: Will your style of clothes change in the future?
questions.sampleZh: 大概会变一点。我希望有几件衣服既能穿着上班，也能穿去看展览，不过我想我还是会继续穿舒服的鞋。

questions.en: Do you like buying designer clothes?
questions.zh: 你喜欢购买名牌服饰吗？
questions.sample: Not particularly. I might buy a designer item if I really liked the cut, but the name on the label doesn't make me want it by itself.
questions.focusWording: Do you like buying designer (brand) clothes?
questions.sampleZh: 没有特别的兴趣。如果真的很喜欢某件设计师品牌衣服的剪裁，我可能会买，不过单看标签上的名字，还不足以让我想要它。

questions.en: Are there any colours you don't like to wear?
questions.zh: 有没有哪种颜色的衣服你不喜欢穿？
questions.sample: Very bright yellow isn't really for me. I like seeing it on other people, but when I try it on, it feels louder than the rest of my clothes.
questions.sampleZh: 我不太适合特别亮的黄色。我喜欢看别人穿，但穿在我身上，总觉得它比我其他衣服都要抢眼。

questions.en: Would you ever buy clothes just because of the brand name?
questions.zh: 你会仅因为品牌名就买一件衣服吗？
questions.sample: No, I'd need to like the item itself. If I wear something often and it lasts, that's a much better reason to buy it than the brand name.
questions.sampleZh: 不会，我得先喜欢东西本身。如果一件衣服我经常穿，又很耐穿，那是比品牌名字更好的购买理由。

questions.en: Do you like to keep things tidy?
questions.zh: 你喜欢把东西收拾整齐吗？
questions.sample: Yes, particularly on my drawing table. I keep the pens in jars and put the paper flat, because a bent corner can spoil a page before I've even started.
questions.sampleZh: 挺喜欢，尤其是我的画桌。我把笔分装在罐子里，把纸平放，因为画还没开始，纸角折坏就可能影响整张作品。

questions.en: Did you keep things tidy when you were a child?
questions.zh: 你小时候会把房间收拾整齐吗？
questions.sample: Not all the time, but I did look after my drawing things. I could leave a jumper on the chair for days and still put every pencil back in the right tin.
questions.focusWording: Did you keep things tidy when you were a child?
questions.sampleZh: 不是一直整齐，不过我挺爱收拾画具的。衣服可能在椅子上放好几天，我还是会把每一支铅笔收回该放的盒子。

questions.en: How do you keep your work or study space tidy?
questions.zh: 你是怎么保持工作或学习空间整洁的？
questions.sample: I put small tools in jars and keep one empty corner of the table for paper. It means I can clear a spot for homework without sorting through everything again.
questions.sampleZh: 我用几个罐子装小工具，另外在桌上留个空角放画纸。这样如果要写作业，就不用又把所有东西从头收一遍。

questions.en: Do you think that it is necessary to be tidy?
questions.zh: 你觉得保持整洁有必要吗？
questions.sample: To a point, yes. I work better when I can find my notes, but spending half an hour arranging every pen would probably make me less productive.
questions.sampleZh: 在一定程度上，是的。找得到笔记时我做事更顺利，但要花半小时把每支笔都摆整齐，可能反倒没那么有效率。

questions.en: Do you try to keep your workspace tidy when you're working or studying?
questions.zh: 工作或学习时，你会尽量让桌面整洁吗？
questions.sample: I try to keep the middle of my table clear. Things can pile up at the edges while I'm working, but I put them away when I finish a drawing.
questions.focusWording: Do you keep your room or workspace tidy?
questions.sampleZh: 我会尽量把桌子中间留空。做事的时候东西可能在桌边堆起来，但画完一张画，我就会把它们收走。

questions.en: Did your parents teach you to be tidy when you were young?
questions.zh: 小时候父母教过你收拾整理吗？
questions.sample: Yes, I was taught to put one thing away before starting a different activity. It wasn't a big rule, but it stopped my small pieces of paper from disappearing.
questions.focusWording: Did your parents teach you to be tidy when you were young?
questions.sampleZh: 教过，小时候大人会提醒我，开始另一件事之前先把手上的东西收好。这算不上什么严厉的规定，却让我那些小纸片不容易弄丢。

questions.en: How do you feel if other people are not tidy?
questions.zh: 如果别人不爱收拾，你会有什么感受？
questions.sample: It depends on whether we're sharing the space. I don't mind what someone does with their own desk, but a clear kitchen table makes it easier for both of us to eat.
questions.sampleZh: 要看是不是共用空间。别人自己的桌子怎么放，我不太介意，但厨房餐桌收干净了，两个人吃饭都方便。

questions.en: Did you have to keep your room tidy when you were a child?
questions.zh: 小时候你被要求把自己的房间收拾整齐吗？
questions.sample: Yes, the floor had to stay clear so nobody tripped. I was free to spread out toys while I played, provided they went back into a box afterwards.
questions.sampleZh: 得收拾，主要是地上要留条路，别让人绊倒。玩的时候玩具可以摊开，玩好再放回盒子就行。

questions.en: Do you think it's possible for someone to be too tidy?
questions.zh: 你觉得有些人会不会过于追求整洁？
questions.sample: Yes, if it stops them enjoying the space. I understand wanting a clear table, but I'd feel uncomfortable in a room where I was afraid to move a cushion.
questions.sampleZh: 会的，如果太讲究整齐，让他们都没办法自在地享受这个空间。我能理解想把桌面清空，但在一个连挪个靠垫都不敢的房间里，我肯定会不舒服。

questions.en: Do you think there are people who can always stay tidy?
questions.zh: 你觉得有人能一直保持整洁吗？
questions.sample: Yes, some people give each item a particular home. I find that easy with pencils and brushes, although loose papers are much harder to keep under control.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得有人可以，他们能给每样东西都安排一个固定位置。铅笔和画笔我觉得容易收好，散着的一张张纸就难管多了。

questions.en: What do you think of people who keep things tidy?
questions.zh: 你怎么看待爱把东西收拾整齐的人？
questions.sample: I appreciate someone who keeps a shared area ready for the next person. At work, putting samples back in order saves everybody time when the shop gets busy.
questions.focusWording: What do you think of people who keep things tidy?
questions.sampleZh: 我挺欣赏会为下一个使用者收好公共空间的人。在店里，把样品按顺序放回去，忙起来时大家都能省时间。

questions.en: Do you find headphones comfortable to wear?
questions.zh: 你觉得戴耳机舒服吗？
questions.sample: Yes, for short periods. I use small wireless earbuds for English listening, but after an hour or so I usually take them out and give my ears a break.
questions.focusWording: Do you find headphones comfortable to wear?
questions.sampleZh: 喜欢，不过每次戴得不久。我用小巧的无线耳机练英语听力，但戴了一个小时左右，我通常就会摘下来，让耳朵歇一会儿。

questions.en: Do you use earphones?
questions.zh: 你平时用耳机吗？
questions.sample: Yes, I wear my wireless earbuds most days. I use them to replay difficult English sentences at home or to listen to music when I'm on the metro.
questions.focusWording: Do you use earphones?
variants: How often do you wear headphones to listen to something?
questions.sampleZh: 戴，我大多数日子都会用无线耳机。在家用它反复听难懂的英语句子，坐地铁时就用来听音乐。

questions.en: What type of headphones do you use?
questions.zh: 你用哪种耳机？
questions.sample: I usually use wireless earbuds. They fit into a small case, so I can take them out on the metro and put them away quickly when I arrive.
questions.focusWording: What type of headphones do you use?
questions.sampleZh: 我通常用无线耳机。它们装在一个小盒子里，坐地铁时拿出来用，到站后也能很快收好。

questions.en: When would you use headphones?
questions.zh: 你在什么情况下会用耳机？
questions.sample: I use them on public transport and when I'm studying in a shared space. They're especially useful if I want to hear the ending of an English word clearly.
questions.sampleZh: 我在乘坐公共交通工具或在公共空间学习时会用耳机。尤其是想听清某个英语单词的词尾时，耳机特别有用。

questions.en: In what situation would you never wear headphones?
questions.zh: 在什么情况下你绝不会戴耳机？
questions.sample: I wouldn't wear them while crossing a busy road. I also take them out when someone starts speaking to me, even if I can hear through them.
questions.focusWording: When do you not use headphones?
questions.sampleZh: 过车多的马路时，我不会戴耳机。有人开始和我说话时我也会摘下来，即使戴着也能听见对方说话。

questions.en: How popular is it to wear headphones in your country?
questions.zh: 在你们国家，戴耳机普遍吗？
questions.sample: Very common from what I see. On the metro, lots of people wear earbuds to watch videos or make calls without filling the whole carriage with sound.
questions.sampleZh: 就我看到的来说，非常常见。地铁上许多人戴着耳机看视频或打电话，这样整个车厢就不至于都听见他们手机里的声音。

questions.en: Have you ever posted anything on social media?
questions.zh: 你在社交媒体上发过内容吗？
questions.sample: Yes, I've shared photos of a postcard I printed in class. One person noticed a small bird in the corner that I hadn't expected anyone to spot.
questions.sampleZh: 发过，我分享过自己在课上印的一张明信片的照片。有人发现了角落里一只小鸟，我原来以为谁也不会注意到它。

questions.en: When did you start using social media?
questions.zh: 你是什么时候开始用社交媒体的？
questions.sample: I started when I was still at school, mainly to stay in touch with classmates. At the time, sending a quick message felt more important than posting anything publicly.
questions.sampleZh: 我还在上学时就开始用了，主要是为了和同学保持联系。那时候，对我来说，给人发条简短的消息比公开发点什么更重要。

questions.en: Do you think you spend too much time on social media?
questions.zh: 你觉得自己花在社交媒体上的时间太多了吗？
questions.sample: Sometimes I do. I might open an app to find a restaurant, then realise I've spent twenty minutes watching videos about dishes I never planned to order.
questions.sampleZh: 有时确实会。我可能本来只是想打开应用找家餐厅，结果回过神来，已经看了二十分钟美食视频，而且介绍的菜我原本根本没打算点。

questions.en: Do your friends use social media?
questions.zh: 你的朋友们用社交媒体吗？
questions.sample: Most of them do. We use group chats to arrange meals, and someone usually sends a picture of a dish before we've even agreed on a restaurant.
questions.focusWording: Do friends use social media?
questions.sampleZh: 大多数朋友都用。我们会在群里约饭，经常连去哪家餐厅都还没定，就已经有人发来某道菜的照片了。

questions.en: What do people often do on social media?
questions.zh: 人们通常在社交媒体上做什么？
questions.sample: People chat, share photos and look for recommendations. In my circle, a conversation about where to eat often starts with someone sharing a post from a local food account.
questions.sampleZh: 大家会聊天、分享照片，也会找推荐。我身边的人聊起去哪儿吃饭，往往是先有人转发了本地美食账号的一篇帖子。

questions.en: Do you usually use social media apps?
questions.zh: 你平时用社交媒体应用吗？
questions.sample: Yes, they're part of my ordinary routine. I message friends, check updates and sometimes save a useful English expression, although I try not to open every notification.
questions.focusWording: Do you usually use social media apps?
questions.sampleZh: 用，它们已经是我日常生活的一部分了。我会给朋友发消息、看看大家的动态，偶尔也会收藏一个有用的英语表达，不过我会尽量避免每条通知都点开。

questions.en: What social media apps do you usually use?
questions.zh: 你通常用哪些社交媒体应用？
questions.sample: I usually use a messaging app for practical things and a photo-sharing app for ideas. A clear picture of a poster or a shop window is often worth saving.
questions.focusWording: What social media apps do you usually use?
questions.sampleZh: 我平常用聊天软件处理日常小事，也用分享图片的软件找灵感。看到设计清楚的海报或有意思的橱窗照片，我常会把它存下来。

questions.en: What do you usually do with social media apps?
questions.zh: 你自己平时在社交媒体上做什么？
questions.sample: I mostly chat with friends and save ideas for food or study. I keep a few useful posts so I can find them again instead of relying on my memory.
questions.focusWording: What do you usually do with social media apps?
questions.sampleZh: 我主要和朋友聊天，也会收藏一些美食或学习方面的点子。我会存下几篇有用的帖子，方便以后再找，不用光靠记忆。

questions.en: Has anyone ever recommended a social media app or website to you?
questions.zh: 有人向你推荐过社交媒体应用或网站吗？
questions.sample: Yes, friends have recommended apps for finding local restaurants. I usually try one if they show me a particular feature, rather than just saying it's popular.
questions.sampleZh: 有，朋友给我推荐过找本地餐厅的应用。如果朋友能给我演示一个具体功能，我通常就会试试。光说它很火，对我吸引力没那么大。

questions.en: Is there anything you really don't like about social media?
questions.zh: 社交媒体有什么让你特别不喜欢的地方吗？
questions.sample: I dislike how easily it can interrupt my attention. When I'm halfway through writing something, one notification can turn into a much longer break than I intended.
questions.sampleZh: 我不喜欢它那么容易打断我的注意力。写东西写到一半，一条通知就可能让我停下来的时间比原本打算的长得多。

questions.en: In the future, do you think you will spend more or less time on social media?
questions.zh: 以后你用社交媒体的时间会变多还是变少？
questions.sample: Probably a little less. I'd rather spend an extra half hour drawing something myself than look through dozens of pictures and forget nearly all of them.
questions.sampleZh: 大概会少一点。同样多出来半小时，我更愿意自己动手画点东西，而不是翻过几十张图片，最后几乎都忘了。

questions.en: Do you enjoy listening to other people singing?
questions.zh: 你喜欢听别人唱歌吗？
questions.sample: Yes, especially when someone chooses a song they clearly enjoy. I don't mind a missed note if I can tell they're having a good time singing it.
questions.focusWording: Do you enjoy listening to other people sing?
questions.sampleZh: 喜欢，尤其是对方选了一首自己真的喜欢的歌。听得出来人家唱得开心，偶尔唱错一个音我并不在意。

questions.en: Do you like singing? Why?
questions.zh: 你喜欢唱歌吗？为什么？
questions.sample: I like singing casually, especially when no one expects a performance. Following a familiar chorus feels relaxing because I don't have to think too hard about the words.
questions.sampleZh: 我喜欢随便唱唱，尤其是在大家都没指望我要表演的时候。跟着熟悉的副歌唱很放松，因为我不用费劲去想歌词。

questions.en: Have you ever learnt how to sing?
questions.zh: 你学过怎么唱歌吗？
questions.sample: Only informally. We sang in school music lessons, and I sometimes copy a singer's timing when I hear a song I like, but I've never trained seriously.
questions.sampleZh: 只算非正式地学过一点。上学时我们在音乐课上唱过歌，听到喜欢的歌时，我有时也会模仿歌手怎么把握节奏，不过我没受过系统训练。

questions.en: Have you ever taken a singing class?
questions.zh: 你上过声乐课吗？
questions.sample: I haven't taken a class devoted entirely to singing. My experience is mostly ordinary school music lessons, where the whole class sang together rather than practising individual voices.
questions.sampleZh: 我没上过专门教唱歌的课。我的经验主要来自学校普通的音乐课，都是全班一起唱，很少单独练自己的声音。

questions.en: Who do you want to sing for?
questions.zh: 你想唱歌给谁听？
questions.sample: I'd be happiest singing for a few close friends. If I missed a note, they'd probably laugh with me and carry on instead of making me start again.
questions.sampleZh: 我最乐意唱给几个亲近的朋友听。哪怕我唱错一个音，他们大概也会和我一起笑笑，接着往下唱，不会让我从头再来。

questions.en: Do you think singing can bring happiness to people?
questions.zh: 你觉得唱歌能给人带来快乐吗？
questions.sample: Yes, because people can join in without being good at it. Even singing a birthday song slightly out of tune can make someone feel part of a group.
questions.sampleZh: 有，因为即使不擅长唱歌，大家还是可以一起唱。就算生日歌唱得有点跑调，也能让人觉得自己融入了这个集体。

questions.en: Is singing popular among people around you?
questions.zh: 你身边的人普遍喜欢唱歌吗？
questions.sample: Yes, quite a few people I know enjoy singing. At the end of a relaxed evening somebody often suggests a familiar song, and even the quieter people join in on the chorus.
questions.focusWording: Is singing popular among people around you?
questions.sampleZh: 挺受欢迎的，我认识的人里喜欢唱歌的不少。轻松聚一晚后，常有人提议唱首大家熟悉的歌，连不太说话的人也会跟着唱副歌。

questions.en: Do you listen to music while driving?
questions.zh: 你开车时会听音乐吗？
questions.sample: I'm usually the passenger, so I'm more likely to choose the music than drive. I like something gentle enough that the driver and I can still talk.
questions.focusWording: Do you listen to music while driving?
questions.sampleZh: 我通常是坐车的人，所以比起开车，我更有可能负责选歌。我喜欢放柔和一点的音乐，这样我和开车的人还能聊聊天。

questions.en: Do your friends think you are good at singing?
questions.zh: 你的朋友觉得你唱歌好听吗？
questions.sample: They wouldn't describe me as a great singer, but they don't mind me joining in. I'm better at remembering a catchy chorus than hitting every high note.
questions.focusWording: Do your friends think you are good at singing?
questions.sampleZh: 他们应该不会说我特别会唱歌，不过也不介意我跟着唱。比起每个高音都唱得上去，我更擅长记住朗朗上口的副歌。

questions.en: Did you do a lot of singing when you were a child?
questions.zh: 你小时候常唱歌吗？
questions.sample: I sang quite a bit with my classmates, especially during music lessons. I liked joining a group because I could enjoy the song without worrying about my voice alone.
questions.sampleZh: 我以前经常和同学一起唱，尤其是在音乐课上。我喜欢大家一起唱，这样就能好好享受歌曲，不用担心只有自己的声音被听见。

questions.en: Do you ever sing while you're doing other things?
questions.zh: 你平时会一边做事一边唱歌吗？
questions.sample: Yes, sometimes when I'm washing dishes or putting things away. It makes an ordinary job feel lighter, and I hardly notice how long it's taking.
questions.sampleZh: 会，有时候洗碗或者收拾东西时就会唱。这样平常的小事也变得轻松些，我几乎不会注意已经做了多久。

questions.en: Would you like to have singing lessons?
questions.zh: 你想上声乐课吗？
questions.sample: I'd try a beginner's lesson, mainly to learn how to stay in tune. I wouldn't aim to perform anywhere, but it would make karaoke with friends more enjoyable.
questions.sampleZh: 我想试试入门课，主要想学学怎么唱得不跑调。我没打算去哪里表演，不过学了以后，和朋友唱卡拉 OK 应该会更开心。

questions.en: Do you like science?
questions.zh: 你喜欢科学吗？
questions.sample: Yes, especially when it explains something I can see. I once looked up why colours change in different light after the same piece of paper looked almost blue by a window.
questions.focusWording: Do you like science?
questions.sampleZh: 喜欢，尤其是科学能解释我亲眼看到的现象时。有一次同一张纸在窗边看着近乎蓝色，我就去查了为什么光线变化会影响颜色。

questions.en: When did you start to learn about science?
questions.zh: 你从什么时候开始学科学？
questions.sample: I remember simple science lessons in primary school. At first it was mostly about observing things around us, which felt more like exploring than learning a set of rules.
questions.sampleZh: 我记得小学时上过一些简单的科学课。最初主要是观察身边的东西，感觉更像在探索世界，而不是在学一套规则。

questions.en: Which science subject is interesting to you?
questions.zh: 你对哪门科学学科感兴趣？
questions.sample: I'm particularly interested in the science of light. Seeing the same object cast quite different shadows at different times makes an ordinary afternoon walk surprisingly interesting.
questions.sampleZh: 我对光学特别感兴趣。同一样东西在不同时刻能投出完全不同的影子，有了这个观察角度，平常的午后散步都会变得有意思。

questions.en: What kinds of interesting things have you done with science?
questions.zh: 你用科学知识做过哪些有趣的事？
questions.sample: I tried mixing coloured light by shining small lamps onto a white wall. The result was different from mixing paints, which made me want to find out why.
questions.sampleZh: 我试过把几盏彩色小灯照向一面白墙，看它们的光混在一起会怎样。结果和混合颜料很不一样，我就想弄明白原因。

questions.en: Do you ever watch TV programmes about science?
questions.zh: 你会看讲科学的电视节目吗？
questions.sample: Sometimes I do, especially if the programme starts with a clear question. I'm more likely to finish an episode about sleep or attention than one with a very abstract title.
questions.sampleZh: 有时会，特别是那些开头就提出一个清晰问题的节目。比起标题很抽象的一集，讲睡眠或注意力的节目我更容易看完。

questions.en: Do Chinese people often visit science museums?
questions.zh: 中国人常去科技馆或科学博物馆吗？
questions.sample: I think many families visit them, especially at weekends or during school holidays. A hands-on display gives children something to do together instead of just reading a long explanation.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得很多家庭会去参观，尤其是在周末或者学校放假的时候。有能动手体验的展项，孩子们就可以一起做点什么，不用光站着读一长段说明。

questions.en: What science subjects did you learn at school?
questions.zh: 你在学校学过哪些科学课程？
questions.sample: I studied biology, chemistry and physics at school. I particularly remember a physics lesson where a glass prism spread ordinary light into a line of colours on the wall.
questions.focusWording: What science subjects did you learn at school?
questions.sampleZh: 我在学校学过生物、化学和物理。我尤其记得一堂物理课，一块玻璃棱镜把普通的光分开，在墙上投出了一条彩色光带。

questions.en: Why do you think some people enjoy learning science?
questions.zh: 你觉得为什么有些人爱学科学？
questions.sample: I think they enjoy the moment when something that seemed mysterious starts to make sense. A simple experiment can give you an answer you can actually see for yourself.
questions.focusWording: Why do you think some people enjoy learning science?
questions.sampleZh: 我想，他们喜欢的是那种原本觉得神秘的东西突然说得通了的瞬间。一个简单的实验，就能让你亲眼看到答案。

questions.en: Which area of science do you follow most closely?
questions.zh: 你平时最关注哪个科学领域？
questions.sample: I follow stories about light and materials. For example, I find it interesting when someone manages to make useful paper from waste that would otherwise be thrown away.
questions.focusWording: Which area of science do you follow (pay most attention to)?
questions.sampleZh: 我会关注光和材料方面的新发现。比如有人把原本会被扔掉的废料做成能正常使用的纸，我就觉得很有意思。

questions.en: Did you learn a lot about science at school?
questions.zh: 你在学校学到的科学知识多吗？
questions.sample: I learned the basics, particularly in biology, chemistry and physics. I didn't remember every formula, but school did teach me to look for evidence before accepting an explanation.
questions.sampleZh: 我学了一些基础知识，主要是生物、化学和物理。我没记住每一个公式，不过学校真的教会了我，在接受一个解释之前，先看看有没有证据。

questions.en: Are you usually interested in new scientific developments?
questions.zh: 你通常对新的科学进展感兴趣吗？
questions.sample: Yes, when I can see a practical example. New ways of making colours from plants interest me, because I'd like to try them on a small print myself.
questions.sampleZh: 通常感兴趣，特别是有实际例子可看的时候。我对从植物中制作颜料的新方法挺好奇，也想亲自用它做一幅小版画试试。

questions.en: Do you think you could enjoy working as a scientist?
questions.zh: 你觉得自己会喜欢当科学家的工作吗？
questions.sample: I might enjoy testing materials, especially if I got to compare how they react to light or water. Writing up the exact steps every time would probably be my biggest challenge.
questions.sampleZh: 我可能会喜欢测试材料，尤其是能比较不同材料遇到光、水之后各有什么反应。每次都要把准确步骤写下来，对我来说大概是最大的挑战。

questions.en: Did you learn about space and the stars at school?
questions.zh: 你在学校学过有关太空和星星的知识吗？
questions.sample: Yes, we covered basic things like planets and the solar system at school. I remember diagrams of their orbits more clearly than the names of all their moons.
questions.focusWording: Have you ever learnt about outer space and stars?
questions.sampleZh: 学过，学校里讲过行星和太阳系之类的基础知识。比起那些行星各自的卫星都叫什么，我对它们的轨道示意图印象更深。

questions.en: Do you like science fiction movies?
questions.zh: 你喜欢科幻电影吗？
questions.sample: I like them if the characters give me a reason to care. An impressive spaceship is fun to look at, but I still want a story I can follow.
questions.focusWording: Do you like science fiction movies?
questions.sampleZh: 如果角色能让我关心他们的遭遇，我就喜欢看。很酷的宇宙飞船看着当然过瘾，不过我还是希望故事本身让我跟得下去。

questions.en: Do you want to know more about outer space?
questions.zh: 你想进一步了解太空吗？
questions.sample: Yes, especially about everyday life on a spacecraft. I'd be just as interested in how people eat and sleep there as in the names of distant stars.
questions.sampleZh: 想，尤其想了解航天器上的日常生活。人们在上面怎么吃饭、怎么睡觉，和遥远的星星叫什么名字，对我来说一样有意思。

questions.en: Would you ever think about having a holiday in space in the future?
questions.zh: 你会考虑将来去太空度假吗？
questions.sample: The idea is exciting, but I don't think I'd choose it for a holiday. I'd rather explore somewhere on Earth where I could walk around and try the local food.
questions.focusWording: Do you want to go into outer space in the future?
questions.sampleZh: 想想挺让人兴奋，但真要度假，我大概不会选它。我还是更愿意去地球上一个能四处走走、尝尝当地美食的地方。

questions.en: Have you watched any sci-fi movies about space?
questions.zh: 你看过和太空有关的科幻电影吗？
questions.sample: Yes, I've seen a few, including stories about astronauts trying to get home. I enjoy the problem-solving scenes more than the long explanations of how the spacecraft works.
questions.focusWording: Have you watched any sci-fi movies about space?
questions.sampleZh: 看过几部，其中有的讲航天员想办法回家的故事。比起花很长时间解释飞船是怎么运作的，我更喜欢看他们想办法解决难题的情节。

questions.en: Are you interested in learning about travelling in space?
questions.zh: 你有兴趣了解太空旅行吗？
questions.sample: Yes, particularly the practical side of it. I'd like to know how astronauts train for ordinary tasks that suddenly become difficult when there's very little gravity.
questions.sampleZh: 感兴趣，特别是实际操作的部分。重力很小的时候，一些再普通不过的事突然就变难了，我想知道航天员是怎么训练自己完成这些事的。

questions.en: Do you enjoy watching films that are about people travelling in space?
questions.zh: 你喜欢看讲述人们太空旅行的电影吗？
questions.sample: Usually, yes, especially when the journey puts people in an unfamiliar situation. Seeing how a crew makes decisions interests me more than watching two spaceships chase each other.
questions.sampleZh: 通常喜欢，尤其是旅程把人带进陌生处境的时候。比起看两艘飞船追来追去，我更感兴趣的是看机组成员怎么一起做决定。

questions.en: How popular are comedy programmes in your country?
questions.zh: 在你们国家，喜剧节目有多受欢迎？
questions.sample: They seem quite popular, especially short comedy clips people can share. My friends are more likely to send me a funny scene than recommend an entire programme.
questions.sampleZh: 看起来挺受欢迎的，尤其是那种可以随手分享的喜剧短片。相比推荐一整个节目，我的朋友们更常给我发其中一个好笑的片段。

questions.en: Are you good at telling jokes?
questions.zh: 你擅长讲笑话吗？
questions.sample: I'm better at telling a funny story about something that happened than remembering a proper joke. If I have to deliver a punchline, I sometimes get the timing wrong.
questions.focusWording: Are you good at telling jokes?
questions.sampleZh: 比起把一个编好的笑话记下来，我更擅长把发生过的趣事讲给别人听。要是非得在结尾抖个包袱，我有时会抓不准时机。

questions.en: Do your friends like to tell jokes?
questions.zh: 你的朋友喜欢讲笑话吗？
questions.sample: Yes, a few of them do. The best jokes in our group usually come from a shared experience, so a single sentence can make everyone laugh.
questions.sampleZh: 会，有几个朋友会讲。我们这群人之间最有意思的笑话，往往都来自大家共同经历过的事，所以有时只要一句话就能让所有人都笑起来。

questions.en: Do you like watching comedy programmes or films?
questions.zh: 你喜欢看喜剧吗？
questions.sample: Yes, especially after a day of studying. I like a comedy with believable characters, because it's easier to laugh when a situation reminds me of something I've actually seen.
questions.focusWording: Do you like watching comedy programs or movies?
questions.sampleZh: 喜欢，尤其是学了一天以后。我喜欢角色真实可信的喜剧，因为碰上让我想起自己亲眼见过的场面的情节时，我更容易笑出来。

questions.en: Have you ever watched a live show?
questions.zh: 你看过现场演出吗？
questions.sample: I've watched live performances at school events, though I haven't been to many professional shows. What I remember is hearing everyone around me react at exactly the same moment.
questions.sampleZh: 我在学校活动上看过现场表演，不过看的专业演出不多。我记得最清楚的，是听到身边所有人恰好在同一瞬间作出反应的感觉。

questions.en: Do you think laughing is important in daily life?
questions.zh: 你觉得欢笑在日常生活中重要吗？
questions.sample: Yes, even a short laugh can break the tension. If I'm worrying about an English mistake and a friend makes me smile, it's much easier to try again.
questions.focusWording: Do you think laughing is important in daily life?
questions.sampleZh: 有帮助，哪怕只是短短笑一下，也能缓解紧张。比如我正为自己犯的一个英语错误发愁，朋友把我逗笑了，我就更容易鼓起劲再试一次。

questions.en: Why do people enjoy humorous things?
questions.zh: 为什么人们喜欢幽默的东西？
questions.sample: Humour gives people a fresh way to look at ordinary problems. Something annoying, like missing a bus, can become a story people actually enjoy hearing over dinner.
questions.focusWording: Why do people enjoy humorous things?
questions.sampleZh: 幽默让人能换个角度看待日常烦恼。像错过公交车这种恼人的事，换种讲法，就能变成大家吃饭时很乐意听的趣事。

questions.en: Do you like it when friends tell you jokes?
questions.zh: 你喜欢朋友给你讲笑话吗？
questions.sample: Yes, especially when we're both relaxed and the joke doesn't put anyone on the spot. A well-timed joke can turn an ordinary meal into a really good evening.
questions.sampleZh: 喜欢，尤其是两个人都很放松，而且这个玩笑不会让谁下不来台的时候。一个时机恰到好处的玩笑，就能把一顿平常的饭变成一个特别开心的晚上。

questions.en: Would you ever go to see a live comedy show?
questions.zh: 你愿意去现场看喜剧演出吗？
questions.sample: Yes, I'd like to try a small live show with a friend. I'm curious whether a joke feels different when the performer can hear the audience reacting.
questions.sampleZh: 想，我想和朋友一起去看一场小型现场演出。我很好奇，当表演者能当场听到观众的反应时，同一个笑话听起来会不会不一样。

questions.en: Do you like getting up early in the morning?
questions.zh: 你喜欢早起吗？
questions.sample: I like the quiet part of an early morning more than the actual getting up. Once I've had breakfast and opened the curtains, I'm usually glad I made the effort.
questions.focusWording: Do you like getting up early in the morning?
questions.sampleZh: 比起早起这件事本身，我更喜欢清晨的安静。等吃了早饭、拉开窗帘，我通常就会庆幸自己努力爬起来了。

questions.en: What do you usually do in the morning?
questions.zh: 你早上通常做什么？
questions.sample: I have breakfast and check what needs doing that day. Lately I often begin with a short English listening exercise, before email and other things start interrupting.
questions.focusWording: What do you usually do in the morning?
questions.sampleZh: 我会吃早饭，再看看当天有哪些事要做。最近我常常先做一小段英语听力练习，趁邮件和别的事情还没开始打断我。

questions.en: What did you do in the morning when you were little? Why?
questions.zh: 小时候你早上一般做什么？为什么？
questions.sample: I got dressed, ate breakfast and left for school. There wasn't much time to choose what to do because I needed to arrive before the first lesson.
questions.sampleZh: 我会穿好衣服、吃早饭，然后出门上学。因为要在第一节课前赶到，基本没多少时间自己挑想做什么。

questions.en: Are there any differences between what you do in the morning now and what you did in the past?
questions.zh: 你现在和过去的早晨有什么不同？
questions.sample: Yes, I can choose more of my own routine now. At school I had to leave at the same time every morning, but my current timetable depends on classes and shop shifts.
questions.sampleZh: 有区别，我现在能自己安排更多事情。上学时每天早上总得在同一时间出门，现在则要看当天几点上课、几点去店里上班。

questions.en: Do you spend your mornings doing the same things on both weekdays and weekends?
questions.zh: 周末和工作日的早晨，你会做同样的事吗？
questions.sample: Not exactly. I keep breakfast as a regular habit, but on weekends I'm much more willing to go out for noodles and let the morning take its time.
questions.focusWording: Do you spend your mornings doing the same things on both weekdays and weekends?
questions.sampleZh: 不完全一样。吃早饭一直是我的习惯，但到了周末，我会更愿意出门吃碗面，让整个早晨过得从容一点。

questions.en: What do you usually do on weekend mornings?
questions.zh: 周末早上你一般做什么？
questions.sample: I like to have a slower breakfast and go out for something I wouldn't make at home. If there's no deadline, my study notes can wait until the afternoon.
questions.focusWording: What do you usually do on weekend mornings?
questions.sampleZh: 我喜欢慢悠悠地吃早饭，出门点些自己在家不会做的东西。如果没有什么事赶着交，我的学习笔记完全可以等到下午再看。

questions.en: When you were a child, did you often have to get up early in the morning?
questions.zh: 小时候，你经常需要一大早就起床吗？
questions.sample: Yes, on school days I did. I needed time for breakfast and the journey, so staying in bed for another ten minutes often meant rushing everything afterwards.
questions.sampleZh: 是的，上学的日子会早起。吃早饭和路上都要留时间，所以在床上多赖十分钟，常常就意味着后来每件事都要赶。

questions.en: Do you usually get up early in the morning?
questions.zh: 你平时早晨会早起吗？
questions.sample: Usually at a reasonable time, although I'm not someone who jumps out of bed at dawn. An early appointment is much more effective than any alarm sound.
questions.sampleZh: 通常会在比较正常的时间起来，不过我不是天一亮就能从床上蹦起来的人。早上要赶着赴约，可比什么闹钟都管用。

questions.en: After you get up in the morning, what do you enjoy doing?
questions.zh: 早上起床后，你喜欢做什么？
questions.sample: I enjoy having a quiet breakfast before opening my messages. That little stretch of time feels like my own, even when the rest of the day is busy.
questions.sampleZh: 我喜欢先安安静静吃完早饭，再打开消息看。即使这一天剩下的时间都很忙，早上这短短的一会儿也像是完完全全属于我的。

questions.en: Have you ever had to wake up very early in the morning?
questions.zh: 你有没有需要在清晨很早就起床的经历？
questions.sample: Yes, I've had to get up very early for exams and travel. I usually put everything I need by the door the night before so I don't forget it.
questions.sampleZh: 有，我以前因为考试或出门旅行，不得不特别早起。我通常会在前一晚把要用的东西都放在门边，以免忘带。

questions.en: Do you always feel bored?
questions.zh: 你总觉得无聊吗？
questions.sample: Not usually. If one thing starts to feel dull, I can switch between drawing, taking a short walk and finding something to listen to while I cook.
questions.focusWording: Do you always feel bored?
questions.sampleZh: 一般不会。要是一件事开始让我觉得无聊，我可以换换花样，比如画张画、出去走一会儿，或者做饭时找点东西听。

questions.en: What things are boring to you?
questions.zh: 哪些事让你觉得无聊？
questions.sample: Repeating a task without seeing any progress bores me. Copying vocabulary lists, for example, is much duller than hearing the same words in a conversation I want to understand.
questions.focusWording: What things are boring to you?
questions.sampleZh: 一件事做来做去又看不到什么进步，我就会觉得无聊。比如，抄词汇表就比在一段我真想听懂的对话里听到同样的单词枯燥得多。

questions.en: Did you find school boring when you were a child?
questions.zh: 你小时候觉得上学无聊吗？
questions.sample: Not on the whole. Copying a paragraph from the board sometimes felt dull, but art lessons and the chance to work on something with my classmates kept me interested.
questions.focusWording: Do you think schooling was boring to you when you were a child?
questions.sampleZh: 整体来说不会。有时照着黑板抄一段话确实有点闷，但美术课、和同学一起动手做东西的机会，能让我对学校生活一直有兴趣。

questions.en: What do you do when you feel bored?
questions.zh: 觉得无聊时你会做什么？
questions.sample: I change the kind of activity I'm doing. If I've been looking at a screen all afternoon, a walk to get something to eat usually works better than another video.
questions.focusWording: What do you do when you feel bored?
questions.sampleZh: 我会换一种类型的活动。如果已经对着屏幕一下午了，走出去买点吃的，通常比再刷一段视频更有用。

questions.en: What do you do to relax?
questions.zh: 你平时是怎么放松的？
questions.sample: I like going out for food, especially with a friend who enjoys trying things. Choosing a dish and talking over dinner helps me forget about deadlines for a while.
questions.focusWording: What do you do to relax?
questions.sampleZh: 我喜欢出门吃东西，尤其喜欢和愿意尝鲜的朋友一起去。挑道菜，边吃边聊，能让我把各种截止日期暂时抛在脑后。

questions.en: Do you think doing sports is a good way to relax?
questions.zh: 你认为运动是放松的好方法吗？
questions.sample: Yes, if I choose something I actually enjoy. Even a fairly gentle walk makes a difference after a day at my desk, and it doesn't feel like another obligation.
questions.focusWording: Do you think doing sports is a good way to relax?
questions.sampleZh: 有帮助，只要选的是自己真喜欢的运动。坐在书桌前一整天以后，哪怕只是出去轻松走走也会感觉好些，而且不会觉得又多了一件必须完成的事。

questions.en: Do you think a vacation is a good way for you to relax?
questions.zh: 你觉得度假对你来说是个好的放松方式吗？
questions.sample: Yes, especially if the holiday isn't packed with activities. I'd rather spend a morning exploring one neighbourhood and having breakfast than rush between five places for photos.
questions.focusWording: Do you think a vacation is a good way for you to relax?
questions.sampleZh: 会，尤其是行程没塞满活动的时候。我宁愿花一个早晨慢慢逛一个街区、吃顿早饭，也不想为了拍照匆匆忙忙地连跑五个地方。

questions.en: Do you think students need more time to relax?
questions.zh: 你觉得学生需要更多休息放松的时间吗？
questions.sample: I think many do. If every free hour feels like a chance to get more work done, it's difficult to return to a book with a clear head.
questions.focusWording: Do you think students need more time to relax?
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得很多人确实需要。如果每段空闲时间都被看成继续工作的机会，真要回头捧起书时，反倒很难静下心来读进去。

questions.en: Do you like trying new things?
questions.zh: 你喜欢尝试新事物吗？
questions.sample: Yes, especially practical things that I can try in an afternoon. A short printing class is ideal because I get to learn one technique and take a finished object home.
questions.focusWording: Do you like trying new things?
questions.sampleZh: 喜欢，尤其是一个下午就可以亲手试一试的东西。短时的印刷体验课就很合适，我既能学会一种方法，也能带着一件成品回家。

questions.en: Do you think young people are more willing to try new things than older people?
questions.zh: 你觉得年轻人比年长者更愿意尝试新事物吗？
questions.sample: Sometimes, but I don't think age explains everything. A curious older person with free time might try far more new activities than a younger person with a crowded schedule.
questions.focusWording: Do you think young people are more willing to try things than older people?
questions.sampleZh: 有时是，不过我觉得年龄说明不了一切。一个好奇心强、又有空闲时间的老年人，尝试的新活动可能比一个日程排得满满的年轻人多得多。

questions.en: Is it important to constantly try out new things in life?
questions.zh: 你觉得在生活中不断尝试新事物重要吗？
questions.sample: It's worth trying something new occasionally, but I don't need a new experience every day. Familiar routines give me enough energy to enjoy the things I do decide to try.
questions.focusWording: Is it important to constantly try out new things in life?
questions.sampleZh: 偶尔尝试点新东西挺值得的，但我并不需要每天都有新体验。熟悉的日常反而让我有足够精力，去享受那些我真正决定要尝试的事。

questions.en: Do young people today have more opportunities to try new things than older people?
questions.zh: 现在的年轻人比年长者有更多尝试新事物的机会吗？
questions.sample: Young people may hear about more opportunities through university groups or social media. Older people can have opportunities too, but they may find them through friends, work or local activities.
questions.focusWording: Do young people today have more opportunities to try new things than older people?
questions.sampleZh: 年轻人也许能通过大学里的社团或社交媒体听说更多机会。年长的人也有机会，只是他们可能更多通过朋友、工作或本地活动发现这些机会。

questions.en: Do you cook at home?
questions.zh: 你在家做饭吗？
questions.sample: Yes, several times a week. I usually make something I can share with my flatmate, like rice and vegetables, and keep the leftovers for lunch the next day.
questions.focusWording: Do you cook at home?
questions.sampleZh: 会，一周会做几次。我一般会做可以和室友一起吃的饭菜，比如米饭配蔬菜，剩下的就留着第二天中午吃。

questions.en: Do you help your family cook?
questions.zh: 你会帮家人做饭吗？
questions.sample: Yes, when I visit I usually take care of one small job, like washing vegetables. It gives us time to chat without everyone crowding around the same pan.
questions.focusWording: Do you help your family cook?
questions.sampleZh: 会，我回去时一般会负责一件小事，比如洗菜。这样大家可以边做边聊，也不用都挤在同一口锅旁边。

questions.en: Do you want to learn to cook well?
questions.zh: 你想把厨艺学好吗？
questions.sample: Yes, I'd love to learn how to bake bread well. I can follow a recipe, but knowing by touch when the dough is ready would be far more useful.
questions.focusWording: Do you want to learn to cook well?
questions.sampleZh: 想，我很希望能把面包烤好。照着食谱一步步做我还行，但要能摸摸面团就判断它好了没有，那就实用多了。

questions.en: Do you do housework at home?
questions.zh: 你在家会做家务吗？
questions.sample: Yes, my flatmate and I split the jobs. I don't mind washing up because I can finish it quickly, and in return I usually get a break from taking the bins out.
questions.focusWording: Do you do housework at home?
questions.sampleZh: 做，我和室友会分担。洗碗我不介意，因为一会儿就洗完了，这样一般就不用再由我去倒垃圾。

questions.en: What do you usually type?
questions.zh: 你平时会打些什么内容？
questions.sample: I type notes about my drawing assignments and short messages about shop shifts. On a full keyboard I can move words around easily until an instruction is clear.
questions.focusWording: What do you usually type?
questions.sampleZh: 我会打字记录绘画作业的要求，也会发短消息沟通文具店的班次。用完整键盘改动字句比较方便，我可以一直改到说明写得清楚为止。

questions.en: Do you type on a desktop or laptop keyboard every day?
questions.zh: 你每天都用台式机或笔记本的键盘打字吗？
questions.sample: Yes, most days I use a laptop keyboard for my assignments. My phone is fine for a quick reply, but I'd find it uncomfortable to type a whole page on it.
questions.focusWording: Do you type on a desktop or laptop keyboard every day?
questions.sampleZh: 会，大多数日子我都会用笔记本电脑的键盘写作业。手机用来回条短消息没问题，可要敲整整一页字，我会觉得不太舒服。

questions.en: When did you learn to type on a keyboard?
questions.zh: 你是什么时候学会用键盘打字的？
questions.sample: I first got used to a keyboard at school. I was slow at the beginning, but typing longer assignments later on made the movements feel much more natural.
questions.focusWording: When did you learn how to type on a keyboard?
questions.sampleZh: 我是在上学时开始用惯键盘的。一开始打得很慢，不过后来要打的作业变长了，手上的动作也就自然多了。

questions.en: Did you write more by hand or type more when you were a child?
questions.zh: 小时候你手写更多，还是打字更多？
questions.sample: I definitely wrote more by hand. Most homework had to go into an exercise book, and typing only became part of my daily routine when I started writing longer assignments.
questions.focusWording: Did you write more by hand or type more when you were a child?
questions.sampleZh: 我以前肯定是手写得更多。大部分作业都得写在练习本上，直到后来开始写篇幅更长的作业，打字才成了我日常习惯的一部分。

cards.en: Describe a place you went to where you remember feeling bored.
cards.zh: 一个你去过而且觉得无聊的地方
cues: Where you went
Who you were with
What you remember about this place
Why you felt bored in this place
cuesZh: 这个地方给你留下了什么印象
为什么你在那里觉得无聊
cards.sample:
I once spent an afternoon in a shopping centre that I usually quite like, and still managed to get very bored. My friend Maggie was choosing a lamp for her new flat, so I went along to keep her company. I thought we'd pick one up and have a coffee in the bookshop afterwards.

The floor we visited was almost entirely full of lighting shops. I remember rows of lamps hanging just above our heads, all switched on at the same time. My friend needed to compare the light from each one and check the sizes on her phone. For the first ten minutes I tried to give her useful opinions. After the fifth shop, the lamps started looking exactly the same to me. There was nowhere to sit down, either.

I can see why the floor was useful to her. She had a real decision to make, and I didn't. That's probably why I found the experience so dull. When we eventually reached the bookshop, I picked up a book and lost track of time almost immediately. It was funny how two floors of the same building could feel so different.
cards.replaceable: 商场、一起去的人和当时逛的店
cards.sampleZh:
有一次，我在一家平时挺喜欢的商场里待了一下午，却还是无聊透了。我的朋友 Maggie 要给新公寓挑一盏灯，我就去陪她。我原以为我们买好一盏灯，就能到书店里喝杯咖啡。

我们去的那一层楼几乎全是灯具店。我还记得一排排灯挂在我们头顶不高的地方，全都同时亮着。朋友需要比较每盏灯的光线，还得在手机上核对尺寸。前十分钟，我还努力提些有用的意见。等逛过第五家，我已经觉得所有的灯看起来都一模一样了。那里甚至连个能坐下的地方都没有。

我完全明白那一层楼为什么对她有用。她确实得做个选择，我却没有。这大概就是我觉得整个过程这么无趣的原因。等我们终于到了书店，我拿起一本书，几乎马上就读得忘了时间。同一栋楼里的两个楼层，竟能带给人这么不同的感受，想想还挺有意思。

cards.en: Describe a person you know about who has a successful business.
cards.zh: 一位生意做得很成功的人
cues: Who the person is
What kind of business this person has
Whether you have used his/her business
Why you think this person's business is successful
cuesZh: 你觉得这门生意为什么能做得好
cards.sample:
Ryan owns a small bicycle repair shop next to our community sports centre. I got to know him at a cycling open day there. While my friend Maggie helped arrange the activities, Ryan set up a small stand and checked people's brakes for free. He was just as patient with a child's little bike as he was with a visitor's expensive racing bicycle.

I used his shop a few weeks later when my bike kept jumping into the wrong gear. Before doing anything, he showed me the loose cable and told me exactly what the adjustment would cost. While he worked, he explained what the gears should sound like when they were running properly. Then he asked me to ride up and down outside and decide for myself whether it felt right.

I think his business is successful because people know what they're paying for and feel comfortable asking questions. On my way past, I often see familiar customers bringing somebody new. The shop is quite small, but one honest repair can bring in another rider without an advertisement. I've already recommended him to a friend who was worried about a noise from her back wheel.
outline: 骑行开放日免费查刹车
Ryan 的独立自行车维修店
cards.replaceable: Ryan、邻里车店和自行车故障均可换成自己的生活例子。
cards.sampleZh:
Ryan 在社区体育中心旁经营一家小型自行车维修店。我在体育中心的一次骑行开放日认识了他。朋友 Maggie 在帮忙安排活动，Ryan 则搭了个小摊位，免费帮大家检查刹车。他对待小朋友的小自行车，和对待一位来客价格不菲的公路赛车一样有耐心。

几周后，我自己的车老是莫名其妙跳到别的挡位，我就去过他店里。动手之前，他先指给我看哪根线松了，又确切告诉我调整一次要多少钱。他一边修一边解释，变速系统正常运转时应该是什么声音。之后还让我在门外来回骑一段，自己判断感觉对不对。

我觉得他的生意成功，是因为顾客知道自己的钱花在什么地方，也可以放心提问。我路过时，经常看到熟客带着新面孔进店。店虽然小，但只要踏踏实实修好一辆车，就可能不用打广告也能带来下一位车友。我已经把他推荐给一个朋友，她正担心自己的自行车后轮有异响。

cards.en: Describe a story you like that has animals in it [e.g. a book, a children's story, a film].
cards.zh: 一个你喜欢的、有动物角色的故事
cues: How you know about this story
What animals are in it
What happens in this story
Why you like this story that has animals in it
cuesZh: 你是怎么知道这个故事的
为什么喜欢这个有动物的故事
cards.sample:
A story with an animal that I really like is The Little Prince. I first came across it as a small illustrated book. I picked it up again during a busy week because a friend told me to look out for the fox. There are other animals in the story, including a snake, but it's the fox I still think about.

The little prince leaves the tiny planet where he has been looking after a rose. On Earth he sees a garden full of roses and begins to wonder what made his own flower special. Then he meets a fox. He wants to play straight away, but the fox asks him to keep coming back and sit a little closer each time. Gradually, each becomes important to the other. Even the colour of a wheat field will remind the fox of the prince's hair.

I like the way an animal can explain friendship through something you can picture. There's no big speech about how to be a good friend. Two characters simply keep turning up for each other. It makes me think about an old friend of mine and the ordinary afternoons that somehow became our favourite memories.
cards.replaceable: 初读方式、最喜欢的插图和联想到的人可以替换。
cards.sampleZh:
我很喜欢的一个有动物的故事是《小王子》。我第一次接触它时，拿到的是一本小小的插画书。后来有一周很忙，因为有位朋友提醒我一定要留意书里的狐狸，我就又把它捡起来读。故事里还有别的动物，比如蛇，但到今天我常常想起的还是那只狐狸。

小王子离开了自己那颗小小的星球，在那里，他一直照料着一朵玫瑰。到了地球，他看见一整座种满玫瑰的花园，于是开始疑惑，自己那朵花究竟特别在哪里。接着他遇见了狐狸。他马上就想跟它一起玩，狐狸却请他一次次回来，每次都比上次坐得近一点。渐渐地，他们对彼此都有了特别的意义。以后狐狸哪怕只看见麦田的颜色，也会想起小王子的头发。

我喜欢这个故事，是因为它让一只动物用看得见、想象得出来的小事讲明白了友谊。书里没有长篇大论地教人怎样做个好朋友。两个角色只是一次又一次出现在对方面前。它让我想起我的一位老朋友，也想起我们一起度过的那些普通下午，不知怎么，它们后来就成了我们最喜欢的回忆。

cards.en: Describe a time when you watched a live sports event.
cards.zh: 一次观看现场体育赛事的经历
cues: What the sports event was
Where and when the sports event took place
Why you watched it live
How you felt about watching the sports event live
cards.focusWording: Describe a live sports event you watched and liked.
focusCues: When and where you watched it
And explain why you liked it
cuesZh: 你为什么选择实时观看
看的时候你有什么感受
cards.sample:
A live sports event I enjoyed was a five-a-side football match at a neighbourhood sports ground. It took place on a Saturday afternoon last summer. My friend Maggie had heard that two local teams were playing, and we decided to go because the ground was within walking distance and neither of us had seen the game played on such a small pitch.

We found a place near one of the goals. From there we could hear the goalkeeper telling a teammate that somebody was coming up behind him. A few minutes later, a player received the ball close to us. We both expected him to shoot. He looked up, rolled it sideways, and a teammate who had been completely unmarked put the ball into the net. The finish was simple, but only because the pass had been so good.

What I liked about being there was having the freedom to watch that second player even before he got the ball. On television I tend to follow whatever the camera chooses. I also liked recognising the people who were cheering on the touchline. It made our Saturday feel like something we were sharing with the neighbourhood.
outline: 社区球场看五人制足球
cards.replaceable: 比赛、场地和进球情节均为公开练习场景，可换成你亲自看过的比赛。
cards.sampleZh:
我很喜欢的一场现场体育赛事，是在社区球场看的五人制足球赛。比赛是在去年夏天一个周六的下午。朋友 Maggie 听说有两支本地队伍对赛，球场走路就能到，而且我们从来没现场看过在这么小的场地上踢的比赛，于是决定去看看。

我们在其中一边的球门附近找了个位置。在那里，可以听见守门员提醒队友，有个人正从后面靠近。几分钟后，一名球员在离我们很近的地方接到球，我们都以为他要射门。他抬起头，把球横着轻轻送出去，另一位完全没人盯防的队友就把球推进了网里。最后那一脚看起来简单，是因为那次传球实在巧妙。

我喜欢亲自到场，因为就算第二位球员还没有拿到球，我也能自己决定去看他跑动。看电视时，我通常只能跟着镜头走。我还喜欢看到边线上欢呼的人里有一些熟悉的面孔。那个星期六的下午，就这样成了一段和街坊们一起分享的时光。

cards.en: Describe a person you know who likes growing plants in their home or garden.
cards.zh: 你认识的一位喜欢在家中或花园里种植物的人
cues: Who this person is
What types of plants this person grows
Where this person grows the plants
Why you think this person likes growing plants
cuesZh: 你觉得对方为什么喜欢种植物
cards.sample:
My aunt grows herbs on the narrow balcony outside her kitchen. There's just enough room for a chair, a shelf and a row of pots. She has mint for drinks, basil for pasta and a little rosemary plant that seems to manage even when she forgets to water it for a day.

She started with two pots that looked so similar she kept picking the wrong leaves. Now she makes labels out of old wooden spoons. She writes the name on one side and a little drawing of a dish on the other. When I visit, she lets me rub a leaf between my fingers and guess which plant it came from. I'm usually right about the mint because the smell is so strong.

I think she enjoys growing herbs because she can see the result of her work almost straight away. If lunch tastes a bit ordinary, she can open the balcony door and come back with something fresh. I like sitting beside the pots with her, especially when she has cut more basil than she needs and I get to take some home.
cards.replaceable: 香草品种、盆器和用法
cards.sampleZh:
我姑姑在厨房外面那条窄窄的阳台上种香草。地方刚好放得下一把椅子、一个架子和一排花盆。她种薄荷做饮料，种罗勒配意面，还有一小盆迷迭香，就算哪天忘了浇水，它好像也长得不错。

最开始只有两盆植物，长得太像，她总是摘错叶子。现在她拿旧木勺当标签，一面写上植物的名字，另一面画一道可以用它来做的菜。我去看她时，她会让我用手指搓一片叶子，再猜是从哪盆摘的。薄荷我一般都猜得出来，因为味道实在太浓了。

我想她喜欢种香草，是因为几乎立刻就能看到自己劳动的成果。要是午饭味道有点平淡，她打开阳台门，转身就能带回来一点新鲜食材。我很喜欢和她一起坐在花盆旁边，尤其是她剪的罗勒比需要的多一点，我还可以带一些回家。

cards.en: Describe a tall building that you like or dislike.
cards.zh: 一座你喜欢或不喜欢的高楼
cues: Where this building is
What it looks like
What you know about it
Why you like or dislike this building
cards.focusWording: Describe a tall building you like/dislike.
focusCues: What it looks like (height, design, function)
Whether you like it or dislike it (and why)
And explain how living/working in such a building might affect people
cuesZh: 你为什么喜欢或不喜欢它
cards.sample:
There's an office tower in our town that I use as a landmark. It stands above a shopping centre, close to a busy road. If a friend asks where we should meet, I tell them to look for the tall glass building and find the bookshop downstairs. Even someone who's never been there usually finds it.

The tower is a simple rectangle, with pale glass windows from top to bottom. On a clear afternoon they reflect the sky, so the top almost disappears. The lower floors have restaurants and shops, and people go through a separate entrance to reach the offices above. Once, when I was waiting for a friend, I saw a whole queue of office workers outside the lifts at lunchtime. That helped me imagine what working there would actually be like.

I like the building, especially when I see it from a distance. Working there would probably suit someone who wanted to buy lunch or pick up a book without going outside in the rain. Personally, I'd want a desk near a window and a good excuse to take the stairs when everyone else was waiting for the lift.
cards.replaceable: 商场名称、塔楼外观、所在路口和等电梯的经历可换成你熟悉的建筑。
cards.sampleZh:
镇上有一栋办公楼，我常拿它当路标。它在一座商场上方，旁边就是一条繁忙的道路。如果朋友问我在哪儿碰头，我就让对方先找那栋高高的玻璃楼，再找楼下的书店。即便以前没去过的人，通常也找得到。

这栋楼就是个简简单单的长方形，从楼顶到楼底都是浅色玻璃窗。晴朗的下午，窗户映着天空，楼顶几乎像是要消失在天色里。底下几层有餐厅和商铺，要去楼上办公区的人走单独的入口。有一次中午，我正在等朋友，看见一大队上班族在电梯外面排着队。那个场景让我大致想象得出，天天在这栋楼上班是什么感觉。

我挺喜欢这栋楼，尤其是从远处看它的时候。如果有人希望下雨天买午餐或者买本书都不用走到室外，在这里上班大概会很合适。要是我自己选，我会希望有张靠窗的办公桌。等大家一窝蜂排队等电梯时，我也正好能给自己找个理由，走楼梯去。

cards.en: Describe an interesting video that you watched on the internet.
cards.zh: 一段你在网上看过的有趣视频
cues: When and where you watched the video
What this video was about
How you found out about this video
Why you thought this video was interesting
cards.sample:
An online video that made me watch a sport differently was a short replay of Simone Biles competing in the Paris Olympics. My friend Maggie sent me the link while we were chatting one evening. I opened it on my phone at home, thinking I'd watch a few seconds and go back to our conversation.

It showed part of the women's all-around final, including her floor exercise. The first time through, I mainly noticed how high she went into the air. Then I dragged the video back and looked at what happened just before a jump. Her first few steps had a very clear rhythm. On the next viewing I watched what she did immediately after landing, because the performance had to carry straight on even after the difficult part.

What interested me was how much you get to choose as a viewer when you can replay something. During a live event I usually follow the commentator and wait for the score. Here I could spend a whole minute thinking about two seconds of movement. Maggie and I ended up sending the clip back and forth, telling each other where to pause. It was a surprisingly good conversation about a very short video.
outline: 在家重看巴黎决赛片段
后来改变看比赛的方式
cards.replaceable: 朋友分享的方法、观看设备和你重看的动作均可换成自己的经历。
cards.sampleZh:
一段让我改变看比赛方式的网络视频，是西蒙·拜尔斯参加巴黎奥运会的一小段回放。一天晚上，我和朋友 Maggie 聊天时，她把链接发给了我。我当时在家，用手机点开，本来只想看几秒就回去接着聊。

视频里有女子个人全能决赛的片段，其中包括她的自由体操。第一遍，我主要看她腾空时跳得有多高。接着我把视频往回拖，去看起跳前发生了什么。她最开始那几步节奏非常清楚。再看一遍时，我盯着她落地后马上做了什么，因为哪怕刚完成一个高难度动作，整套表演也得立刻继续。

让我觉得有趣的是，有了回放，观众可以自己决定看什么。看直播时，我通常跟着解说听，然后等分数。可这次，我可以花整整一分钟琢磨两秒钟的动作。后来 Maggie 和我把片段来回发给对方，告诉对方该在哪里暂停。视频非常短，我们却意外地聊得很尽兴。

cards.en: Describe a person's home you visited that you liked, but would not want to live in.
cards.zh: 一处你拜访过、喜欢却不愿住的家
cues: When you visited this home
Who lives/lived in this home
Why you liked it
Why you would not want to live in this person's home
cuesZh: 你什么时候去过这所房子
为什么自己不想住在那里
cards.sample:
A home I like visiting belongs to my aunt. I stayed there for a weekend last spring. Her flat is on the top floor of an old building above a row of small shops. The kitchen opens onto a narrow balcony where she grows mint, basil and rosemary in pots of different sizes.

My favourite moment on that visit came just before lunch. We were making pasta and she sent me outside with a pair of scissors. I brought back a handful of basil, and we ate beside the open balcony door. From my chair I could see a line of rooftops and hear someone opening up the fruit shop below. It was an ordinary meal, but being able to pick part of it just seconds before eating made it feel special.

I wouldn't choose to live there myself because the building has several flights of stairs and no lift. By the time I'd carried my weekend bag to her door, I needed to put it down for a minute. I can happily do that for a visit. Bringing my weekly shopping up those stairs would be a different matter.
cards.replaceable: 拜访时间、住宅楼层和不想长住的原因
cards.sampleZh:
我喜欢去做客的一处住家，是我姑姑的家。去年春天，我在那里住过一个周末。她的公寓位于一排小商店上方一栋旧楼的顶层。厨房连着一道窄阳台，上面摆着大小不一的花盆，种着薄荷、罗勒和迷迭香。

那次探访我最喜欢的一刻，就在午饭快做好之前。我们正在做意面，姑姑递给我一把剪刀，让我去阳台一趟。我带回来一把罗勒，随后我们就坐在敞开的阳台门旁吃饭。从椅子上望出去，可以看到一排屋顶，还听得见楼下水果店开门的声音。那只是顿普通午餐，但刚摘下来的食材几秒钟后就吃进嘴里，让它显得很特别。

我自己却不会选在那里长期住，因为上楼要走好几段楼梯，也没有电梯。那次提着周末的行李走到门口，我就得把包放下来喘口气。偶尔去看她，爬这点楼我很乐意。每周都得把买来的东西提上去，就又是另一回事了。

cards.en: Describe a time when you wrote a message, email or letter to someone, but you had to wait a long time for the person to reply.
cards.zh: 一次发出消息、邮件或信件后等了很久才收到回复的经历
cues: When this happened
Who you sent the message/email/letter to
Why you wrote to this person
How you felt about waiting a long time for this person to reply
cuesZh: 迟迟等不到回复时是什么感受
cards.sample:
Last spring, I sent Maggie a message about doing a language exchange together. We were taking the same evening class, and we'd both said we needed more chances to speak. I suggested meeting at a café on Saturday and spending twenty minutes on each language. I asked her to choose a time because she often had plans at weekends.

Normally Maggie replied the same day, so by Thursday I was starting to wonder whether she actually wanted to come. I checked the message and realised I'd written a whole paragraph about the café. My question was right at the bottom. On Friday she finally replied. She'd seen the first line while she was out, meant to read the rest at home, and then forgotten about it.

I felt relieved, especially because she suggested a time herself and offered to bring a picture we could describe. We met the following week and had such a good conversation that we stayed until the café closed. The long wait taught me something quite small but useful. Now, when a friend needs to decide something, I put the question at the start of my message.
outline: 和 Maggie 一起上晚课
cards.replaceable: 可把咖啡店、练习时长或碰面时带的照片换成自己的细节。
cards.sampleZh:
去年春天，我发消息给 Maggie，想约她做一次语言交流。我们在上同一个晚课班，都说过平时开口的机会太少。我提议周六去咖啡店，每种语言各聊二十分钟。她周末常有安排，所以我请她挑时间。

Maggie 一般当天就会回消息。到了周四，我开始想，她是不是真的愿意来。我重新看了看自己发的消息，才发现我写了一大段介绍咖啡店的话，要问的问题却在最下面。她周五终于回了，说她在外面时扫了一眼第一行，本想回家再看后面，结果忘了。

我松了一口气，尤其是她自己提了具体时间，还说可以带一张照片给我们练习描述。我们第二周见了面，聊得很开心，一直坐到咖啡店打烊。等了这么久，我倒是学到了一件虽小却有用的事。现在，如果有事需要朋友拿主意，我会把问题写在消息开头。

cards.en: Describe a place you went to on holiday that you would recommend.
cards.zh: 一个你度假去过、愿意推荐的地方
cues: Where you went for your holiday
Why you went to this place
What you did while you were there
Why you would recommend this place for a holiday
cards.focusWording: Describe a place you have travelled to that you would like to recommend.
focusCues: What you saw and did there
And explain why you want to recommend it to others
cuesZh: 为什么推荐别人去那里度假
cards.sample:
I'd recommend a small seaside town on the east coast, about two hours from the nearest big city by train. I went there for a short holiday one autumn weekend to celebrate my friend Maggie’s birthday. She’d shown me a picture of the market near the old railway station. We booked one night so we could celebrate with friends and explore the next morning.

After breakfast, we went back to the harbour market where we’d shared a lemon tart the night before. Fishing boats were coming in, and someone at one stall was writing the names of the day's fish on a board. My friend asked what he would cook at home. He pointed to a small silver fish and sent us to a café across the road to try it. Later, we walked along the harbour wall and watched two children trying to fly a kite.

I'd recommend the town to anyone who wants a break without a long list of sights to see. Our best memory came from asking one simple question in the market. If I went again, I'd take an earlier train and leave another morning free just to walk around.
outline: 去海滨小镇给 Maggie 过生日
在老车站港边市场分柠檬挞
推荐给喜欢慢慢逛的人
cards.replaceable: 乘车距离、当地摊贩推荐的鱼和沿岸的活动
cards.sampleZh:
我想推荐东部海岸的一座小镇，从最近的大城市坐火车过去大约两小时。秋天的一个周末，我和朋友 Maggie 去那里度了个短假，给她过生日。她给我看过老火车站旁那个市场的照片。我们订了一晚住宿，这样既能跟朋友们庆生，第二天早上又能四处逛逛。

吃过早饭，我们又回到港边的市场，前一晚大家就是在这里分着吃柠檬挞的。渔船正陆续靠岸，一位摊主在板子上写当天有哪些鱼。朋友问他，如果是他自己在家，会选哪种鱼做菜。他指了指一种小银鱼，让我们去马路对面的小餐馆尝尝。后来，我们沿着港口的防波堤散步，看着两个孩子努力把风筝放起来。

如果有人想放个假，又不想对着长长的景点清单赶路，我会推荐这里。我们最难忘的回忆，就来自在市场里随口问的一个问题。如果再去一次，我会坐早一点的火车，多留出一个上午随便逛逛。

cards.en: Describe a law to help the environment which you think your country should have.
cards.zh: 一项你认为自己国家应当制定的环保法律
cues: What this law would be
Why your country needs this law
Whether this law would be popular
Why this law would help the environment
cuesZh: 你希望出台什么环保法律
cards.sample:
I'd like my country to introduce a law about the way shops set up sound equipment near busy markets. The basic aim would be to keep the sound where shoppers actually need to hear it. A shop using a speaker for ordinary announcements would have to keep the volume low and point it towards its own customers.

I thought of this after hearing an outdoor speaker at a shop beside a market. The advert travelled across the road, yet the customers standing at the counter could barely hear the person taking their order. I think a sign with the day's offers would have done a better job. Under the new rule, shops could try signs first, and market staff could help them check how far any necessary announcements carried.

I imagine nearby workers would welcome quieter afternoons. Some shop owners might worry about losing business, so a trial period would give them time to find another way to attract customers. To me, noise is part of the environment too. If two friends can talk while they buy vegetables and the seller can hear an order the first time, the street is a better place to spend time.
cards.replaceable: 可把市场摊位、告示牌上的优惠或试行安排换成自己的设想。
cards.sampleZh:
我希望我们国家能出台一项法律，管一管繁忙市场附近的商店怎样摆放和使用音响设备。最基本的目标，是让声音留在顾客确实需要听见的地方。店铺如果用音箱播放日常通知，就应该把音量调低，朝向自家的顾客。

我是听见市场旁一家店的户外音箱后想到这个问题的。广告声一路传到了马路对面，站在柜台前的顾客却快听不清接单的人在说什么。我觉得把当天的优惠写在牌子上，效果说不定更好。按我设想的新规，商店可以先试试告示牌。确有必要播通知时，市场工作人员也可以帮着去听听声音到底传了多远。

我想，附近工作的人会欢迎更安静的下午。有些店主可能会担心生意受影响，因此可以给一段试行期，让他们慢慢寻找别的揽客方式。对我来说，声音也是生活环境的一部分。如果两个朋友买菜时能边走边聊，摊主也能一遍就听清顾客要什么，这条街待起来就舒服多了。

cards.en: Describe some local news that people in your town or city were very interested in.
cards.zh: 一条你所在的城镇或城市里很受关注的本地新闻
cues: What the news was about
How you found out about the news
Who was involved
Why people were so interested in this local news
cuesZh: 为什么当地人这么关心
cards.sample:
A piece of local news that got people talking was the opening of a birdwatching platform in a park beside the river. I first heard about it when Maggie sent me a picture from the park's noticeboard. The picture showed a wide ramp leading down to the platform, with enough room for a wheelchair user and a friend to sit side by side.

The park staff had asked local birdwatchers where to put it. A group of wheelchair users also tried the route before it opened. They pointed out that a high wooden rail would block the view for someone sitting down, so the team put a lower viewing window in one part of the rail. I liked seeing that small detail in the photograph.

People were interested for different reasons. Some families wanted somewhere they could take both a grandparent and a small child. Others were surprised to learn how many kinds of birds they could see close to home. On my first visit, a boy beside me spotted a bird standing still among the reeds. I would have walked straight past it without the platform and his quiet advice about where to look.
outline: Maggie 发来公园公告照片
男孩指给我看芦苇里的鸟
cards.replaceable: 可替换公园景观、消息渠道或第一次去时看到的鸟。
cards.sampleZh:
有条本地新闻引起了不少讨论，说的是河边公园的观鸟平台开放了。我第一次听说这件事，是 Maggie 把她在公园公告栏拍的照片发给了我。照片上有一条宽坡道，向下通往平台。平台上空间充足，坐轮椅的人和朋友可以并排看鸟。

公园工作人员先问了当地的观鸟爱好者，平台适合建在哪儿。开放前，还有一群轮椅使用者试走了这条路线。他们指出，木栏杆太高会挡住坐着的人的视线，于是施工团队在一段栏杆靠下的位置留了一个观鸟窗口。我很高兴照片里能看见这个小细节。

大家关注这件事的原因各不相同。有些家庭想找个能同时带老人和小孩去的地方，另一些人则没想到在家附近就能看到这么多种鸟。我第一次去时，身旁的一个男孩发现芦苇里有只鸟，一动不动地站着。要是没有这个平台，也没有他轻声提醒我往哪儿看，我肯定会直接从旁边走过去。

cards.en: Describe a childhood friend who you remember well.
cards.zh: 一位你记得很清楚的童年朋友
cues: Who this person is
When and where you became friends
What you used to do together
Why you remember this childhood friend well
cuesZh: 你们何时、在哪里成为朋友
你们小时候常一起做什么
你为什么对这位朋友记忆深刻
cards.sample:
The childhood friend I remember best is Maggie. We met in our first year of primary school. During an art lesson, we both spotted a bird on the window ledge and decided to draw it. At break, she handed me her drawing and asked if she could keep mine. That was the start of a little habit.

On Fridays we'd exchange bird cards. We cut them from the backs of old drawing pads, so every card was a slightly different size. Sometimes we drew a real bird we'd seen on the way to school. On rainy days we'd invent one. Maggie once gave me a bird with pockets in its wings because I'd complained about losing my bus ticket. I spent the whole walk home trying to think of something equally funny to draw for her.

I remember her so well because those cards showed she actually listened to what I said. An ordinary complaint I had at lunch could come back the next week as a picture that made us both laugh. We still meet occasionally. Even now, when I see a bird standing somewhere unexpected, I find myself wondering how Maggie would draw it.
outline: 小学一年级美术课画同一只鸟
为丢车票的我画翅膀带口袋的鸟
至今看到特别的鸟仍会想起她
cards.replaceable: 认识的年级、交换卡片的日子、让对方记住的小烦恼
cards.sampleZh:
我记得最清楚的童年朋友是 Maggie。我们是小学一年级认识的。有一节美术课，我们俩同时看到窗台上站着一只鸟，就都把它画了下来。课间，她把她的画递给我，问能不能留下我画的那张。我们的小习惯就这么开始了。

后来每到周五，我们都会交换自己画的鸟卡。卡片是从用完的画本背板上剪下来的，所以每张大小都不太一样。有时我们画上学路上真见过的鸟，遇上下雨天就自己编一只。有一回，我跟她抱怨把公交车票弄丢了，结果她送给我一只翅膀上长了口袋的鸟。那天放学，我一路上都在想，也得给她画个同样好笑的东西。

我之所以这么清楚地记得她，是因为这些卡片让我知道，她真的有在听我说话。午饭时随口一句抱怨，到了下星期就可能变成逗得我们俩哈哈大笑的一张画。我们现在偶尔还会见面。就算现在，我看到有只鸟站在一个意想不到的地方，还是会不自觉地想，Maggie 会怎么画它呢？

cards.en: Describe a type of food that you like to eat on special occasions.
cards.zh: 一种你喜欢在特殊场合吃的食物
cues: What this food is
How this food is prepared
Where and when you eat this food
Why you like to eat this type of food on special occasions
cuesZh: 为什么在特别的日子喜欢吃它
cards.sample:
On birthdays I like to eat a lemon tart with a thin pastry base and a smooth yellow filling. I usually have it at home with friends, but the one I remember best came from a stall at a weekend market next to an old railway station. We bought it to share on Maggie's birthday.

The baker showed us an empty pastry case and explained how she made it. First she rolled out the pastry, pressed it into a round tin and baked it on its own so the bottom stayed crisp. For the filling, she gently heated lemon juice, sugar, butter and eggs, stirring until the mixture thickened. Once the shell had cooled, she filled it and left the tart to chill. I'd always wondered how the pastry stayed crisp underneath, so it was nice to find out.

That evening we ate it on a bench while someone played music nearby. What I look forward to on a birthday is that first bite. The lemon makes your mouth water, then you taste the sweet pastry. It's also easy to cut a small slice for somebody who's already full, so everyone can join in.
outline: 生日爱吃薄皮、黄馅的柠檬挞
擀面压模，挞皮先单独烤脆
小火搅拌柠檬蛋馅，灌入晾凉的壳再冷藏
给 Maggie 过生日时分享，酸甜又好分
cards.replaceable: 可以替换庆祝的场合、甜点的大小和摆盘方式。如果换成别的点心，制作步骤也要一起更换。
cards.sampleZh:
过生日的时候，我喜欢吃柠檬挞。它的挞皮很薄，里面是细滑的黄色馅料。我通常会和朋友在家里吃，不过印象最深的一次，是我们在老火车站旁的周末市场从一个摊位上买的。那天 Maggie 过生日，我们买来大家一起分。

烘焙师给我们看了一个还没装馅的挞壳，也讲了她是怎么做的。她先把面团擀开，压进圆形烤模里，单独烤一遍，让底部能保持酥脆。做馅时，她把柠檬汁、糖、黄油和鸡蛋放在一起小火加热，不停搅拌，直到馅料变稠。挞壳晾凉后，她再把馅倒进去，冷藏一会儿。我一直很好奇挞的底部为什么还能那么脆，这次总算弄明白了。

那天傍晚，我们坐在长椅上吃柠檬挞，旁边还有人在演奏。每次过生日让我最期待的，就是咬下第一口的感觉。先是柠檬的酸味让人口水直流，接着就尝到了挞皮的甜味。还有一个好处，即使有人已经吃饱了，也能给对方切一小块，这样大家都能分到一口。

cards.en: Describe a time when you had to get up very early.
cards.zh: 一次你不得不很早起床的经历
cues: Where you were
What time you had to get up
Why you had to get up so early
How you felt about getting up very early
cards.focusWording: Describe a time when you got up early.
focusCues: And explain how you felt about it
cuesZh: 那次早起让你感觉怎样
cards.sample:
One Sunday I had to get up much earlier than usual for a second-hand book sale. The van bringing the donated books could only stop outside the community hall before the street market opened. We'd promised the driver that someone would be at the door to help, so I set my alarm for half past five.

My room was still dark when it rang. I put on the clothes I'd left on a chair, filled a bottle with water and walked down the quiet street. Ryan was already there, holding the door open with his foot. We carried the boxes in two at a time. The labels on the sides told us which ones belonged near the children's tables and which ones could wait at the back.

For the first few minutes I would happily have swapped places with anybody still in bed. Once we'd finished, though, we had time for breakfast and a proper look around. When the first visitor asked where to find travel books, I knew exactly where to take her. That felt like a pretty good return for one early start.
outline: 第一位客人顺利找到书
cards.replaceable: 开始时间、运输工具和场地布置
cards.sampleZh:
有一个星期天，我为了二手书义卖不得不比平常早起很多。送捐赠图书的货车只能赶在街市开张前停到社区礼堂外面。我们答应了司机，门口一定有人帮他搬书，所以我把闹钟定在了五点半。

闹钟响的时候，屋里还是黑的。我穿上前一晚放在椅子上的衣服，装满一瓶水，沿着安静的街道走过去。Ryan 已经到了，正用脚抵着门。我们每次搬两个箱子进去。光看侧面的标签，就知道哪些该放在儿童区的桌子附近，哪些可以先放在后面。

刚开始那几分钟，我真希望能跟任何一个还躺在床上的人交换位置。不过，等我们做完，居然还有时间吃早饭，好好巡视一圈。第一位客人问旅行类图书在哪里时，我马上知道该带她去什么地方。为了这点收获早起一次，我觉得很值。

cards.en: Describe a person you know who is good at learning languages.
cards.zh: 你认识的一位擅长学语言的人
cues: How you know this person
What languages this person speaks
How this person learned to speak these languages
Why you think this person is good at learning languages
cuesZh: 对方怎样学会说这些语言
为什么觉得这个人擅长学外语
cards.sample:
My friend Maggie, who I've known since primary school, is one of the best language learners I know. She speaks Spanish and English, and she can also have everyday conversations in French. I noticed how good she was when we went out for a meal and she helped a visitor understand a menu without making either of them feel awkward.

I used to imagine she spent hours memorising lists of words. Then one afternoon we were waiting for our food, and she showed me what she actually did. She played a few seconds of a podcast, paused it and copied the speaker's voice. Later she sent a short voice message using the same expression. If the person replied using a different word, she listened carefully and sometimes changed her own sentence.

What impresses me is how quickly she puts a new phrase to work. She doesn't wait until she knows every word in the conversation. I find that encouraging because I get nervous about using a new expression in front of people. I've started trying her idea with my own recordings. Even if I only use one new expression that day, it feels like an expression I can actually remember.
cards.replaceable: 朋友会的语言、录音的内容和她帮助别人的场景
cards.sampleZh:
我的朋友 Maggie 是我小学起就认识的。论学语言，她是我身边最厉害的几个人之一。她会说西班牙语和英语，还能用法语进行日常对话。有一次出去吃饭，她帮一位外地来的客人看懂了菜单，两个人聊得都很自然，谁也没觉得尴尬。那次我才特别留意到她有多擅长这件事。

我以前以为她一定是花好几个小时一张张背单词表。后来有天下午，我们在等上菜，她给我看了自己真正的练法。她播放几秒钟的播客，按下暂停，然后模仿说话人的声音。过后，她又用同一个表达发了一条简短的语音消息。如果对方回复时用了另一个词，她就仔细听，有时还会调整自己的那句话。

最让我佩服的是，她学到一个新说法，很快就会拿出来用。就算对话里并非每个词都认识，她也愿意开口。我有时会因为要当着别人的面用新表达而紧张，所以这件事挺鼓励我的。我已经开始用她的办法给自己录音。哪怕一整天只用到一个新表达，我都觉得这次是真的能把它记住。

cards.en: Describe a time when you had to change a plan you had made.
cards.zh: 一次不得不改变原计划的经历
cues: What your plan was
Why you needed to change it
How difficult it was to change your plan
How you felt about having to change the plan you had made
cuesZh: 你对这次改动有什么感受
cards.sample:
I once had to move a speaking practice call from Friday evening to Saturday morning. Maggie and I had agreed to call each other from home and spend half an hour talking in English. I had even put a picture of a harbour on my desk because I wanted to practise describing it without looking at notes.

Just before the call, a shop beside the market started playing a recorded advert through an outdoor speaker. It kept repeating the same offer. I could close my window, but Maggie could still hear the words through my microphone. After asking me to repeat my first sentence twice, she started laughing. We decided to stop and try again the next morning before the market opened.

Changing the plan was fairly easy because neither of us had an early appointment. I was annoyed at first, though, because I'd set aside the whole evening. On Saturday I could hear Maggie's questions properly, and we ended up talking for longer than we'd planned. Since then, when we choose a time for a call, we also check whether we'll actually have a quiet place to talk.
outline: 约好周五晚在家练口语
重新选时间也考虑环境
cards.replaceable: 可把港口照片、原定练习时长或周末具体时间替换掉。
cards.sampleZh:
有一次，我不得不把原定周五晚上的口语练习电话改到周六早上。我和 Maggie 约好各自在家打电话，用英语聊半小时。我甚至在书桌上摆了一张港口的照片，准备练习不看笔记描述画面。

快到通话时间时，市场旁的一家店开始用户外音箱播放录好的促销广告，同一句优惠信息来回放。我可以关窗，但 Maggie 还是能通过我的麦克风听清广告词。她让我把第一句话重复了两遍，自己都笑了起来。我们就决定先挂断，改到第二天早上市场开门前再练。

改时间还算容易，因为我们俩早上都没有别的约。不过我起初还是有点烦，毕竟已经特意留出了一整个晚上。周六早上，我终于能清楚听见 Maggie 的问题了，结果比原定时间聊得还久。从那以后，我们选通话时间时也会确认，到时候到底有没有安静说话的地方。

cards.en: Describe a problem you had with some technology [e.g. a computer, a phone].
cards.zh: 你使用科技产品时遇到的一个问题
cues: What the technology was
What problem you had
Whether you fixed the problem
How you felt about this problem you had with some technology
cuesZh: 你用的是哪种技术或设备
你对这件事有什么感受
cards.sample:
A problem I had with technology was getting a poster to print the way it looked on my screen. I was helping to advertise a neighbourhood film night, and the design included the film title, the room number and the time. We planned to use the shared printer at the community centre to make several copies for nearby noticeboards.

The first copy looked fine from a distance. Up close, the right edge of the title was missing and part of the starting time had been cut off. I opened the original file and all the words were still there. That was a useful clue. I checked the paper size in the print settings and tried fitting the whole design onto one sheet. In the preview I could finally see a white border all the way round.

I printed one copy before sending the rest. This time even the last digit of the time was clear. At first I was annoyed that a design I'd already finished still needed work. Afterwards, I was glad we'd found the mistake before putting the posters up. A handsome poster isn't much use if people have to guess when the film starts.
cards.replaceable: 可替换海报内容、被裁的位置和实际处理过程。
cards.sampleZh:
我遇到过一个技术问题：怎样让海报印出来和在屏幕上看起来一样。我当时在帮忙宣传一场社区电影之夜，设计稿上有片名、房间号和开场时间。我们打算用社区中心的共享打印机多印几份，贴到附近的公告栏上。

第一张从远处看似乎没问题。走近看，片名右端不见了一截，开场时间也被裁掉了一部分。我打开原始文件，发现所有文字都还在，这是一个有用的线索。我检查了打印设置里的纸张尺寸，又试着把整张设计缩放到一页纸上。在预览中，我终于看清了围绕整张海报的一圈白边。

我先印了一张，再把其余的发到打印机。这次，连开场时间的最后一位数字都很清楚。一开始我有点烦，明明设计已经完成，怎么还得返工。后来我很庆幸，大家在贴海报以前就发现了问题。海报再漂亮，如果观众还得猜电影几点开始，也就没什么用了。

cards.en: Describe an advertisement you saw with a famous person in it.
cards.zh: 一则你见过的、有名人出现的广告
cues: What the advertisement was for
Who the famous person was
What happened in the advertisement
How you felt about seeing this famous person in an advertisement
cuesZh: 看到这位名人出现在广告里你有什么感受
cards.sample:
An advertisement I remember was a practice advert that my friend Maggie showed me on a screen. Her class had put together a short television advert for an imaginary sports bag. They used a picture of Simone Biles, the American gymnast, and timed it to fit a break in a sports programme.
