questions.sample: A change of activity usually helps once boredom sets in. Someone who's spent the afternoon looking at a screen could walk to a market and pick out something for dinner. It gives both their eyes and their mind a break.
questions.sampleZh: 开始觉得无聊时，换件事做通常就有帮助。比如，一个人整个下午都对着屏幕，可以去市场走走，挑点东西做晚饭。眼睛能休息一下，脑子也能换换思路。

questions.en: Why are some teachers' classes boring? Are there any solutions?
questions.zh: 为什么有些老师的课很无聊？有什么改善办法？
questions.sample: A class gets dull when the teacher does all the talking and has no way to tell who's following. One simple fix is to pause for a question in pairs, then invite two students to compare their answers.
questions.sampleZh: 如果老师一直在讲，也无从知道谁真的听懂了，课堂就很容易变得乏味。有个简单的办法，是停下来给出一个问题，让学生两人一组讨论，再请两位同学说说各自的答案有什么不同。

questions.en: Why do some young people feel bored when talking with old people?
questions.zh: 为什么有些年轻人与老年人聊天时会觉得无聊？
questions.sample: Sometimes they lack a shared reference. A teenager may have no idea who the actor in an older person's story is. Showing a photograph or explaining why that actor mattered can turn the same story into a real conversation.
questions.sampleZh: 有时是因为两个人不熟悉对方讲的那些人和事。长辈故事里提到的演员，一个十几岁的孩子可能连名字都没听过。如果拿张照片给他看，或者讲讲当年大家为什么喜欢这位演员，同一个故事就可能变成一段有来有往的聊天。

questions.en: Some people think governments should give financial assistance to anyone who wants to start a business. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人认为政府应该给所有想创业的人提供资金支持。你同意吗？
questions.sample: I'd support small start-up grants, but giving money to everyone who asks seems unfair. A new bakery might deserve help buying an oven if the owner has customers lined up. A short business plan would help assess that.
questions.sampleZh: 我支持给初创企业发小额补助，不过只要有人申请就给钱，似乎不太公平。举个例子，如果一家新面包店虽然还缺个烤箱，却已经有顾客等着下单，那店主就可能值得扶持。一份简短的商业计划能帮助判断这种情况。

questions.en: Some people say it's easy to start a new business. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，创办一家新企业很容易。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Opening a small online shop can be fairly straightforward. Getting enough people to come back is much harder. Someone selling handmade mugs still has to set prices, pack orders and sort things out when a parcel arrives broken.
questions.sampleZh: 开一家小网店可能相当容易，难的是让足够多的顾客一再回来。一个卖手工马克杯的人，照样要给产品定价、打包发货，还要处理杯子寄到时摔坏了之类的问题。

questions.en: Why do some customers prefer to buy from a small shop?
questions.zh: 为什么有些顾客更愿意在小店买东西？
questions.sample: In a small shop the owner may remember what a customer needs. A neighbourhood fruit seller, for example, can pick a melon that's ready to eat tonight. That little conversation is worth more to some shoppers than a huge selection.
questions.sampleZh: 小店老板可能记得顾客需要什么。比如，街坊水果店的老板知道你今晚就打算吃，可以给你挑个熟得正好的瓜。对一些顾客来说，这几句交流比有一大堆商品可以选更有价值。

questions.en: What do you think about the idea that customers expect too much from businesses these days?
questions.zh: 有人认为，如今顾客对商家的期望过高。你怎么看？
questions.sample: Some expectations have risen too far. Wanting a clear price or a replacement for a faulty product is reasonable. Expecting a tiny shop to answer messages at midnight and deliver for free the next morning seems a bit much.
questions.sampleZh: 有些期待确实高得有点过了。希望价格标得清楚，或者买到有毛病的产品后能换货，都很合理。但要求一家小店半夜回复消息，第二天一早还要免费送到，就有点过分了。

questions.en: What kinds of businesses have opened in your area recently? [e.g. cafés]
questions.zh: 你住的地方最近新开了哪些类型的店或企业？比如咖啡馆。
questions.sample: A few small bakeries and repair shops have opened near the bus stops in my area. One shop fixes shoes while you wait. I can see why that spot works, because people walk past it on their way home every day.
questions.sampleZh: 我住的地方，公交站附近最近开了几家小面包店和维修铺。其中有一家可以当场修鞋。我能理解老板为什么选在那里，因为人们每天下班回家都会经过。

questions.en: Why might a new business not be successful?
questions.zh: 新创办的企业为什么可能经营不成功？
questions.sample: A new business can run out of cash before it finds regular customers. Imagine a restaurant paying high rent from its first month. Even if people enjoy the food, a few quiet weeks can make the bills hard to cover.
questions.sampleZh: 新店可能还没攒下回头客，手里的钱就先花完了。比如，一家餐厅从开业的第一个月起就要付很贵的房租。哪怕顾客喜欢它的菜，连着几个星期生意清淡，也可能让它付不起账单。

questions.en: Do you think the best form of advertising for a business is having satisfied customers?
questions.zh: 对一家企业来说，你觉得让顾客满意就是最好的广告吗？
questions.sample: For a neighbourhood service, satisfied customers can be its best advertisement. I'd take a friend's recommendation for a hairdresser seriously because I can actually see the haircut. A brand opening in a new city may still need paid ads.
questions.sampleZh: 如果做的是街坊邻里的生意，满意的顾客很可能就是最好的广告。比如朋友给我推荐理发师，我会认真考虑，因为我能直接看到他剪完的效果。但一个品牌刚进一座新城市时，可能还是需要花钱做广告。

questions.en: What do you think about the idea that businesses should use more of their profits to help society?
questions.zh: 有人认为企业应该拿出更多利润回馈社会。你怎么看？
questions.sample: Businesses that are doing well should put some profits back into their communities. A sports shop could pay for equipment at a nearby school, for instance. It makes sense to choose something the business knows about and can maintain.
questions.sampleZh: 经营得不错的企业应该拿出一部分利润回馈社区。比如，一家体育用品店可以出钱给附近的学校添置器材。最好选企业自己熟悉、而且有能力长期做下去的事情。

questions.en: Do you think it's likely that, in the future, most businesses will be able to make a profit without damaging the environment?
questions.zh: 你觉得将来大多数企业都有可能在不破坏环境的情况下盈利吗？
questions.sample: I expect many firms to cut their environmental impact, although completely avoiding harm is a high bar. A repair shop can earn money by extending the life of a phone, yet even that shop needs electricity and replacement parts.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得很多企业都能减少对环境的影响，但要做到完全没有损害，要求就很高了。一家维修店可以靠延长手机的使用寿命来赚钱，但就连这样的店也需要用电和更换零件。

questions.en: Why do some people start their own business?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人选择自己创业？
questions.sample: Independence is a big attraction. Someone who makes cakes at home might want to choose their own recipes and deal directly with customers. They may accept irregular earnings because they care about having control over their work.
questions.sampleZh: 能自己做主很有吸引力。比如，有人在家做蛋糕，可能希望自己决定用什么配方，也愿意直接和顾客打交道。为了能按自己的想法工作，他们也许愿意接受收入不那么稳定。

questions.en: Do most people prefer shopping at big stores or small stores?
questions.zh: 大多数人更喜欢在大商店还是小商店购物？
questions.sample: For a weekly shop, I'd say big stores have the edge because families can buy everything in one visit. For a quick breakfast or a missing ingredient, the little shop downstairs often wins simply because it's closer.
questions.sampleZh: 要是每周集中采购一次，我觉得大商店更占优势，因为一家人要的东西能一趟买齐。但如果只是买份早餐，或者做饭时缺一样配料，楼下的小店常常更受欢迎，就因为它近。

questions.en: What makes a business successful?
questions.zh: 是什么让一个企业成功？
questions.sample: A successful business gives people a reason to return and charges enough to cover its costs. Take a lunch shop near an office. A reliable meal, a short wait and a sensible price matter more than a fancy sign.
questions.sampleZh: 一门生意要想成功，既要有让顾客愿意再来的理由，价格也得足够覆盖成本。拿办公楼附近的午餐店来说，饭菜一直做得好、等餐时间短、价钱合适，这些都比漂亮的招牌重要。

questions.en: What makes a business fail?
questions.zh: 是什么导致一个企业失败？
questions.sample: One common cause of failure is ignoring what customers actually need. A shop can stock beautiful furniture, but if most people nearby rent small flats, large expensive sofas may sit there for months while the owner keeps paying rent.
questions.sampleZh: 常见的原因之一，是没留意顾客真正需要什么。一家店可以摆满漂亮的家具，可要是附近大多是租小公寓的人，那些又大又贵的沙发可能几个月都卖不出去，店主却还得继续交房租。

questions.en: Do you think children should learn about animals at school?
questions.zh: 你觉得孩子们应该在学校学习有关动物的知识吗？
questions.sample: Yes, animals give children a very concrete way to understand nature. Watching a butterfly emerge, for example, makes a life cycle easier to remember than a diagram alone. Teachers can also show children how to observe without disturbing it.
questions.sampleZh: 应该学，因为通过动物，孩子可以很直观地认识自然。比如，亲眼看一只蝴蝶破蛹而出，比只看一张图更容易记住它的生长过程。老师也可以顺便教孩子怎样在不打扰动物的情况下观察它们。

questions.en: Some people think that people who live in cities should not have pets. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人认为，住在城市里的人不应该养宠物。你同意吗？
questions.sample: I wouldn't rule out pets for everyone in a city. A well-cared-for indoor cat may be perfectly comfortable in a flat. The important questions are whether the owner has enough time and whether the animal's needs can be met.
questions.sampleZh: 我不认同城市居民一概不能养宠物。一只得到妥善照顾、平时就在室内活动的猫，完全可能在公寓里过得很舒服。真正需要考虑的是主人有没有足够的时间，以及动物的需要能不能得到满足。

questions.en: How popular is having animals as pets in your country?
questions.zh: 在你们国家，养宠物有多普遍？
questions.sample: Pet ownership seems quite common in Chinese cities, particularly cats and small dogs. Walking through a neighbourhood park in the evening, you're likely to see owners chatting while their dogs sniff around. It can become part of people's social lives.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国城市里，养宠物好像挺常见的，尤其是养猫和小型犬。傍晚去社区公园散步，很可能看到狗狗四处闻闻，而主人们站在一旁聊天。养宠物也可能成为人们社交生活的一部分。

questions.en: What kinds of animals are often in children's stories?
questions.zh: 哪些动物经常出现在儿童故事里？
questions.sample: Rabbits, bears, foxes and wolves turn up a lot. Their different appearances make characters easy to recognise. Children can follow a story about a tiny rabbit outsmarting a much larger wolf before they understand every word.
questions.sampleZh: 兔子、熊、狐狸和狼都很常见。它们长得不一样，孩子很容易分清谁是谁。就算孩子还不能听懂每一个词，也能跟上“小兔子靠机智胜过大灰狼”这样的故事。

questions.en: Some people think it's a good idea to take children to see animals in zoos. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人认为带孩子去动物园看动物是个好主意。你同意吗？
questions.sample: A visit can be worthwhile if the animals have proper space and children are taught to watch quietly. Seeing the size of a giraffe in person is memorable. I'd avoid places where the main attraction is animals performing tricks.
questions.sampleZh: 如果动物有足够的活动空间，大人也教孩子安静地观察，我觉得值得去。亲眼看到长颈鹿到底有多高，会是一次难忘的体验。至于主要靠动物表演把戏来吸引游客的地方，我会避开。

questions.en: How might older people benefit from having a pet?
questions.zh: 养宠物可能给老年人带来哪些好处？
questions.sample: A pet can give an older person company and a small daily routine. Feeding a cat in the morning gives the day a familiar start. A dog can also provide a reason to go outside and greet neighbours.
questions.sampleZh: 宠物既能给老人作伴，也能让每天有一点固定的安排。比如，每天早上喂猫，就给新的一天开了个熟悉的头。养狗还让人有个出门走走、和邻居打声招呼的理由。

questions.en: What do you think about the idea that animals are just as intelligent as humans?
questions.zh: 有人认为动物和人一样聪明。你怎么看？
questions.sample: I don't think there's a single fair test of intelligence for every species. People are especially good at using language, while a dog can find a familiar smell we would completely miss. It depends on what ability we're comparing.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得没有一种智力测试能公平地衡量所有物种。人特别擅长用语言，狗却能靠气味认出我们根本察觉不到的东西。所以答案取决于我们比的是哪种能力。

questions.en: Why have many people's attitudes towards animals changed in recent years? [e.g. keeping animals in captivity, wearing fur, being vegetarian]
questions.zh: 为什么近年来许多人对动物的态度发生了变化？可以考虑圈养动物、穿皮草或吃素等例子。
questions.sample: People can now see much more about how animals live and how products are made. A video showing conditions on a fur farm may change someone's shopping habits. Living with pets can also make animal welfare feel personal.
questions.sampleZh: 现在人们能更清楚地看到动物是怎么生活的，也能了解很多产品是怎么做出来的。一段展示毛皮养殖场环境的视频，就可能改变一个人的购物习惯。自己养过宠物，也会让人更切身地关心动物过得好不好。

questions.en: Do you think animals might deserve to have the same rights as humans?
questions.zh: 你觉得动物也应该享有和人一样的权利吗？
questions.sample: Animals deserve strong protection against cruelty, but giving them exactly the same rights as humans wouldn't always make sense. Voting, for example, is a human responsibility. For an animal, freedom from unnecessary pain and room to move are more meaningful.
questions.sampleZh: 动物当然应该受到有力的保护，免遭虐待，但和人享有完全一样的权利，在一些情况下说不通。比如，投票是人承担的一项社会责任。对动物来说，免受不必要的痛苦、有地方自由活动，才更有实际意义。

questions.en: Many people regard pets as members of their family. What do you think?
questions.zh: 许多人把宠物当作家人，你怎么看？
questions.sample: It makes sense to me. A pet may share a home with someone for many years, and people organise their days around its meals and care. I'd still respect the fact that animals have different needs from people.
questions.sampleZh: 我能理解这种感情。一只宠物可能在一个人的家里生活许多年，吃饭、照顾它，都会成为主人每天安排的一部分。不过我也会记得，动物有自己的需要，和人的需要并不完全一样。

questions.en: What are the advantages of keeping a pet?
questions.zh: 养宠物有哪些好处？
questions.sample: Pets can offer company and make ordinary days more active. Someone who works from home might otherwise spend an entire afternoon indoors. Taking a dog out gets them moving and can lead to a friendly conversation along the way.
questions.sampleZh: 宠物能陪伴人，也让日常生活多一点活动。在家工作的人本来可能整个下午都不出门。带狗出去遛一圈，自己动了起来，路上还可能跟人愉快地聊上几句。

questions.en: Why do people always tell children stories with animals?
questions.zh: 为什么人们常给孩子讲有动物的故事？
questions.sample: Animal characters make difficult ideas easier to talk about. A fox who takes all the food can start a conversation about sharing without pointing at a particular child. Children also remember a story more easily when each character looks different.
questions.sampleZh: 用动物当主角，有些不太好讲的道理就变得容易开口了。一只把食物全拿走的狐狸，可以引出关于分享的讨论，又不用点名说哪个孩子做错了。每个角色的样子各不相同，孩子也更容易记住故事。

questions.en: What types of sports competition do people in your country like to watch?
questions.zh: 在你们国家，人们通常喜欢看哪些体育赛事？
questions.focusWording: What sports events do people in your country usually watch?
questions.sample: Basketball games and table tennis matches attract plenty of viewers in China. A close table tennis final is easy to get caught up in because the score can change so quickly. Big international football matches draw attention too.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国，篮球和乒乓球比赛都很有观众缘。一场比分咬得很紧的乒乓球决赛尤其容易让人看入迷，因为得分变化特别快。重大的国际足球比赛也很受关注。

questions.en: What competitions do children usually have at school besides art and music?
questions.zh: 除了美术和音乐比赛，孩子们在学校通常还参加哪些比赛？
questions.focusWording: What competitions do children usually have at school besides art and music?
questions.sample: Schools often hold running races, relay events and ball games on sports day. There are also competitions such as maths quizzes and English speeches. A relay is especially good fun because classmates have a reason to cheer for the whole team.
questions.sampleZh: 学校在运动会上常常安排跑步、接力和球类比赛，此外也有数学知识竞赛、英语演讲之类的活动。接力赛特别有意思，因为大家可以给全队同学一起加油。

questions.en: Should governments invest in hosting big sports events?
questions.zh: 政府应该投资举办大型体育赛事吗？
questions.focusWording: Should the government invest in hosting big sports events?
questions.sample: Governments should invest when local people will use the facilities afterwards. A stadium that becomes a community sports centre could justify the cost. A huge venue that stays locked for most of the year is much harder to defend.
questions.sampleZh: 如果赛后当地居民还能继续使用这些设施，政府就值得投入。比如，一座场馆后来能变成社区体育中心，这笔钱可能花得值。要是花重金建成后，大半年都锁着门，就很难说服大家了。

questions.en: Some people say that being at a sports match is always better than watching it on TV or online. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，到现场看体育比赛总比在电视或网上看好。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Being there is exciting, but it isn't always better. At a football ground you can join the chants and feel the crowd react. At home the replay may show exactly why a goal was ruled out.
questions.sampleZh: 在现场看确实激动人心，但不一定每次都是现场更好。在足球场，你可以跟着喊口号，亲身感受全场观众的反应。在家看电视，则可以通过回放看清楚某个进球为什么被判无效。

questions.en: Do you think showing sports competitions on TV or online encourages more people to do sport?
questions.zh: 你觉得电视或网络转播体育比赛能鼓励更多人参加运动吗？
questions.sample: Yes, seeing a match can make a sport look worth trying. After a badminton final, friends might book a court together while they're still excited. Affordable courts and basic equipment make it easier for that first burst of interest to last.
questions.sampleZh: 会，亲眼看过一场比赛可能就会觉得这项运动值得一试。比如看完羽毛球决赛，几个朋友可能会趁着兴奋劲一起订个场地。如果场地价格能负担得起，也能弄到基本的器材，这份一时的热情就更容易延续。

questions.en: What types of competitions do children often take part in?
questions.zh: 孩子们通常参加哪些类型的比赛？
questions.sample: Children enter all sorts of competitions, from class quizzes to swimming races and storytelling contests. The ones they enjoy often depend on what their school offers. A child who dislikes running might be quite keen on a team science challenge.
questions.sampleZh: 孩子会参加各种比赛，从班级知识问答，到游泳比赛、讲故事比赛都有。他们最终喜欢哪一种，往往也取决于学校提供什么活动。一个不爱跑步的孩子，说不定就很喜欢组队参加科学挑战赛。

questions.en: How important is competition to a young person's confidence and development?
questions.zh: 竞争对年轻人建立自信和成长有多重要？
questions.sample: A fair competition can build confidence because children get a clear chance to test something they've practised. The result isn't the only part that matters. A nervous child who finishes a speech has already learned something about handling pressure.
questions.sampleZh: 公平的比赛可以帮孩子建立自信，因为他们有机会在明确的场合试一试自己练过的本领。比赛结果并不是唯一重要的东西。一个很紧张的孩子能坚持讲完整场演讲，就已经学到了怎么面对压力。

questions.en: Some people say the most competitive people always succeed in life. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，最好胜的人在人生中总会取得成功。你同意吗？
questions.sample: No, the desire to win can help someone practise, but it doesn't guarantee success. In a busy restaurant kitchen, a cook who refuses to share a pan because another cook is a rival can slow down the whole team.
questions.sampleZh: 我不同意。想赢的心态能让人多练习，但不能保证成功。在忙碌的餐厅后厨，如果一个厨师把另一个厨师当成对手，连一口锅都不肯借给对方，反而可能拖慢整个团队。

questions.en: Do you think international events improve relations between countries?
questions.zh: 你觉得国际活动能改善国家之间的关系吗？
questions.sample: They can improve relations by bringing people together for a shared experience. Athletes who train together may get to know one another beyond a flag or a uniform. A friendly tournament helps, even if deeper disagreements remain.
questions.sampleZh: 能。国际活动让来自不同国家的人有了共同的经历。运动员一起训练后，认识的就不只是对方的国旗或队服，还有后面的那个人。哪怕一些更深的分歧还在，一场友好的比赛也能起点作用。

questions.en: Do you think neighbouring countries have a more intense rivalry than countries that are geographically further apart? [e.g. in sport]
questions.zh: 你觉得相邻国家之间的竞争会比彼此相距较远的国家之间更激烈吗？比如在体育比赛中。
questions.sample: Neighbouring teams often have a stronger rivalry because fans meet regularly and know the history behind each match. A game between two nearby cities can mean a lot to local supporters, even if the teams are fairly small.
questions.sampleZh: 邻近队伍之间的竞争往往更强，因为球迷经常见面，也熟悉每一场交锋的历史。哪怕两支球队的规模都不大，附近两座城市之间的一场比赛，对当地支持者也可能意义非凡。

questions.en: What do you think about the idea that the only way to achieve world peace is to eliminate competition?
questions.zh: 有人认为，消除竞争是实现世界和平的唯一途径。你怎么看？
questions.sample: I wouldn't try to remove all competition. A match with clear rules lets opponents compete and still shake hands afterwards. For peace, I think countries need better ways to resolve disagreements and more chances to work on shared problems.
questions.sampleZh: 我不赞成消除所有竞争。一场规则清楚的比赛，允许双方尽力争胜，赛后照样握手。要实现和平，我觉得各国更需要找到解决分歧的好办法，也需要更多一起处理共同问题的机会。

questions.en: Why do some people like to watch sports events?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人喜欢观看体育赛事？
questions.sample: Part of the pleasure is that nobody knows what will happen next. Even a team that's losing can turn the game around at the last minute. Watching with friends also gives people something to celebrate or argue about afterwards.
questions.sampleZh: 乐趣之一就在于没人知道接下来会发生什么。哪怕是落后的队伍，也有可能在最后一分钟扭转局面。和朋友一起看，赛后还有值得一起庆祝或者争论的话题。

questions.en: Where do people normally watch sports events?
questions.zh: 人们通常在哪里观看体育赛事？
questions.sample: Most viewers can watch at home on a television or phone. For a big final, some prefer a café showing the game because there's a crowd to react with. People who live near the venue may buy tickets.
questions.sampleZh: 大部分观众在家用电视或手机就能看。到了重要的决赛，有些人更喜欢去有转播的咖啡馆，因为能和一群人一起欢呼或叹气。住得离比赛场馆近的人，也可能直接买票进场。

questions.en: What are the advantages of watching sports events online?
questions.zh: 在线观看体育赛事有哪些好处？
questions.sample: Online coverage makes it easier to follow a match that doesn't fit your schedule. You can watch highlights on the train or replay a point you missed. It's also practical when a tournament takes place in another time zone.
questions.sampleZh: 网上看比赛，不用完全被赛程牵着走。可以在火车上看精彩集锦，也可以倒回去看看错过的那一分。如果比赛在另一个时区举行，这种看法尤其方便。

questions.en: What sports matches are suitable for children to attend?
questions.zh: 哪些体育比赛适合带孩子去现场观看？
questions.sample: Local school matches or a daytime badminton tournament can work well for children. They can see the players clearly and ask questions between points. Shorter events with comfortable seating are easier for families than a late match in a packed stadium.
questions.sampleZh: 本地学校的比赛，或者安排在白天的羽毛球赛，都很适合带孩子去。孩子能看清运动员的动作，也可以趁两分之间的空当提问。相比很晚才开场、体育场又挤得满满的比赛，时间短一些、座位舒服的赛事对家庭更友好。

questions.en: Why do some people spend a lot going to other countries to watch sports events?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人愿意花很多钱去国外看体育比赛？
questions.sample: Some fans see an overseas match as a once-in-a-lifetime chance. They may have followed one player for years and want to hear the crowd in person. The trip often doubles as a holiday with other supporters.
questions.sampleZh: 有些球迷把出国观赛看成一辈子难得一次的机会。他们可能关注一名运动员好几年了，很想亲自感受现场观众的声音。这趟行程也常常能顺便变成和其他球迷一起度的假。

questions.en: What sports games are popular in your country?
questions.zh: 哪些体育比赛在你们国家很受欢迎？
questions.sample: Basketball and table tennis are easy to spot in China. Basketball courts give groups of friends somewhere to meet after school, while a table tennis game only needs two players. Badminton is another common choice in community sports halls.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国，篮球和乒乓球很常见。篮球场能让几个朋友放学后聚在一起，而打乒乓球只要凑齐两个人就行。在社区体育馆里，羽毛球也是常见的选择。

questions.en: How common is it for people to grow plants at home in your country?
questions.zh: 在你们国家，人们在家种植物有多普遍？
questions.sample: Growing a few plants at home seems fairly common, even in city flats. People might keep a pot of green onions by the kitchen window or flowers on a balcony. A full vegetable garden is easier to manage outside cities.
questions.sampleZh: 在家里养几盆植物似乎挺普遍的，即使住城市公寓也可以。有人在厨房窗边种一盆小葱，或者在阳台上养几盆花。想打理一整个菜园，在城外通常更方便。

questions.en: Why do some people grow their own fruit and vegetables?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人自己种水果和蔬菜？
questions.sample: Some enjoy picking food just before they cook it. A handful of home-grown herbs can make a simple meal feel special. Others like knowing how the food was grown and having something small to look after each morning.
questions.sampleZh: 有些人喜欢在下锅前才把食材摘下来。一小把自己种的香草，就能让一顿简单的饭吃起来有点特别。也有人喜欢清楚知道食物是怎么种出来的，并且享受每天早上都有点东西要照料的感觉。

questions.en: Some people think all children should learn how to grow plants. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人认为所有孩子都应该学习如何种植物。你同意吗？
questions.sample: I think every child should get the chance to grow something simple. Planting a bean in a cup lets them see that growth takes time and regular care. A school can run the activity even without a large garden.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得每个孩子都应该有机会试着种点简单的植物。把一颗豆子种在杯子里，他们就能看到，生长既要时间，也需要持续的照料。学校就算没有大花园，也完全可以安排这个活动。

questions.en: Do you think, in the future, people will grow more of their own food?
questions.zh: 你觉得将来人们自己种来吃的食物会更多吗？
questions.sample: More people may grow herbs and a few vegetables, especially if shared gardens become available. Still, someone with a tiny balcony is unlikely to grow a whole week's food. I'd expect home growing to remain a supplement for most city families.
questions.sampleZh: 如果共享菜园变多了，也许会有更多人种几种香草和蔬菜。不过，只有一个小阳台的人，大概种不出自己一周需要的全部食物。对大部分城市家庭来说，我觉得自己种的东西还是以补充为主。

questions.en: What are the benefits of having plants inside the home?
questions.zh: 在室内种植物有什么好处？
questions.sample: Indoor plants can make a small room feel more pleasant, particularly when there's little greenery outside. Looking after one also creates a quiet routine. Checking whether a new leaf has opened is a nice break from staring at a screen.
questions.sampleZh: 室内植物能让小房间待起来更舒服，尤其是窗外没什么绿意的时候。照料植物也给人添了一件能静下心来做的日常小事。盯屏幕久了，去看看新叶子有没有展开，就是个不错的休息方式。

questions.en: Some people say everyone can easily grow their own fruit and vegetables. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，每个人都能轻松种出自己吃的水果和蔬菜。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Not everyone has suitable space or time. A sunny balcony might produce plenty of tomatoes, while a window facing another building may get very little light. Someone who travels for work would also need a way to water the plants.
questions.sampleZh: 并非人人都有合适的空间和时间。一个朝阳的阳台也许能收获很多番茄，可一扇正对着另一栋楼的窗子，可能晒不到多少太阳。常常出差的人还得想办法在自己不在时给植物浇水。

questions.en: How realistic is it for countries to produce all of their own food?
questions.zh: 一个国家要完全依靠自己生产所需的食物，有多现实？
questions.sample: For most countries, producing absolutely everything would be difficult. Some crops need heat or rainfall that the local climate can't provide. Growing enough basic food at home seems more realistic than trying to produce every fruit that shoppers want.
questions.sampleZh: 对大多数国家来说，完全靠自己生产所有需要的食物并不容易。有些作物需要的温度或降水，当地气候根本提供不了。与其把消费者想吃的每一种水果都种出来，更现实的是先保证本国能生产足够的基本食物。

questions.en: Do you think science and technology always have positive effects on the food that is produced on farms?
questions.zh: 你觉得科学技术对农场生产出来的食物总是有积极影响吗？
questions.sample: Technology can help farms produce better food, but its effects depend on how it's used. A soil sensor might help a farmer avoid wasting water. Relying too heavily on a single crop, however, can leave a farm vulnerable.
questions.sampleZh: 技术可以帮农场生产更好的食物，但效果取决于怎么用。比如，土壤传感器可以帮农民避免浪费水。可是太依赖单一作物，也会让农场在出问题时更容易受到冲击。

questions.en: Do you think, in the future, population growth will be the most significant challenge for the farming industry?
questions.zh: 你觉得未来人口增长会是农业面临的最大挑战吗？
questions.sample: Population growth will add pressure, but I doubt it will be the biggest problem everywhere. In a farming area with unreliable rainfall, securing water may be more urgent. Losing part of a harvest matters even when local demand barely changes.
questions.sampleZh: 人口增长会给农业带来压力，但我不觉得它在每个地方都是头等难题。在降水不稳定的农业地区，如何保证用水可能更紧迫。就算当地的需求几乎没变，收成损失一部分也是个大问题。

questions.en: What are the advantages of growing vegetables or flowers at home?
questions.zh: 在家种蔬菜或花有什么好处？
questions.sample: Vegetables can go straight from the balcony into dinner, and flowers make a home brighter. There's also the pleasure of seeing progress. A plant that started as a handful of seeds can become a gift for a neighbour.
questions.sampleZh: 蔬菜可以直接从阳台摘下来做晚饭，鲜花能让家里更明亮。看着植物一点点生长，本身也是一种乐趣。最初的几颗种子，最后可能长成一份能送给邻居的礼物。

questions.en: Is it easy to grow plants at home?
questions.zh: 在家种植物容易吗？
questions.sample: It can be easy if the plant suits the flat. A hardy plant near the right window needs relatively little attention. Trying to grow something that needs full sun in a dark room is much more frustrating.
questions.sampleZh: 如果选的植物适合住处，养起来可以很轻松。把一株好养的植物放在合适的窗边，平时就不用花太多心思。反过来，想在昏暗的房间里种需要充足日照的植物，就容易让人觉得挫败。

questions.en: Why do some people like to grow plants?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人喜欢种植物？
questions.sample: Growing plants gives people a slow, visible result for a little regular effort. After a busy week, discovering a new flower can feel surprisingly rewarding. It also gives neighbours who exchange cuttings an easy subject to talk about.
questions.sampleZh: 每天花一点时间照顾植物，就能慢慢看到实实在在的变化。忙完一周后，忽然发现开了一朵新花，可能比想象中更有成就感。邻居之间交换枝条扦插时，也自然就有话聊了。

questions.en: Will people still live in tall buildings in the future?
questions.zh: 未来人们还会住在高楼里吗？
questions.focusWording: Will people live in tall buildings in the future?
questions.sample: Yes, tall apartment buildings will probably remain part of city life. When many people want to live near the same metro line, building upwards saves space. Reliable lifts and good shared areas will matter more as those buildings age.
questions.sampleZh: 会，高层公寓楼很可能仍然是城市生活的一部分。很多人都想住在同一条地铁线附近，往高处盖就能节约用地。等这些楼的楼龄越来越长，可靠的电梯和好用的公共空间会更重要。

questions.en: Why do many people prefer to buy land and build their own houses?
questions.zh: 为什么许多人更喜欢买地自己盖房？
questions.focusWording: Why do many people prefer to buy land and build their own houses?
questions.sample: Where people are able to buy a plot, building their own house gives them control over the space. A family with grandparents might want a downstairs bedroom and a small garden, features they can't easily find together in a ready-made home.
questions.sampleZh: 在允许买地自建住宅的地方，自己盖房就能自己决定怎么安排空间。比如，和祖父母同住的一家人，可能想在一楼设一间卧室，还想有个小花园，而买现成的房子不一定容易同时满足这两个要求。

questions.en: Is it important to protect historic buildings? Why?
questions.zh: 保护历史建筑重要吗？为什么？
questions.focusWording: Why should historical buildings be protected?
questions.sample: Historic buildings are worth protecting because they let people experience a place's history at street level. An old market hall can show how goods were sold and neighbours met. A photograph preserves its appearance, but you can't walk through it.
questions.sampleZh: 历史建筑值得保护，因为人在街上走时就能亲身感受到这个地方的过去。一座老市场大厅，可以让人想象以前商贩怎么卖货、街坊怎么见面。照片能留下它的模样，但没法让人走进去看。

questions.en: How usual is it in your country to live in tall buildings?
questions.zh: 在你的国家，住在高楼里常见吗？
questions.sample: High-rise flats are quite common in many Chinese cities. Several apartment towers may share one courtyard, a small playground and shops near the gate. Smaller towns and rural areas tend to have more low-rise housing.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国不少城市，住高层公寓很常见。几栋住宅楼可能共用一个院子、一小块游乐场，出小区门口就是商店。在规模小些的城镇和乡村，低层住宅通常更多。

questions.en: What are the disadvantages of living in a very tall building?
questions.zh: 住在特别高的楼里有哪些不便？
questions.sample: The main drawback is depending on the lift for almost every trip. A long wait is annoying when you're rushing to work, and a breakdown is a bigger problem for someone carrying shopping or pushing a pram.
questions.sampleZh: 主要的不方便是，出门回家几乎都得靠电梯。急着上班时等电梯很烦。如果电梯出故障，手里提着一堆东西或者推着婴儿车的人就更麻烦了。

questions.en: Do you think, in the future, more people will live in tall buildings?
questions.zh: 你觉得未来会有更多人住进高楼吗？
questions.sample: I expect the number to rise in growing cities where land near jobs is expensive. A single apartment block can house many families close to public transport. Elsewhere, people may still choose smaller buildings if there's enough space.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得在那些还在发展、工作机会附近地价又高的城市，住高楼的人数会增加。一栋公寓楼就可以让许多家庭住在公共交通站点附近。在空间充足的地方，人们还是可能选择规模小些的楼房。

questions.en: Do you think a country's climate can influence the design of its buildings?
questions.zh: 你觉得一个国家的气候会影响当地的建筑设计吗？
questions.sample: Climate has a strong influence on design. In wet areas, a sloping roof can help rain run off, while shaded balconies are useful in hot places. Those features make everyday life more comfortable and reduce some maintenance problems.
questions.sampleZh: 气候对建筑设计的影响很大。在多雨的地方，倾斜的屋顶便于排水。在炎热的地方，能遮阳的阳台就很实用。这些设计既让日常生活更舒服，也能减少一些维护上的麻烦。

questions.en: Why do some people decide to design their own house?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人决定自己设计住宅？
questions.sample: People sometimes design their own house because ordinary layouts don't suit their routines. A musician might need a room for practice, or a large family might want the kitchen next to the dining area. Those choices can make daily life easier.
questions.sampleZh: 有些人亲自设计房子，是因为常见的户型不适合自己的生活习惯。音乐人可能需要一间练习室，大家庭可能想把厨房放在餐厅旁边。这些选择能让每天过得更方便。

questions.en: How challenging do you think the job of an architect is?
questions.zh: 你觉得建筑师这份工作有多大挑战？
questions.sample: It's a demanding job because an architect has to balance several needs at once. A client may want large windows, a low budget and privacy from the street. Finding a design that meets all three takes patience and judgement.
questions.sampleZh: 建筑师这份工作挺有挑战，因为他们得同时照顾好几个方面。客户可能既想要大窗户，又想控制预算，还不想被街上的人看到屋里。要拿出能兼顾三者的方案，需要耐心和判断力。

questions.en: Some people think new buildings should not be constructed in historical city centres. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人认为，在历史悠久的市中心不应再建新楼。你同意吗？
questions.sample: New buildings can belong in historic centres if they fit the scale of the street. A small modern library might serve people who live there. A tower that blocks the view of an old square would be a different matter.
questions.sampleZh: 只要体量和整条街道相称，新建筑也可以建在历史城区。一间规模不大的现代图书馆，可能正好能服务周围居民。但如果是一座挡住古广场景观的高塔，那就得另当别论了。

questions.en: Do you think it is better to extend an existing city or build a new one?
questions.zh: 你觉得扩建现有城市和新建一座城市，哪个更好？
questions.sample: Usually I'd improve an existing city first. Extending a metro line or rebuilding unused housing can serve people who already have jobs and friends nearby. A new city needs schools, shops and transport before it can feel like a community.
questions.sampleZh: 通常我会优先改善现有城市。延长一段地铁线，或者改造空置住房，就能服务那些工作和朋友都已经在当地的人。一座新城得先有学校、商店和交通设施，才能慢慢有社区的感觉。

questions.en: Why might it be important to consult local residents when planning new developments in a city?
questions.zh: 在规划城市里的新开发项目时，为什么征求当地居民的意见可能很重要？
questions.sample: Residents know small details that a plan on paper can miss. A patch of open ground might be the only place where older people exercise together. Asking them early gives planners a chance to preserve what already works.
questions.sampleZh: 居民知道很多图纸上看不出来的细节。一块看似普通的空地，也许是附近老人唯一能一起锻炼的地方。早点问问他们的意见，规划者就有机会保留那些本来就很好用的空间。

questions.en: Are there many tall buildings in your country?
questions.zh: 你们国家的高楼多吗？
questions.sample: Yes, especially around business districts and new residential developments in Chinese cities. You can often see office towers near a major station and groups of apartment buildings just beyond them. The skyline looks quite different in smaller towns.
questions.sampleZh: 有，特别是在中国城市的商务区和新建住宅区一带。大型车站附近常常能看到高层写字楼，再往外走一点，又是成片的公寓楼。小城镇的天际线看起来就很不一样。

questions.en: What are the differences between those tall buildings in your country?
questions.zh: 你们国家的高楼之间有哪些不同？

context.zh: 这里讨论的是你所在国家的高楼。可以选两三座熟悉的建筑，说出它们的区别。
context.en: Are there many tall buildings in your country?

questions.sample: Some high-rises are glass office towers with busy entrances, while others are apartment blocks with balconies and washing hanging outside. The ground floor can tell you a lot, too. Residents need groceries nearby, while office workers look for lunch.
questions.sampleZh: 有些高楼是入口人来人往的玻璃写字楼，有些则是带阳台、外面晾着衣服的居民楼。看看一楼也能看出不少区别。居民需要就近买菜，而上班族想找地方吃午饭。

questions.en: Why are different places laid out and designed differently?
questions.zh: 为什么不同地方的布局和设计各不相同？
questions.sample: A place is usually laid out around the people using it and the land available. A market needs easy access for deliveries and space for shoppers to stop. A residential street may need quieter paths and a safe play area instead.
questions.sampleZh: 一个地方的布局通常取决于谁来用、能用多少地。市场要方便送货，也要给顾客留出停下来挑选的空间。住宅街区可能更需要安静的小路和让孩子安全玩耍的地方。

questions.en: What are the advantages of living in tall buildings?
questions.zh: 住在高楼里有哪些好处？
questions.sample: Higher floors often have an open view and get good natural light. Tall apartment buildings can also fit many homes close to shops and transport. For a commuter, being able to walk to a station is a clear benefit.
questions.sampleZh: 住高层往往视野开阔，采光也好。高层公寓还能让许多住户都靠近商店和公共交通。对通勤的人来说，能步行去车站就是一个很实际的好处。

questions.en: Why do some people like to remodel and decorate their homes themselves?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人喜欢自己改造、布置家里？
questions.sample: Doing the work yourself lets you control both the cost and the little details. Someone might turn an awkward corner into a reading bench that fits perfectly. It's satisfying to use something you designed with your own hands.
questions.sampleZh: 亲自动手可以同时把控预算和各种小细节。比如，有人能把一个不好利用的角落改成尺寸刚刚好的阅读长椅。每天用着自己亲手设计、亲手做出来的东西，很有满足感。

questions.en: What kind of interior design style do most people like?
questions.zh: 大多数人喜欢什么样的室内设计风格？
questions.sample: Simple, practical rooms seem to appeal to many people, particularly in smaller flats. Light colours and furniture with storage make limited space easier to use. People still add character through things like family photos, plants or a favourite lamp.
questions.sampleZh: 简单实用的风格似乎挺受欢迎，在小户型里尤其如此。浅色调和带储物空间的家具，能让有限的空间更好用。人们也可以用家庭照片、植物或自己喜欢的一盏灯，让房间有个人特色。

questions.en: What kinds of videos are popular in your country?
questions.zh: 哪些类型的视频在你们国家很受欢迎？
questions.sample: Food clips, comedy sketches and short travel videos all seem popular in China. Food videos are easy to share because people can save a recipe or recognise a local dish, even if they only have a minute to watch.
questions.sampleZh: 美食短片、搞笑小品和简短的旅行视频，在中国好像都很受欢迎。美食视频特别容易被转发，因为哪怕只有一分钟，人们也可以收藏一个食谱，或者认出一道自己熟悉的家乡菜。

questions.en: What skills can people learn by watching a video?
questions.zh: 人们可以通过观看视频学会哪些技能？
questions.sample: Videos are especially helpful for skills where movement matters, such as folding dumplings or adjusting a bicycle seat. You can pause at the awkward part and copy the hand position. Making a first attempt afterwards helps the lesson stick.
questions.sampleZh: 如果一件事很讲究动作，视频尤其有用，比如包饺子，或者调自行车座椅的高度。碰到难的那一步，可以按暂停，对着画面模仿手怎么放。看完再亲手试一次，也更容易记牢。

questions.en: Do younger people and older people like the same kinds of videos?
questions.zh: 年轻人和老年人喜欢看同样类型的视频吗？
questions.sample: There's plenty of overlap, especially with humour and food. A teenager might send a cooking clip to a grandparent and both enjoy it. Their choices can still differ because they follow different creators and have different amounts of spare time.
questions.sampleZh: 两代人喜欢的类型有不少重合，特别是在搞笑和美食上。十几岁的孩子给祖父母发一段做菜视频，双方都可能喜欢。不过他们关注的创作者不一样，空闲时间也有多有少，选择自然还是会有区别。

questions.en: Why do some videos become very popular around the world?
questions.zh: 为什么有些视频能在世界各地走红？
questions.sample: A video can travel worldwide when people understand it without much explanation. A funny reaction or a clever trick may work in several languages. If viewers can describe it in one sentence, they're more likely to send it to friends.
questions.sampleZh: 如果观众不用听很多解释就能看明白，一个视频就有机会传遍世界。一个好笑的反应，或者一个巧妙的小技巧，换成好几种语言也依然有意思。如果观众能用一句话说清它好在哪儿，就更容易把它发给朋友。

questions.en: Do you think people can master any skill by watching videos?
questions.zh: 你觉得单靠看视频，人们就能掌握任何一种技能吗？
questions.sample: Watching can show the steps, but mastery takes practice and feedback. A swimmer may understand a stroke perfectly on screen and still struggle to breathe at the right moment in the water. A coach can spot what the video cannot.
questions.sampleZh: 看视频能看清步骤，但要熟练掌握还得靠练习和反馈。一个人可能在屏幕上把某个泳姿看得特别明白，真的下水后却还是掌握不好换气的时机。教练能注意到的动作问题，视频本身可看不出来。

questions.en: Do you think watching a video is a more effective way to learn than reading instructions?
questions.zh: 你觉得通过看视频学习比阅读操作说明更有效吗？
questions.sample: Video works better for a moving task, such as tying a knot. Reading is often quicker when you need one precise detail, like the correct oven temperature. I would choose the format according to the part I'm trying to learn.
questions.sampleZh: 要学的是一个动态的动作，比如打绳结，看视频更有效。如果只是查一个明确的细节，比如烤箱该调到多少度，读文字通常更快。我会根据当下要弄明白的是哪一部分来选。

questions.en: How might the news be influenced by videos that people record on their phones?
questions.zh: 人们用手机拍下的视频可能怎样影响新闻报道？
questions.sample: A phone recording can bring attention to an event before a reporter arrives. It lets viewers see details that an eyewitness might forget. However, a clip may begin halfway through an incident, so journalists still need to establish what happened earlier.
questions.sampleZh: 在记者赶到之前，一段手机录像就可能先让公众注意到某件事。观众能从画面里看到一些目击者事后可能记不清的细节。不过，视频也可能从事情进行到一半才开始录，所以记者仍然需要查清楚之前发生了什么。

questions.en: To what extent should people trust the news videos that they see?
questions.zh: 人们对自己看到的新闻视频应该信到什么程度？
questions.sample: I'd treat a news clip as one piece of evidence. Before sharing it, I'd check who recorded it, when it was filmed and whether another reliable report gives the same account. A real clip can still have a misleading caption.
questions.sampleZh: 我会把新闻视频看作一项证据。转发之前，我会先看看是谁拍的、什么时候拍的，以及其他可靠报道讲的是不是同一回事。哪怕画面是真的，配上的文字也可能误导人。

questions.en: Do you think, in the future, the public's appetite for news videos will lead to the end of print journalism?
questions.zh: 你觉得未来公众对视频新闻的需求会导致纸媒新闻消失吗？
questions.sample: Video will probably reduce demand for printed newspapers, but I doubt it will end print journalism by itself. Some readers still want a long investigation they can read slowly. A moving image is useful, but it can't explain every background detail.
questions.sampleZh: 视频可能会减少人们对纸质报纸的需求，但光靠视频，我不觉得就会让纸媒新闻消失。有些读者还是想找一篇长篇调查报道，慢慢读下去。影像很有用，却无法把每一处背景都说清楚。

questions.en: Which is more helpful, watching videos or reading books?
questions.zh: 看视频和读书哪个更有帮助？
questions.sample: For practical tasks I'd choose video, but books are more helpful when I need to understand an argument. I can reread one difficult paragraph and make a note beside it, which is harder when a speaker keeps moving on.
questions.sampleZh: 学实际操作时我会选视频，但要理解一套论证，书更有帮助。哪一段难懂，我可以反复读，还可以在旁边写笔记。要是说话的人一直往下讲，就比较难做到这点。

questions.en: Are there any differences between the videos that young men and young women like to watch?
questions.zh: 年轻男性和年轻女性喜欢看的视频有什么区别？
questions.sample: You may see some differences in the channels people follow, though gender is a poor guide to any one viewer. A woman who plays football and a man on the same team may both watch the same match analysis.
questions.sampleZh: 人们关注的频道可能确实有些区别，可光凭性别很难判断一个人会看什么。一位踢足球的女性和她的男性队友，很可能都想看同一场比赛的分析。

questions.en: How do popular types of homes in the city and in the countryside compare?
questions.zh: 城市里受欢迎的住宅类型和乡村里受欢迎的住宅类型有什么异同？
questions.sample: City homes are more often flats in shared buildings because space is expensive. In the countryside, families may have a separate house with room for tools or a courtyard. That difference affects everything from parking to where children play.
questions.sampleZh: 城市土地贵，住房更多是同一栋楼里的公寓。在乡村，一家人可能有一栋独立的房子，还有放工具的地方或者自家的院子。这种区别会影响很多小事，从车停哪里，到孩子在哪里玩。

questions.en: What kinds of gifts might visitors take when going to someone's home?
questions.zh: 人们去别人家做客时，可能会带哪些礼物？
questions.sample: Fruit, tea or something to share with the family are sensible choices. A visitor who knows the host well might bring a favourite snack. I'd avoid anything too large if the person lives in a small flat.
questions.sampleZh: 水果、茶叶，或者能让主人一家一起分享的食物，都是合适的选择。如果很熟悉主人，还可以带他最喜欢的零食。假如对方住在小公寓里，我会尽量避免带太占地方的东西。

questions.en: Do you think a friend should be welcomed into a person's home at any time?
questions.zh: 你觉得朋友无论什么时候来家里做客，都应该受到欢迎吗？
questions.sample: Even close friends should usually check before dropping by. Someone may be working from home or looking after a sleeping child. A quick message gives the host a chance to suggest a better time and makes the visit more relaxed.
questions.sampleZh: 就算是好朋友，一般也该在上门前打个招呼。对方可能正在家办公，或者正在照看刚睡着的孩子。发条简短的消息，对方觉得不方便就能另约时间，见面时大家也更放松。

questions.en: What do people need to consider most when choosing a place to live?
questions.zh: 人们选择住处时，最需要考虑什么？
questions.sample: I'd put affordability and the daily commute first. A beautiful flat loses some of its appeal if the rent leaves no room for ordinary expenses. Testing the journey at rush hour can reveal more than a weekend viewing.
questions.sampleZh: 我会先看自己能不能负担得起，以及每天怎么通勤。一套房子再漂亮，如果付完房租就没余钱应付日常开销，也会一下子失去吸引力。亲自在高峰时段试着走一趟，可能比周末去看房更能说明问题。

questions.en: How usual is it to visit people at home in your country?
questions.zh: 在你的国家，上门拜访别人常见吗？
questions.sample: In China, home visits are quite normal among relatives and close friends, especially during festivals. People who have only recently met may choose a restaurant first. It lets them talk without anyone feeling they need to prepare a whole meal.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国，亲戚和熟悉的朋友之间互相到家里拜访是挺平常的事，过节时尤其如此。刚认识不久的人可能会先选在餐馆见面。这样大家可以好好聊，不会有谁觉得自己还得准备一整桌饭菜。

questions.en: How easy is it to find a good place to live in your country nowadays?
questions.zh: 如今在你们国家，找到一个合适的住处有多容易？
questions.sample: Finding somewhere suitable can be difficult in bigger Chinese cities because many people want the same convenient locations. There may be plenty of listings, yet very few within a person's budget and a reasonable journey from work.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国较大的城市里，找个合适的住处可能不容易，因为很多人看中的都是同样方便的位置。房源看起来可能很多，但既在预算内、离上班地点又不算远的，往往没几个。

questions.en: Do you think it is the government's responsibility to ensure that everyone has somewhere to live?
questions.zh: 你觉得确保人人有地方住，是政府的责任吗？
questions.sample: I think governments should make sure people have access to basic housing, especially in an emergency. That could mean temporary accommodation or affordable rental homes. People can still choose and pay for more space or a preferred location themselves.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得政府应该保证人们能获得最基本的住房，遇到紧急情况时尤其如此。具体形式可以是临时住处，也可以是租金可负担的住房。至于更大的空间或更中意的位置，人们依然可以自己选择并付费。

questions.en: Do you think new homes should ever be built on public 'green spaces' in cities?
questions.zh: 你觉得在某些情况下，可以在城市的公共绿地上建新住宅吗？
questions.sample: Only as a last resort. A public park may be the only free outdoor space for hundreds of nearby residents. I'd look at vacant buildings and unused sites first, then ask residents before giving up an established green area.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得只有实在没有其他办法时才可以考虑。对附近几百名居民来说，一个公共公园可能是唯一能免费使用的户外空间。我会先看看有没有空置的建筑和闲着的地块，真要占用现成的绿地，也应该先问居民。

questions.en: To what extent could people's lives be influenced by the area they live in?
questions.zh: 居住的地区能在多大程度上影响一个人的生活？
questions.sample: The area can shape a surprising number of daily habits. A safe path to school may let a child walk with friends, while a busy road may mean a parent drives them. Local shops and transport also affect how people spend their time.
questions.sampleZh: 住在哪里，能影响的日常习惯比人想象的要多。一条安全的上学路，可能让孩子能和朋友一起走去学校。换成一条车辆繁忙的马路，家长可能就得开车送。附近的商店和交通条件也会影响人们怎么安排时间。

questions.en: Do Chinese people like to visit others' homes?
questions.zh: 中国人喜欢去别人家做客吗？
questions.sample: Many Chinese people enjoy visiting relatives or close friends at home because they can talk without being rushed. It often feels more personal than meeting in a restaurant. With new acquaintances, a public place may feel easier for everyone.
questions.sampleZh: 很多中国人都喜欢去亲戚或好朋友家串门，因为可以慢慢聊，不用赶时间。在家里见面通常也比在餐厅更亲近一些。要是和刚认识的人见面，公共场合可能让双方都感觉更自在。

questions.en: What do Chinese people do when they visit others?
questions.zh: 中国人去别人家做客时通常做什么？
questions.sample: Guests often sit down for tea, catch up with the family and sometimes stay for a meal. At a family gathering, helping to prepare the food can be part of the visit because people can chat while they're working.
questions.sampleZh: 客人往往会坐下来喝杯茶，和主人一家聊聊近况，有时也会留下来吃饭。家人团聚的时候，一起动手做饭本身也是串门的一部分，边干活边聊天正合适。

questions.en: What kind of place do people in your country like to live in?
questions.zh: 你们国家的人喜欢住在什么样的地方？
questions.sample: Many people value practical neighbourhoods with shops, transport and somewhere to walk. A young worker might accept a smaller flat close to an office. A family with children might put a nearby school or a quieter street first.
questions.sampleZh: 许多人喜欢生活方便的社区，附近要有商店、有交通，也有地方散步。刚参加工作的人可能宁愿房子小一点，也想住在办公室附近。有孩子的家庭，可能会更看重附近有没有学校、街道安不安静。

questions.en: How often do you visit your relatives or friends?
questions.zh: 你多久去看望一次亲友？
questions.sample: I visit friends or relatives about twice a month. We usually pick a weekend afternoon, because nobody has to rush home from work first. If we can't find a day that suits everyone, I'll call and we'll try again the following week.
questions.sampleZh: 我大概每个月去看亲友两次。我们一般挑周末下午，因为谁都不用先从工作单位匆匆赶回家。要是找不到大家都有空的日子，我就打个电话，下一周再约。

questions.en: Why do people sometimes take a long time to reply to messages?
questions.zh: 为什么有时人们隔了很久才回复消息？
questions.sample: Often people see a message at a bad moment and mean to return to it. A question about a weekend trip, for example, may need a look at a work schedule first. A delayed reply doesn't always mean a lack of interest.
variants: In what situations do people spend a long time responding to others' messages?
questions.sampleZh: 很多人看到消息的时候刚好不方便，就想着等一等再回。比如有人来问周末要不要去旅行，可能得先看一眼工作安排才能答复。回得慢不一定说明对这件事没兴趣。

questions.en: What can people do when they don't receive a response to a message?
questions.zh: 发了消息却没收到回复时，人们可以怎么做？
questions.sample: It helps to decide whether the message is urgent before following up. A deadline may justify one short reminder or a phone call. If it's just a photo sent for fun, giving the other person some space is usually fine.
questions.sampleZh: 要不要跟进，最好先看消息急不急。如果有明确的截止时间，可以简短提醒一次，或者打个电话。如果只是一张觉得有意思、随手发去的照片，给对方一点空间通常就好。

questions.en: Do you think it is fair to expect people to reply quickly to messages at all times?
questions.zh: 要求别人无论什么时候都迅速回消息，你觉得合理吗？
questions.sample: No, quick replies shouldn't be expected around the clock. People may be in class, driving or simply having dinner with their family. Agreeing on a phone call for urgent matters takes some pressure off ordinary messages.
questions.sampleZh: 不公平，不能要求别人一天到晚都得马上回消息。他们可能在上课、开车，也可能只是想和家人好好吃顿饭。事先约定有急事就打电话，平时发消息就不会有那么大的压力。

questions.en: How can people show respect when communicating online?
questions.zh: 人们在网上交流时，可以怎样表达对他人的尊重？
questions.sample: Respect online often comes down to timing and tone. I would make a clear request, give the other person time to answer and ask before forwarding a private message. Those small choices matter even when you can't see someone's reaction.
questions.sampleZh: 在网上尊重别人，往往体现在发消息的时间和语气上。我会把请求说清楚，给对方留出回应的时间，要转发私信也会先征求同意。即使看不到对方的表情，这些小小的选择也一样重要。

questions.en: Do you think people show more respect when communicating with strangers than with their friends?
questions.zh: 你觉得人们和陌生人交流时，会比和朋友交流时更尊重对方吗？
questions.sample: People are often more formal with strangers, but that doesn't always mean greater respect. With a close friend, respect might mean remembering a difficult date or giving an honest answer. Polite words and considerate behaviour can look quite different.
questions.sampleZh: 人们面对陌生人时往往更正式，但这不一定说明他们对陌生人更尊重。对亲近的朋友，尊重可能是记得某个让他难受的日子，或者愿意给他一个诚实的答复。客套话和真正体谅人的举动，表现出来可能很不一样。

questions.en: Some people say modern communications technology has made it acceptable to ignore people. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，有了现代通信技术，不理会别人也变得可以接受了。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Technology has made it easier to leave a message unanswered, but it hasn't made that acceptable in every situation. A person doesn't owe an instant reply to a meme. Ignoring a teammate who needs a decision is harder to justify.
questions.sampleZh: 科技确实让人更容易把消息搁着不回，却没有让这种做法在任何情况下都合理。朋友发个表情包，你没有义务立刻回。要是队友正在等你拿主意，你却一直不理，就比较说不过去了。

questions.en: Do you think body language and tone are more important than words when communicating?
questions.zh: 交流时，你觉得肢体语言和语气比说出来的话更重要吗？
questions.sample: Tone and body language can change the meaning of the same words, especially during an apology. For instructions, though, the actual words matter more. A friendly smile won't tell a visitor which train platform they need.
questions.sampleZh: 语气和肢体语言能改变同一句话传达的意思，道歉时尤其如此。不过，要是给人指路或者讲具体步骤，准确的用词就更重要。光是友好地笑一笑，可没法告诉游客该去哪个站台。

questions.en: Some people think that if people learned to communicate more effectively, all disagreements could be avoided. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人认为，只要人们学会更有效地沟通，一切分歧都可以避免。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Clearer communication would prevent plenty of misunderstandings, but some disagreements come from genuinely different needs. Two flatmates can understand each other perfectly and still prefer different temperatures at night. They need a practical compromise as well as a good conversation.
questions.sampleZh: 沟通更清楚，确实能避免不少误解，但有些分歧来自人们真正不同的需求。两个室友完全能理解对方，却还是可能喜欢不同的夜间室温。除了好好谈，他们还得找到一个双方都能接受的具体办法。

questions.en: Do you think, in the future, artificial intelligence will have a positive or negative effect on communication?
questions.zh: 你觉得未来人工智能会给人际沟通带来正面还是负面的影响？
questions.sample: I expect a positive effect when AI helps people understand each other across languages. A visitor could translate a question and start a conversation that otherwise wouldn't happen. It becomes less helpful if someone lets a tool write every personal reply.
questions.sampleZh: 如果人工智能能让说不同语言的人互相理解，我看好它的积极作用。一个外地来的人可以先翻译一句问题，开启一段原本没法进行的对话。但如果连每一条私人回复都交给工具代写，帮助就没那么大了。

questions.en: In what situations do people not respond to messages at all?
questions.zh: 在哪些情况下，人们根本不会回复消息？
questions.sample: People often leave advertising messages or suspicious links unanswered because no real conversation is expected. In a busy group chat, they may also assume someone else has replied. A direct question with a person's name is easier to notice.
questions.sampleZh: 广告消息或者可疑链接，人们往往就不回了，因为对方本来也没打算跟你认真聊。在消息很多的群聊里，人们也可能以为别人已经回过。直接点名问一个问题，会更容易让对方留意到。

questions.en: What would you do if you did not receive a reply after sending out a message?
questions.zh: 如果发出去的消息一直没有收到回复，你会怎么做？
questions.sample: I'd wait a little, then send one short follow-up if I needed an answer. For instance, I'd mention the booking deadline for a shared trip. If there were no deadline, I'd be happy to leave the conversation for another day.
questions.sampleZh: 我会先等一等，如果确实需要答复，再简短地追问一次。比如，大家一起出游的话，我会提一下最晚什么时候得预订。要是并不赶时间，我也乐意改天再聊。

questions.en: Why do some people prefer sending a message instead of making a call?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人更喜欢发消息而不是打电话？
questions.sample: A message lets the other person reply when they're free. It's also handy for details that are easy to mishear, like a building number or a meeting time. A written address saves both people from repeating it on a call.
questions.sampleZh: 发消息可以让对方等到有空时再回。有些细节听起来容易出错，比如楼号或者见面时间，写下来也很方便。把地址发成文字，双方就不用在电话里来回重复了。

questions.en: How do you show your respect in your messages?
questions.zh: 你在发消息时怎样表达对对方的尊重？
questions.sample: I try to say what I need clearly and avoid making a non-urgent request sound urgent. If I message someone late, I'll say that tomorrow is fine. It shows I value their time as well as my own.
questions.sampleZh: 我会尽量把自己的需要说清楚，也不会把一件不急的事说得火烧眉毛似的。如果很晚才联系别人，我会说“明天回也行”。这样对方知道，我珍惜自己的时间，也尊重他的时间。

questions.en: Why do some people feel angry when others don't reply to their message?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人在别人不回消息时会生气？
questions.sample: Silence can feel personal when someone is waiting for a decision or sharing something important. Without a voice or facial expression, it's easy to imagine the worst. A brief reply saying you'll get back to them can take away that uncertainty.
questions.sampleZh: 当一个人正在等别人做决定，或者刚刚分享了一件重要的事，没有回应很容易让他觉得这是冲着自己来的。既听不到语气，也看不到表情，人就很容易往坏处想。简单回一句“我晚点答复你”，就可以消除这份不确定。

questions.en: When do people usually choose to go on vacation?
questions.zh: 人们通常选择什么时候去度假？
questions.focusWording: When do people usually choose to go on vacation?
questions.sample: Families with school-age children often travel during school holidays, while office workers may use public holidays or their annual leave. People with flexible schedules sometimes choose quieter weekdays because tickets can be cheaper and attractions less crowded.
questions.sampleZh: 有学龄孩子的家庭通常选在学校放假的时候出游，上班族则可能用法定假期或年假。时间比较灵活的人，有时会挑不那么忙的工作日，因为票价可能更便宜，景点也没那么挤。

questions.en: What influence does tourism have on local people?
questions.zh: 旅游业对当地居民有什么影响？
questions.focusWording: What influence does tourism have on local people?
questions.sample: Tourism can bring customers to local restaurants, guesthouses and small shops. At the same time, residents may face higher rents or crowded buses during busy seasons. The gains are easier to see when local people own the businesses visitors use.
questions.sampleZh: 旅游业可以给当地餐馆、民宿和小商店带来顾客。同时，到了旺季，居民也可能遇到房租上涨或公交车拥挤的问题。如果游客光顾的商家本来就是当地人经营的，旅游给他们带来的收益就更看得见。

questions.en: How do people usually plan holidays?
questions.zh: 人们通常会怎样规划假期？
questions.focusWording: How do people make preparations for their vacation?
questions.sample: Most people first agree on dates, a budget and who is going. Then they book the main transport and somewhere to stay. Checking travel times between attractions beforehand can save a family from spending half the day on buses.
variants: What preparations do people need to make before going away on holidays?
questions.sampleZh: 大多数人会先商量好日期、预算，还有哪些人一起去。接下来再订主要的交通和住处。出发前查一查景点之间要走多久，就不至于带着家人去了以后，发现半天都要花在公交车上。

questions.en: What kinds of places do people from your country go to for a holiday?
questions.zh: 你们国家的人喜欢去什么样的地方度假？
questions.sample: Some people choose coastal cities or mountain areas for a change of scenery. Others travel to a city they know for its food or museums. A short train ride is especially attractive when the holiday only lasts a couple of days.
questions.sampleZh: 有人会为了换换风景，选择海滨城市或者山区。也有人会去一座以美食或博物馆闻名的城市。如果假期只有两三天，坐一小段火车就能到的地方尤其有吸引力。

questions.en: Why do many countries try to attract large groups of international tourists?
questions.zh: 为什么许多国家设法吸引大批外国游客？
questions.sample: International visitors spend money on accommodation, meals, transport and local guides. Large groups can fill hotels even outside the busiest season. Countries also hope visitors will enjoy the trip and recommend the destination when they go home.
questions.sampleZh: 国际游客会在住宿、餐饮、交通和当地导游服务上花钱。即便不在最旺的时段，大型旅行团也可能把酒店的房间订满。各国也希望游客玩得开心，回去以后愿意把这个目的地推荐给别人。

questions.en: How do people make decisions about when to take their holidays?
questions.zh: 人们如何决定什么时候去度假？
questions.sample: People tend to compare their time off with the price and weather at the destination. A couple might move a trip by one week if trains are cheaper then. Families often have less flexibility because of school dates.
questions.sampleZh: 人们往往会把自己能休假的时间，和目的地的价格、天气放在一起考虑。比如，如果晚一周火车票便宜一些，一对情侣或夫妻可能就会把行程推迟一周。有孩子的家庭受到学校放假日期的限制，挪动的余地通常小一点。

questions.en: How do the places older and younger people like to spend their holidays compare?
questions.zh: 老年人和年轻人喜欢去的度假地点有什么异同？
questions.sample: Older travellers may put comfort and easy transport higher on the list, while younger people may accept a longer journey for an unusual experience. Their choices still overlap. A walkable historic town can suit both groups very well.
questions.sampleZh: 年长的旅行者可能更看重舒适和交通便利，年轻人则可能愿意走更远的路，换一种少见的体验。不过两类人的选择也有很多重合。一个适合步行游览的历史小镇，可能双方都很喜欢。

questions.en: How can people choose a good place to go for their holiday?
questions.zh: 人们可以怎样为自己选一个合适的度假地点？
questions.sample: I would start with what people want to do and how much time they actually have. If the aim is a restful weekend, a nearby town with one good walking route may be better than a famous city far away.
questions.sampleZh: 我会先看大家想做什么，以及实际有多少时间。如果只是想周末放松一下，附近一个有条好走的步行路线的小镇，可能比远方的知名大城市更合适。

questions.en: What are the advantages and disadvantages of planning every detail of a holiday in advance?
questions.zh: 提前计划好假期的每个细节，有什么好处和坏处？
questions.sample: Detailed planning can save money and make popular attractions easier to visit. The downside is that a late train can upset the whole schedule. I like the idea of booking the essentials and leaving one afternoon open to suggestions.
questions.sampleZh: 计划细一点，可以省钱，也更容易去成热门景点。缺点是，一趟火车晚点就可能打乱整个行程。我喜欢先订好最要紧的几项，再留出一个下午，到时候听听大家想去哪儿。

questions.en: Some people say mass tourism returns little benefit to local communities. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，大众旅游给当地社区带来的好处很少。你同意吗？
questions.sample: It depends on where the money goes. If visitors stay in an outside-owned resort and eat every meal there, little may reach the surrounding town. Buying from local markets and hiring local guides changes that quite a bit.
questions.sampleZh: 这要看游客的钱最后流向哪里。如果他们住在外地人经营的度假村，连每一餐也在那里吃，周边的小镇可能就分不到多少好处。去本地市场买东西、请当地人做导游，情况就会很不一样。

questions.en: Do you think mass tourism can continue without restriction?
questions.zh: 你觉得大众旅游可以一直不受限制地发展下去吗？
questions.sample: Busy destinations will probably need some limits. A narrow mountain path can only hold so many people before it becomes unpleasant or the ground gets damaged. Timed entry can spread visitors across the day while still supporting local businesses.
questions.sampleZh: 热门目的地大概还是需要一些限制。一条窄窄的山路能容纳的人有限，再多就走得不舒服了，地面也可能被踩坏。分时入场可以把游客分散到一天之中，同时让当地商家仍然有生意做。

questions.en: What is the ideal length for a holiday?
questions.zh: 度假的理想时长是多少？
questions.sample: For a nearby destination, three or four days feels about right to me. That's enough time to slow down after the journey and explore one place properly. A long international flight would make a longer stay more worthwhile.
questions.sampleZh: 如果去的是附近，我觉得三四天挺合适。路上奔波完以后，有时间慢下来，也能把一个地方好好逛一逛。如果得坐长途国际航班，待久一点才更值得。

questions.en: Is it important to plan a holiday ahead?
questions.zh: 提前做假期计划重要吗？
questions.sample: Some advance planning is important, especially for trains, flights and accommodation during a public holiday. Nobody wants to arrive and find every affordable room taken. Once those things are settled, there's room to decide what to do each morning.
questions.sampleZh: 提前做一些计划很重要，尤其是在公共假期，火车、飞机和住宿都要留意。谁都不想到了当地才发现，负担得起的房间已经全订完了。把这些事落实后，每天早上再决定当天玩什么也来得及。

questions.en: Where do young people in your country often go for holidays?
questions.zh: 你们国家的年轻人通常去哪里度假？
questions.sample: Young people in China often head for cities with interesting food, live music or a few well-known sights. Nearby camping areas are another option for a group of friends. A limited budget makes a good train connection especially appealing.
questions.sampleZh: 中国的年轻人常常会选有特色美食、现场音乐或者几处知名景点的城市。一群朋友一起出去的话，附近的露营地也是个选择。预算有限时，坐火车方便的地方格外有吸引力。

questions.en: What kinds of rules do most schools have?
questions.zh: 大多数学校有哪些类型的校规？
questions.sample: Most schools have rules about arrival times, classroom behaviour and handing work in. There are usually safety rules as well, such as walking on the stairs. Children tend to remember a rule better when someone explains the reason for it.
questions.sampleZh: 大多数学校都对到校时间、课堂行为和交作业有规定。通常也有安全方面的校规，比如上下楼梯时要慢走。如果有人解释为什么要这样做，孩子往往更记得住。

questions.en: Do you think, in the future, everyone in the world will be subject to the same laws?
questions.zh: 你觉得将来世界各地的人都会受到同一套法律的约束吗？
questions.sample: I expect countries to share some basic rules, but a single set of laws for everyone seems unlikely. A fishing community and a large inland city face different local problems. New technology may encourage agreement in a few areas first.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得各国会有一些共同的基本规则，但要让全世界所有人都适用同一整套法律，可能性不大。渔村和内陆大城市面对的本地问题并不一样。倒是新技术可能先推动各方在少数问题上形成共识。

questions.en: Why are rules important for schoolchildren?
questions.zh: 为什么规则对在校儿童很重要？
questions.sample: Rules make a school day more predictable. If everyone knows how to take turns in a science lab, students can concentrate on the experiment instead of arguing over equipment. Clear limits also help quieter children get a fair chance.
variants: Do you think school rules are important?
questions.sampleZh: 校规能让学生对在校的一天有比较清楚的预期。如果大家都知道在科学实验室里得轮流用设备，学生就可以专心做实验，不必为谁先用争执。明确的规则也能让比较安静的孩子有公平的参与机会。

questions.en: How can teachers and parents help their children follow rules?
questions.zh: 老师和家长可以怎样帮助孩子遵守规则？
questions.sample: Adults can explain a rule, model it and respond consistently when it is broken. A teacher who puts their own phone away during a discussion sets a clearer example than a poster alone. Children also deserve a chance to ask why.
questions.sampleZh: 大人可以先解释规则，自己照着做，遇到违反规则的情况也要前后一致地处理。比如，老师在讨论时自己先把手机收起来，比墙上只挂一张海报更能作示范。孩子也应该有机会问一句为什么。

questions.en: What types of jobs are rules especially important in?
questions.zh: 在哪些类型的工作里，遵守规则尤其重要？
questions.sample: Clear rules matter most in jobs where one mistake affects other people's safety. A train driver and a colleague on the platform need to understand the same signal immediately. There isn't always time for them to discuss what it means.
questions.sampleZh: 在那些一个失误就可能影响他人安全的工作中，清楚的规则尤其重要。比如，列车司机和站台上的工作人员要能立刻对同一个信号作出相同的理解。并不是每次都有时间停下来商量这个信号是什么意思。

questions.en: Some people think there should be rules about what people can wear at work. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人认为单位应该规定员工上班时可以穿什么。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Dress rules make sense when clothing affects safety or helps the public recognise staff. A chef needs suitable clothes in a hot kitchen. For someone doing desk work away from customers, more freedom usually seems reasonable.
questions.sampleZh: 如果穿什么关系到安全，或者能让公众一眼认出工作人员，着装规定就有道理。厨师在高温厨房里需要合适的工作服。但如果一个人是在不直接接触客户的办公室里工作，给他多一点穿衣自由通常也很合理。

questions.en: Do you think employees should be involved in making company rules?
questions.zh: 你觉得员工应该参与制定公司的规章制度吗？
questions.sample: Employees should have a voice, especially when a rule changes their daily routine. A manager may suggest a handover form without realising that it repeats work already done. Asking staff to try it first can produce a much better rule.
questions.sampleZh: 员工应该有发言权，特别是当一条规定会改变他们每天的工作方式时。主管也许会提出增加一张交接表，却没意识到上面的内容大家已经填过一次了。先请员工试用，往往能把规定改得更好。

questions.en: How might technology become more important in law enforcement?
questions.zh: 科技今后可以怎样在执法中发挥更重要的作用？
questions.sample: Technology may help officers organise evidence and respond more quickly. For example, the time recorded by a camera can help establish when an incident happened. People still need to check the context because a short recording rarely tells the whole story.
questions.sampleZh: 科技可以帮助执法人员整理证据，也能让他们更快作出反应。比如，摄像头记录下来的时间，可以帮助判断事情发生在什么时候。不过仍然需要有人核实前因后果，因为一小段录像通常讲不完全部经过。

questions.en: Do you think, in the future, crime will disappear and laws will become unnecessary?
questions.zh: 你觉得未来犯罪会消失，以至于法律也不再有必要吗？
questions.sample: I doubt crime will disappear. New ways of doing business also create new opportunities for people to cheat, and communities will continue to disagree about acceptable behaviour. Laws give them a common way to deal with those disputes.
questions.sampleZh: 我不觉得犯罪会消失。新的交易方式也会带来新的骗人机会，而且社会上对哪些行为可以接受，以后还是会有分歧。法律给大家提供了一种共同处理这些纠纷的办法。

questions.en: How does technology affect the law?
questions.zh: 科技对法律有什么影响？
questions.sample: Technology creates questions that older laws may not have covered clearly. A personal photograph, for example, can now be copied and shared in seconds. Lawmakers need to consider who should control that image and how a complaint can be handled.
questions.sampleZh: 科技会带来一些旧法律未必讲得足够清楚的问题。比如，一张私人照片现在几秒钟就可以被复制、转发。立法者需要考虑，谁有权决定这张照片怎么用，以及遇到投诉应该怎么处理。

questions.en: What environmental laws does your country already have?
questions.zh: 你们国家已经有哪些环保法律？
questions.sample: One example from China is the law on noise pollution. It concerns everyday problems such as excessive noise from construction or businesses near people's homes. I find it easy to relate to because a noisy street can affect a whole neighbourhood.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国，一个例子就是噪声污染防治方面的法律。它涉及的都是日常生活中的问题，比如施工或住宅附近商家产生的过大噪声。这一点我很容易理解，因为一条街太吵，受影响的可能是整个街区。

questions.en: How can a sense of national identity be developed?
questions.zh: 人们如何培养国家认同感？
questions.sample: A sense of national identity can grow through shared stories, language and public occasions. A child who hears how a grandparent celebrated the Spring Festival may feel connected to people they have never met. Schools and museums can add other perspectives.
questions.sampleZh: 共同的故事、语言和公共活动，都可以慢慢培养国家认同感。一个孩子听爷爷奶奶讲小时候怎么过春节，就有可能对许多自己从未见过的人产生一种亲切感。学校和博物馆还可以补充不同的视角。

questions.en: Do you think many people read local newspapers in your area?
questions.zh: 你觉得你住的地方有很多人读当地报纸吗？
questions.sample: I wouldn't expect many younger residents to buy a printed local paper every day. Local news is easy to find on a phone. A printed copy still appeals to some older readers who enjoy sitting down with it over breakfast.
questions.sampleZh: 我不太觉得有很多年轻居民会每天买一份当地的纸质报纸，因为用手机就很容易看到本地新闻。但对一些年长读者来说，早餐时坐下来翻一份纸报，仍然是一种享受。

questions.en: How useful is the internet for getting local news?
questions.zh: 互联网在获取本地新闻方面有多大帮助？
questions.sample: The internet is useful for news that changes quickly, such as a closed road or a delayed metro service. A local notice can reach residents before they leave home. I would check an official update before forwarding an unexpected claim.
questions.sampleZh: 对于变化很快的消息，互联网很有用，比如道路临时封闭，或者地铁延误。居民还没出门，就可能已经看到了本地通知。遇到出人意料的说法，我还是会先查一查官方消息再转发。

questions.en: Some people say people are more interested in local news than national news. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，与全国性新闻相比，人们对本地新闻更感兴趣。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Often people pay closer attention to local news because it changes what they'll do tomorrow. A new bus route can affect their commute immediately. A major national event may still take priority when it affects jobs or schools across the country.
questions.sampleZh: 很多时候，人们确实更留心本地新闻，因为它可能改变自己明天要做的事。新开的一条公交线路，可能马上就会影响通勤。不过，如果一条重大的全国新闻关系到各地的就业或学校，它也可能更受关注。

questions.en: Why do some people want to be very involved in their local community?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人愿意积极参与当地社区的事务？
questions.sample: Some people get involved because they want to improve something they use every day. A parent might join a neighbourhood meeting to ask for a safer crossing near school. Working with neighbours also gives people a chance to get to know one another.
questions.sampleZh: 有些人积极参与，是因为想改善自己每天都要用到的东西。比如，有家长参加社区会议，是想争取在学校附近设一个更安全的过街点。和邻居一起做事，也给了大家互相认识的机会。

questions.en: Do you think local communities were stronger in the past than they are today?
questions.zh: 你觉得过去的社区比今天更有凝聚力吗？
questions.sample: In some places, people probably knew their neighbours better because families stayed on the same street longer. Communities can still be close today, though. A residents' chat group can connect someone who needs help with a neighbour they've barely met.
questions.sampleZh: 在某些地方，过去的人可能确实更熟悉邻居，因为一家人常常会在同一条街上住更久。不过，现在的社区也可以关系紧密。居民群甚至能把一个需要帮忙的人，和一个平时几乎没见过面的邻居联系起来。

questions.en: What impact does not providing enough facilities for local people have on communities?
questions.zh: 如果给当地居民提供的设施不够，会对社区产生什么影响？
questions.sample: A shortage of shared facilities makes it harder for people to meet naturally. Without a playground or a community room, children and older residents may spend more time indoors. Those missing everyday encounters can gradually weaken local ties.
questions.sampleZh: 公共设施不足，人们自然碰面、顺便打交道的机会就会变少。没有游乐场或社区活动室，孩子和老人可能都会在家里待得更久。少了这些日常的碰面，邻里联系也可能慢慢变弱。

questions.en: How important is national identity to a country's economy? [e.g. buying locally produced goods]
questions.zh: 国民对本国的认同感，对一国的经济有多重要？比如，这会不会影响人们购买本国产品？
questions.sample: National identity can help local brands if shoppers feel proud to support domestic products. That connection might persuade someone to try a new brand once. Quality, price and service will still decide whether they buy it again.
questions.sampleZh: 如果买本国的产品会让消费者感到自豪，国家认同感就能给本土品牌带来帮助。这份感情可能会让人愿意先试一次新品牌。不过，之后还会不会再买，终究还是取决于质量、价格和服务。

questions.en: Do you think, in the future, national identities will ever be replaced by a single global identity?
questions.zh: 你觉得将来各国的国家认同有可能被一种统一的全球认同取代吗？
questions.sample: A shared global identity may grow, especially around issues like climate and sport. I don't expect it to replace national identities altogether. People can care about the world and still feel a strong attachment to a local language or festival.
questions.sampleZh: 共同的全球认同感可能会增强，特别是在气候、体育这样的话题上。但我不觉得它会完全取代国家认同。人们可以既关心世界，也依然对本地的语言或节日有深厚感情。

questions.en: Do people read the newspaper where you live?
questions.zh: 你住的地方，人们读报纸吗？
questions.sample: Most people around me seem more likely to read newspaper articles on a phone than buy the printed edition. They may discover a report through a link a friend shares. So the reporting still reaches them through a different route.
questions.sampleZh: 我身边的人似乎更常在手机上看报纸刊登的文章，而不是去买纸质版。他们也许是点开朋友分享的一条链接，才读到某篇报道。所以报道还是能传到他们那里，只是换了一种途径。

questions.en: Do people prefer local or international news?
questions.zh: 人们更喜欢本地新闻还是国际新闻？
questions.sample: For everyday decisions, local news probably has the stronger pull. It tells people about transport, schools or changes in their neighbourhood. International news becomes more important when a major event affects travel, prices or someone they know abroad.
questions.sampleZh: 要说和每天的安排有关的事，本地新闻大概更吸引人，因为它讲的是身边的交通、学校、社区变化。等到国际大事影响了出行、物价，或者影响到自己在国外认识的人时，国际新闻就会更重要。

questions.en: Do you think it's important to have a national identity?
questions.zh: 你认为拥有国家认同感重要吗？
questions.sample: I think national identity can give people a sense of belonging and shared responsibility. During a festival, familiar traditions can connect people who live far apart. There's also room to recognise that people from the same country have very different experiences.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得国家认同感能让人有归属感，也能让人感到自己对大家有一份责任。过节时，熟悉的传统可以把相隔很远的人联系起来。同时也要看到，即便来自同一个国家，每个人的经历也可能很不相同。

questions.en: Some people say it's easy for children to make new friends. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说孩子很容易交到新朋友。你同意吗？
questions.sample: It can be easy when children have an activity in common. Two children building a sandcastle can start playing before they know each other's names. A shy child entering an established class might need more time and a little help.
questions.sampleZh: 如果有可以一起做的事，孩子交朋友有时挺容易。两个孩子一起堆沙堡，可能还没问对方叫什么名字，就已经玩起来了。不过，一个害羞的孩子刚进到同学们早已熟悉的班级，可能需要多一点时间，也需要别人搭把手。

questions.en: Where can young children make new friends?
questions.zh: 年幼的孩子可以在哪里交到新朋友？
questions.sample: Playgrounds, classrooms and after-school clubs give children regular chances to meet. A place with a shared activity often works best. Children making something together at an art table already have a reason to speak to the person beside them.
questions.sampleZh: 游乐场、教室还有课后社团，都能给孩子提供经常碰面的机会。有共同活动的地方往往最合适。几个孩子在手工桌旁一起做东西，本来就有理由开口和坐在旁边的人说话。

questions.en: Do you think it's important for children to have a best friend?
questions.zh: 你觉得孩子有一个最要好的朋友很重要吗？
questions.sample: A close friend can help a child feel secure, especially on the first day at a new school. I wouldn't say every child needs one best friend, though. A small circle can provide plenty of support and different kinds of company.
questions.sampleZh: 有一个亲密的朋友可以让孩子觉得安心，特别是转到新学校的第一天。但我不会说，每个孩子都一定得有一个唯一最好的朋友。一个小小的朋友圈也能提供充分的支持，还能带来不同的陪伴。

questions.en: What are the advantages of people having friends who are older than they are?
questions.zh: 和比自己年长的人交朋友有哪些好处？
questions.sample: An older friend may offer a longer view of a problem. Someone worried about their first job can hear what an experienced friend found difficult at the beginning. That conversation also lets both people see beyond their own age group.
questions.sampleZh: 年长的朋友看一件事，可能会把眼光放得更远一些。一个刚找到第一份工作、心里忐忑的人，可以听一位有经验的朋友讲讲他最初也觉得哪些事难。这样的交流还能让两个人都看到自己这个年龄圈子之外的经验。

questions.en: Some people say that as people get older, they argue less with their friends. Is that true?
questions.zh: 有人说，人们年纪越大，和朋友争吵的次数就越少。真是这样吗？
questions.sample: Some people do argue less because they learn which small disagreements to let go. With close friends, they may also become more comfortable saying what they mean. Age alone won't solve a problem if neither person listens.
questions.sampleZh: 有些人确实会争吵得少一些，因为他们逐渐学会了哪些小分歧可以放一放。面对亲密的朋友，他们也可能更能坦然说出自己的真实想法。但如果两个人都不愿意听对方说话，光是年纪变大也解决不了问题。

questions.en: Why don't people always keep the same friends as they get older?
questions.zh: 为什么随着年龄增长，人们的朋友圈有时会变？
questions.sample: Moving city, changing jobs or having a different routine can gradually reduce contact. Two school friends used to see each other every day without making plans. After graduation, keeping that friendship going takes much more deliberate effort.
questions.sampleZh: 搬到另一座城市、换工作，或者生活作息变了，都可能让联系慢慢变少。上学时的两个朋友不用约，每天就会见面。毕业后要维持这段友谊，就得更主动地花心思了。

questions.en: How much does friendship contribute to people's well-being?
questions.zh: 友谊能在多大程度上提升一个人的幸福感？
questions.sample: Friendship makes a big difference because it gives people someone to share everyday worries and good news with. A short walk and an honest conversation can make a difficult week feel less lonely, even when the friend can't solve the problem.
questions.sampleZh: 友谊很重要，因为日常的烦恼和好消息，都有人可以一起分享。就算朋友没法替你解决问题，一起走一小段路、坦诚地聊一聊，也能让难熬的一周不那么孤单。

questions.en: Do you think people should value friendship above other types of relationships?
questions.zh: 你觉得人们应该把友谊看得比其他人际关系更重要吗？
questions.sample: I wouldn't put friendship above every other relationship. A close friend may understand parts of your life that a relative doesn't, while a family member may offer support in another way. The care people show matters more than the label.
questions.sampleZh: 我不会把友谊放在其他所有关系之上。一位亲密朋友可能理解你生活中亲人不了解的那一面，而家人又能用另一种方式支持你。重要的是彼此怎么关心对方，而不只是这段关系叫什么名字。

questions.en: How might society change in the future if friendship and other social bonds were stronger?
questions.zh: 如果友谊和其他社会联系都更牢固，未来的社会可能会有什么变化？
questions.sample: Stronger social ties could make it easier for people to ask for and offer help. During a power cut, neighbours who know one another are more likely to check on someone living alone. Small actions like that can build trust.
questions.sampleZh: 如果人们的社会联系更牢，求助和伸出援手都可能变得更容易。比如停电时，彼此认识的邻居更有可能去看看独居的人是否安好。这样的小举动积累起来，就能建立信任。

questions.en: Do you still keep in touch with your friends from childhood? Why or why not?
questions.zh: 你还和童年的朋友保持联系吗？为什么？
questions.sample: Yes, I still message a friend from primary school now and then. We play a word game online, and whenever one of us comes up with a really odd answer, that usually gets us talking about other things as well.
questions.sampleZh: 有，我现在还会偶尔和一个小学时的朋友发消息。我们在网上玩一个文字游戏，每次谁想出了一个特别稀奇的答案，往往就会从这个答案聊到别的事情。

questions.en: How important is childhood friendship to children?
questions.zh: 童年时期的友谊对孩子有多重要？
questions.sample: Childhood friendships give children a place to practise sharing, disagreeing and making up. Those lessons are hard to learn from instructions alone. Having one familiar face in class can also make a difficult school day much easier.
questions.sampleZh: 童年友谊给孩子机会练习怎么分享、怎么面对分歧、怎么和好。这些事情只靠大人讲道理，很难真正学会。就算班里只有一个熟悉的面孔，也能让孩子在学校里不顺心的那一天好过许多。

questions.en: What do you think of communicating via social media?
questions.zh: 你怎么看通过社交媒体与人交流？
questions.sample: Social media is convenient for staying in touch across cities or time zones. A voice message can feel more personal than a quick text. For a sensitive discussion, though, I'd prefer a call so I could hear the other person's immediate response.
questions.sampleZh: 如果不在同一座城市，甚至不在同一时区，社交媒体也能让彼此很方便地保持联系。比起匆匆打几个字，发一段语音有时更亲切。不过遇到比较敏感的话题，我会更愿意打电话，这样就能听到对方即时的反应。

questions.en: Do you think online communication through social media will replace face-to-face communication?
questions.zh: 社交媒体上的线上交流将来会取代面对面交流吗？
questions.sample: I don't expect it to replace meeting in person. Online messages are excellent for quick updates, but a shared meal lets people notice pauses, expressions and small changes in mood. Those details matter when a friend is having a difficult time.
questions.sampleZh: 我不觉得它会取代见面。线上消息很适合快速说说近况，可坐下来一起吃顿饭，就能注意到对方说话时的停顿、表情，还有情绪上细微的变化。朋友遇到难处时，这些细节很重要。

questions.en: What's the difference between having younger friends and older friends?
questions.zh: 和比自己年轻的人做朋友，与和比自己年长的人做朋友，有什么不同？
questions.sample: Younger friends may introduce someone to interests they have never tried, while older friends may have already faced a decision they're worrying about. That's a rough pattern, of course. Personality and life experience can matter more than the age gap.
questions.sampleZh: 年轻一些的朋友可能会带你接触以前没试过的兴趣，而年长的朋友可能已经面对过你现在正为之发愁的选择。当然，这只是一个大致的区别。有时候，一个人的性格和经历比年龄差距更重要。

questions.en: Has technology changed people's friendships? How?
questions.zh: 科技改变了人们之间的友谊吗？是怎样改变的？
questions.sample: Technology makes it much easier to keep friendships going after people move away. Friends can share a photo while the moment is still fresh. The risk is mistaking a quick reaction to a post for a proper conversation.
questions.sampleZh: 搬去别的地方以后，有了科技，维持友谊就容易多了。朋友能趁着一件事还新鲜，就互相分享照片。要小心的是，别把对一条动态随手点个赞，当成和朋友好好聊过了。

questions.en: What are the differences between food for special occasions and the food people eat every day?
questions.zh: 特别场合吃的食物和人们平时吃的食物有哪些不同？
questions.sample: Everyday meals are usually chosen for convenience, while celebration food often takes longer to make and carries a familiar meaning. A family might cook a quick bowl of noodles on a weekday and spend hours making dumplings together for a festival.
questions.sampleZh: 平时吃什么，通常图个方便。庆祝时吃什么，则往往做起来更花时间，也承载着大家熟悉的意义。一家人在工作日可能随手煮碗面，到了节日却愿意花几个小时坐在一起包饺子。

questions.en: How much can food traditions reveal about a culture?
questions.zh: 我们能在多大程度上通过饮食传统了解一种文化？
questions.sample: Food traditions reveal a lot about what a community grows, remembers and celebrates. Sharing dishes from one table, for example, tells a visitor something about the social side of a meal. One dish alone won't explain an entire culture.
questions.sampleZh: 饮食传统能让人了解一个地方种什么、记得什么、庆祝什么。比如，大家围着同一张桌子分享菜肴，这个习惯就能让来访者感受到吃饭时人们怎样相处。但光靠一道菜，解释不了一整个文化。

questions.en: When do people eat special food in your country?
questions.zh: 在你的国家，人们会在什么场合吃一些特别的食物？
questions.sample: In China, special food often appears at festivals and family milestones. People eat mooncakes around the Mid-Autumn Festival, while a birthday meal may include long noodles. The exact dishes can vary by region and by family.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国，节日或家中重要的人生节点，往往会吃一些特别的食物。中秋节前后大家吃月饼，过生日时饭桌上可能会有长寿面。具体做哪些菜，各地、各家都有自己的习惯。

questions.en: Why is food such an important part of celebrations?
questions.zh: 为什么食物是庆祝活动中这么重要的一部分？
