questions.sample: Food gives people something to do together before the celebration even begins. While one person prepares fillings and another folds dumplings, there's time to catch up. Later, sharing the finished dish makes the occasion feel like a joint effort.
questions.sampleZh: 在庆祝活动正式开始前，食物就给了大家一件能一起做的事。一个人调馅，另一个人包饺子，边做就有时间聊聊近况。等到大家一起吃做好的东西时，这场庆祝也会让人觉得是共同完成的。

questions.en: How have people's cooking and eating habits changed in recent years?
questions.zh: 近年来，人们做饭和吃饭的习惯发生了哪些变化？
questions.sample: Many people now use delivery apps and buy ingredients that weren't easy to find locally before. At the same time, some use short cooking videos to learn recipes from other regions. A weekday dinner can involve less preparation and a wider choice.
questions.sampleZh: 如今很多人会点外卖，也能买到以前在当地不太容易买到的食材。与此同时，有些人会看短视频，学着做其他地区的菜。一顿工作日晚餐，准备起来可能更省事，能选的东西却更多了。

questions.en: Do you think cooking meals at home has more advantages than disadvantages?
questions.zh: 你觉得在家做饭利大于弊吗？
questions.sample: For regular meals, I think home cooking usually has more benefits. You can choose the ingredients, adjust the portion and keep leftovers for tomorrow. The main cost is time, especially for someone arriving home late after a long commute.
questions.sampleZh: 如果是日常吃饭，我觉得自己做饭通常好处更多。食材可以自己选，分量可以自己调，多出来的还能留到明天吃。主要的代价是要花时间，对那些通勤很久、下班到家已经很晚的人尤其如此。

questions.en: Do you think, in the future, family members will eat meals together more often?
questions.zh: 你觉得未来一家人在一起吃饭的次数会更多吗？
questions.sample: I doubt families will automatically eat together more often. Flexible working could help some households arrange dinner, but different shifts and long commutes pull others apart. Choosing one regular family meal may matter more than changes in technology.
questions.sampleZh: 我不觉得家人聚在一起吃饭的次数自然而然就会增加。弹性工作可能方便一部分家庭安排晚餐，可轮班不同、通勤又长，也会让另一些家庭更难凑到一起。主动约定定期一起吃一顿，可能比科技怎么变更管用。

questions.en: Do you think food traditions can be influenced by location and climate?
questions.zh: 你觉得地理位置和气候会影响饮食传统吗？
questions.sample: Definitely. Places near the sea can build traditions around fresh seafood, while colder areas may have ways of preserving vegetables for winter. Over time, a practical response to local conditions can become a dish that people associate with home.
questions.sampleZh: 当然会。沿海地区可以围绕新鲜海产形成自己的饮食习惯，比较寒冷的地方可能会想出把蔬菜腌存过冬的办法。时间长了，当初为了适应当地条件而做的一道菜，就可能成为人们心里家的味道。

questions.en: Do you think, in the future, communities will be able to maintain their food traditions?
questions.zh: 你觉得各地社区将来还能保留自己的饮食传统吗？
questions.sample: I think many communities can keep these traditions alive if younger people actually take part in cooking. A written recipe helps, but making a dish beside an older relative teaches details like how the dough should feel.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得很多地方都能保住这些传统，前提是年轻一代真的也参与做饭。写下来的食谱很有用，但和长辈一起做，才能学到一些细节，比如面团揉好后摸起来该是什么感觉。

questions.en: Why are there special foods on special occasions or events?
questions.zh: 为什么一些特别的日子或活动有专门吃的食物？
questions.sample: Special dishes give an occasion an identity that people recognise immediately. Mooncakes, for instance, bring the Mid-Autumn Festival to mind even before anyone mentions the date. Preparing or giving them also creates a simple way to include others.
questions.sampleZh: 特别的食物会让人一眼就认出这是什么场合。比如，别人就算没说日期，看到月饼，我们也会想到中秋节。准备或者赠送这些食物，也是一种很自然地邀请别人一起过节的方式。

questions.en: Are there any differences between the food people eat today and the food people ate in the past?
questions.zh: 人们今天吃的食物和过去吃的食物有什么不同？
questions.sample: People today often have access to food from farther away and a wider choice throughout the year. Someone in an inland city can order ingredients from another region quite easily. Family favourites still stay on the table despite that extra choice.
questions.sampleZh: 今天的人通常吃得到来自更远地方的食物，一年四季可以选的东西也更多。一个住在内陆城市的人，同样能很方便地从外地买到食材。选择虽然多了，家人一直喜欢的菜仍然还在饭桌上。

questions.en: Do people today prefer eating at home or in a restaurant?
questions.zh: 现在人们更喜欢在家吃饭还是去餐馆？
questions.sample: For an ordinary evening, many people prefer eating at home because it's comfortable and usually cheaper. A restaurant is attractive when friends meet after work, especially if nobody has time to shop, cook and wash up afterwards.
questions.sampleZh: 普通的一个晚上，很多人愿意在家吃，因为自在，通常也更便宜。和朋友下班后聚会时，餐馆就很有吸引力，特别是大家都没时间买菜、做饭、洗碗的时候。

questions.en: Why do people have to get up early?
questions.zh: 人们为什么不得不早起？
questions.focusWording: Why do people get up early?
questions.sample: Work and school schedules are probably the biggest reasons people get up early. A long bus journey can mean leaving home well before the first lesson starts. Others wake early by choice because they enjoy a quiet walk or breakfast.
questions.sampleZh: 工作和上学的时间安排，可能是人们早起的最主要原因。要是坐公交去学校的路很长，就得在第一节课开始前很久出门。也有人是主动早起，因为他们喜欢安安静静地散步或者吃顿早餐。

questions.en: What are the benefits of arriving on time?
questions.zh: 准时到场有什么好处？
questions.focusWording: What are the benefits of arriving on time?
questions.sample: Arriving on time helps people trust one another and keeps the next part of the day on schedule. At a team meeting, everyone can hear the same explanation, so nobody has to repeat it for a late arrival.
questions.sampleZh: 准时到能建立彼此的信任，也能让接下来的安排按时进行。比如，团队开会时大家都在场，就能同时听到同一段说明，不用为迟到的人再从头讲一遍。

questions.en: If everyone went to bed early, would everyone get up early?
questions.zh: 如果人人都早睡，是否就会人人都早起？
questions.focusWording: If everyone went to bed early, would everyone get up early?
questions.sample: No, an early bedtime wouldn't make everyone wake up at the same hour. People need different amounts of sleep, and some have shifts or family duties during the night. A quieter evening gives them a chance to rest, but no guarantee.
questions.sampleZh: 不会。即使大家都早睡，也不意味着人人会在同一个时间醒来。每个人需要的睡眠时长不同，还有人夜里得上班或者照顾家人。晚上安静一些是给了大家休息的机会，却不能保证一定早起。

questions.en: Some people say the early morning is the best part of the day. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，清晨是一天中最好的时段。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Early morning is lovely when the street is quiet and there's no need to rush. I wouldn't call it the best time for everyone, though. Someone who thinks more clearly in the evening may enjoy that part of the day much more.
questions.sampleZh: 街道还很安静、自己又不用赶路的时候，清晨确实很美好。但我不会说它对所有人都是最佳时段。有人到晚上思路才更清晰，那他可能会更喜欢一天里稍晚的那段时间。

questions.en: Why do many people dislike getting up early?
questions.zh: 为什么许多人不喜欢早起？
questions.sample: Getting up early feels unpleasant when it cuts short the sleep people need. Some stay up because it's their only free time after work. Others simply find that they're more alert later in the day, even with a regular routine.
questions.sampleZh: 如果早起占掉了原本需要的睡眠，那肯定不好受。有些人晚睡，是因为下班或照顾完家人后，那是一天里唯一属于自己的空闲时间。也有人即使作息相当规律，到晚一些的时候还是会更有精神。

questions.en: What are the advantages of arriving early for an appointment?
questions.zh: 赴约时提前到，有哪些好处？
questions.sample: Arriving a little early leaves time for small surprises, like finding the right floor in an unfamiliar building. It also gives you a chance to sit down and collect your thoughts before an interview or an important conversation.
questions.sampleZh: 提前一点到，能给意想不到的小事留出时间，比如在一栋不熟悉的大楼里找对楼层。面试或者重要谈话前，也可以先坐一会儿，理理思路。

questions.en: What are some situations when it's not good to arrive very early?
questions.zh: 在哪些情况下，提前太久到场反而不合适？
questions.sample: Turning up very early at someone's home can make the host feel rushed. They might still be cooking or getting ready. If my bus arrived half an hour ahead of time, I'd usually take a short walk nearby first.
variants: Is it good to arrive early in any situation?
questions.sampleZh: 去别人家做客时到得太早，很容易让主人觉得手忙脚乱。他们可能还在做饭，或者还没收拾好。如果我坐的公交提前半小时到了，我通常会先在附近走一小圈。

questions.en: Why do some people think it's important to be on time while others don't?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人很看重守时，有些人却不太在意？
questions.sample: People who work with tight schedules may see lateness as passing inconvenience on to others. Friends meeting for a relaxed picnic may treat the time more loosely. Trouble starts when both sides assume their own expectation is obvious.
questions.sampleZh: 日程安排紧的人，可能觉得自己迟到就等于给别人添麻烦。朋友约着轻松野餐，对几点到也许就看得宽松些。问题常常出在，双方都以为自己的期待本来就应该是大家默认的。

questions.en: Why do people sometimes not notice time passing?
questions.zh: 人们为什么有时会察觉不到时间在流逝？
questions.sample: People lose track of time when an activity holds their attention and gives them no natural stopping point. A student editing a video might keep adjusting one small detail after another, then look up and realise an hour has passed.
questions.sampleZh: 一件事很吸引人，又没有自然的停顿点时，人往往就会忘记时间。一个学生在剪视频，可能一直在接连调整一个个小细节，等到抬头才发现，一小时都过去了。

questions.en: Why are deadlines necessary? [e.g. for work or study]
questions.zh: 为什么有必要设定截止日期？可以谈谈工作或学习中的情况。
questions.sample: A deadline helps people decide what needs doing first and lets others organise their work. If a student hands in their part of a group presentation late, the whole team has less time to practise and fix mistakes.
questions.sampleZh: 截止日期能帮人判断先做什么，也让其他人能安排好自己的工作。如果一个学生拖到很晚才交出小组展示里自己负责的内容，其他人排练和改错的时间就都少了。

questions.en: Some people say success today mainly depends on being skilled at managing time effectively. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，如今能否成功，主要取决于是否善于管理时间。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Managing time well helps, but success also depends on skills, support and opportunities. A designer can organise every hour carefully and still need useful feedback from a client. A good schedule creates room to do the work well.
questions.sampleZh: 善于安排时间当然有帮助，但成功还取决于能力、支持和机会。设计师可以把每个小时都安排得井井有条，却仍然需要客户提供有用的反馈。好的日程安排，能为把事情做好创造条件。

questions.en: Do you know anyone who likes to get up early?
questions.zh: 你认识喜欢早起的人吗？
questions.sample: One of the stallholders at our local market loves getting up early, even on her days off. She likes to do a crossword over breakfast before anyone calls. By the time the street gets busy, she's had an hour to herself.
questions.sampleZh: 我们当地市场有位摊主很喜欢早起，就连休息日也一样。她喜欢在还没人打电话来之前，一边吃早餐一边做填字游戏。等街上热闹起来，她已经独自清静了一个小时。

questions.en: What kinds of occasions need people to arrive early?
questions.zh: 有哪些场合需要提前到？
questions.sample: Airport departures, job interviews and performances all reward an early arrival. There may be a check-in queue or a particular entrance to find. A little extra time reduces stress and helps avoid holding up other people.
questions.sampleZh: 赶飞机、参加面试、去看演出，这几种场合都适合提前到。可能要排队办理手续，也可能得找一个特定的入口。多留一点时间能缓解紧张，也能避免耽误别人。

questions.en: Why do some people like to stay up late?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人喜欢熬夜？
questions.sample: Late at night may be the only time some people have entirely to themselves. After work or family duties, they can read, watch something or finish a hobby in peace. Others feel more creative once the day's interruptions have stopped.
questions.sampleZh: 对有些人来说，深夜是一天里唯一完全属于自己的时间。工作和家庭事务告一段落，他们终于能安静地读书、看点东西，或者继续做自己喜欢的事。也有人觉得，白天那些打扰一旦停下来，自己的创造力反而更强。

questions.en: What kind of people like getting up early?
questions.zh: 什么样的人喜欢早起？
questions.sample: People who enjoy quiet routines often like getting up early. A runner may appreciate an empty path before traffic builds up, and someone with a busy family might value a peaceful breakfast. The attraction is often the uninterrupted time.
questions.sampleZh: 喜欢安静作息的人通常也喜欢早起。喜欢跑步的人可能享受车流多起来之前空荡荡的小路。家里平时很忙的人，也许很珍惜一顿清静的早餐。真正吸引他们的，往往是那段不被打扰的时间。

questions.en: Do lots of people in your country speak more than one language?
questions.zh: 你们国家会说不止一种语言的人多吗？
questions.sample: Yes, quite a few people in China use more than one language, although their levels vary. Someone may use a local or minority language at home and Mandarin at school or work. Others have studied English but rarely use it in conversation.
questions.sampleZh: 是的，在中国有不少人会说不止一种语言，不过熟练程度不一样。有人在家使用本地语言或少数民族语言，上学、工作时则讲普通话。还有些人学过英语，只是平时很少用英语交谈。

questions.en: What are the best ways for adults to learn a new language?
questions.zh: 成年人学习一门新语言最有效的方法有哪些？
questions.sample: Adults learn well when practice fits a real need. Someone preparing for a meeting could rehearse a short introduction, record it and ask a partner for feedback. Using the same expressions in an actual conversation helps them stay in memory.
questions.sampleZh: 当练习能满足一个实际需要时，成年人通常学得更好。比如，要准备一场会议，可以先练一段简短的自我介绍，录下来，再请练习伙伴提意见。等到真的和人交谈时用上同样的表达，就更容易记住了。

questions.en: Why do children often find learning languages easier than adults?
questions.zh: 为什么孩子常常觉得学语言比成年人来得容易？
questions.sample: Children often get many chances to hear and repeat a language while playing. They may try a new phrase before worrying about every grammar mistake. Adults can learn well too, but work and other duties may leave them fewer hours to practise.
questions.sampleZh: 孩子们在玩耍时，往往有很多听一种语言、模仿它的机会。他们可能会先试着把新学的短语说出来，不会一开始就担心每个语法错误。成年人也能学得很好，不过工作和其他责任可能让他们练习的时间少一些。

questions.en: Do you think you need to speak more than one language to get a good job?
questions.zh: 你觉得要找到一份好工作，就必须会说不止一种语言吗？
questions.sample: It depends on the job. A local electrician can build an excellent career using one language, while someone answering questions from overseas customers may need two. Being able to communicate clearly in the language the job requires comes first.
questions.sampleZh: 这取决于做什么工作。本地的电工可以只用一种语言就把事业做得很好，而一位负责回答海外客户问题的人，可能就得会两种。首先要做到的，是用岗位所需的语言把事情表达清楚。

questions.en: How important is it for people to know other languages when they travel?
questions.zh: 对旅行的人来说，懂其他语言有多重要？
questions.sample: Even a few phrases are valuable when travelling. Being able to ask which platform you need or explain a food preference can make an ordinary day much easier. A translation app can help with anything more complicated.
questions.sampleZh: 出门旅行时，哪怕只会几句外语也很有价值。能问清楚该去哪个站台，或者能说明自己的饮食偏好，一天的行程就可能轻松许多。更复杂的内容，还可以请翻译软件帮忙。

questions.en: What do you think about the idea that knowing the vocabulary of another language is more useful than knowing the grammar?
questions.zh: 有人认为，学一门外语时，掌握词汇比掌握语法更有用。你怎么看？
questions.sample: For a beginner trying to buy a ticket, a few key words may be more useful than perfect grammar. As conversations become more complex, grammar starts to matter. Mixing up yesterday and tomorrow can change the meaning of a perfectly familiar verb.
questions.sampleZh: 对一个刚学外语、正要买票的人来说，知道几个关键词，可能比语法完全正确更有用。但等到交谈变得复杂，语法就重要起来了。如果把昨天和明天搞混，就算动词本身很熟悉，也可能把意思表达错。

questions.en: Some people say it's impossible to understand another culture without understanding its language. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，如果不懂一个文化群体的语言，就不可能理解它的文化。你同意吗？
questions.sample: You can learn a great deal through translated books, music and friendships, so I wouldn't call it impossible. Knowing the language does open another door. A joke, a polite refusal or a family nickname can be difficult to translate fully.
questions.sampleZh: 通过翻译过来的书、音乐和朋友，你也可以了解一种文化的许多方面，所以我不会说这绝不可能。不过，懂当地语言确实会多打开一扇门。一个笑话、一句委婉的拒绝，或者家人之间的昵称，有时很难完全翻译出来。

questions.en: How might the number of languages a person speaks affect their sense of identity?
questions.zh: 一个人会说几种语言，可能怎样影响他对自己身份的认同？
questions.sample: Speaking several languages can give someone a sense of belonging in more than one community. They might tell stories in one language at home and build friendships in another at university. That can broaden their identity without replacing where they come from.
questions.sampleZh: 会说几种语言，可以让人在不止一个群体里都有归属感。有人在家里用一种语言讲故事，到了大学又用另一种语言结交朋友。这能丰富一个人对自己身份的理解，同时保留他和家乡的联系。

questions.en: How desirable would it be for technology to replace the need for people to learn other languages?
questions.zh: 如果科技让人们不再需要学外语，你觉得这在多大程度上是件好事？
questions.sample: I'd welcome technology that removes pressure in an emergency, such as asking for directions at a clinic abroad. I wouldn't want it to replace language learning altogether. Sharing a joke without pausing for a translation creates a different kind of connection.
questions.sampleZh: 如果科技能缓解紧急时的压力，我会很欢迎，比如在国外的诊所里问路。但我不希望它完全取代语言学习。和别人分享一个笑话，中间不用停下来等翻译，那种亲近感是另一回事。

questions.en: Does speaking other languages help at work?
questions.zh: 会说外语对工作有帮助吗？
questions.sample: Yes, when colleagues or customers use different languages, it can make a real difference. A worker who can explain a delay directly may solve a problem in one call. For some local roles, technical ability will matter much more.
questions.sampleZh: 有帮助。当同事或客户说不同的语言时，这项能力可能非常有用。一个员工如果能直接向客户解释延误的原因，可能一通电话就把问题说清楚了。不过有些只面向本地的岗位，更看重的还是专业技术。

questions.en: Do people learn any languages other than English?
questions.zh: 除了英语，人们还会学习其他语言吗？
questions.sample: Certainly. Some people study Japanese or Korean because they enjoy films and music, while others learn French or Spanish for university or work. Having a specific reason gives learners a good excuse to keep using the language outside class.
questions.sampleZh: 当然有。有些人因为喜欢电影和音乐学日语或韩语，另一些人则为了上大学或者工作学法语或西班牙语。有一个具体的目的，就更容易在课堂之外找到机会，继续使用这门语言。

questions.en: Why is it easier for children to learn new things than for adults?
questions.zh: 为什么孩子比成年人更容易学会新东西？
questions.sample: Children often have more time set aside for learning, and they're used to being beginners. A child may fall off a bicycle and immediately have another go. An adult might worry about looking foolish or finding time for a second lesson.
variants: Do you think it is easier for children to learn new skills than for adults?
questions.sampleZh: 孩子往往有更多专门用来学习的时间，也很习惯当初学者。一个孩子从自行车上摔下来，可能马上就愿意再试一次。成年人可能会担心出丑，也可能在发愁什么时候才能有空上第二节课。

questions.en: How do people learn new things?
questions.zh: 人们通常怎样学习新事物？
questions.sample: A common way is to watch someone demonstrate a task, try it and get feedback. That works for cooking as well as for using software. A small first attempt usually reveals which part of the explanation you need to hear again.
questions.sampleZh: 一个常见的过程是先看别人示范，再自己试，最后听取反馈。学做饭是这样，学用软件也一样。先做一次小小的尝试，通常就会发现刚才的讲解里哪一部分需要再听一遍。

questions.en: What is the most important thing for learning a language well?
questions.zh: 学好一门语言，最重要的是什么？
questions.sample: Regular use matters more to me than studying for a long time once in a while. A learner who describes one part of their day aloud has to find the words themselves. Checking just one difficult expression afterwards makes the practice manageable.
questions.sampleZh: 对我来说，经常用这门语言，比偶尔一次学很久更重要。学习者如果试着开口描述一天里的某个片段，就得自己想办法把想说的话说出来。练完只查一个让自己卡壳的表达，练习就比较容易坚持。

questions.en: What kinds of plans do people make regularly? [e.g. with friends or family, for work]
questions.zh: 人们经常制订哪些计划？例如，和亲友的安排或工作计划。
questions.sample: People regularly plan meals, journeys and the jobs they need to finish that week. They also make small plans with friends, such as choosing a time for dinner. Those ordinary decisions can prevent several last-minute phone calls.
questions.sampleZh: 人们会定期安排吃什么、怎么出行，以及这一周要完成哪些工作。和朋友之间也会有些小计划，比如约好几点吃饭。这些普通的决定，有时能省下好几通临时打来打去的电话。

questions.en: Do you think it's important for everyone to plan their everyday lives?
questions.zh: 你觉得对每个人来说，规划自己的日常生活都很重要吗？
questions.sample: A little planning helps almost everybody, but a timetable for every minute would be tiring. Picking two important tasks and leaving some spare time can be enough. That way, an unexpected call doesn't make the whole day feel like a failure.
questions.sampleZh: 稍微做点计划，几乎对每个人都有帮助，但要把每一分钟都排满，就太累了。选出两件重要的事，再留一点空闲，可能就够了。这样，即使突然接到一通电话，也不会觉得一天的安排全被打乱了。

questions.en: Why do some people enjoy making plans?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人喜欢做计划？
questions.sample: Planning can turn a vague idea into something people feel able to do. Listing the train times and cost of a weekend trip makes it seem possible. Some also enjoy imagining the experience long before they set off.
questions.sampleZh: 做计划可以把一个模糊的念头，变成一件让人觉得自己办得到的事。把周末旅行的车次、花费一项项列出来，出游就变得可行了。还有一些人，光是出发前提前想象这趟经历，就已经觉得很开心。

questions.en: Do employees find it easy when things change at work?
questions.zh: 工作中出现变化时，员工容易适应吗？
questions.sample: Changes are easier when employees understand the reason and get time to learn. Introducing a new booking system without training can make experienced staff feel like beginners. A short practice session and someone available for questions can make a big difference.
questions.sampleZh: 如果员工明白为什么要改，又有时间学习，适应变化就容易一点。推出新的预约系统却不给培训，会让原本经验丰富的员工也觉得自己像个新手。安排一次简短的练习，再留一个能随时回答问题的人，就能帮上很大忙。

questions.en: When a company is planning changes, do you think it's necessary for the employees to be involved?
questions.zh: 公司计划作出调整时，你觉得有必要让员工参与吗？
questions.sample: Yes, people doing the work can spot problems that are invisible from a meeting room. A cleaner, for example, will know whether a new timetable allows enough time between rooms. Listening early can save the company from changing the plan twice.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得有必要，因为真正做这份工作的人能发现会议室里看不出来的问题。比如，一名清洁工就知道，新的时间表有没有给两个房间之间的清扫安排留够时间。早点听听意见，可以省得公司把计划改了又改。

questions.en: Do you think employees who can easily adapt to change at work are more successful?
questions.zh: 你觉得容易适应工作变化的员工更容易取得成功吗？
questions.sample: They often have an advantage because they can continue working when a tool or a team changes. But adaptation includes asking good questions. Quietly accepting an unrealistic new deadline might look flexible without helping the project succeed.
questions.sampleZh: 他们往往有优势，因为即使工具或者团队变了，他们也能继续把工作做下去。不过，会适应还包括能提出有用的问题。面对不切实际的新截止日期，一声不响地答应可能显得很灵活，却未必对项目有帮助。

questions.en: What should the priorities be for improving society?
questions.zh: 想让社会变得更好，哪些事应该优先考虑？
questions.sample: I'd start with affordable housing, reliable public services and chances to learn. These affect people's choices every day. A safe, affordable bus route to school or work can improve life more directly than a large project that few residents use.
questions.sampleZh: 我会先考虑可负担的住房、可靠的公共服务，还有学习的机会。这些事每天都会影响人们有哪些选择。一条安全、车费不贵、能到学校或工作地点的公交线路，可能比一个没多少居民用得上的大型项目更直接地改善生活。

questions.en: What part could individuals play in helping to improve their society?
questions.zh: 个人可以发挥什么作用，让自己生活的社会变得更好？
questions.sample: Individuals can start with a problem they understand and work with other people on it. A resident might help organise a weekend reading group for children. It's small enough to maintain, but it gives families a regular place to meet.
questions.sampleZh: 个人可以从自己熟悉的问题开始，再和别人一起动手做点事。比如，一位居民可以帮忙给孩子们组织周末读书小组。规模小，办下去不太难，却能给各家人一个可以定期见面的地方。

questions.en: Do you think, in the future, the speed of change in society is likely to keep increasing?
questions.zh: 你觉得未来社会变化的速度很可能会越来越快吗？
questions.sample: Change will probably speed up in areas such as communication because information and new tools spread so quickly. Other changes take much longer. A city can introduce a transport app in months, while building the railway itself may take years.
questions.sampleZh: 在通信等领域，社会变化很可能会继续加快，因为信息和新工具传播得特别快。但另一些变化要花的时间长得多。一座城市可以几个月就推出一个交通应用，真正修好一条铁路却可能需要几年。

questions.en: Do people often change their plans?
questions.zh: 人们经常改变自己的计划吗？
questions.sample: Small plans change quite often because people depend on the weather, transport and one another's schedules. A group may move a picnic indoors when it rains. Bigger commitments, such as a wedding date, are usually harder to rearrange.
questions.sampleZh: 小计划挺常变，因为人们要看天气、交通，也受其他人日程的影响。比如下雨了，大家可能把野餐改到室内。像婚礼日期这样的重大安排，通常就难改得多。

questions.en: Would you tell others if you change your plan?
questions.zh: 如果你更改计划，会告诉其他人吗？
questions.sample: Yes, if the change affects someone else, I'd tell them as soon as I could. A friend who has already set off deserves a phone call. For a plan that only affects my own afternoon, there's less need to announce it.
questions.sampleZh: 会。如果改变计划会影响别人，我会尽早告诉他们。要是朋友都出门了，我应当直接打个电话。如果只是我自己下午的安排有了变化，就没什么必要专门通知谁。

questions.en: Why do you think parents still make plans for their children nowadays?
questions.zh: 为什么现在仍有家长替孩子做计划？
questions.sample: Parents often plan because younger children can't yet judge travel time, costs or competing commitments. Choosing a suitable activity can be helpful. As children get older, letting them plan part of their own weekend gives them useful practice.
questions.sampleZh: 家长常常替孩子做计划，是因为年纪小的孩子还不太会判断路上要多久、要花多少钱，以及几件事放在一起会不会冲突。大人帮忙选个合适的活动是有用的。等孩子长大一点，让他们自己安排周末的一部分，也是很好的练习。

questions.en: How does technology help people make plans?
questions.zh: 科技怎样帮助人们制订计划？
questions.sample: A shared calendar makes it easier to find a time when everyone is free. Maps can show whether two places are actually close enough to visit on the same day. Those tools make practical details visible before plans are final.
questions.sampleZh: 共享日历能让人更容易找到大家都有空的时间。地图也可以帮你看看两处地方到底离得够不够近，能不能放在同一天游览。这些工具能在计划敲定前，把实际要考虑的细节摆到眼前。

questions.en: Do you think people like the process of making plans more, or the moment of carrying them out?
questions.zh: 人们更喜欢制订计划的过程，还是把计划付诸行动的那一刻？
questions.sample: It depends on the person and the activity. Planning a holiday can be exciting because everything still seems possible. For someone organising a team event, the best moment may be seeing people arrive and enjoy what they've prepared.
questions.sampleZh: 看人，也看要做的事。规划旅行时，一切似乎都有可能，所以光是计划就让人兴奋。但对组织团队活动的人来说，最开心的一刻可能是看到大家陆续到场，享受自己准备好的活动。

questions.en: Why do people often want to buy the latest technology for their homes?
questions.zh: 为什么人们总想给家里添置最新的科技产品？
questions.sample: People are attracted by the promise of saving time or making an ordinary task easier. A vacuum that works while someone is at the office sounds appealing. Friends' recommendations can help, although a new model may add little to what they already own.
questions.sampleZh: 新科技能省时间、让日常琐事更轻松，这样的好处很吸引人。比如，一台能在人上班时自己打扫的吸尘器，听起来就很方便。朋友的推荐也会推一把，不过新款的功能可能只比家里现有的产品多一点点。

questions.en: What types of modern technology do many people use in their homes?
questions.zh: 许多人在家里会用到哪些现代科技？
questions.sample: Smartphones, Wi-Fi routers and smart televisions are common examples. Some families also use robot vacuums or speakers to set reminders. The products that last tend to solve an ordinary problem, like keeping the floor clean when both adults work.
questions.sampleZh: 智能手机、无线路由器和智能电视都是常见的例子。有些家庭还会用扫地机器人，或者通过音箱设置提醒。能一直用下去的产品，往往能解决一个日常问题，比如家里两个大人都上班时，该怎么把地面保持干净。

questions.en: Do you think it's possible to live without a computer at home?
questions.zh: 你觉得家里没有电脑也能生活吗？
questions.sample: Yes, someone can handle messages, payments and entertainment on a phone. It becomes much less convenient if they need to write long documents or manage large spreadsheets. For those tasks, having a keyboard and a bigger screen is a real advantage.
questions.sampleZh: 可以，发消息、付款、娱乐这些事，用手机都能处理。可要是经常得写长文档或者做大表格，就会不方便得多了。处理这些任务时，有键盘和大一点的屏幕，优势很明显。

questions.en: What are the benefits for students of using technology in education?
questions.zh: 在教学中运用科技，对学生有哪些好处？
questions.sample: Technology lets students revisit explanations and practise at their own pace. A student who misses a step in a maths lesson can pause a recording and try the problem again. Feedback is especially helpful when it shows exactly where the mistake happened.
variants: Do you think it is good to use technology in education?
questions.sampleZh: 科技能让学生回头再看没弄懂的讲解，也可以按自己的节奏练习。如果学生在数学课上漏听了一个步骤，就能暂停录像，把题目再做一次。反馈要是能具体指出错在哪一步，就特别有用。

questions.en: Can technology have a negative effect on communication between students?
questions.zh: 科技会对学生之间的交流产生负面影响吗？
questions.sample: Yes, especially in group projects. A short message like "That's fine" can sound friendly to one student and annoyed to another. Sometimes a two-minute conversation after class clears up what twenty messages couldn't.
questions.sampleZh: 会，尤其是做小组项目的时候。比如同样一句“可以啊”，有的同学觉得语气很友善，另一个同学却可能觉得对方不高兴了。有时候，课后当面聊上两分钟，就能把来回发二十条消息也说不清的误会解开。

questions.en: Do you think, in the future, online learning will eventually replace face-to-face classroom teaching?
questions.zh: 你觉得将来线上学习最终会取代面对面的课堂教学吗？
questions.sample: I expect online lessons to stay, but I doubt they'll replace classrooms completely. You can watch a recorded lecture whenever you like. It's much harder to practise a group discussion or learn to use lab equipment that way.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得线上课程会一直存在，但我不太相信它们会完全取代课堂。录好的讲座，你想什么时候看都可以。可要用这种方式练习小组讨论，或者学会操作实验设备，就困难多了。

questions.en: What do you think about the idea that it would be desirable to use technology for medical treatment instead of doctors and nurses?
questions.zh: 有人认为，用技术代替医生和护士来提供治疗是件好事。你怎么看？
questions.sample: I'd welcome technology that gives medical staff more time with patients. I wouldn't want a machine to handle every part of treatment, though. A nervous patient might need someone to notice their hesitation and explain the options again.
questions.sampleZh: 如果技术能让医护人员有更多时间陪伴病人，我会很欢迎。不过，我不希望治疗的每个环节都交给机器。病人紧张得犹豫不决时，可能需要有人留意到这一点，再把几种选择解释一遍。

questions.en: Do you think, in the future, technology is likely to cause mass unemployment in society?
questions.zh: 你觉得未来科技很可能会导致社会出现大规模失业吗？
questions.sample: Some jobs will disappear, especially if most of the day involves repeating the same steps. Whether that leads to mass unemployment depends partly on training. A warehouse might need fewer people counting boxes and more people maintaining its equipment.
questions.sampleZh: 有些工作会消失，尤其是那些一天中大半时间都在重复相同步骤的岗位。至于这会不会引发大规模失业，一部分取决于人们能得到什么培训。比如，仓库可能不再需要那么多人清点箱子，却需要更多人维护设备。

questions.en: Some people think artificial intelligence that is capable of complex decision-making might pose a threat to humanity. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人认为，能够作出复杂决策的人工智能可能会威胁人类。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Yes, in situations where nobody can question its decisions. Imagine being turned down for a job because a system misunderstood your background. I'd want a real person to be able to explain the decision and change it.
questions.sampleZh: 会，尤其是在没有人能质疑它的决定时。想象一下，系统误解了你的背景，导致你被一份工作拒之门外。我希望能有一个真正的人解释这个决定，也有权改变它。

questions.en: What are the advantages and disadvantages of AI?
questions.zh: 人工智能有哪些优点和缺点？
questions.sample: AI can turn messy meeting notes into a useful summary in seconds. Its weakness is that a wrong detail can sound just as convincing as a correct one. I'd still check names and dates before sending that summary around.
questions.sampleZh: 人工智能几秒钟就能把凌乱的会议笔记整理成一份有用的摘要。它的弱点是，写错的细节和正确的信息听起来可能一样可信。所以在把摘要发给大家之前，我还是会核对人名和日期。

questions.en: Do you think people today should learn about AI technology?
questions.zh: 现在的人应该了解人工智能技术吗？
questions.sample: Yes, even people who aren't interested in computers would benefit from learning the basics. If an AI tool writes an email for you, it helps to know which details to check and which private information to leave out.
questions.sampleZh: 应该。即使对电脑不感兴趣，了解一点基础知识也有好处。比如让人工智能帮你写邮件时，你最好知道哪些内容需要核实，哪些私人信息不该放进去。

questions.en: Should children learn to use AI?
questions.zh: 孩子应该学习使用人工智能吗？
questions.sample: Yes, with some guidance. Children could ask it for clues to a puzzle, try solving it themselves, and then discuss whether the clues helped. That's a much better introduction than letting it finish a whole assignment for them.
questions.sampleZh: 应该，不过最好有人指导。孩子可以让它给一道谜题提供线索，自己试着解，再一起讨论这些线索有没有帮助。这样入门，比直接让人工智能替他们做完整份作业好得多。

questions.en: How can AI help in our lives?
questions.zh: 人工智能怎样帮助我们的日常生活？
questions.sample: One everyday use is planning meals. You tell it what you have in the fridge, and it suggests dishes that use those ingredients. When you're tired after work, even two sensible suggestions can save a trip to the supermarket.
questions.sampleZh: 一个日常用途是安排吃什么。你告诉它冰箱里有什么，它就能推荐几道用得上这些食材的菜。下班很累的时候，哪怕只有两条靠谱的建议，也可能帮你省下跑一趟超市的工夫。

questions.en: Do you think students are overly reliant on AI?
questions.zh: 你觉得学生过于依赖人工智能了吗？
questions.sample: Some are, particularly when they ask AI for an answer before they've understood the question. You notice the problem when someone submits a polished paragraph but struggles to explain the first sentence in their own words.
questions.sampleZh: 有些学生确实如此，尤其是自己还没弄懂问题，就先去问人工智能要答案的时候。一个人交上来一段很漂亮的文字，却连第一句话都很难用自己的话解释，你就能看出问题了。

questions.en: What can teachers do to stop students from relying too much on AI?
questions.zh: 教师可以怎样避免学生过分依赖人工智能？
questions.sample: I'd give students something small to do before they open an AI tool. For example, they could write down their own argument first. Afterwards, ask them which suggestion they accepted or rejected and what made them decide.
questions.sampleZh: 我会让学生在打开人工智能工具前，先自己做一件小事。比如，先写下自己的观点。用完工具后，再问他们采纳或拒绝了哪条建议，以及为什么作出这个决定。

questions.en: Why do companies sometimes use famous people to advertise things?
questions.zh: 为什么企业有时会请名人为产品做广告？
questions.sample: A famous face makes people stop and look. If the person also has a clear connection to the product, the advert is easier to remember. A runner talking about shoes makes more sense to me than a random film star.
questions.sampleZh: 一张熟悉的名人面孔能让人停下来看一眼。如果这个人和产品本身也有明显的联系，广告就更容易被记住。对我来说，请跑步运动员讲跑鞋，比随便找个电影明星更有说服力。

questions.en: Where do people often see advertisements?
questions.zh: 人们经常在哪里看到广告？
questions.sample: They're everywhere on a normal trip to work. You might see one on your phone before you leave, another on a lift screen and several on the metro. The ones near station exits often advertise places within walking distance.
questions.sampleZh: 平时上班路上，到处都能看到广告。你可能还没出门就在手机上看到一条，进电梯又在屏幕上看到一条，到了地铁上还能再看到好几条。车站出口附近的广告，经常会介绍步行就能到的地方。

questions.en: Which do you think is better for companies to spend money on: advertising online or advertising in public places?
questions.zh: 你觉得企业把广告预算投到网上好，还是投到公共场所好？
questions.sample: It depends who the company needs to reach. A shop by a metro exit might get more customers from a sign at that exit. For a language course that anyone can join from home, I'd spend the money online.
questions.sampleZh: 要看企业想接触什么人。开在地铁口的店，把招牌放在那个出口，可能就能带来更多顾客。如果推广的是人人都能在家参加的语言课，我会把这笔钱投在线上。

questions.en: How important is advertising for increasing sales?
questions.zh: 对于提高销量，广告有多重要？
questions.sample: It can make a big difference when people have never heard of a product. An advert might persuade me to try a new drink once. Whether I keep buying it has much more to do with the taste and price.
questions.sampleZh: 如果人们从没听说过某个产品，广告就可能起很大作用。一则广告也许能说服我尝一次新的饮料。至于以后还会不会再买，口味和价格的影响就大多了。

questions.en: What might the qualities of an effective advertisement be?
questions.zh: 一则有效的广告可能具备哪些特点？
questions.sample: A good advert gives me one clear reason to remember the product. For instance, a suitcase advert could show someone lifting it onto a train with one hand. That tells me more about its weight than a long list of features.
questions.sampleZh: 好广告会给我一个明确的理由，让我记住产品。例如，行李箱广告可以拍一个人单手把箱子提上火车。这个画面比列一长串功能更能让我明白箱子有多轻。

questions.en: How truthful are advertisements about the things they advertise?
questions.zh: 广告对产品或服务的描述有多真实？
questions.sample: It varies. A shop can show the actual price of a phone quite accurately, but "all-day battery life" depends on how you use it. I'd trust a clear demonstration more than a beautiful picture and a big promise.
questions.sampleZh: 得分情况。商店可以把一部手机的实际价格标得很准确，但所谓“全天续航”得看你怎么用。比起一张漂亮的图和一个响亮的承诺，我更相信清楚直观的演示。

questions.en: What do you think about the idea that companies should not target their advertising at children?
questions.zh: 有人认为企业不应专门针对儿童投放广告。你怎么看？
questions.sample: I mostly agree. Young children don't always realise that their favourite cartoon character is trying to sell them something. I'd be particularly uncomfortable with an advert that encourages a child to keep asking their parents until they give in.
questions.sampleZh: 我基本同意。小孩子不一定意识得到，自己最喜欢的卡通人物正在向他们推销东西。如果一则广告鼓动孩子不停地求父母买，直到父母让步，我会尤其反感。

questions.en: Do you think there should be more restrictions on which products can be advertised?
questions.zh: 你觉得对于哪些产品可以做广告，应该有更多限制吗？
questions.sample: Yes, especially for products where the audience could misunderstand the risks. I wouldn't want gambling adverts appearing inside a game that children play. For ordinary things like shoes, clearly showing the price and terms would usually be enough.
questions.sampleZh: 应该，尤其是观众容易误判风险的产品。我不希望赌博广告出现在孩子们玩的游戏里。至于鞋子之类的日常用品，通常把价格和购买条件说清楚就够了。

questions.en: Do you think advertising might ultimately have a harmful or beneficial effect on society?
questions.zh: 你觉得从长远看，广告给社会带来的会是好处还是危害？
questions.sample: On balance, advertising can help when it's honest. It's one way a tiny local bakery can tell people it exists. The downside is the constant pressure to spend, especially when adverts follow you around long after you've lost interest.
questions.sampleZh: 总的来说，诚实的广告能帮上忙。比如，社区里一家很小的面包店可以通过广告让大家知道它的存在。问题是，广告也会不断催人消费，尤其是你早就没兴趣了，它还追着你反复出现。

questions.en: What are the advantages and disadvantages of advertisements?
questions.zh: 广告有哪些优缺点？
questions.sample: Adverts can save you time by showing you a shop or service nearby. They can also push you into buying something you never planned to buy. A countdown on a shopping app is a good example of that pressure.
questions.sampleZh: 广告可以告诉你附近有哪些商店或服务，帮你节省时间。它也可能促使你买下原本没打算买的东西。购物软件上的倒计时，就是这种消费压力的一个好例子。

questions.en: Why are many advertisements endorsed by celebrities? How useful are they?
questions.zh: 为什么很多广告由名人代言？效果如何？
questions.sample: Celebrities bring an audience with them, so a new brand can get attention very quickly. They're most useful when people trust their judgement about that product. An actor reading out the features of a washing machine might not convince many buyers.
questions.sampleZh: 名人自带受众，所以新品牌能很快得到关注。如果大家也信任这位名人对那款产品的判断，代言效果就最好。让一个演员照着念洗衣机的功能，恐怕说服不了多少买家。

questions.en: What is the most important factor in an advertisement?
questions.zh: 广告中最重要的因素是什么？
questions.sample: For me, it's a clear message. Even a funny advert has failed if I remember the joke but can't name the product. Showing one problem and how the product solves it gives people something useful to take away.
questions.sampleZh: 对我来说，最重要的是把信息传达清楚。广告再好笑，如果我只记住笑话，却说不出产品的名字，它也算失败。展示一个具体问题，再让大家看到产品怎样解决它，观众就能记住真正有用的东西。

questions.en: Why are some advertisements boring?
questions.zh: 为什么有些广告很无聊？
questions.sample: Some repeat the same claim so often that people stop listening. A clip might feel fresh the first time, but if it interrupts every video you watch that evening, you'll probably reach for the skip button immediately.
questions.sampleZh: 有些广告总在重复同一个卖点，次数多了，人们也就不再听了。一段广告第一次看可能很新鲜，但如果你那天晚上看的每个视频都被它打断，你大概会立刻去按跳过。

questions.en: Is advertising important for a company? Why?
questions.zh: 广告对公司重要吗？为什么？
questions.sample: Usually, yes. A company can make a brilliant product, but customers have to find it somehow. A neighbourhood repair shop may only need a sign and a few local notices, while a new national brand has a much bigger job.
questions.sampleZh: 通常是的。企业可以做出很棒的产品，但顾客总得有渠道知道它。街坊里的一家维修店也许只需要一个招牌，再贴几张本地告示。而一个刚起步、面向全国的品牌，要做的宣传工作就多得多。

questions.en: Which is more effective, online advertising or offline advertising?
questions.zh: 网络广告和线下广告哪个更有效？
questions.sample: Online adverts often work better when a business needs a quick response. Someone can see a concert announcement and book a ticket straight away. An offline poster may work better if the concert is aimed at people living near the venue.
questions.sampleZh: 企业想让顾客迅速作出反应时，线上广告通常更有效。一个人可以看到演唱会的消息，马上就订票。如果演唱会主要面向场馆附近的居民，一张贴在当地的海报也许效果更好。

questions.en: At what age do children start to have their own opinions?
questions.zh: 孩子一般几岁开始有自己的看法？
questions.sample: Quite early, I think. A little child who insists on the red cup already has a preference of their own. Giving reasons for an opinion, like why a classroom rule seems unfair, usually comes a bit later.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得挺早的。一个小孩坚持要用红色的杯子，就已经有自己的偏好了。至于能说出某个看法背后的理由，比如为什么觉得班里的一条规定不公平，通常要再晚一些。

questions.en: Who has the most influence on children's opinions - parents or teachers?
questions.zh: 父母和老师，谁对孩子形成自己的看法影响更大？
questions.sample: Parents probably have more influence at first because children hear them talk about everyday things for years. Teachers can have a bigger influence on particular subjects, though. One enthusiastic science teacher can change how a child feels about experiments.
questions.sampleZh: 一开始父母的影响大概更大，因为孩子从小就听父母谈论日常生活里的各种事情。不过在某个具体学科上，老师的影响也许更大。一位充满热情的科学老师，就能改变孩子对做实验的感受。

questions.en: Who do most young people discuss their opinions with?
questions.zh: 大多数年轻人会和谁讨论自己的观点？
questions.sample: For personal topics, many talk to close friends first. It's easier to admit you're unsure about something when nobody is judging you. If the question is about choosing a course or a job, they may turn to an older relative.
questions.sampleZh: 谈到私人的事情，很多人会先找亲近的朋友聊天。知道对方不会评判自己，就更容易承认有些事自己也拿不准。如果问题是选课或找工作，他们也许会去请教一位年长的亲戚。

questions.en: Do you think teachers should ask children's opinions in lessons?
questions.zh: 你觉得老师上课时应该询问孩子们的看法吗？
questions.sample: Definitely. Asking why two characters made different choices in a story can reveal much more than asking children to repeat the plot. Even a child with a surprising answer gets to practise explaining the thinking behind it.
questions.sampleZh: 当然应该。问孩子故事里的两个人物为什么作了不同的选择，比让他们复述情节更能看出他们在想什么。哪怕有个孩子给出了出人意料的答案，也有机会练习把自己的思路讲清楚。

questions.en: Are there situations when people should not give their real opinions?
questions.zh: 有没有一些场合，人们不应该说出自己的真实想法？
questions.sample: Yes. If a friend is about to give a speech, that's hardly the moment to announce that you dislike their outfit. You can be honest about something that helps them now and leave an unnecessary comment to yourself.
questions.sampleZh: 有。比如朋友马上要上台演讲了，这显然不是说“我不喜欢你这身衣服”的好时候。你可以坦诚地说一些眼下对朋友有帮助的话，没必要的评价则可以留在心里。

questions.en: Does culture affect the way in which people express their opinions?
questions.zh: 文化会影响人们表达观点的方式吗？
questions.sample: Yes, it can affect how directly someone speaks. In some families, a gentle question like "Could we try another way?" is a normal way to disagree. Someone used to a very direct answer might miss the disagreement entirely.
questions.sampleZh: 会，文化会影响一个人表达得有多直接。在有些家庭，一句温和的“我们能不能换个办法？”就是表达不同意的常见方式。习惯听直截了当的回答的人，甚至可能完全听不出来对方有异议。

questions.en: How much does social media influence people's opinions today?
questions.zh: 当今社交媒体对人们的看法影响有多大？
questions.sample: Quite a lot, especially when the same opinion comes up in several videos in a row. It can start to feel as if everyone agrees. A conversation with people outside that online circle can give a very different impression.
questions.sampleZh: 影响挺大的，特别是连续刷到好几个视频都在表达同一个看法时。慢慢地，你可能觉得所有人都同意。可要是和那个网络圈子以外的人聊一聊，得到的印象也许会完全不同。

questions.en: Some people think society needs more people who aren't afraid to express unpopular opinions. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人认为，社会需要更多敢于表达不受欢迎观点的人。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Yes, as long as they're willing to explain their reasons and listen in return. If everyone stays quiet when a plan looks risky, a whole team can make a costly mistake. One uncomfortable question can save a lot of trouble.
questions.sampleZh: 我同意，前提是这些人愿意解释自己的理由，也愿意听别人的意见。如果一项计划看起来有风险，大家却都不出声，整个团队可能就会犯下代价高昂的错误。一个问出来有点尴尬的问题，有时能省掉很多麻烦。

questions.en: What do you think about the idea that it is increasingly difficult to distinguish fact from opinion?
questions.zh: 有人认为，现在越来越难区分事实和观点。你怎么看？
questions.sample: I think it is getting harder in short videos, where a number and a personal reaction often appear together. "The ticket costs fifty yuan" is a fact you can check. Whether that makes it a bargain is a judgement.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得在短视频里确实越来越难分。一个数字往往和某个人的感受一起出现。“票价五十元”是可以核实的事实，但这张票算不算划算，就是个人判断了。

questions.en: Do children communicate more with teachers or with parents?
questions.zh: 孩子跟老师交流得多，还是跟父母交流得多？
questions.sample: I imagine most children talk more with their parents overall. At home they can talk over breakfast or on the way to school. A teacher might see them for several hours, but has to share that time among a whole class.
questions.sampleZh: 总体来说，我猜大多数孩子和父母聊得更多。他们可以在家吃早饭时聊，也可以在上学路上聊。老师虽然每天可能见他们好几个小时，却得把这些时间分给全班孩子。

questions.en: What types of businesses are successful in your country?
questions.zh: 在你们国家，哪些类型的企业经营得比较成功？
questions.sample: In China, businesses that make everyday errands easier can do well. A small shop offering breakfast near a busy metro station is a good example. Customers walk past every morning and care about getting something fresh without a long wait.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国，能让日常小事变得更方便的生意往往做得不错。比如在繁忙的地铁站旁边开一家早餐店。顾客每天早晨都从那里路过，他们想买点新鲜的东西，又不想排很久的队。

questions.en: How easy is it to start a successful business?
questions.zh: 创办一家能取得成功的企业有多容易？
questions.sample: Setting one up can be fairly easy. Making it last is the hard part. For example, a café might be full during its opening week because people are curious. It still needs enough regular customers once that excitement passes.
questions.sampleZh: 把一家企业开起来可能挺容易，难的是一直经营下去。比如一家咖啡馆开业第一周，可能因为大家都好奇而坐得满满当当。等新鲜劲儿过去，它还是得有足够多的回头客。

questions.en: Do you think making money is the most important thing for a business?
questions.zh: 你觉得对企业来说，赚钱是最重要的事吗？
questions.sample: It has to earn enough to keep operating, but money shouldn't guide every decision. A repair company that charges customers for work they don't need might earn more today and lose all its recommendations a few months later.
questions.sampleZh: 企业得赚够维持经营的钱，但不该让钱决定每个选择。一家维修公司如果把顾客根本不需要的服务也算进账单，眼下或许能多赚一点，几个月后可能就再也没人愿意向别人推荐它了。

questions.en: Why are some people more successful than other people?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人比其他人更成功？
questions.sample: Part of it is preparation, and part is opportunity. Two people can work equally hard, yet only one might meet a manager who gives beginners a chance. What they do after they get that chance matters as well.
questions.sampleZh: 一部分是准备，一部分是机会。两个人可能同样努力，却只有一个人碰上了愿意给新手机会的主管。得到了机会以后怎样把握，也同样重要。

questions.en: Do you think being successful at work is necessary for a successful life?
questions.zh: 你觉得事业成功是人生成功的必要条件吗？
questions.sample: No. Someone can have an ordinary job and still build the life they want. A parent who has time to care for a child and play music with friends might feel more successful than someone with a much bigger title.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得不是。一个人即使工作普通，也可以过上自己想要的生活。一位家长有时间照顾孩子，又能和朋友一起玩音乐，可能比一个头衔显赫得多的人更有成就感。

questions.en: What do you think about the idea that having a positive attitude always brings financial success?
questions.zh: 有人认为，只要保持积极心态，就一定能在经济上取得成功。你怎么看？
questions.sample: Being positive can help you try again after a setback, but it doesn't guarantee money. You can be optimistic about a shop and still open it in the wrong location. Checking costs and listening to customers matter too.
questions.sampleZh: 遇到挫折时，乐观能帮人再试一次，但它不能保证赚到钱。你可能对一家店充满信心，却还是把它开在了错误的地方。核算成本、听听顾客怎么说，同样重要。

questions.en: Why is fame seen as a desirable form of success by many people?
questions.zh: 为什么很多人把成名看作一种值得追求的成功？
questions.sample: Fame is easy for other people to see. Someone with a big following gets invited to events, and that attention can look like success from the outside. Quieter achievements, such as becoming an excellent teacher, don't always get the same coverage.
questions.sampleZh: 名气很容易被别人看见。粉丝很多的人会受邀参加各种活动，从外面看，那些关注很像是成功。像成为一名出色的老师这类不那么引人注目的成就，就不一定能得到同样多的报道。

questions.en: Why are some successful people unhappy with their lives?
questions.zh: 为什么有些成功人士对自己的生活并不满意？
questions.sample: Sometimes the thing they were chasing turns out to be different from the life they actually enjoy. A promotion might give someone a better salary but also mean travelling every week and missing evenings with their family.
questions.sampleZh: 有时，他们一直追求的东西，最后却和自己真正喜欢的生活不一样。升职也许意味着更高的工资，却也可能意味着每周都要出差，没法在晚上陪伴家人。

questions.en: Some people say it is impossible to feel successful without contributing to the good of society. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，如果没有为社会作出贡献，人就不可能觉得自己成功。你同意吗？
questions.sample: I wouldn't go that far. Learning to swim after years of being afraid of water can feel like a real personal success. Helping other people gives some achievements extra meaning, but it isn't the only reason to feel proud.
questions.sampleZh: 我不会说得那么绝对。一个人怕水很多年后终于学会游泳，就完全可以把它看成一次真正的个人成功。帮助别人确实会让一些成就更有意义，但让人自豪的理由还有很多。

questions.en: Other than making money, what is more important for a company?
questions.zh: 除了赚钱，对一家公司来说什么更重要？
questions.sample: Keeping customers' trust is more important than squeezing a little extra profit from one sale. If a shop admits a mistake and deals with it quickly, that customer may come back for years and tell friends about the experience.
questions.sampleZh: 比起从一笔生意里再挤出一点利润，保住顾客的信任更重要。如果一家店肯承认错误并迅速处理，顾客也许今后好几年都会回来，还会把这次经历讲给朋友听。

questions.en: Does money equal success?
questions.zh: 金钱等同于成功吗？
questions.sample: No. Money can show that an idea sold well, but it can't tell you everything about a person's life. A teacher might earn a modest salary and still feel successful when a struggling student finally starts to enjoy learning.
questions.sampleZh: 不等同。赚到钱可能说明一个点子卖得好，却不能说明一个人的生活到底怎样。一位老师收入也许不高，但看到一个原本学得很吃力的学生终于开始喜欢学习，依然会感到很成功。

questions.en: How can companies help protect the environment?
questions.zh: 公司可以如何帮助保护环境？
questions.sample: They can begin with the things they buy and throw away every day. A takeaway restaurant could make cutlery optional and use packaging that actually fits each order. Small changes can add up when hundreds of meals leave the shop daily.
questions.sampleZh: 企业可以从每天买进和丢弃的东西做起。比如，外卖店可以让顾客自己选择是否需要餐具，并按每笔订单的分量选合适的包装。店里每天要送出几百份餐，这些小变化累积起来就很可观。

questions.en: Is it difficult to do business in today's world?
questions.zh: 在当今世界做生意困难吗？
questions.sample: Yes, in some ways. Online tools make it easier to reach customers, but they also make it easy for customers to compare ten competitors in a minute. A business needs a clear reason for people to choose it again.
questions.sampleZh: 在某些方面，是的。线上工具让企业更容易接触顾客，也让顾客能在一分钟内比较十家竞争对手。企业得给人一个明确的理由，让他们下次还愿意选自己。

questions.en: Do you think it's important to teach children to work in groups?
questions.zh: 你觉得教孩子学会小组合作重要吗？
questions.sample: Yes, because working together takes practice. When children build a model in pairs, they have to share the materials and agree on an idea. Those little disagreements teach them something that simply sitting at the same table never would.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得重要，因为合作需要练习。两个孩子一起做模型，就得分享材料，还得就做什么达成一致。这些小小的意见分歧能教会他们一些事情，光坐在同一张桌子旁可学不到。

questions.en: What are some of the personal qualities of a good group leader?
questions.zh: 优秀的团队领导者通常具备哪些个人品质？
questions.sample: A good leader listens carefully and gives people clear responsibilities. They should also be willing to admit mistakes. If the leader can say, "That was my decision and it didn't work," the team is more likely to speak honestly.
questions.sampleZh: 好的领导者会认真倾听，也会让每个人清楚自己的职责。他们还应该愿意承认错误。如果领导能说“这是我做的决定，它没奏效”，团队成员就更有可能说出真心话。

questions.en: What can be difficult about leading a group?
questions.zh: 带领一个团队可能会遇到哪些困难？
questions.sample: Balancing different voices can be difficult. One person may speak confidently about every idea while someone quieter has spotted a serious problem. The leader has to keep things moving and still give that quieter person a chance to speak.
questions.sampleZh: 兼顾不同人的声音可能很难。有人对每个想法都能很自信地发表意见，另一个不太爱说话的人却可能已经发现了一个严重的问题。领导既要推动事情往前走，又得给那个安静的人开口的机会。

questions.en: What activities do young children do in groups at school in your country?
questions.zh: 在你的国家，年幼的孩子会在学校分组做哪些活动？
questions.sample: In Chinese primary schools, children often do classroom cleaning in small groups. Some sweep while others wipe the board or arrange the desks. They might also rehearse a short performance together for a school celebration.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国的小学，孩子们经常分小组打扫教室。有的人扫地，其他人擦黑板或摆好桌椅。他们也可能一起排练一个小节目，在学校的庆祝活动上表演。

questions.en: Why do some children prefer not to work in groups?
questions.zh: 为什么有些孩子不喜欢分组合作？
questions.sample: Group work can feel unfair if one child always takes over the fun parts. A quiet child might also need time to think before speaking. Giving everyone a clear job helps more than simply telling the class to work together.
questions.sampleZh: 如果好玩的部分总是被同一个孩子抢走，其他孩子就容易觉得小组合作不公平。安静的孩子开口之前也许还需要一点思考时间。给每个人分配清楚的任务，比只是告诉全班“大家要合作”有用得多。

questions.en: Do you agree that the success of a group depends entirely on the ability of its leader?
questions.zh: 有人认为，一个团队能否成功完全取决于领导者的能力。你同意吗？
questions.sample: No. A leader can set the direction, but the members still have to do the work and tell each other when something goes wrong. Even a clear plan falls apart if nobody shares the information the others need.
questions.sampleZh: 我不同意。领导者可以指明方向，但事情仍需成员们完成，出了问题也要互相通报。即便计划十分清楚，只要没人把其他人需要的信息说出来，它照样会落空。

questions.en: What are the advantages of countries working together on joint projects?
questions.zh: 各国合作开展项目有哪些好处？
questions.sample: Countries can bring different skills and equipment to the same problem. For example, rivers cross borders, so measuring water quality on just one side gives an incomplete picture. Sharing the results makes it easier to understand where a problem began.
questions.sampleZh: 不同国家可以带着各自的技能和设备，一起来解决同一个问题。比如，河流会跨越国界，只在一侧监测水质，了解的情况就不完整。各国共享结果之后，就更容易弄清楚问题是从哪里开始的。

questions.en: Do you think, in the future, there will still be a need for translators and interpreters for international projects?
questions.zh: 你觉得未来国际合作项目还需要笔译和口译人员吗？
questions.sample: Yes, especially when the exact meaning matters. A tool can translate the basic words in a message, but a polite hesitation might actually signal disagreement. An experienced interpreter can notice that and ask the speaker to clarify.
questions.sampleZh: 需要，尤其是在意思必须传达得非常准确的时候。工具能把一条消息里的基本词句翻出来，但一个礼貌的迟疑其实可能表示反对。有经验的口译员能留意到这一点，并请说话人再解释清楚。

questions.en: Do you think the use of modern technology will ever be able to guarantee the success of international projects?
questions.zh: 你觉得现代科技有朝一日能保证国际合作项目成功吗？
questions.sample: No. Video meetings and shared files make cooperation easier, but they can't make two countries agree on what counts as success. People still have to settle questions about money, deadlines and who is responsible when something changes.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得不能。视频会议和共享文件能让合作更方便，却不能让两个国家自动就“怎样才算成功”达成一致。资金怎么安排、期限是哪天，以及情况变化后由谁负责，这些问题仍然要靠人来谈妥。

questions.en: Why do some people prefer to work by themselves?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人更愿意独自工作？
questions.sample: They can choose their own pace and spend time concentrating without interruptions. Writing a first draft, for example, may be easier alone. They can still get feedback later by asking a friend to read what they've written.
questions.sampleZh: 独自工作时，人们可以自己掌握节奏，专心做事而不被打扰。比如，写初稿可能一个人更容易些。等写完以后，他们仍然可以请朋友读一读，听听意见。

questions.en: What should a leader do to make team members want to follow him or her?
questions.zh: 领导者怎样才能让团队成员愿意追随自己？
questions.sample: I'd say they should show people why their work matters and share the difficult parts. If a deadline gets tight, a leader who stays to solve the problem with the team earns more trust than one who only sends reminders.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得领导应该让大家明白手上的工作为什么重要，也要一起承担困难的部分。临近截止日期时，留下来和团队一起解决问题的领导，比只会发消息催进度的领导更能赢得信任。

questions.en: What group tasks are there in schools?
questions.zh: 学校里有哪些需要小组完成的任务？
questions.sample: Schools often ask groups to make posters, carry out simple experiments or prepare short plays. A play works particularly well because there are different jobs. A child who dislikes acting can organise the props or help write the lines.
questions.sampleZh: 学校经常让学生分组做海报、完成简单的实验，或者排练短剧。短剧尤其适合合作，因为有许多不同的任务。不喜欢表演的孩子可以负责道具，或者帮忙写台词。

questions.en: What advantages are there for students experiencing teamwork at school?
questions.zh: 学生在校期间参与团队合作有哪些好处？
questions.sample: Students find out what they're good at while learning to depend on other people. Someone might discover they're better at explaining a difficult idea than designing slides. That's hard to learn from an assignment you complete entirely on your own.
questions.sampleZh: 学生在学会依靠别人的同时，也能发现自己的长处。有的人可能会意识到，比起设计幻灯片，自己更擅长把一个难懂的概念讲清楚。如果一项作业从头到尾都靠自己完成，就很难有这样的发现。

questions.en: Why is it good for young people to have ambitions?
questions.zh: 为什么有抱负对年轻人有好处？
questions.sample: Ambition gives young people a reason to make choices now. A student who wants to design games might start learning some basic coding on weekends. Even if that goal changes, the skills they pick up along the way stay useful.
questions.sampleZh: 志向能让年轻人有理由现在就作出选择。比如，一个想设计游戏的学生，可能会从周末学一些基础编程开始。以后目标即使变了，这一路学到的本领依然有用。

questions.en: What kinds of ambitions do young people often have in your country?
questions.zh: 在你们国家，年轻人通常有哪些志向？
questions.sample: Young people in China have quite different goals. Some hope to get into a particular university or find a stable job close to home. Others want to start a small business or turn an interest like photography into paid work.
questions.sampleZh: 中国年轻人的目标各不相同。有些人想考进某所大学，或者在离家近的地方找到一份稳定的工作。还有人想做点小生意，或者把摄影之类的爱好变成能带来收入的工作。

questions.en: Do you agree that it is good to have ambitious people in a work team?
questions.zh: 有人认为，工作团队中有雄心勃勃的人是好事。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Usually, yes. An ambitious teammate might volunteer for a difficult task that everyone else avoids. It works best when they're interested in the team's result. If they only care about getting credit, other people may stop sharing ideas.
questions.sampleZh: 通常是好事。有抱负的队友，可能愿意主动接下其他人都在躲的难题。如果他们在意的是团队的成果，效果就最好。要是他们只想把功劳揽在自己身上，其他人可能就不愿再分享想法了。

questions.en: Do you think parents should help their children decide what ambitions to follow?
questions.zh: 你觉得父母应该帮孩子决定追求什么目标吗？
questions.sample: Parents can help children explore options, especially ones they've never heard of. Taking a child who loves drawing to meet a designer could be valuable. After that, I'd let the child decide whether the work actually appeals to them.
questions.sampleZh: 家长可以帮助孩子了解各种可能性，尤其是孩子以前连听都没听过的选择。比如，带一个爱画画的孩子去见见设计师，可能很有价值。见过以后，我会让孩子自己决定，这份工作究竟吸不吸引他。

questions.en: Why are some people ambitious to take on higher positions at work?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人希望在工作中担任更高的职位？
questions.sample: A higher position often gives people a say in decisions that affect their everyday work. A nurse, for example, might want to lead a team because they have ideas about improving shifts. Of course, better pay can be attractive too.
questions.sampleZh: 职位越高，人们通常越能参与那些会影响自己日常工作的决定。比如，一名护士想带团队，可能是因为对怎样改进排班有自己的想法。当然，更高的收入也有吸引力。

questions.en: Do you think ambitious people are always successful at work?
questions.zh: 你觉得有抱负的人在工作中总能成功吗？
questions.sample: No. Ambition might get someone to apply for a promotion, but it doesn't make them good at listening or solving problems. Someone who wants to manage a team still has to earn the trust of the people on it.
questions.sampleZh: 不是。有抱负也许会促使一个人申请晋升，却不会自动让他擅长倾听或解决问题。想管理一支团队的人，仍然得靠实际表现赢得成员的信任。

questions.en: Why does the world need ambitious people?
questions.zh: 为什么世界上需要有抱负的人？
questions.sample: Some problems take years to solve, and someone has to be willing to begin. A person who wants every village in their area to have a library might start with one shelf of donated books and keep building from there.
questions.sampleZh: 有些问题要花很多年才能解决，总得有人愿意迈出第一步。比如，有人希望让自己所在地区的每个村子都有图书馆，他可以先用捐来的书摆起一个书架，再从那里一点点做大。

questions.en: Do you think people who are not ambitious are at a disadvantage in life?
questions.zh: 你觉得没有远大抱负的人在生活中会处于劣势吗？
questions.sample: They can be at a disadvantage when opportunities go to whoever speaks up first. But a person who enjoys a settled routine may be perfectly happy without a promotion. It depends on what kind of life they're trying to lead.
questions.sampleZh: 如果机会往往给最先主动争取的人，没有抱负的人可能会吃亏。不过，一个人如果喜欢稳定的日子，即使不升职也可能过得很开心。得看他想过怎样的生活。

questions.en: Do you think society values some kinds of ambition more than others?
questions.zh: 你觉得社会对某些志向比对其他志向更看重吗？
questions.sample: Yes. People tend to notice ambitions with an obvious title or prize, like becoming a company director. Wanting to be a patient parent or a really dependable neighbour takes effort too, but it rarely gets announced at a celebration.
questions.sampleZh: 会。人们更容易注意到那些带有明确头衔或奖项的志向，比如成为公司董事。想做一个有耐心的家长，或者一个真正靠得住的邻居，也需要付出努力，但这类志向很少会在庆祝会上被郑重宣布。

questions.en: Why should children have ambitions?
questions.zh: 孩子为什么应该有志向？
questions.sample: Having something to aim for makes practice feel worthwhile. A child who wants to play one favourite song on the piano has a reason to keep trying the tricky part. At that age, a small, changeable goal is plenty.
questions.sampleZh: 有了想实现的目标，练习就会变得值得。一个孩子想用钢琴弹出自己最喜欢的那首歌，就有理由继续练习那段难弹的地方。在那个年纪，有一个小小的、以后还可以改变的目标就够了。

questions.en: What do you think of people going after high positions?
questions.zh: 你怎么看待那些追求更高职位的人？
questions.sample: I respect it when someone wants the responsibility as well as the title. A good question is whether they'd still want the role if it meant more difficult conversations and less praise. A higher position usually brings both.
questions.sampleZh: 如果一个人不只想要头衔，也愿意担起责任，我会很尊重他。可以问问他，如果这个职位意味着要面对更多难谈的事，得到的赞赏还更少，他是否还想做。更高的职位往往两样都会带来。

questions.en: Why are some young people keen on being fans of superstars?
questions.zh: 为什么有些年轻人热衷于追星？
questions.sample: Following a star gives some young people a sense of belonging. Two classmates who hardly know each other can start chatting about the same singer's new song. The performances and success story can be part of the attraction too.
questions.sampleZh: 对有些年轻人来说，追星能带来归属感。两个原本不熟的同学，可能因为同一位歌手的新歌就聊起来了。明星的表演和走向成功的经历，也可能是吸引他们的原因。

questions.en: Is it good for a person to be ambitious?
questions.zh: 一个人有抱负是好事吗？
questions.sample: Generally, yes. A goal can push someone to attempt things they would normally put off, like applying for a course. The problem starts when each achievement immediately feels too small and they stop enjoying anything they've done.
questions.sampleZh: 总体上是好事。目标能推动一个人去尝试那些他平时总会拖延的事，比如申请一门课程。问题在于，如果每次取得一点成绩就立刻觉得它太小，慢慢地，他就无法享受自己做成的任何事了。

questions.en: Do you think it is necessary to be ambitious when working in a team in a company?
questions.zh: 在公司里和团队一起工作时，有抱负是必要的吗？
questions.sample: It's helpful to care about the team's goal, but every employee doesn't need to want a promotion. A team also needs someone who's happy to check the figures carefully while a more ambitious colleague presents the work to a client.
questions.sampleZh: 关心团队目标当然有帮助，但没必要每个员工都想升职。一个团队也需要这样的人：当更有抱负的同事去给客户做汇报时，他愿意安下心来把数字仔细核对一遍。

questions.en: Should parents support their children in pursuing their ambitions?
questions.zh: 父母应该支持孩子追求自己的志向吗？
questions.sample: Yes, though support can mean asking good questions as well as giving encouragement. If a teenager wants to become a photographer, the family could help them try a weekend project before spending a lot on equipment or training.
questions.sampleZh: 应该，不过支持除了鼓励，还可以是问些好问题。比如一个青少年想当摄影师，家人可以先帮他在周末尝试一个小项目，再考虑要不要花大价钱买设备或上培训班。

questions.en: How easy or difficult is it to work as a doctor?
questions.zh: 你觉得当医生容易还是难？
questions.sample: It's demanding, even after the long training. Doctors may have to switch from a routine appointment to a worried family asking difficult questions. They need to stay focused on details while explaining things in language people can actually understand.
questions.sampleZh: 这份工作很有挑战性，即使已经完成了漫长的培训也是如此。医生可能刚结束一次常规问诊，就要面对焦虑的家属和他们提出的棘手问题。他们得一边留心各种细节，一边用大家真正听得懂的话把情况解释清楚。

questions.en: Do you think it's interesting for schoolchildren to learn biology?
questions.zh: 你觉得学生在学校学习生物有趣吗？
questions.sample: It can be fascinating when children can see the lesson happening in front of them. Watching seeds grow under different conditions gives them something to compare every morning. Memorising a long list of plant parts is unlikely to feel as exciting.
questions.sampleZh: 如果孩子能亲眼看到课上学的事情正在发生，生物可以非常有趣。观察种子在不同条件下生长，他们每天早上都有新的变化可以比较。相比之下，背一长串植物各部位的名称，大概没那么令人兴奋。

questions.en: Why do many children want to become a doctor?
questions.zh: 为什么许多孩子想成为医生？
questions.sample: Doctors are among the first professionals children see helping someone who feels unwell. A child may remember a doctor calming them down before an examination. That simple memory can make the job feel both important and personally meaningful.
questions.sampleZh: 在孩子最先接触的专业人士中，医生就是会帮助生病的人的一类。一个孩子可能一直记得，有位医生在检查前让自己平静下来。这样一段简单的记忆，就能让孩子觉得这份工作既重要，又和自己有真切的联系。

questions.en: What do you think about the idea that large sums of public money should be used to finance medical research?
questions.zh: 有人认为应该投入大量公共资金来支持医学研究。你怎么看？
questions.sample: I think a substantial amount is worthwhile, especially for questions that private companies have little reason to study. I'd also expect researchers to explain what they're trying to find out, how the money is spent and what the public learns.
questions.sampleZh: 我认为投入相当一笔资金是值得的，尤其是用来研究那些私营企业没什么动力研究的问题。我也希望研究人员能说明白，他们想弄清什么，钱是怎么花的，公众又从中了解到了什么。

questions.en: Do you agree that doctors are paid too much for the work they do?
questions.zh: 有人认为，相对于医生所做的工作，他们的报酬过高了。你同意吗？
questions.sample: I wouldn't make that judgement about doctors as a group. Long training, night shifts and responsibility for difficult decisions deserve fair pay. Two doctors with the same job title may also work very different hours in very different conditions.
questions.sampleZh: 我不会把所有医生放在一起下这样的判断。漫长的培训、值夜班，以及作出艰难决定的责任，都应该得到合理的报酬。两位职称相同的医生，工作时长和工作条件也可能天差地别。

questions.en: Do you think biology is easier for students than other science subjects, such as physics or chemistry?
questions.zh: 你觉得对学生来说，生物比物理、化学等其他理科科目更容易吗？
questions.sample: It depends on the student. Someone who enjoys observing plants or comparing diagrams might find biology more approachable. A student who likes turning a problem into an equation may feel more comfortable with physics, even if both subjects take practice.
questions.sampleZh: 这得看学生本人。喜欢观察植物或对比图示的人，可能觉得生物更容易入门。喜欢把问题转化成方程的学生，也许学物理更得心应手，尽管这两门课都需要练习。

questions.en: Why can a good understanding of human biology be useful throughout a person's life?
questions.zh: 为什么深入了解人体生物学可以让人终身受益？
questions.sample: It helps people make sense of changes they experience at different ages. Understanding what a doctor means by a joint or a muscle, for instance, makes it easier to ask sensible questions instead of just nodding through an appointment.
questions.sampleZh: 它能帮助人们理解自己在不同年龄经历的身体变化。比如，你明白医生说的关节或肌肉是什么，就更容易提出有意义的问题，而不会整场看诊都只顾着点头。

questions.en: Do you agree that the increasing use of technology in health care may not always be positive?
questions.zh: 有人认为，医疗中越来越多地使用科技，并非总是好事。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Yes. A digital system can make an appointment quicker for some people and harder for someone who doesn't use a smartphone. I'd keep a staffed desk available so that introducing a new tool doesn't quietly shut patients out.
questions.sampleZh: 我同意。数字系统可能让一些人更快挂上号，却让不会用智能手机的人更难就诊。我会保留有人值班的服务台，免得引进一项新工具，却在不知不觉间把一部分患者挡在门外。

questions.en: Do you think medical discoveries should always be shared worldwide for free?
questions.zh: 你觉得所有医学发现都应该在全球免费共享吗？
questions.sample: I'd like important findings to be easy to read worldwide. A research team shouldn't have to repeat years of work because it can't access a paper. Producing a safe treatment from that discovery can still involve costs that someone must cover.
questions.sampleZh: 我希望世界各地的人都能方便地查阅重要研究成果。一个研究团队不应该因为看不到一篇论文，就不得不重复别人做了几年的工作。不过，从一个新发现到制成安全的治疗产品，仍会产生成本，总得有人承担。

questions.en: Why is some doctors' pay high and others' low?
questions.zh: 为什么有些医生收入很高，而有些医生收入较低？
questions.sample: Pay can vary with experience, location, hours and the kind of work involved. A doctor covering emergency calls at night has a different schedule from someone seeing booked appointments during the day. Different hospitals may also have very different budgets.
questions.sampleZh: 收入会随着经验、工作地点、工时和工作内容而有所不同。负责夜间急诊的医生，与白天接待预约病人的医生，作息就不一样。不同医院的预算也可能相差很大。

questions.en: Do you think doctors should be paid more?
questions.zh: 你觉得应该提高医生的收入吗？
questions.sample: Some should, particularly where long shifts and heavy responsibilities aren't properly recognised. I'd look at actual working conditions before raising everyone's salary by the same amount. Extra pay for difficult hours might make a bigger difference in some hospitals.
questions.sampleZh: 有些医生应该加薪，特别是那些长时间值班、承担重任却没有得到相应回报的人。在决定给所有人涨一样多的工资前，我会先看看实际工作条件。在一些医院，给辛苦时段增加补贴可能更管用。

questions.en: Do you think it is better for people to make decisions quickly or slowly?
questions.zh: 你觉得做决定快一点好，还是慢慢想清楚再决定好？
questions.sample: I'd decide quickly when a choice is easy to undo, like picking a place for lunch. For something expensive or hard to change, like moving to another city, taking a few days to compare the options seems sensible.
questions.sampleZh: 如果做了选择也很容易改变，比如选个地方吃午饭，我会很快决定。碰到花费高或很难改变的事，比如搬到另一座城市，花几天比较各种选择会比较明智。

questions.en: What small decisions do people need to make in their everyday lives?
questions.zh: 人们在日常生活中需要做哪些小决定？
questions.sample: People decide when to leave home, what to eat and which task to start first. Each choice seems tiny, but they can affect the whole day. Missing one bus might change when you can have breakfast or arrive at work.
questions.sampleZh: 人们会决定几点出门、吃什么、先做哪项任务。每个决定看起来都很小，却可能影响一整天。比如错过一班公交车，就可能改变你能在什么时候吃早饭、几点到单位。

questions.en: What important decisions do people make at different stages of their lives?
questions.zh: 人们在人生的不同阶段会作出哪些重要决定？
questions.sample: When people leave school, they may choose a subject or their first job. Later, a decision might concern where to raise a family or how to care for an older relative. The people affected by the choice often change over time.
questions.sampleZh: 人们离开学校时，可能要选择接下来学什么专业，或做哪一份工作。再往后，要决定的也许是在哪里养育孩子，或者怎样照顾年长的亲人。随着时间推移，受一个决定影响的往往也不再是同一群人。

questions.en: Why do people sometimes ask for advice when making important decisions?
questions.zh: 人们在做重要决定时，为什么有时会向别人征求建议？
questions.sample: Someone with experience may notice a cost or difficulty that isn't obvious at first. Before accepting a job far from home, for example, talking to a person who makes that journey daily could reveal what the commute is really like.
questions.sampleZh: 有经验的人可能会注意到一些一开始不容易看到的成本或困难。比如，在接受一份离家很远的工作之前，和每天都走这条路的人聊聊，能让你知道真实的通勤体验是什么样。

questions.en: Do you think it is possible for a large group of people to reach a good decision?
questions.zh: 你觉得一大群人有可能共同作出一个好决定吗？
questions.sample: Yes, if everyone understands what has to be decided. It helps to collect ideas in smaller groups first and compare them afterwards. Otherwise, a room full of people can end up following the loudest voice simply to finish on time.
questions.sampleZh: 可以，前提是每个人都明白究竟要决定什么。先分成几个小组收集想法，再把这些想法放在一起比较，会更有帮助。否则，一屋子人可能只是为了按时结束讨论，最后就听了嗓门最大的那个人。

questions.en: Do you agree that the best decisions are based on logic, and not emotion?
questions.zh: 有人认为，最好的决定要靠理性而非情感。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Both can matter. Logic helps you compare the rent and travel time for two flats. But if you feel uncomfortable in one neighbourhood every evening, that feeling belongs in the decision too, even if it's harder to measure.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得两者都有分量。理性分析能帮你比较两套公寓的租金和通勤时间。不过，如果你每晚待在其中一个街区都觉得不舒服，这种感觉也该纳入决定，即使它更难衡量。

questions.en: What kinds of important decisions might leaders have to make?
questions.zh: 领导者可能需要作出哪些重要决定？
questions.sample: Leaders may have to decide which work continues when time or money is limited. A school head, for instance, might have to choose between repairing a playground now and replacing classroom computers. Each choice affects a different group of people.
questions.sampleZh: 时间或资金有限时，领导者可能得决定哪些工作能继续开展。比如，校长也许得在马上修操场和更换教室电脑之间作出选择。每个选择都会影响到不同的人。

questions.en: To what extent do you think leaders should be influenced by public opinion when they are making important decisions?
questions.zh: 你觉得领导者做重要决定时，应该在多大程度上受到公众意见的影响？
questions.sample: Leaders should listen closely to the people who will live with the result. A public meeting can reveal problems a plan has missed. Still, the most popular idea today might prove expensive or unfair, so reasons and evidence matter too.
questions.sampleZh: 领导者应该认真听听那些日后要承受决定后果的人的意见。一次公开会议也许能发现方案原本忽略的问题。不过，当下最受欢迎的想法也可能成本过高，或对某些人不公平，因此理由和证据同样重要。

questions.en: Do you agree that business leaders should always consider the wider impact of their decisions on society?
questions.zh: 有人认为，企业领导者作决定时始终应该考虑这些决定对整个社会的影响。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Yes, although the amount of checking can match the size of the decision. Closing a factory affects workers, families and nearby shops. A leader should understand those effects before announcing a closure, even when the business has few alternatives.
questions.sampleZh: 应该，不过事先要了解得多细，可以根据决定的分量来定。关闭一家工厂会影响工人、他们的家人，还有周边的商店。即使企业已经没多少其他选择，领导者也应该先弄清这些影响，再宣布关闭。

questions.en: Do you think most people's decisions are made in their 20s?
questions.zh: 你觉得人们一生中的大部分决定都是在二十多岁时做出的吗？
questions.sample: Many big decisions happen in people's twenties, but I doubt that's when most decisions are made. Changing careers at forty or deciding how to live after retirement can matter just as much as choosing a first job.
questions.sampleZh: 人们确实会在二十多岁时做很多重大决定，但我不太相信一生中大多数决定都在这个时期做出。四十岁时转行，或者退休后决定怎么生活，都可能和选择第一份工作一样重要。

questions.en: What if people in a group have different opinions on a decision?
questions.zh: 如果团队成员对一个决定意见不一，该怎么办？
questions.sample: I'd ask everyone to explain the reason behind their choice first. Two people who disagree about the best venue might actually agree that cost matters most. Once the group sees that, comparing real prices is more useful than arguing.
questions.sampleZh: 我会请每个人先讲讲自己为什么作出这个选择。两个人可能对选哪个场地意见不一，实际却都认为费用最重要。团队一旦发现这一点，去比较真实报价就比继续争论有用多了。

questions.en: Do you think it is a good idea to make a small decision every day?
questions.zh: 你觉得每天做一个小决定是个好主意吗？
questions.sample: Yes. Picking one small thing for yourself each day builds confidence without much risk. A child could choose what to pack for an afternoon trip, then notice afterwards which items were useful and what they'd take next time.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得是。每天自己决定一件小事，风险不大，又能培养信心。比如，让孩子自己决定下午出游要带什么，回来后再看看哪些东西派上了用场，下次又会带些什么。

questions.en: How can we tell the difference between an important and an easy decision?
questions.zh: 我们怎样区分重要的决定和容易做的决定？
questions.sample: I'd separate importance from difficulty. A decision is important if it has lasting effects, costs a lot or affects other people. It can still be easy to make, especially if one option fits your needs much better than the rest.
questions.sampleZh: 我会把重要程度和难易程度分开看。如果一个决定影响长远、花费很大，或者会影响到别人，它就是重要的。不过重要的决定照样可以很容易做，尤其是有一个选项明显比其他选项更符合你的需要时。

questions.en: Do younger people and older people enjoy different sorts of books?
questions.zh: 年轻人和老年人喜欢的书籍类型不同吗？
questions.sample: Sometimes, although age isn't a perfect guide. Younger readers may enjoy stories about starting university because the situations feel close to home. An older reader can enjoy exactly the same book for the memories it brings back.
questions.sampleZh: 有时会不同，不过不能只凭年龄判断。年轻读者也许喜欢讲刚上大学的故事，因为那些情境离自己的生活很近。年长的读者可能同样喜欢这本书，只是因为它唤起了过去的回忆。

questions.en: Why do you think some books remain popular for so many years?
questions.zh: 为什么有些书能长久地受到欢迎？
questions.sample: They often explore feelings people recognise across generations, like losing a friend or wanting to belong. The details may feel old, but the characters' choices still matter. Parents or teachers also keep introducing those books to new readers.
questions.sampleZh: 这些书通常写到了不同年代的人都能理解的感受，比如失去朋友，或者渴望找到归属感。书里的一些生活细节也许显得过时了，但人物面临的选择仍能打动人。家长和老师也一直在把这些书介绍给新的读者。

questions.en: Some people say that films are usually not as good as the books they are based on. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，根据书籍改编的电影通常不如原著。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Sometimes a film loses the thoughts that made a character interesting on the page. But a good actor can communicate a lot with one look, and music can change how a scene feels. I'd judge the two versions separately.
questions.sampleZh: 有时候，电影会省掉原著里让人物变得有趣的内心活动。但好演员可以用一个眼神传达很多东西，配乐也能改变一个场景给人的感觉。我愿意把书和电影当作两个作品，分别来看。

questions.en: What types of things do people most enjoy reading in your country?
questions.zh: 在你的国家，人们最喜欢读哪类内容？
questions.sample: In China, I see interest in everything from online serials to practical guides. Short chapters are convenient on a busy commute, while a parent helping a child choose books may look for a print edition they can read together.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国，我看到读者的兴趣很广，从网络连载到实用指南都有人看。通勤忙碌的时候，篇幅短的章节读起来很方便。而帮孩子挑书的家长，可能更想找一本能和孩子一起翻着看的纸质书。

questions.en: Do you think it is better to read the book first before seeing the film based on it?
questions.zh: 你觉得看改编电影之前先读原著更好吗？
questions.sample: I usually prefer the book first because I can picture the setting and characters for myself. After seeing a film, the actor's face tends to stay in my head. Someone who finds the book difficult might prefer the opposite order.
questions.sampleZh: 我自己通常喜欢先读书，因为这样可以按自己的想象勾画场景和人物。看过电影之后，脑海里很容易一直是演员的脸。不过觉得原著难读的人，也许更喜欢反过来。

questions.en: Do you think watching movies based on novels can make people want to read more?
questions.zh: 你觉得看由小说改编的电影，能让人更想读书吗？
questions.sample: Yes. A film sometimes leaves you curious about a character who only appears briefly. Reading the novel can tell you what happened before that scene or why the character made a choice the film had no time to explain.
questions.sampleZh: 会。有时电影里的一个角色只出现了一小会儿，却让你很好奇。去读小说，你也许就能知道那一幕之前发生过什么，或者电影没时间交代清楚的、人物作出某个选择的原因。

questions.en: How does reading stories benefit children's development?
questions.zh: 阅读故事对儿童成长有哪些好处？
questions.sample: Stories let children try out other people's points of view. If two characters fall out over a toy, a child can think about how each one feels. Talking about what could happen next also gives them a reason to use new words.
questions.sampleZh: 故事能让孩子试着站在别人的角度看事情。两个角色如果因为一件玩具闹翻了，孩子可以想想双方分别有什么感受。聊一聊接下来可能发生什么，也给了他们运用新词的机会。

questions.en: What are the benefits and drawbacks of reading historical novels?
questions.zh: 读历史小说有哪些好处和局限？
questions.sample: They can make another period feel real by showing what people wore, ate or worried about. The drawback is that an invented scene may stick in your memory as history. An author's note about the research can really help.
questions.sampleZh: 历史小说通过描写当时的人穿什么、吃什么、担心什么，让别的年代变得真实可感。缺点是，虚构的场景也可能被你当成史实记下来。如果作者附上一段说明，讲讲自己做了哪些考证，会很有帮助。

questions.en: Some people say that reading non-fiction is more worthwhile than reading fiction. Do you think so?
questions.zh: 有人说，读非虚构作品比读虚构作品更值得。你同意吗？
questions.sample: No, they do different things. A guide can teach me how to fix a loose shelf, while a novel can help me understand why a character finds an ordinary conversation difficult. Both can be worthwhile for quite different reasons.
questions.sampleZh: 我不同意，两种书能带给人的东西不一样。一本实用指南可以教我修好松动的架子，一部小说则可能让我理解，为什么一次普通的谈话对某个角色来说都那么困难。两种阅读都可能很值得，只是原因不同。

questions.en: What kinds of films are popular in your country?
questions.zh: 哪些类型的电影在你们国家比较受欢迎？
questions.focusWording: What kinds of movies do people in China like to watch?
questions.sample: Comedies and animated films seem to draw broad audiences in China. A family can go together during a holiday and find something to enjoy across different ages. Crime stories and science fiction also appeal to people who want a bigger cinema experience.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国，喜剧和动画电影似乎都能吸引很广泛的观众。节假日一家人一起去看，不同年龄的人都能找到自己的乐趣。对想在影院里获得更强烈观影体验的人来说，犯罪题材和科幻电影也很有吸引力。

questions.en: Why do some movies cost a lot to produce?
questions.zh: 有些电影为什么制作成本特别高？
questions.focusWording: Why do some movies cost a lot to produce?
questions.sample: Some scenes need a large crew working for days, even if they only last a minute on screen. A crowded historical street needs costumes, extras, lighting and somewhere to film. Bad weather can make the whole team come back tomorrow.
questions.sampleZh: 有的场景在银幕上只有一分钟，却要一大群人忙上好几天。光是一条人来人往的古代街道，就需要服装、群众演员、灯光，还得找地方拍。如果天气不好，整个剧组第二天都得再来一趟。

questions.en: What changes has technology brought to film production?
questions.zh: 科技给电影制作带来了哪些改变？
questions.focusWording: What changes has technology brought upon film?
questions.sample: Digital cameras and editing software let filmmakers try changes without shooting everything again. Effects can create places that would be impossible to build, and smaller teams can now make convincing films. A believable performance and a good story still matter.
questions.sampleZh: 有了数码摄影机和剪辑软件，电影人可以尝试不同改法，不用每次都全部重拍。特效能创造现实中根本搭不出来的地方，现在小团队也能拍出让人信服的电影。当然，可信的表演和好故事仍然重要。

questions.en: To what extent can films promote intercultural understanding?
questions.zh: 电影能在多大程度上促进不同文化之间的相互理解？
questions.sample: They can do quite a lot by showing ordinary moments, like what happens around a family's dinner table. One film can't represent an entire country, though. Watching different directors helps you notice where their experiences and opinions differ.
questions.sampleZh: 电影在这方面能发挥很大作用，只要呈现日常的小事就可以，比如一家人围着饭桌时会发生什么。不过，一部电影不能代表整个国家。多看几位导演的作品，能帮你发现他们的经历和看法有哪些不同。

questions.en: Do you think that films can better develop people's creativity than reading books?
questions.zh: 和书籍相比，电影更能激发人的创造力吗？
