questions.sample: I wouldn't say films are always better. A film can inspire someone to experiment with light or music. A book leaves the faces, voices and scenery to the reader, which gives a different part of the imagination a workout.
questions.sampleZh: 我不会说电影一定更好。一部电影可能启发一个人去尝试光线或音乐的不同用法。一本书则把人物的面孔、声音和周围的景色留给读者想象，锻炼的是想象力的另一个方面。

questions.en: Is watching a film at the cinema different from watching one at home?
questions.zh: 去电影院看电影和在家看电影有区别吗？
questions.sample: Yes. At the cinema, the big screen and shared laughter can make a scene feel more powerful. At home you can pause, turn on subtitles or talk about a detail, which suits a complicated film better for some people.
questions.sampleZh: 有区别。在电影院，大银幕和大家一起笑起来的气氛，会让一个场景更有感染力。在家里可以暂停、打开字幕，或者停下来聊某个细节。有些人觉得，看情节复杂的电影时这样更合适。

questions.en: Why do some people think watching films is a waste of time?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人觉得看电影浪费时间？
questions.sample: If someone sees films only as entertainment, two hours on the sofa may seem unproductive. They might also have sat through several movies they didn't enjoy. A film about a subject they care about could feel very different.
questions.sampleZh: 如果一个人把电影纯粹看作消遣，那在沙发上坐两个小时也许会显得没做什么有用的事。他也可能已经硬着头皮看过好几部自己不喜欢的电影。换成一部讲自己在意的话题的电影，感觉也许就完全不同。

questions.en: Is it true that people often watch films so they can forget about their everyday lives?
questions.zh: 人们看电影，常常是为了暂时忘掉日常生活的事吗？
questions.sample: Yes, that's one reason. Following a mystery for an evening can give someone a break from thinking about tomorrow's work. Others deliberately choose a film close to their own lives because it helps them understand what they're going through.
questions.sampleZh: 是的，这是一个原因。花一晚上跟着悬疑故事找答案，可以让人暂时不去想第二天的工作。也有人特意选和自己的生活很接近的电影，因为它能帮助他们理解自己正在经历的事情。

questions.en: When a movie is based on real events, how important is it to get all the facts right?
questions.zh: 一部电影如果改编自真实事件，准确呈现所有相关事实有多重要？
questions.sample: The central events and their consequences should be accurate, especially when real people are portrayed. Combining two short conversations into one scene seems less serious. I'd want the film to say clearly when it has changed an important part.
questions.sampleZh: 核心事件和造成的后果应该准确，尤其是影片在描写真实人物时。把两段简短对话合成一场戏，问题似乎没那么大。不过，如果电影改动了某个重要部分，我希望它能明确告诉观众。

questions.en: Do you think films can play an important role in teaching people about the real world?
questions.zh: 你觉得电影能在帮助人们认识现实世界方面发挥重要作用吗？
questions.sample: Yes, particularly when a film takes viewers into a place or job they know little about. A documentary can show what a market looks and sounds like before sunrise. It can also leave questions that viewers want to explore afterwards.
questions.sampleZh: 可以，尤其是电影把观众带到一个他们知之甚少的地方，或带他们走进一份陌生职业时。比如，纪录片能让人看到日出前的市场是什么模样，也听到那里的声音。它还可能留下几个让观众看完后想自己去探究的问题。

questions.en: Do you think that, in the future, movies on serious topics won't be made because of people's attention spans?
questions.zh: 你觉得未来会不会因为观众难以长时间集中注意力，就没有人拍严肃题材的电影了？
questions.sample: I doubt serious films will disappear. People can stay focused for a long time when they care about a person or a question. Directors may change how they open a film, but difficult subjects can still attract an audience.
questions.sampleZh: 我不觉得严肃电影会消失。如果人们在意某个人或某个问题，他们完全可以专注很长时间。导演或许会调整电影开头的拍法，但有难度的题材依然能吸引观众。

questions.en: Do people's movie preferences change as they get older?
questions.zh: 人们喜欢看的电影类型会随着年龄增长而变化吗？
questions.sample: They often do, as people recognise different things in a story. Someone who loved the adventures in a film as a teenager might watch it again years later and pay more attention to the relationship between the parents.
questions.sampleZh: 经常会，因为人在故事里留意或认同的东西会变。一个人十几岁时可能最喜欢电影里的冒险情节，多年后重看同一部电影，却会更留意片中父母之间的关系。

questions.en: Should documentary films be completely truthful?
questions.zh: 纪录片应该完全忠于事实吗？
questions.sample: They should be truthful about facts and tell viewers when a scene has been recreated. A director still has to choose whom to interview and what to leave out. Being open about those choices is more realistic than claiming complete neutrality.
questions.sampleZh: 纪录片应该如实呈现事实，如果某个场景是重演的，也要告诉观众。导演仍然得选择采访谁、哪些素材不放进去。坦诚交代这些选择，比宣称自己完全中立更实际。

questions.en: Why are some children very popular at school?
questions.zh: 为什么有些孩子在学校里特别受欢迎？
questions.sample: Some children make other pupils feel welcome. They remember names, invite someone new into a game or make the group laugh without putting anyone down. Being good at a sport can attract attention, but kindness helps those friendships last.
questions.sampleZh: 有的孩子能让其他同学感到自己很受欢迎。他们记得别人的名字，会邀请新同学加入游戏，也能把大家逗笑却不拿任何人开涮。擅长运动也许能吸引注意，但友善才能让那些友谊延续下去。

questions.en: What are the advantages for a child of being popular at school?
questions.zh: 在学校受欢迎对一个孩子有哪些好处？
questions.sample: They may find it easier to join activities and feel comfortable speaking up in class. If a game starts during break, somebody is likely to invite them. That sense of belonging can make an unfamiliar school feel much less stressful.
questions.sampleZh: 他们可能更容易加入活动，在课堂上也更敢发言。课间有人玩游戏时，很可能会有人主动邀请他们。有了这种归属感，即使到了陌生的学校，压力也会小很多。

questions.en: Some people say that, in general, everybody likes popular children. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，一般来说，那些人缘好的孩子谁都喜欢。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Not necessarily. Being popular means many children notice or like someone, but classmates can have very different tastes. The child who keeps everyone laughing might be lovely at break and quite distracting to the person sitting beside them in class.
questions.sampleZh: 不一定。受欢迎意味着有很多孩子注意到或喜欢一个人，但同学们的喜好可以很不一样。一个总能把大家逗笑的孩子，课间也许特别讨人喜欢，上课时却可能让坐在旁边的同学很难集中注意力。

questions.en: Sometimes being popular at work is not a good thing. Why is that?
questions.zh: 在工作中受欢迎有时并不是好事。你觉得为什么会这样？
questions.sample: A popular colleague can end up agreeing to every request because they don't want to disappoint anyone. It's also awkward if that person becomes a manager. Their old friends may expect special treatment, even when the fairest answer is no.
questions.sampleZh: 人缘好的同事可能不想让任何人失望，于是什么请求都答应了。如果这个人后来成了主管，处境也会有些尴尬。老朋友可能指望得到特殊照顾，即使最公平的做法是说“不”。

questions.en: Do you think managers can easily get their team to like them?
questions.zh: 你觉得管理者容易赢得团队成员的喜爱吗？
questions.sample: They can earn trust, but they can't make a team like them on demand. A manager who listens and keeps promises has a good start. Constantly trying to please everyone can backfire when a difficult decision eventually comes up.
questions.sampleZh: 他们能靠行动赢得信任，却没法要求团队想喜欢自己就马上喜欢自己。愿意倾听、说到做到，就是很好的开始。一味想让所有人满意，等到终于必须作出艰难决定时，反而可能适得其反。

questions.en: Do you think being popular at work always leads to promotion and success?
questions.zh: 你觉得在职场上受欢迎，就一定会得到晋升并取得成功吗？
questions.sample: No. Being easy to work with can bring opportunities, but a promotion may require skills you haven't shown yet. A well-liked salesperson might still need practice planning shifts or handling complaints before they're ready to run the shop.
questions.sampleZh: 不会。好相处可能给你带来机会，但升职也许需要一些你还没展现过的本领。一个很受欢迎的销售员，可能还得练习排班和处理投诉，才能真正准备好管理一家店。

questions.en: To what extent do you think a person's popularity and their social status are linked?
questions.zh: 你觉得一个人的受欢迎程度和社会地位有多大关联？
questions.sample: There's a connection, but it works differently in different groups. A person with a high position gets noticed more, which can look like popularity. In a neighbourhood, the most popular person might simply be the one who brings everyone together.
questions.sampleZh: 两者确实有关联，但在不同群体里，这种关联的表现并不相同。地位高的人更容易受到关注，从外面看似乎就很受欢迎。而在一个社区里，最受欢迎的也许只是那个总能把大家聚到一起的人。

questions.en: Some people say that society tends to value popularity above other personal qualities, such as honesty. Do you think so?
questions.zh: 有人说，比起诚实等其他个人品质，社会往往更看重一个人是否受欢迎。你觉得呢？
questions.sample: It can look that way online because likes are easy to count and honesty isn't. In everyday situations, the balance may change. If I needed someone to look after my keys, I'd pick a dependable person regardless of their following.
questions.sampleZh: 在网上看起来可能是这样，因为点赞数很容易数出来，诚实却没法这么量化。但在日常生活中，轻重就可能不一样了。比如我需要找人帮忙保管钥匙，我会选一个靠得住的人，不会在意他有多少粉丝。

questions.en: Do you think society will value popularity more, or less in the future?
questions.zh: 你觉得未来社会会更看重一个人是否受欢迎，还是会看得更淡？
questions.sample: I think online popularity may get even more attention because numbers are so visible. But the more often people see a famous account promoting something disappointing, the more they may value recommendations from a smaller circle they actually trust.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得网络人气可能会得到更多关注，因为那些数字人人都看得到。不过，人们越常看到大账号推销令人失望的东西，就越可能珍惜来自身边小圈子、自己真正信得过的推荐。

questions.en: Why do people want to be popular?
questions.zh: 人们为什么希望自己受欢迎？
questions.sample: Often it's about belonging. Knowing that somebody will save you a seat or ask you along to lunch feels good. For other people, popularity also brings opportunities, like being invited to join a project or speak at an event.
questions.sampleZh: 很多时候是因为想有归属感。知道有人会帮你留个位子，或者喊你一起去吃午饭，感觉很好。对另一些人来说，受欢迎还能带来机会，比如受邀加入一个项目，或者到活动上发言。

questions.en: Is it easier to become popular nowadays?
questions.zh: 如今想成为受欢迎的人更容易吗？
questions.sample: It's easier to get noticed quickly because one video can reach thousands of people. Staying popular is another matter. The people who watched that clip may forget the creator's name as soon as the next interesting video appears.
questions.sampleZh: 现在更容易迅速受到关注，因为一个视频就可能被几千个人看到。但能不能一直受欢迎是另一回事。看过短片的人，可能下一条有趣的视频一出现，就忘了作者叫什么。

questions.en: What are the qualities of being a good teacher?
questions.zh: 一位好老师应具备哪些品质？
questions.sample: A good teacher can explain one idea in several ways and notice when a student is lost. Patience matters too. If students feel safe saying "I don't get it," the teacher can fix the problem before the class moves on.
questions.sampleZh: 好老师能用好几种方式解释同一个概念，也能看出学生什么时候没跟上。耐心同样重要。如果学生敢放心说“我没懂”，老师就能在全班开始学下一部分之前，把问题解决掉。

questions.en: Do you think good teachers are always popular among students?
questions.zh: 好老师一定受学生欢迎吗？
questions.sample: No. A good teacher may give difficult feedback or insist that everyone practises something again. Students might only appreciate that later, when they can finally solve a problem they used to avoid or explain it to someone else.
questions.sampleZh: 不一定。好老师有时会提出不太好听的意见，或者坚持让大家把某件事再练一遍。学生也许要到后来终于能解决一道过去总躲着的问题，甚至能给别人讲清楚时，才会体会到当时的用意。

questions.en: Is it important for a teacher to be popular?
questions.zh: 对老师来说，受学生欢迎重要吗？
questions.sample: It helps if students enjoy being in the classroom, but being trusted matters more. A teacher who treats everyone fairly can get students to ask questions and accept correction, even if they don't think every lesson is exciting.
questions.sampleZh: 学生喜欢待在课堂上当然有帮助，但让他们信任老师更重要。老师如果公平地对待每个人，学生就会愿意提问、接受纠正，即使他们不觉得每一堂课都特别精彩。

questions.en: What would make a student happy at school?
questions.zh: 什么能让学生在学校感到快乐？
questions.focusWording: What things make students happy at school?
questions.sample: Having one friend to sit with can make a huge difference, especially at a new school. A student can also feel happy when effort pays off, like finally answering a question they were too shy to attempt last week.
questions.sampleZh: 有一个能坐在一起的朋友，就可能带来很大的不同，尤其是刚到一所新学校时。学生看到努力有了回报，也会开心，比如终于答出了一个自己上周还害羞得不敢尝试的问题。

questions.en: Do you think doing a job that you like is more important than other things?
questions.zh: 你觉得从事自己喜欢的工作比其他因素更重要吗？
questions.focusWording: Is it more important to like your job?
questions.sample: Liking your job matters because you spend so much of your week there. I'd still weigh it against a reliable income and reasonable hours. Even work you love can become exhausting if you never have an evening to yourself.
questions.sampleZh: 喜欢自己的工作很重要，因为一周里有那么多时间是在工作中度过的。不过，我还是会同时考虑收入是否稳定、工时是否合理。就算做的是热爱的事，如果连一个属于自己的晚上都没有，也会让人筋疲力尽。

questions.en: How can the arts spread positive emotions in society?
questions.zh: 艺术怎样在社会中传递积极情绪？
questions.focusWording: How can the arts spread positive influence in society?
questions.sample: The arts can give people a shared experience they carry home. A neighbourhood concert, for instance, might get strangers singing the same chorus. Even after the music stops, they've got something friendly to talk about when they meet again.
questions.sampleZh: 艺术能带给人们一段可以带回家的共同体验。比如一场社区音乐会，也许能让素不相识的人一起唱出同一段副歌。就算音乐停了，下次见面时，他们也有一个让人愉快的话题可以聊。

questions.en: What kinds of things do young children often enjoy doing at school?
questions.zh: 年幼的孩子在学校里通常喜欢做哪些事？
questions.sample: Many young children enjoy activities where they can move, make things or play together. Acting out a story gets them out of their seats and lets them choose a role. That feels different from simply hearing the story read aloud.
questions.sampleZh: 许多年幼的孩子喜欢能动一动、做点东西或和别人一起玩的活动。把故事演出来，既能让他们离开座位，又能自己选角色。这和平时只是坐着听别人朗读故事，感觉很不一样。

questions.en: How can teachers make children happy at school?
questions.zh: 老师可以怎样让孩子们在学校过得开心？
questions.sample: Teachers can notice the little things that make a school day easier. Greeting a child by name and pairing a new pupil with a friendly classmate can help. Letting children choose between two activities also gives them some control.
questions.sampleZh: 老师可以留意那些能让孩子在学校过得更顺心的小事。进门时叫着名字打招呼，把新同学和一个友好的孩子安排成搭档，这些都有帮助。让孩子在两种活动中自己挑，也会让他们觉得有一点自主权。

questions.en: Some people say that learning at school should always be enjoyable for children. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，学校里的学习应该始终让孩子们感到愉快。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Learning should feel encouraging, but it won't always be enjoyable in the moment. Reading aloud or practising multiplication can feel frustrating at first. A patient teacher can make the difficulty manageable until the child gets the pleasure of succeeding.
questions.sampleZh: 学习应该让孩子受到鼓励，但学习中的每一刻未必都愉快。大声朗读或练乘法，一开始可能让人很挫败。有耐心的老师能帮孩子把困难控制在可以应付的范围内，直到他们体会到成功的快乐。

questions.en: Do you think it's important for people to enjoy the work they do?
questions.zh: 你觉得喜欢自己从事的工作重要吗？
questions.sample: Yes, because some degree of enjoyment makes it easier to stay interested and keep learning. People don't have to love every task. Even a job with repetitive paperwork can feel rewarding if the person enjoys helping customers solve problems.
questions.sampleZh: 重要，因为只要能从工作中得到一些乐趣，就更容易保持兴趣、继续学习。人们不必喜欢每一项任务。即使工作中有重复的文书处理，只要喜欢帮助顾客解决问题，也可以觉得这份工作很有价值。

questions.en: Some people say a high salary is the best way to help people feel positive at work. Do you think so?
questions.zh: 有人说，高薪最能让人以积极的心态对待工作。你觉得呢？
questions.sample: A good salary matters if someone is worried about paying the bills. Beyond that, a manager who respects people's time or thanks them for good work can change how they feel every day. Money alone won't fix a hostile workplace.
questions.sampleZh: 一个人如果还在发愁账单怎么付，一份不错的薪水当然重要。在此之外，一位尊重员工时间、也会感谢他们认真工作的主管，能改变员工每天的感受。光靠钱解决不了充满敌意的工作氛围。

questions.en: Do you think it would be better for employees if companies involved them in all decision-making?
questions.zh: 你觉得如果公司让员工参与所有决策，会对员工更有利吗？
questions.sample: I'd involve employees in decisions that affect how they work. A cashier may spot a problem with a new checkout design that a manager missed. Asking everyone to approve every small purchase, though, would leave less time for their actual jobs.
questions.sampleZh: 我会让员工参与那些和他们工作方式有关的决定。收银员也许能一眼看出新收银台设计里主管没发现的问题。但如果连每一笔小额采购也要每个人批准，就会挤占大家做本职工作的时间。

questions.en: How important are the arts in developing wellbeing and positivity in society? [e.g. film, literature, music]
questions.zh: 电影、文学、音乐等艺术形式，对提升社会整体幸福感、培养积极心态有多重要？
questions.sample: They're important because people need ways to express feelings they can't always put into words. A song can comfort someone on a hard day, while discussing a novel can help friends understand an experience they've never had themselves.
questions.sampleZh: 艺术很重要，因为有些情绪人们未必说得出口，需要通过别的方式表达。一首歌能在难熬的一天给人安慰。朋友一起讨论一本小说，也能借此理解自己从来没有经历过的事。

questions.en: Do people with a positive attitude contribute more to society?
questions.zh: 心态积极的人会为社会作出更多贡献吗？
questions.sample: A positive attitude can help someone encourage a tired group, but it isn't the only way to contribute. A cautious person who points out a weak bridge or a mistake in a budget may save everyone a great deal of trouble.
questions.sampleZh: 积极的心态能帮助一个人给疲惫的团队打气，但作出贡献不只这一种方式。一个谨慎的人指出一座桥不够牢固，或者一份预算里有错误，也可能替大家免去很大的麻烦。

questions.en: Do you think encouraging people to have a more positive attitude is the best way to have a happier society in the future?
questions.zh: 你觉得鼓励人们以更积极的态度生活，是让未来社会更幸福的最好办法吗？
questions.sample: It can help, but I'd start with conditions that make daily life easier. Safe parks, time to see family and neighbours who look out for each other give people reasons to feel positive. Simply asking everyone to smile won't create those conditions.
questions.sampleZh: 鼓励乐观会有帮助，不过我会先改善那些能让日常生活轻松一点的条件。安全的公园、陪家人的时间，以及互相照应的邻居，都能给人真正乐观的理由。光是要求大家微笑，创造不出这些条件。

questions.en: When do you think people are happiest?
questions.zh: 你觉得人们什么时候最快乐？
questions.sample: Often it's when they can give their full attention to something or someone they care about. It might be a relaxed meal after a busy week. There's no urgent train to catch, and nobody's checking messages under the table.
questions.sampleZh: 常常是能把全部注意力放在自己在意的人或事上的时候。也许是忙了一周后，一顿能放松享受的饭。不用急着去赶车，也没有人躲在桌子底下看消息。

questions.en: Do you think teachers are able to spot the unhappy children?
questions.zh: 你觉得老师能看出哪些孩子不开心吗？
questions.sample: Sometimes. A teacher might notice that a normally talkative child suddenly sits alone at break. A quiet child can be harder to read, though, so a private, gentle question is better than guessing what's wrong in front of the class.
questions.sampleZh: 有时能。一个平时爱说话的孩子突然在课间独自坐着，老师也许一下就会注意到。但本来就安静的孩子更难看出来。和他私下温和地聊一句，会比当着全班的面猜他出了什么事更好。

questions.en: Should teachers know what children are doing all the time?
questions.zh: 老师应该随时掌握孩子在做什么吗？
questions.sample: During school activities, teachers should know children are safe and can get help. They don't need to follow every conversation or decide every game. A little space lets children practise making choices and sorting out small disagreements themselves.
questions.sampleZh: 在学校活动期间，老师应该知道孩子是否安全，以及他们需要时能不能得到帮助。老师不必听到每一句对话，也不用替他们决定玩什么游戏。留一点空间，孩子才能练习自己作选择、自己解决小分歧。

questions.en: What skills do children need to learn before they start school?
questions.zh: 孩子上学前需要学习哪些技能？
questions.focusWording: What skills should children learn before they start school?
questions.sample: Taking turns, asking for help and handling simple daily tasks are good starting points. A child who can tell a teacher they need the toilet or open their own lunch box will find those first school days a little easier.
questions.sampleZh: 学会轮流、开口求助、自己处理简单的日常事务，都是很好的起点。一个孩子如果能告诉老师自己想上厕所，或者能独自打开饭盒，刚入学的那几天就会轻松一些。

questions.en: Is it easier for adults to learn from others than to learn completely by themselves?
questions.zh: 对成年人来说，向别人学比完全自学更容易吗？
questions.focusWording: Is it easier for adults to learn from others than to learn by themselves?
questions.sample: Often, yes. Adults have limited time, so a person who can spot a mistake may save them hours of guessing. Still, someone learning to edit photos might prefer to watch a short lesson and experiment alone at their own pace.
questions.sampleZh: 常常是这样。成年人的时间有限，有人能帮忙看出错误，也许能省下几个小时自己瞎猜的工夫。不过，学修图的人也可能更喜欢先看一小段教程，再按自己的节奏一个人试。

questions.en: Is it good that many people now turn to the Internet to learn skills?
questions.zh: 如今很多人上网学技能，你觉得这是好事吗？
questions.focusWording: Is it good that many people now turn to the Internet to learn skills?
questions.sample: Generally, yes. It gives people access to lessons they might never find nearby, from repairing clothes to speaking another language. It works best when they actually try the task afterwards and compare a couple of sources if instructions seem unclear.
variants: How useful is the internet when you're learning a new skill?
questions.sampleZh: 总体上是好事。不管是修补衣物还是学说另一门语言，网上都能找到一些在附近也许根本找不到的课。看过后自己动手试，碰到讲不清楚的步骤再对照两三个来源，效果最好。

questions.en: Are there differences in how parents and teachers help children learn new skills?
questions.zh: 父母和老师帮助孩子学习新技能的方式有区别吗？
questions.sample: Parents can build practice into ordinary routines, like teaching a child to measure ingredients while making dinner. Teachers can watch a whole class attempt the same skill and break it into clear steps. The two kinds of support fit together well.
questions.sampleZh: 家长可以把练习放进日常生活里，比如做晚饭时教孩子量食材。老师可以观察全班尝试同一项技能，再把这个过程拆成几个清楚的步骤。这两种支持正好能够互相补充。

questions.en: How can children benefit from learning new skills from one another?
questions.zh: 孩子们互相学习新技能，能得到哪些好处？
questions.sample: A classmate may remember exactly which part felt confusing because they learned it yesterday. Children also get to practise explaining. Showing a friend how to fold a paper plane can teach the person giving the instructions as much as the learner.
questions.sampleZh: 同学也许还很清楚哪个地方最让人困惑，因为他自己昨天才学会。孩子们在教别人的时候，也练习了表达。拿教朋友折纸飞机来说，负责讲步骤的孩子得到的收获，可能一点不比学的人少。

questions.en: Is learning new skills from another person different from learning by yourself?
questions.zh: 跟别人学一项新技能和自学有什么区别吗？
questions.sample: Yes. Another person can see a mistake that you don't notice, such as holding a paintbrush too tightly. Learning alone gives you freedom to repeat the same exercise ten times without feeling that you're taking up somebody else's time.
questions.sampleZh: 有区别。别人能看出你自己没注意到的错误，比如把画笔握得太紧。一个人学的好处是，你可以自由地把同一个练习重复十次，也不用觉得自己在占用别人的时间。

questions.en: Some people say that employees should pay to learn any new skills they need for their work. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，员工学习工作需要的新技能，费用都应该自己承担。你同意吗？
questions.sample: If the employer introduces new software and requires everyone to use it, the employer should cover the training. If someone chooses a course for a future career change, it's more reasonable for them to pay some or all of the cost.
questions.sampleZh: 如果雇主引进新软件，要求所有员工使用，培训费就应该由雇主承担。如果是某个人为了将来转行主动去学一门课，那么自己承担一部分或者全部费用就比较合理。

questions.en: Do you think people today need a broad range of skills, or specialised skills?
questions.zh: 你觉得如今人们更需要掌握多种技能，还是需要专业技能？
questions.sample: Most people need a mix. A designer needs depth in design, but it also helps to explain ideas, manage a deadline and understand a client's budget. A collection of unrelated skills may be less useful than a few that work together.
questions.sampleZh: 大多数人两种都需要。设计师需要在设计本身上下功夫，同时，能把想法说清楚、按时完成任务、看懂客户的预算也很有帮助。比起学一堆互不相关的技能，掌握几项能搭配使用的本领也许更实用。

questions.en: Some people say that to be successful today, people have to continually upgrade their skills. Do you think so?
questions.zh: 有人说，如今想要成功就必须不断提升自己的技能。你觉得呢？
questions.sample: In many jobs, yes, though it doesn't mean taking a course every month. A shop owner who learns to manage online orders might keep customers whose habits have changed. Sometimes one well-chosen skill matters more than constantly chasing the newest tool.
questions.sampleZh: 很多岗位确实如此，不过这不意味着每个月都得上一门课。比如店主学会处理网上订单，就可能留住那些购物习惯已经改变的顾客。有时候，选对一项技能比不停追着最新工具跑更重要。

questions.en: Do you think people skills might be more important than work skills?
questions.zh: 你觉得与人打交道的能力有可能比具体的工作技能更重要吗？
questions.sample: In some roles, yes. A team leader who can't explain a decision may struggle even with strong technical knowledge. In other jobs, the technical basics are essential. You'd want the person repairing your bicycle to know how the brakes work.
questions.sampleZh: 在某些岗位上，可能是这样。团队负责人即使技术知识很扎实，如果说不清为什么作某个决定，工作也会很吃力。而在其他一些工作中，技术基础是必不可少的。你肯定希望给你修自行车的人知道刹车是怎么工作的。

questions.en: Why is self-discipline important when learning a new skill?
questions.zh: 学习新技能时，自律为什么重要？
questions.sample: Improvement is often too slow to notice from one day to the next. Self-discipline helps you keep practising after the first excitement fades. Ten minutes of speaking practice most evenings will usually achieve more than one very long session every few weeks.
questions.sampleZh: 进步常常很慢，从今天到明天几乎感觉不出来。最初的兴奋感过去之后，自律能帮你继续练习。大多数晚上花十分钟练口语，通常比隔几周一次练很长时间收获更多。

questions.en: What are the differences between learning from a teacher and learning by oneself?
questions.zh: 跟老师学和自学有什么区别？
questions.sample: A teacher chooses an order and can adjust it when you get stuck. By yourself, you decide exactly what you want to practise, which is liberating. The tricky part is spotting gaps in your knowledge when nobody is checking your progress.
questions.sampleZh: 老师会帮你安排学习顺序，遇到困难还可以调整。自学时，你可以完全决定自己想练什么，这种自由很舒服。难的是，没人检查进度的时候，你不容易发现自己还有哪些知识没掌握。

questions.en: How do adults learn a new skill?
questions.zh: 成年人是怎样学习新技能的？
questions.sample: Adults often begin with a problem they actually need to solve. They might ask a colleague for a quick demonstration, then try the task themselves. Learning to use a spreadsheet makes more sense when you've got a real budget to organise.
questions.sampleZh: 成年人常常是从一个自己确实需要解决的问题开始学起。他们可能先请同事简单演示，再自己动手试。如果手头真有一份预算要整理，学怎么用电子表格就更有意义了。

questions.en: How can parents and teachers teach children new skills?
questions.zh: 家长和老师可以怎样教孩子新技能？
questions.sample: I'd show the skill slowly, let the child try and give feedback on one small thing at a time. With tying shoelaces, correcting every movement at once can be overwhelming. One clear tip gives the child something they can use immediately.
questions.sampleZh: 我会先放慢动作示范，让孩子自己试，然后每次只针对一个小地方给反馈。比如学系鞋带，如果把每个动作的问题一下子都指出来，孩子可能会不知所措。一条清楚的提示，马上就能用得上。

questions.en: Where can children learn new skills?
questions.zh: 孩子可以在哪里学到新技能？
questions.sample: School is one place, but children also learn in kitchens, playgrounds and community clubs. A grandparent can show a child how to plant seeds at home. A sports club gives them a chance to practise taking turns with children they don't already know.
questions.sampleZh: 学校是一个地方，厨房、游乐场和社区俱乐部也都能让孩子学到东西。祖父母可以在家教孩子播种。参加体育俱乐部，则让他们有机会和原本不认识的小朋友练习轮流参与。

questions.en: Why should children learn new skills?
questions.zh: 孩子为什么要学习新技能？
questions.sample: New skills give children more independence and help them discover interests they didn't know they had. Learning to ride a bike, for instance, can turn an ordinary afternoon in the park into something they can enjoy with friends for years.
questions.sampleZh: 新技能让孩子更独立，也能帮他们发现自己还不知道的兴趣。比如学会骑自行车以后，一个原本普通的公园下午，就可能变成他们往后很多年都能和朋友一起享受的活动。

questions.en: Do you think parents should help their children learn to be organised?
questions.zh: 你觉得父母应该帮助孩子学会有条理地做事吗？
questions.sample: Yes, because small habits make home life easier for everyone. Parents could give school bags a regular spot by the door and let the children pack them. Taking over the whole job each evening wouldn't teach them very much.
questions.sampleZh: 应该，因为小习惯能让全家人的生活更省心。父母可以在门边给书包设一个固定的位置，再让孩子自己把东西装好。每天晚上都包办整件事，反而教不了他们多少东西。

questions.en: Is it important for all employees to be well organised at work?
questions.zh: 对所有员工来说，在工作中做事有条理都很重要吗？
questions.sample: Every employee needs some organisation, though it looks different across jobs. A cook has to prepare ingredients in time, while a receptionist needs to keep track of appointments. In both cases, one missed detail can create extra work for other people.
questions.sampleZh: 每个员工都需要一定的条理性，只是在不同工作中表现不一样。厨师要及时备好食材，前台接待则得记清各个预约。两种工作都是漏掉一个小细节，就可能给别人添一堆事。

questions.en: How can teachers encourage children to be well organised at school?
questions.zh: 老师可以怎样鼓励孩子们在校做事有条理？
questions.sample: They can build short routines into the day. Before pupils go home, give them two minutes to check tomorrow's timetable and pack what they'll need. Doing that together a few times is more helpful than repeatedly saying, "Be more organised."
questions.sampleZh: 老师可以把简短的固定步骤安排进一天里。放学前，给学生两分钟看一眼明天的课表，把会用到的东西装好。带着大家一起做几次，比反复叮嘱“做事要有条理”有用得多。

questions.en: Some people say that children who are well organised will always do better at school. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，做事有条理的孩子在学校里一定表现得更好。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Being organised helps children remember homework and find their notes. It doesn't guarantee higher marks. A very tidy student might still misunderstand a question, while a student with a messy desk might have an excellent grasp of the subject.
questions.sampleZh: 做事有条理能帮孩子记住作业、找到笔记，但不能保证分数更高。桌面很整齐的学生照样可能理解错题意，桌子乱的学生也可能对这门课掌握得非常好。

questions.en: How can people save time by being well organised?
questions.zh: 做事有条理，可以怎样帮助人们节省时间？
questions.sample: Grouping similar tasks can save a lot of repeated effort. Instead of visiting three shops on three separate evenings, someone could write a list and do one trip. Keeping everyday items in a fixed place also cuts down on searching.
questions.sampleZh: 把类似的任务放在一起做，能省去很多重复的工夫。与其分三个晚上分别跑三家店，可以先写好清单，一趟一起办完。把常用物品放在固定的位置，也能少花时间到处找。

questions.en: Being well organised in everyday life can sometimes have disadvantages. Why do you think that is?
questions.zh: 日常生活安排得井井有条，有时也会有弊端。你觉得为什么会这样？
questions.sample: A very detailed plan can become a burden. If a friend unexpectedly offers you a concert ticket, you might turn it down just because it wasn't on the schedule. Organisation works better when there's room for pleasant surprises.
questions.sampleZh: 计划安排得太细，有时会变成负担。如果朋友突然多出一张演唱会门票请你去，你可能只因为行程表上没写，就把它推掉了。安排生活时给愉快的意外留点空间，效果会更好。

questions.en: Why might smaller communities be easier to organise than larger communities?
questions.zh: 为什么小社区可能比大社区更容易组织起来？
questions.sample: In a small community, people are more likely to know whom to contact and what each neighbour needs. Agreeing on a clean-up date might take one conversation. A larger area needs more ways to reach people and hear different views.
questions.sampleZh: 在小社区，人们更可能知道有事该联系谁，也更了解每个邻居需要什么。商量哪天一起搞清洁，也许聊一次就定好了。地方更大，就需要更多渠道去联系居民，听取不同的意见。

questions.en: Some people say that no community can function without clear rules and strong organisation. Do you think so?
questions.zh: 有人说，如果缺少清晰的规则和有效的组织，任何社区都无法正常运转。你觉得呢？
questions.sample: Some clear expectations are necessary, especially when people share money or facilities. But a small group can work through trust and simple agreements. A neighbourhood book club doesn't need a committee and a rulebook just to choose next month's novel.
questions.sampleZh: 有些事情确实得事先说清楚，尤其是大家要共用经费或设施时。不过一个小团体靠信任和简单约定也可以运作。社区读书会不过是挑下个月读哪本小说，用不着专门成立委员会，再写一本规章手册。

questions.en: Do you think only the international community can effectively tackle the big issues the world is facing? [e.g. environmental issues]
questions.zh: 你觉得只有国际社会共同努力，才能有效应对环境问题等全球重大挑战吗？
questions.sample: International cooperation matters for problems that cross borders, but local action still counts. A city can make its buses easier to use without waiting for a worldwide agreement. Larger improvements often happen when many places act and share what worked.
questions.sampleZh: 对于跨国界的问题，国际合作很重要，但地方上的行动同样有用。一座城市可以先改善公交服务，让大家更方便乘车，不用等到全世界达成协议。很多地方分别开始行动，再交流哪些做法有效，往往就能带来更大的改善。

questions.en: Do you think it is important for managers to be well organized?
questions.zh: 对管理者来说，做事有条理重要吗？
questions.sample: Definitely. When a manager loses track of deadlines, the whole team feels the pressure. A clear schedule doesn't have to be fancy. Knowing who's doing what and checking in before something becomes urgent already makes a big difference.
questions.sampleZh: 非常重要。管理者如果记不住截止日期，压力会落到整个团队身上。清楚的进度表不必多花哨。知道谁负责什么，在事情变得紧急之前问问进展，就已经很有帮助。

questions.en: What can people do to become more organized?
questions.zh: 人们怎样才能让自己做事更有条理？
questions.sample: I'd start with one habit, like writing tomorrow's three most important tasks before finishing work. Then keep the list somewhere visible. An elaborate planning app is little help if adding tasks takes longer than doing the tasks themselves.
questions.sampleZh: 我会从一个习惯开始，比如每天下班前写下明天最重要的三件事，再把清单放在看得见的地方。一个功能复杂的计划软件，如果录入任务花的时间比做任务还长，就帮不上什么忙。

questions.en: Are organized people more likely to be successful at work or in their studies?
questions.zh: 做事有条理的人在工作或学业上更容易成功吗？
questions.sample: They're often in a better position because they can spread work out and notice problems early. A student who starts revising before exam week has time to ask questions. Success still depends on understanding the material and doing the work.
questions.sampleZh: 他们往往比较有优势，因为能把工作分散安排，也能早点发现问题。比如，一个在考试周之前就开始复习的学生，还有时间把不会的地方拿去问。最后能不能成功，仍然要看是否理解内容、是否真的去做了。

questions.en: Do you think children should learn to be organized from a young age?
questions.zh: 孩子应该从小学着有条理地做事吗？
questions.sample: Yes, if it starts with tasks that suit their age. A young child can put crayons back in one box after drawing. Being asked to plan a whole week would be too much, but a simple routine gives them an achievable first step.
questions.sampleZh: 应该，只要从符合年龄的小任务开始。小孩子画完画后，就能把蜡笔收回同一个盒子。让他安排整整一周可能要求太高，但一个简单的固定步骤，就是他做得到的第一步。

questions.en: Why is it important for people to be organized?
questions.zh: 为什么做事有条理很重要？
questions.sample: Being organised makes it easier to keep promises to other people. If you note an appointment and leave enough travel time, your friend doesn't have to wait. It also frees up attention for the task itself rather than remembering every little detail.
questions.sampleZh: 做事有条理，更容易兑现对别人的承诺。比如把约会记下来，把路上需要的时间留足，朋友就不用等你。这样还能腾出注意力专心做眼前的事，不用一直在脑子里记着每个小细节。

questions.en: Some people say that instead of asking for help, it's better for people to try to help themselves. Do you think so?
questions.zh: 有人说，与其向别人求助，人们最好先尝试自己解决问题。你同意吗？
questions.sample: I'd try first when a mistake is easy to fix. Figuring out one phone setting on your own can build confidence. If a problem could affect other people or waste hours of work, asking someone early is the more sensible choice.
questions.sampleZh: 如果出错了也好纠正，我愿意先自己试。独自弄明白手机里的一项设置，就能建立一点信心。如果一个问题会影响别人，或者可能白白耗掉几个小时的工作，那早点请教更明智。

questions.en: Why do some people not like to ask for help?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人不喜欢开口求助？
questions.sample: Some worry that admitting a difficulty will make them look unprepared. Others simply don't want to interrupt someone who's busy. A colleague saying, "I've got ten minutes if you want to look at it together," can make asking much easier.
questions.sampleZh: 有些人担心，承认自己遇到了困难会显得没准备好。还有人只是不想打扰正在忙的人。如果同事主动说一句“你想一起看看的话，我现在有十分钟”，对方开口求助就容易多了。

questions.en: What types of jobs do people do that help other people?
questions.zh: 哪些工作能帮助别人？
questions.sample: Teachers, carers and social workers are obvious examples, but less visible jobs help too. A bus driver who waits until an older passenger has found a seat makes an ordinary journey easier. Helping people isn't limited to a job with that word in its title.
questions.sampleZh: 老师、照护人员和社工都是明显的例子，不过一些不那么显眼的岗位也在帮人。比如，公交司机等一位老年乘客坐稳再开车，就让对方普通的一段路程变得轻松些。帮助别人并不限于职称里写明要提供帮助的工作。

questions.en: Some people say that people should always help their neighbours. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人认为，人们任何时候都应该帮助邻居。你同意吗？
questions.sample: It's good to help when you reasonably can. Picking up a parcel for a neighbour is a small kindness, but offering to care for their pet for a month is a different commitment. People can be helpful and still have limits.
questions.sampleZh: 在能力和条件允许时帮忙是好事。替邻居收个快递，是件小小的善举。答应替对方照顾宠物一个月，就是分量完全不同的承诺了。一个人可以乐于助人，也可以有自己的限度。

questions.en: Why should parents teach their children to help others?
questions.zh: 为什么父母应该教孩子帮助别人？
questions.sample: It teaches children to notice what somebody else might need. A parent can show this by holding a door for someone carrying shopping. Later the child may recognise a similar situation and offer help without waiting to be told.
questions.sampleZh: 这样能教孩子留意别人可能需要什么。家长可以自己作个示范，比如帮一个拎着购物袋的人扶住门。以后孩子遇到相似的场景，就可能不用人提醒也会主动帮忙。

questions.en: When do people usually ask for help?
questions.zh: 人们在什么情况下会向别人求助？
questions.sample: Often it's when they've tried something and can't see the next step. People also ask quickly when time is short, like at a crowded station just before a train leaves. In that situation, a clear direction is worth more than guessing.
questions.sampleZh: 人们往往是已经试过，却想不出下一步怎么走时才求助。时间很紧也会让人马上开口，比如在人很多的车站，火车就快开了。这种时候，得到一句清楚的指路，比自己猜来猜去有用得多。

questions.en: Do you think giving time is more valuable for society than giving money?
questions.zh: 你觉得为他人付出时间比捐钱对社会更有价值吗？
questions.sample: It depends on what's needed. An older neighbour might value an hour of company more than a gift. A local shelter that needs to pay its electricity bill may benefit more from money, even if the donation only takes a minute.
questions.sampleZh: 得看对方需要什么。独居的年长邻居也许觉得有人陪一个小时比收到礼物更珍贵。当地一家收容机构如果正要付电费，给它捐钱可能更有帮助，即使捐款本身只花一分钟。

questions.en: If everyone did more to help their local community, would society as a whole be greatly improved?
questions.zh: 如果每个人都为自己所在的社区多做一点，整个社会会因此得到很大改善吗？
questions.sample: I think it would improve in very visible ways. If more neighbours checked on someone living alone or looked after shared spaces, daily life would feel less lonely and more pleasant. Bigger problems like housing costs would still need wider decisions.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得会，而且这种改善会很明显。如果有更多邻居愿意去看看独居者，或者照看大家共用的地方，日常生活就会少一点孤单、多一点愉快。当然，住房成本之类的大问题，仍然需要在更大范围内作决定。

questions.en: Do you think global problems will only be solved by greater international cooperation?
questions.zh: 你觉得只有加强国际合作，才能解决全球性问题吗？
questions.sample: For some problems, yes, because no single country controls the whole situation. Pollution that travels across a border is one example. But cooperation has to be backed by actual changes at home, or an international meeting won't achieve much.
questions.sampleZh: 有些问题确实如此，因为没有哪个国家能独自掌控全局。跨越国界的污染就是一个例子。不过，合作也得有各国在国内采取的实际行动来支撑，否则开一次国际会议也很难取得什么成果。

questions.en: Should children be taught to be kind to others?
questions.zh: 应该教孩子善待他人吗？
questions.sample: Yes. Kindness is easier to understand when children see what it looks like in a small moment. Making space for a new pupil at lunch gives that pupil somewhere to sit and shows everyone else a simple way to include them.
questions.sampleZh: 应该。孩子能从日常小事里亲眼看见什么是善意，比只听概念更容易理解。午饭时给新同学腾出一个位子，既让他有地方坐，也让其他人看到，用一个简单的动作就能接纳新同学。

questions.en: Should people be very kind when they help others?
questions.zh: 帮助别人时，人们应该表现得特别友善吗？
questions.sample: Yes, particularly in how they offer. Asking "Would you like a hand?" gives the other person a choice. Taking over without asking may feel embarrassing, even when the helper is friendly and genuinely wants to make things easier.
questions.sampleZh: 应该，尤其是提出帮助的方式要友善。先问“需要帮忙吗？”，就把选择留给了对方。没问过就接手，有时反而会让对方尴尬，即使帮忙的人很友好，也真心想让事情轻松一点。

questions.en: Can kids provide any help to parents?
questions.zh: 孩子能给父母帮上忙吗？
questions.sample: Absolutely. A child can set the table, match socks or put books away while a parent is busy. Small tasks save a little time and allow the child to feel involved, as long as the responsibility suits their age.
questions.sampleZh: 当然能。父母很忙的时候，孩子可以摆餐具、把袜子配成对，或者把书收回去。只要分给孩子的责任适合他的年龄，这些小任务既能帮家里省一点时间，也能让孩子觉得自己参与其中。

questions.en: Should parents give children advice? Why?
questions.zh: 父母应该给孩子建议吗？为什么？
questions.sample: Yes, because parents may recognise a situation their child is facing for the first time. I'd listen before giving advice, though. A teenager talking about a difficult friend might want help choosing words, or they might just need someone to listen.
questions.sampleZh: 应该，因为有些情形孩子第一次遇到，父母却可能很熟悉。不过给建议之前，我会先听听孩子怎么说。一个青少年谈起一位不好相处的朋友时，可能希望有人帮他想想怎么措辞，也可能只需要有人听他说。

questions.en: What kind of advice should parents give to their children?
questions.zh: 父母应该给孩子什么样的建议？
questions.sample: Useful advice helps children make their own decisions. If two friends want different games, a parent could suggest taking turns or combining the ideas. Giving a practical option teaches more than saying, "You must always do what I tell you."
questions.sampleZh: 有用的建议能够帮助孩子自己作决定。如果两个朋友想玩不同的游戏，家长可以建议他们轮流选，或者把两个想法结合起来。给出一个能实践的选择，比一句“你必须永远照我说的做”更能让孩子学到东西。

questions.en: Should parents help their kids with their homework?
questions.zh: 家长应该辅导孩子做作业吗？
questions.sample: They should help children understand what to do, especially if a question is confusing. I wouldn't write the answer for them. Asking "Which part do you already know?" gives the child a starting point and shows the parent where help is needed.
questions.sampleZh: 家长应该帮孩子弄清楚要做什么，特别是题目让他们困惑的时候。但我不会替他们写答案。问一句“哪一部分你已经会了？”，既给孩子一个起点，也让家长知道哪里需要帮忙。

questions.en: How important is it for children to do a number of sports?
questions.zh: 对孩子来说，参加多种体育运动有多重要？
questions.sample: Trying several sports is valuable because children can discover what suits them. A child who dislikes competitive running might love badminton or swimming. There's no need to fill every afternoon with coaching. A little variety and time to play are enough.
questions.sampleZh: 尝试几种运动很有价值，因为孩子可以发现什么适合自己。一个不喜欢赛跑的孩子，也许特别喜欢羽毛球或游泳。没必要每天下午都排满训练课，有一点变化，再留出自由玩耍的时间，就够了。

questions.en: What skills and qualities do people need to be good at sport?
questions.zh: 想要在运动方面表现出色，人们需要哪些技能和素质？
questions.sample: It depends on the sport, but coordination, patience and the ability to take feedback help in most of them. A badminton player might lose the same point repeatedly. Staying calm enough to change one movement can matter more than hitting harder.
variants: What qualities should an athlete have?
questions.sampleZh: 得看是什么运动，不过在大多数项目里，协调能力、耐心和听得进反馈都很有用。一个羽毛球选手也许总是用同样的方式丢分。这时，能冷静下来调整一个动作，可能比更用力地击球更重要。

questions.en: In what ways is technology becoming more important in sports?
questions.zh: 科技正在哪些方面对体育运动发挥越来越重要的作用？
questions.sample: Coaches can now replay a movement slowly and show an athlete exactly what happened. Timing systems can also settle a close finish more clearly. For ordinary runners, even a basic watch makes it easier to see whether their pace is consistent.
questions.sampleZh: 现在教练可以慢放一个动作，让运动员清楚看到刚才到底发生了什么。计时系统也能在双方几乎同时冲线时更准确地判定结果。对普通跑步爱好者来说，甚至一块简单的手表都能帮他们判断自己的配速稳不稳定。

questions.en: What sports are popular with young people in your country?
questions.zh: 在你的国家，哪些运动受年轻人欢迎？
questions.sample: Basketball and badminton are popular choices among young people in China. Both can be social and fairly easy to organise after class. At a park, two friends can start a badminton game without needing to find a full team.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国，篮球和羽毛球都很受年轻人欢迎。两种运动都能让人交朋友，放学后也比较容易组织。在公园里，两个人就可以打起羽毛球，不用非得凑齐一整支队伍。

questions.en: Is it true that most young people enjoy taking part in sports competitions?
questions.zh: 大多数年轻人真的喜欢参加体育比赛吗？
questions.sample: I wouldn't assume most do. Plenty enjoy playing with friends but feel nervous when scores are announced or people are watching. A friendly school tournament might appeal to them more than a competition where only the strongest players get a turn.
questions.sampleZh: 我不会认为大多数年轻人都喜欢参赛。很多人喜欢和朋友玩，可一报比分，或者一有人围观，就会紧张。气氛轻松、人人能参与的校园小比赛，也许比只有最强的几个人能上场的比赛更吸引他们。

questions.en: Why is it difficult to become a top sports professional today?
questions.zh: 如今成为顶尖职业运动员为什么很难？
questions.sample: The standard is extremely high, and many talented athletes are competing for very few places. Progress takes coaching, regular practice and access to facilities. Even after years of preparation, an injury or one poor performance can affect a selection decision.
questions.sampleZh: 顶尖赛事的标准非常高，很多有天赋的运动员却只能争取很少的名额。进步需要教练指导、规律训练，还要用得到合适的场地和设施。哪怕准备了多年，一次受伤或一场发挥失常，都可能影响选拔结果。

questions.en: Some people say that professional sportspeople deserve the high salaries they receive. Do you think so?
questions.zh: 有人说，职业运动员拿这么高的薪水是他们应得的。你觉得呢？
questions.sample: Some do, especially when huge audiences pay to watch them and their careers are short. Still, the gap between sports can seem unfair. An athlete in a less televised event can train just as hard and earn a fraction of the money.
questions.sampleZh: 有些运动员确实配得上高薪，尤其是当大量观众愿意花钱看他们比赛，而他们的职业生涯又很短时。不过，不同运动之间的收入差距有时会让人觉得不公平。一个很少上电视的项目的运动员，训练也许同样辛苦，收入却只相当于别人的一小部分。

questions.en: Why do some sports not receive much global recognition?
questions.zh: 为什么有些体育项目在世界范围内的认可度不高？
questions.sample: Some are played mainly in one region, so audiences elsewhere don't know the rules or the famous players. Limited TV coverage adds to the problem. When a newcomer can't follow what's happening, it's harder for the sport to build interest.
questions.sampleZh: 有些项目主要在某个地区开展，其他地方的观众既不熟悉规则，也不认识有名的选手。电视转播少，让这个问题更突出。如果新观众连场上发生了什么都看不明白，这项运动就更难培养起大家的兴趣。

questions.en: Do you think governments or private companies should fund major sporting events?
questions.zh: 你觉得大型体育赛事应该由政府还是由私营企业出资？
questions.sample: I'd use a mix, depending on who benefits. Companies can pay for advertising and the main show if they expect a return. Public money makes more sense for transport or facilities residents can still use long after the event ends.
questions.sampleZh: 我会考虑两方共同出资，具体看谁会受益。企业如果预期能有回报，可以为广告宣传和主要赛事活动出钱。公共资金则更适合用于交通或场馆设施，因为比赛结束很久以后，当地居民仍然可以使用它们。

questions.en: Do you think life is better for older people now than it was in the past?
questions.zh: 你觉得如今老年人的生活比过去更好吗？
questions.sample: In some ways it is. Video calls make staying in touch easier, and plenty of older people enjoy activities that weren't accessible to them before. Others find daily tasks harder when booking appointments or buying tickets suddenly requires a smartphone.
questions.sampleZh: 在某些方面，确实更好了。视频通话让保持联系更容易，许多老年人也能享受以前没机会参加的活动。不过也有人发现，预约或买票突然都得用智能手机，普通的生活小事反而变难了。

questions.en: What can younger and older people learn from each other?
questions.zh: 年轻人和老年人可以互相学习什么？
questions.sample: Older people can share practical skills and explain how their town has changed. Younger people might show them how to use a new app. The exchange works well when each person asks what the other actually wants to learn.
questions.sampleZh: 老年人可以分享实用技能，也可以讲讲他们所在的城镇这些年发生了哪些变化。年轻人则可以教他们用一款新软件。如果双方都先问问对方真正想学什么，这样的交流效果会很好。

questions.en: What kinds of activities do older people enjoy?
questions.zh: 老年人喜欢参加哪些活动？
questions.sample: Many older people enjoy activities that let them meet the same group regularly. A weekly choir is a good example. People get to sing songs they know and stay for a chat afterwards, even if they don't fancy doing much exercise.
questions.sampleZh: 不少老年人喜欢能让自己定期和一群老熟人见面的活动。每周一次的合唱就是个例子。大家可以唱些自己熟悉的歌，结束后再留下来聊聊天，即使不太想运动也能参加。

questions.en: Some people say that older people only remember good things about the past. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，老年人只记得过去的好事。你同意吗？
questions.sample: No. People often choose cheerful stories when talking to grandchildren, but that doesn't mean the hard memories have disappeared. Sometimes an ordinary object, like an old school bag, can bring back a difficult time as clearly as a happy one.
questions.sampleZh: 我不同意。人们和孙辈聊天时可能更愿意讲开心的故事，但这不代表艰难的记忆就消失了。有时一个普通物件，比如一只旧书包，就能把一段难熬的往事唤回来，清晰程度不亚于快乐的回忆。

questions.en: What can cause older and younger people to misunderstand each other?
questions.zh: 哪些因素会让老一辈和年轻人之间产生误解？
questions.sample: The same behaviour can mean different things to each generation. A young person checking a phone at dinner might be arranging the journey home, while a grandparent sees it as ignoring the conversation. A quick explanation can prevent unnecessary hurt.
variants: Why is there a generation gap between the young and the old?
questions.sampleZh: 同一种行为，在两代人眼里可能有不同的意思。年轻人吃饭时看手机，可能是在安排回家的路线，祖父母却觉得他根本没听大家说话。简单解释一句，就能避免不必要的伤感情。

questions.en: Do you think younger people have more respect for older people now than in the past?
questions.zh: 你觉得现在的年轻人比过去更尊重老年人吗？
questions.sample: I think the way respect is shown has changed more than the amount. A young person might openly disagree with a grandparent yet spend an afternoon helping them book a trip. Someone from an earlier generation might have shown respect through silence.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得变得更多的是表达尊重的方式，而不是尊重本身的程度。一个年轻人也许会当面和祖父母意见相左，却又愿意花一整个下午帮他们预订行程。换作更早的一代人，可能会用保持沉默来表示尊重。

questions.en: Do you think the media doesn't focus enough on the older generation?
questions.zh: 你觉得媒体对老年群体的关注不够吗？
questions.sample: Often it doesn't, or it shows older people only when discussing illness and care. I'd like to see more ordinary stories about their work, friendships and hobbies. An older musician preparing for a local performance has a story worth telling too.
questions.sampleZh: 媒体往往关注得不够，有时也只有在讨论疾病和照护时才会呈现老年人的形象。我更想看到他们工作、交友和发展爱好的日常故事。比如，一位上了年纪的音乐家在为社区演出做准备，也有值得讲述的故事。

questions.en: Some people say there should be no fixed retirement age. Do you think so?
questions.zh: 有人说，不应该设定固定的退休年龄。你觉得呢？
questions.sample: I'd favour some flexibility. A person doing physically demanding work may want to stop earlier than someone who enjoys a few hours of teaching. The important part is having a real choice, rather than working longer simply because retirement is unaffordable.
questions.sampleZh: 我赞成有一定的弹性。一个长期从事重体力工作的人，可能希望早点退休，而一个喜欢每周教几小时课的人也许想继续。重要的是人能真正自己选择，不会只是因为负担不起退休生活而不得不多工作几年。

questions.en: If a country has lots of older people, how might that affect the country?
questions.zh: 如果一个国家老年人口很多，会给这个国家带来哪些影响？
questions.sample: It may need more accessible housing, transport and care services. There are benefits too. Retired people often have time and experience to offer, whether that's mentoring a younger colleague, volunteering locally or helping families look after children.
questions.sampleZh: 这个国家可能需要更多方便老年人使用的住房、交通和照护服务。同时也有好处。退休人士通常有时间、有经验，可以指导年轻同事、在社区当志愿者，或帮家人照顾孩子。

questions.en: What kinds of things do the elderly remember for a long time?
questions.zh: 老年人通常会长久记得哪些事？
questions.sample: Big turning points often stay with people, like leaving home for a first job. Tiny details can last too, like the smell of a family kitchen or a song from a wedding. Memories linked to strong feelings seem especially easy to bring back.
questions.sampleZh: 人生的重要转折点常常让人记很久，比如为了第一份工作离开家乡。很小的细节也能留下来，比如家里厨房的味道，或婚礼上听过的一首歌。那些与强烈情感相关的记忆，似乎特别容易被唤起。

questions.en: What sports are popular among older people?
questions.zh: 哪些运动在老年人中比较受欢迎？
questions.sample: Walking, tai chi and badminton are activities you often see older people doing in Chinese parks. They can choose their own pace and meet friends at the same time. Some older people still enjoy much more demanding sports, depending on their interests.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国的公园里，经常能看到老年人散步、打太极或打羽毛球。他们可以按自己的节奏来，同时还能和朋友见面。当然，有些老年人仍然喜欢对体能要求高得多的运动，这得看个人兴趣。

questions.en: What do old people usually do in their daily life?
questions.zh: 老年人日常生活通常会做些什么？
questions.sample: That depends on health, family and whether they're still working. A retired person might go to the market in the morning, cook lunch and meet friends later. Someone else might spend much of the day working or looking after a grandchild.
questions.sampleZh: 要看他们的身体状况、家庭情况，以及是否还在工作。一位退休的人可能早晨去菜市场，中午做饭，晚些时候会朋友。另一个人却可能一天中大部分时间都在工作，或者照顾孙辈。

questions.en: What types of famous people often give interviews?
questions.zh: 哪些类型的名人经常接受采访？
questions.sample: Actors and singers often give interviews when they have something new to release. Athletes are usually interviewed after a match, when people want to hear about a particular moment. Experts can also become familiar faces when their subject is in the news.
questions.sampleZh: 演员和歌手有新作品要推出时，经常会接受采访。运动员通常在赛后接受采访，因为大家想听他们聊聊某个具体瞬间。某个专业领域一旦成为新闻热点，相关专家也可能频频出镜，成为大家熟悉的面孔。

questions.en: Why do some famous people dislike giving interviews?
questions.zh: 为什么有些名人不喜欢接受采访？
questions.sample: Some have had a casual remark taken out of context, so they worry about how their words will be used. Others simply want to discuss their work without being asked personal questions about family or relationships.
questions.sampleZh: 有些人随口说过的话曾被断章取义，所以会担心自己的话又被怎样使用。另一些人只是想聊作品，不想被问到关于家人或感情生活的私人问题。

questions.en: Some people say that interviews with famous people are always interesting. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，名人访谈总是很有意思。你同意吗？
questions.sample: No. If a celebrity gives the same prepared answers in every interview, even a fan may lose interest. A thoughtful follow-up about a specific choice, like why a musician changed one line of a song, can make the conversation feel fresh.
questions.sampleZh: 不一定。如果一位名人每次受访都给出相同的标准答案，连粉丝也可能失去兴趣。针对某个具体选择作出有思考的追问，比如问音乐人为什么改了某一句歌词，就能让对话有新鲜感。

questions.en: What helps someone to do well in an interview for a new job?
questions.zh: 哪些因素能帮助求职者在面试中有好的表现？
questions.sample: A specific example is more persuasive than a string of positive adjectives. Instead of saying "I'm organised," someone could explain how they divided a project into weekly tasks and caught a problem early. It also helps to know what the job involves.
questions.sampleZh: 一个具体例子比一连串夸自己的形容词更有说服力。比如，一个人可以讲自己怎样把项目拆成每周的任务、怎样早早发现了问题，而不只是说“我做事有条理”。了解这份工作的具体内容也很有帮助。

questions.en: How important are the clothes a person wears for a job interview?
questions.zh: 求职面试时，一个人的穿着有多重要？
questions.sample: Clothes matter mostly because they're part of a first impression. Something clean, comfortable and suitable for that workplace is usually enough. After the first few minutes, clear answers and relevant examples should matter much more than the price of a jacket.
questions.sampleZh: 穿着重要，主要是因为它构成第一印象的一部分。通常穿得干净、舒适，又适合那个工作环境，就足够了。面试开始几分钟之后，回答是否清楚、例子是否切题，应该比一件外套卖多少钱重要得多。

questions.en: Do you think interviews are a good way of choosing the right person for a job?
questions.zh: 你觉得面试是为一个职位选出合适人选的好办法吗？
questions.sample: They're useful for seeing how someone explains ideas and responds to questions, but nerves can hide real ability. I'd combine a short interview with a realistic task. Watching a designer improve a simple layout tells you something talking alone can't.
questions.sampleZh: 面试有助于了解一个人怎样表达想法、回答问题，但紧张可能会掩盖真实能力。我会把简短面试和一项贴近实际工作的任务结合起来。看设计师动手改一个简单的版式，就能了解到一些光靠聊天看不出来的东西。

questions.en: Some people say that people can only interact effectively if they are genuinely interested in each other. Do you think so?
questions.zh: 有人说，只有真心对彼此感兴趣，人们才能进行有效交流。你觉得呢？
questions.sample: Genuine interest makes a conversation warmer, but effective communication doesn't always require a personal connection. Two strangers can sort out a delivery perfectly well by listening carefully, confirming the address and being clear about the time.
questions.sampleZh: 真心对对方感兴趣，会让谈话更有温度，但有效沟通未必都需要有私人的情感联系。两个陌生人只要认真听、核对好地址、说清楚时间，也完全能把一次送货安排妥当。

questions.en: How important is body language when people are interacting with each other?
questions.zh: 人与人交往时，肢体语言有多重要？
questions.sample: It's very useful for picking up feelings that words miss. A person might say they're fine while looking uncomfortable and stepping back. Still, gestures can mean different things across cultures, so I'd check what someone means before assuming too much.
questions.sampleZh: 肢体语言很有用，能帮人察觉话语没有表达出来的感受。一个人嘴上说“没事”，看起来却很不自在，还往后退了一步。不过，不同文化里的同一个手势可能意思不同，所以我会先问清楚对方的意思，再下判断。

questions.en: How do you think the society would be affected if, in the future, humans mainly interacted with artificial intelligence and not with each other?
questions.zh: 如果未来人们主要和人工智能互动，彼此之间的交流很少，你觉得社会会受到什么影响？
questions.sample: People might get used to a conversation partner that never interrupts and usually responds immediately. That could make real disagreement feel harder to handle. We'd have to make time for activities where people listen, compromise and share experiences face to face.
questions.sampleZh: 人们可能会习惯一个从不打断自己、通常又马上回答的对话伙伴。这样一来，现实中碰到有人意见不同，也许会觉得更难应对。我们得刻意留出时间参加一些面对面的活动，好好听别人说话、彼此作出让步、分享共同经历。

questions.en: What should people wear to a job interview?
questions.zh: 人们参加工作面试应该穿什么？
questions.sample: I'd wear something neat that suits the role and lets me feel like myself. A formal office might call for a jacket, while a design studio could be more relaxed. Wearing uncomfortable new shoes would only give me another distraction.
questions.sampleZh: 我会穿得整洁、符合岗位，也让自己感到自在。正式的办公室可能适合穿外套，设计工作室的着装则可能更随意。一双不舒服的新鞋只会给我平添一件分心的事。

questions.en: Why do we need to attend interviews when applying for jobs?
questions.zh: 申请工作时为什么需要参加面试？
questions.sample: A CV lists achievements but doesn't explain how a person thinks or what they contributed to a team. An interview gives both sides a chance to ask questions. The applicant may also discover whether the work fits their expectations.
questions.sampleZh: 简历列出了成绩，却说不清一个人怎样思考，也未必能解释他在团队里具体做了什么。面试给双方都提供了提问的机会。求职者也可以借此弄清这份工作是否符合自己的期待。

questions.en: What should people do to prepare for a job interview?
questions.zh: 人们应该如何为工作面试做准备？
questions.sample: I'd read the job description carefully and prepare two short examples from relevant projects. Practising those examples aloud helps spot details that aren't clear. I'd also check the route the day before and prepare one genuine question about the role.
questions.sampleZh: 我会仔细读职位说明，从做过的相关项目里准备两个简短的例子。把它们大声讲出来练习，有助于发现哪些细节还没讲清楚。我也会提前一天查好路线，并准备一个自己确实想了解的岗位问题。

questions.en: Why do some people think interviews are a waste of time?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人认为面试是在浪费时间？
questions.sample: They can feel pointless when every applicant gets vague questions and gives rehearsed answers. Someone may spend a whole day travelling without learning much about the actual job. A shorter conversation and a relevant task would make the time feel better spent.
questions.sampleZh: 如果每位应聘者被问到的都是模糊的问题，回答也都是事先背好的，面试就容易让人觉得毫无意义。有人可能花整整一天赶路，最后却没真正了解这份工作的内容。把谈话缩短，再配一项与岗位相关的任务，会让人觉得时间花得更值。

questions.en: Why do some people dislike being interviewed?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人不喜欢接受面试或采访？
questions.sample: Being asked to think aloud under pressure makes some people freeze, even when they know the subject well. Others dislike the feeling that one awkward sentence will represent their whole personality. A friendly interviewer and clear questions can help.
questions.sampleZh: 有些人即使很熟悉主题，被要求在压力下当场说出自己的思路也会脑中一片空白。另一些人则不喜欢那种感觉：仿佛一句说得不自然的话，就会被拿来判断整个人。友善的面试官和清楚的问题都能减轻这种压力。

questions.en: What kinds of people are usually interviewed?
questions.zh: 通常什么样的人会接受采访或面试？
questions.sample: It depends on the purpose. Reporters interview witnesses to find out what happened and experts to explain what it means. Employers interview applicants, while a researcher might interview ordinary residents because their day-to-day experience is exactly what the study needs.
questions.sampleZh: 得看目的。记者采访目击者是为了弄清发生了什么，采访专家是为了说明这些事意味着什么。雇主会面试求职者，而研究人员可能访谈普通居民，因为研究需要了解的恰恰是他们的日常经历。

questions.en: What kinds of places are often crowded in your country?
questions.zh: 在你们国家，什么样的地方经常人多拥挤？
questions.sample: In China, railway stations often get crowded before major holidays, when lots of passengers are trying to get home on the same day. A Saturday market can feel just as packed on a smaller scale, especially around a stall where people stop to taste things.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国，大节日前火车站经常很挤，因为许多旅客都想在同一天回家。周六的集市虽然规模小些，逛起来也可能一样拥挤，尤其是能停下来试吃的摊位附近。

questions.en: Why do some people choose to visit popular places when they are not crowded?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人会挑人少的时候去热门地点？
questions.sample: They can actually see and enjoy what they came for. At a museum on a quiet weekday, you can stand in front of one painting for several minutes. At peak times, you may spend longer waiting for a clear view.
questions.sampleZh: 因为这样才能真正看到并享受到自己专程来看的东西。比如在一个安静的工作日去博物馆，你能在一幅画前慢慢站上几分钟。到了高峰时段，可能光是等到视线不被别人挡住，就要花更长时间。

questions.en: What are the advantages of living in a neighbourhood where there are a lot of people?
questions.zh: 住在居民众多的街区有哪些好处？
questions.sample: A busy neighbourhood often has enough customers to support convenient shops, food stalls and frequent public transport. There's usually someone around if you need directions. For a person living alone, even a familiar face at the corner shop can feel reassuring.
questions.sampleZh: 热闹的社区里顾客多，往往养得起方便居民的小店和小吃摊，也有足够的乘客让公交车开得更勤。想问路时，身边通常就有人。对独居的人来说，哪怕只是在街角的小店看见一张熟悉的面孔，也会觉得安心。

questions.en: How important is it to have quiet areas in a crowded city?
questions.zh: 在一座拥挤的城市里，有安静的区域有多重要？
questions.sample: They're very important because a short break from traffic and crowds can change the feel of an entire day. A small park or quiet library gives people somewhere to read, think or sit with a friend without having to raise their voices.
questions.sampleZh: 这样的安静场所很重要，因为哪怕只是暂时远离车流和人群，一整天的感受都可能不一样。小公园或安静的图书馆让人有地方看书、想事情，或者和朋友坐一坐，说话也不用提高嗓门。

questions.en: Some people say it can be exciting to be in a crowded place. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，身处拥挤的地方也可能让人兴奋。你同意吗？
questions.sample: At a concert, yes. When a whole crowd sings the same line, even strangers feel like part of one group. A packed bus feels very different because everyone is just trying to get somewhere.
questions.sampleZh: 如果是在演唱会上，我同意。全场一起唱同一句歌词时，哪怕彼此不认识，也会觉得自己是这个集体的一员。挤公交车的感觉就很不一样，因为大家都只想着赶到目的地。

questions.en: Why might people move away from crowded cities at different stages of their lives?
questions.zh: 在人生的不同阶段，人们可能出于哪些原因搬离拥挤的城市？
questions.sample: A student may leave a big city after graduation because rent eats up most of a starting salary. Later on, parents might want more space for their children, while retired people may want a quieter neighbourhood.
questions.sampleZh: 学生毕业后可能会离开大城市，因为房租就要花掉大半起薪。到了有孩子的阶段，父母可能希望孩子有更大的活动空间，而退休后的人可能更想住在安静的社区。

questions.en: How has modern technology made it easier to live in isolated places?
questions.zh: 现代科技怎样让人们在偏远地区生活得更方便？
questions.sample: A good internet connection lets someone in a village work from home and order things the local shops don't sell. Video calls also make a difference when the nearest relative lives several hours away.
questions.sampleZh: 网络连接稳定，住在村里的人就能在家工作，也能买到当地商店不卖的东西。如果连住得最近的亲戚都在几小时车程之外，能打视频电话也会让生活很不一样。

questions.en: What could governments do to encourage people to live in less densely populated areas?
questions.zh: 政府可以做什么来鼓励人们住在人口密度较低的地方？
questions.sample: I would start with reliable buses, schools and places to work. Cheap housing might persuade a family to move, but they probably won't stay if their children have to travel an hour to school.
questions.sampleZh: 我会先从稳定的公交服务、上学的地方和工作机会做起。房价便宜或许能吸引一个家庭搬过去，但如果孩子上学单程就得花一小时，他们大概住不长久。

questions.en: Do you think that, in the future, cities might become unliveable after their population reaches a certain point?
questions.zh: 你觉得未来一座城市的人口达到一定规模后，会不会变得不再适合居住？
questions.sample: It could happen if housing and transport fail to keep up. I wouldn't put a number on it, though. A very large city with several good metro lines can feel easier to live in than a smaller one with constant traffic jams.
questions.sampleZh: 如果住房和交通跟不上人口增长，就有可能。但我觉得很难划出一个具体的人口数字。一座有好几条便捷地铁线路的大城市，住起来可能比一座总是堵车的小城市更轻松。

questions.en: Do you think it is a good trend to have more big cities?
questions.zh: 大城市越来越多，你觉得这是个好趋势吗？
questions.sample: Bigger cities can give people more choices, especially when they're looking for a first job. I think it's a good trend only if people on ordinary salaries can still afford to live reasonably close to work.
questions.sampleZh: 大城市能让人有更多选择，尤其是找第一份工作的时候。我觉得这个趋势有个前提，就是拿普通工资的人也能负担得起离上班地点不太远的住处。

questions.en: Do you think there are some people who enjoy crowded places?
questions.zh: 你觉得有些人喜欢人多拥挤的地方吗？
questions.sample: Yes, especially people who get energy from being around others. Someone who loves street food might enjoy a busy night market because there are different smells, people to watch and dishes to share.
questions.sampleZh: 有，尤其是那些和别人在一起就觉得有精神的人。喜欢街头小吃的人可能就爱逛热闹的夜市，因为那里闻得到各种食物的香味，能看看来往的人，还能和人分着尝几道菜。

questions.en: Why do people go to crowded places?
questions.zh: 为什么人们会去人多拥挤的地方？
questions.sample: Often the things people want are all in one place. A big market has plenty of choice and a stadium has the match they came to see, so they accept the crowd as part of the visit.
questions.sampleZh: 很多时候，人们想要的东西都集中在一个地方。大市场里选择多，体育场里又有他们专程来看的一场比赛，所以他们也就接受了人多是这次体验的一部分。

questions.en: Will people use bikes more or less in cities in the future?
questions.zh: 将来人们在城市里骑自行车会更频繁，还是更少？
questions.sample: I expect bikes to become more common for short trips, especially between home and the nearest metro station. If a city provides safe cycle lanes and somewhere to park, cycling can be quicker than waiting for a bus.
questions.sampleZh: 我估计短途出行时骑自行车的人会更多，尤其是从家到最近地铁站这一段。如果城市里有安全的自行车道，也有地方停车，骑车可能比等公交还快。

questions.en: Will there be more or less green space in cities in the future?
questions.zh: 未来城市里的绿地会变多还是变少？
questions.sample: It may go either way. A growing city needs land for homes, but it can still turn empty corners into small parks. I think several green spaces within walking distance matter more than one huge park far away.
questions.sampleZh: 两种情况都有可能。不断扩张的城市需要拿地来盖房子，但也能把空着的街角改成小公园。我觉得步行就能到的几块绿地，比很远的地方有一座特别大的公园更有用。

questions.en: Which cities are overcrowded in your country?
questions.zh: 在你的国家，哪些城市人多拥挤？
questions.sample: Guangzhou and Wuhan come to mind, especially around their main railway stations before a holiday. I'd describe those areas as overcrowded at peak times. A residential street in the same city can feel completely different once the morning rush is over.
questions.sampleZh: 我会想到广州和武汉，尤其是节假日前这些城市的大型火车站周围。我觉得那些地方在高峰时段算得上人满为患。不过早高峰一过，同一座城市里的居民街道可能完全是另一番景象。

questions.en: What types of special events do people celebrate in your culture?
questions.zh: 在你们的文化里，人们会庆祝哪些特别的事情？
questions.sample: In China, families often celebrate weddings, birthdays and the arrival of a baby. Getting into university can lead to a special meal too. Usually the most important part is gathering people who don't see each other often.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国，家庭常常会庆祝结婚、生日和新生儿出生。考上大学了，大家也可能专门吃一顿饭庆祝。通常最重要的，是把平时不常见面的人聚在一起。

questions.en: Some people say that parties with friends are more enjoyable than parties with family. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，和朋友聚会比和家人聚会更开心。你同意吗？
questions.sample: It depends on the occasion. At a party with friends, I can joke about something that happened yesterday and everyone understands. At a family birthday, hearing an old story about my grandparents can be just as enjoyable.
questions.sampleZh: 这得看是什么场合。和朋友聚会时，我可以拿昨天发生的事开玩笑，大家马上就懂。家人聚在一起过生日时，听他们讲爷爷奶奶从前的故事，也能让我觉得一样开心。

questions.en: Do you think it's important to have food at a party with friends?
questions.zh: 你觉得朋友聚会时准备食物重要吗？
questions.sample: I think so, although it can be very simple. Sharing some fruit or ordering a few dishes gives people time to settle in. Someone who feels shy can join the conversation by offering another person some food.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得挺重要的，但不一定要准备得多复杂。分点水果或者点几道菜，大家就有时间慢慢放松下来。害羞一点的人，也可以借着给别人递吃的，自然地加入谈话。

questions.en: Which do you think is a better place to have a party with friends: a public place or someone's home?
questions.zh: 你觉得朋友聚会选在公共场所好，还是在某个人家里好？
questions.sample: For a few close friends, I'd choose someone's home. We can pick our own music and talk without watching the clock. For a larger group, a restaurant is easier because nobody has to cook or clean afterwards.
questions.sampleZh: 如果只是几个好朋友，我会选在某个人家里。我们可以自己选音乐，也不用老看时间。人多的话，去餐厅更省事，因为谁都不用做饭，也不用在结束后收拾。

questions.en: How important are the clothes that people wear at celebrations?
questions.zh: 参加庆祝活动时，人们的穿着有多重要？
questions.sample: Clothes can show that you understand the occasion. I'd make more effort for a wedding than for a friend's birthday meal. Once people have arrived, though, how they treat the host matters much more than what they wear.
questions.sampleZh: 穿着能看出一个人懂不懂这个场合的分寸。参加婚礼时，我会比去朋友的生日饭局更花心思打扮。不过人到了以后，他们怎么对待主人，远比穿什么重要。

questions.en: Some people say that people should spend less money on celebrating special events and save the money instead. Do you think so?
questions.zh: 有人说，人们应该少花钱庆祝特别的日子，把钱存起来。你觉得呢？
questions.sample: If the bill will make next month difficult, I'd keep the celebration small. A homemade cake and a meal with close friends can still feel special. Spending more makes sense when someone can comfortably afford it.
questions.sampleZh: 如果这次庆祝的花销会让下个月的生活很紧张，我就会办得简单一点。自己做个蛋糕，约几个好朋友吃顿饭，一样可以很特别。手头宽裕的时候，多花一点也说得过去。

questions.en: Why do many countries have large celebrations for their national days?
questions.zh: 为什么许多国家会为国庆日举行大型庆祝活动？
questions.sample: National days give people a chance to remember an event they learned about in school and celebrate it together. A free concert or a light show also lets families take part without having to organise anything themselves.
questions.sampleZh: 国庆日让人们有机会一起纪念在学校里学过的历史事件。免费的音乐会或灯光秀，也能让普通家庭直接参加庆祝，不用自己张罗活动。

questions.en: Do you think workers should be paid during national day celebrations, even if the businesses they work for are closed?
questions.zh: 你觉得国庆庆祝期间，即使企业停业，员工也应该照常领工资吗？
questions.sample: Yes, I think workers should still be paid. They didn't choose to close the shop, and their rent is due whether it's open or not. A paid holiday also lets more families actually enjoy the celebration.
questions.sampleZh: 是的，我觉得员工在这期间也应该拿工资。关店并不是他们决定的，店开不开，他们的房租都照样要交。假期带薪，也能让更多家庭真正享受庆祝活动。

questions.en: Do you think that, in the future, having an 'international day' that all countries celebrate might create greater respect and understanding in the world?
questions.zh: 你觉得未来如果设立一个让所有国家共同庆祝的“国际日”，会让世界各地的人更加相互尊重和理解吗？
questions.sample: It might help if people shared something specific, such as family recipes or stories from their hometowns. Simply putting the same date on everyone's calendar would do little, but a conversation could change how two people see each other.
questions.sampleZh: 如果大家愿意分享具体的东西，比如家里的菜谱或者家乡的故事，这样的节日或许有帮助。单是在所有人的日历上标出同一天，作用不大，但一次真诚的交流可能改变两个人看待彼此的方式。

questions.en: When do people like to hold a party?
questions.zh: 人们喜欢在什么场合办聚会？
questions.sample: People often have a party when there's good news to share, like a graduation, a new job or a birthday. Friday evening is a popular choice because guests can stay a little longer without worrying about work the next morning.
questions.sampleZh: 有好消息想分享时，人们往往会办个聚会，比如毕业、找到新工作或过生日。周五晚上很受欢迎，因为客人不太需要担心第二天一早上班，可以多待一会儿。

questions.en: Do you think people nowadays prefer attending big parties or small gatherings with close friends? Why?
questions.zh: 现在人们更喜欢大型派对，还是和好友小聚？为什么？
questions.sample: My impression is that many people prefer a small gathering after a busy week. At a table for four, everyone gets a turn to talk. Big parties still make sense for weddings or important anniversaries.
questions.sampleZh: 我的感觉是，忙了一周以后，很多人更喜欢小范围聚聚。四个人围着一张桌子，每个人都有机会说话。遇到婚礼或重要的周年纪念日，办一场大聚会仍然很合适。

questions.en: Are there any differences between how young people and older people celebrate events with parties?
questions.zh: 年轻人和老年人办聚会庆祝事情的方式有什么不同？
questions.sample: Younger guests might enjoy a playlist, games or taking pictures together. Older relatives may prefer a long meal where they can hear each other clearly. At a family birthday, it's quite easy to have both.
questions.sampleZh: 年轻的客人可能喜欢自己选的音乐、玩游戏或一起拍照。年纪大些的亲戚可能更喜欢慢慢吃顿饭，彼此说话也能听得清楚。家人聚在一起过生日时，这两种安排完全可以兼顾。

questions.en: Do you think it's a waste of money for governments to celebrate national events?
questions.zh: 政府花钱庆祝国家大事，你觉得是浪费吗？
questions.sample: A free public celebration can be worth the money, especially if children and older people can attend. I'd question the cost if the whole budget went on a short fireworks show while local parks lacked basic facilities.
questions.sampleZh: 如果公共庆祝活动免费，孩子和年长者也能参加，我觉得这笔钱值得花。但如果全部预算都用来放一场短短的烟花，而社区公园连基本设施都缺，我就觉得这笔钱花得值得商量。

questions.en: What festivals are the most important for people in your country?
questions.zh: 哪些节日对你们国家的人最重要？
questions.sample: For many families, Spring Festival is the biggest one because relatives travel home for the reunion dinner. Mid-Autumn Festival matters too. Even people who live apart may send mooncakes and call each other that evening.
questions.sampleZh: 对很多家庭来说，春节是最重要的节日，因为亲人们会回家一起吃年夜饭。中秋节也很有意义。即使住在不同地方，人们也可能互相寄月饼，并在那天晚上打个电话。

questions.en: At what age should children start studying history at school?
questions.zh: 孩子应该从几岁开始在学校学历史？
questions.sample: I think children can begin around seven or eight with short stories and pictures. A lesson about what their grandparents used at school is easier to follow at that age than a list of dates and rulers.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得七八岁左右就可以开始，用小故事和图片来讲。对这个年龄的孩子来说，听老师讲爷爷奶奶上学时用过什么东西，比记一串年份和统治者的名字更容易理解。

questions.en: Why don't some students enjoy studying history?
questions.zh: 为什么有些学生不喜欢学历史？
questions.sample: Some lessons focus so much on remembering dates that students miss the people behind them. If a class starts with a letter from a child who lived at the time, the same period can suddenly feel real.
questions.sampleZh: 有些课太强调记年份，学生反而看不到那些年代里真实生活过的人。如果老师用当年一个孩子写的信开始这堂课，同一段历史一下子就会让人觉得很真切。

questions.en: Some people say that students should learn more about people's lives in the past, and not just important events. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，除了重大历史事件，学生还应该更多地了解过去人们的生活。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Yes. Knowing what a shopkeeper earned or what a family ate helps students understand why a major change mattered. Otherwise they may remember when an event happened without understanding what it changed for ordinary people.
questions.sampleZh: 同意。知道当时的店主能赚多少钱，或者普通人家每天吃什么，可以帮助学生理解一次重大变化对老百姓意味着什么。否则，他们也许记得事情发生的时间，却不明白它怎样改变了人们的生活。

questions.en: How much do most people know about ancient history?
questions.zh: 大多数人对古代历史了解多少？
questions.sample: Many people remember a few names, famous buildings and stories from school. Detailed knowledge is less common. For example, a person may recognise a piece of ancient pottery without knowing who used it or what it held.
questions.sampleZh: 很多人还记得上学时学过的几个名字、著名建筑和故事，但真正了解细节的就比较少了。比如一个人可能认得一件古代陶器，却说不出是谁在用、里面原来装过什么。

questions.en: Do tourists ever visit a country because of its ancient history?
questions.zh: 有些游客会因为一个国家有悠久的古代历史，就专门去那里旅行吗？
questions.sample: Definitely. Some visitors travel to Xi'an especially to see the Terracotta Warriors. Seeing the size of the figures and the differences between their faces offers something quite different from looking at a small picture in a textbook.
questions.sampleZh: 当然会。有些游客专门去西安看兵马俑。站在那里看到陶俑实际有多大、每一张脸又有什么不同，和只看课本上的一幅小图片，感受很不一样。

questions.en: Some people say that technology will make it easier to find out more about ancient history. Do you think so?
questions.zh: 有人说，科技会让人们更容易了解古代历史。你觉得呢？
questions.sample: Yes, because people can now examine old objects without always moving or damaging them. A clear digital picture of a faded letter, for instance, can be shared with several researchers who read it in different ways.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得会，因为现在人们往往不用移动或损伤文物，就能仔细研究它。比如把一封字迹已经褪色的信拍成清晰的数码照片，就能发给好几位研究者，让他们分别解读。

questions.en: How difficult might it be for historians to be sure about what happened in the past?
questions.zh: 历史学家要确切弄清过去发生了什么，可能有多难？
questions.sample: It can be very difficult because only part of the evidence survives, and two people can describe the same event differently. Historians have to compare letters, objects and records before deciding which explanation fits best.
questions.sampleZh: 有时非常难，因为能保存到今天的证据只是其中一部分，而两个人对同一件事的描述也可能不同。历史学家得把信件、实物和各种记录放在一起比较，再判断哪种解释最符合现有证据。

questions.en: Do you think using historians to advise on historical films might ensure that the films are completely accurate?
questions.zh: 你觉得聘请历史学家担任历史题材电影的顾问，就能保证影片完全符合史实吗？
questions.sample: Historians can help a film get the clothes, buildings and language right. Complete accuracy is harder. A director may combine two characters into one so the audience can follow a story in two hours.
questions.sampleZh: 历史学家可以帮助电影还原当时的服装、建筑和语言。要做到完全准确就难多了。为了让观众在两小时内能跟上故事，导演可能会把两个真实人物合成一个角色。

questions.en: What challenges might historians of the future face when researching the history of modern times? [e.g. data from social media]
questions.zh: 未来的历史学家研究我们这个时代时，可能会遇到哪些挑战？比如，他们该如何处理社交媒体上的数据？
questions.sample: There may be too much material rather than too little. A future historian might find thousands of posts about one event, but some could be jokes, copied stories or pictures with the wrong date attached.
questions.sampleZh: 他们面对的可能是材料太多，而不是太少。未来的历史学家也许能找到几千条讨论同一件事的帖子，但其中可能有玩笑、转发来的说法，还有标错日期的照片。

questions.en: Besides big historical events, what else is important when learning history?
questions.zh: 除了重大历史事件，学习历史时还有什么重要的？
questions.sample: I think everyday objects and local stories deserve attention. An old train ticket can start a good discussion about who could afford to travel, how long a journey took and what people packed for the trip.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得日常用品和当地人的故事也值得关注。一张旧火车票就能引出不少有意思的问题，比如当时谁坐得起火车、一趟旅程要花多久，还有人们出门都带些什么。

questions.en: Do you think people should learn ancient history before learning modern history?
questions.zh: 你认为人们应该先学古代史再学现代史吗？
questions.sample: Starting with ancient history gives events a clear order, but it isn't essential. Some students become interested through a modern issue, like how their city grew. They can then look backwards to understand where the changes began.
questions.sampleZh: 从古代史学起，事情先后顺序很清楚，但也不一定非得这样。有些学生是因为一个现代问题才对历史感兴趣，比如自己住的城市是怎样发展起来的。他们可以再往回追，看看变化是从哪里开始的。

questions.en: Is it important to learn how people in the past lived their lives?
questions.zh: 了解过去的人怎样生活重要吗？
questions.sample: Yes, it helps us understand changes that are easy to take for granted. Finding out how a family cooked before it had a fridge tells us something about shopping, daily work and the time needed to prepare dinner.
questions.sampleZh: 重要。这能帮助我们理解一些今天容易被当成理所当然的变化。比如，了解一家人在没有冰箱时怎么做饭，就能知道他们当时怎么买菜、每天要做哪些家务，以及准备一顿饭得花多少时间。

questions.en: How do children learn history before they attend school?
questions.zh: 孩子还没上学时是怎样了解历史的？
questions.sample: Young children often pick up history by asking what an unfamiliar object does. At a small museum, a child might turn the dial on an old telephone and ask how people called their friends. A conversation like that teaches a little everyday history.
questions.sampleZh: 小孩子往往是从问一件陌生的东西怎么用开始，慢慢了解历史的。在一家小博物馆里，孩子可能会转一转老式电话的拨号盘，问以前的人怎样给朋友打电话。这样聊几句，就能学到一点关于过去日常生活的知识。

questions.en: Do you think children should begin learning history from an early age?
questions.zh: 孩子应该从小开始学历史吗？
questions.sample: Yes, as long as it feels like discovering a story. Showing a child two pictures of the same street, taken years apart, can lead to more questions than asking them to memorise the name of a king.
questions.sampleZh: 应该，只要整个过程像是在发现一个故事。给孩子看看同一条街相隔许多年拍的两张照片，可能比让他们背一位国王的名字，更容易引出他们自己的问题。

questions.en: What are the differences between young people's leisure time activities and those of old people?
questions.zh: 年轻人和老年人平时的休闲活动有什么不同？
questions.focusWording: Do younger and older people do the same things to relax?
questions.sample: Some activities overlap, like walking in the park or watching a comedy. Younger people may also play online games with friends, while older neighbours might prefer playing cards together. Having time and company matters as much as age.
questions.sampleZh: 有些活动是一样的，比如在公园散步或者看喜剧。年轻人也可能和朋友一起打网络游戏，而年长的邻居可能更喜欢聚在一起打牌。有没有空、有没有人作伴，有时和年龄一样重要。

questions.en: What activities can families do together to build good relationships?
questions.zh: 家人可以一起做哪些活动来增进感情？
questions.focusWording: What do families usually do to strengthen their relationships?
questions.sample: Cooking a meal together works well because everyone can do something, even a child washing vegetables. People tend to talk more naturally while their hands are busy, and sitting down to eat gives the family a shared result.
questions.sampleZh: 一起做顿饭就很好，因为每个人都能帮上点忙，连小孩子也能洗洗菜。手上有事做时，大家往往更容易自然地聊起来。最后坐下一起吃饭，也能共享一起劳动的成果。

questions.en: Should people spend more time with their family than with their friends?
questions.zh: 人们陪家人的时间应该比陪朋友的时间多吗？
questions.focusWording: Should people spend more time with family than with their friends?
questions.sample: I wouldn't set a fixed rule. A parent who's been away all week may want a quiet evening with family. Someone who has just moved to a new city may need time with friends to feel settled.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得不用规定一个固定比例。一位离家工作了一周的父亲或母亲，可能想和家人安安静静地过个晚上。刚搬到新城市的人，则可能更需要和朋友待一待，好让自己在新地方安顿下来。

questions.en: What do people in your country like to do in the evening with their friends?
questions.zh: 在你的国家，人们晚上喜欢和朋友一起做什么？
questions.sample: In China, some friends meet for badminton or go out for karaoke in the evening. Booking a court after work is handy because everyone knows when and where to meet. Afterwards, people can stay for a drink if they've got time.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国，有的朋友晚上会约着打羽毛球，或者去唱歌。下班后订个球场很方便，大家都知道几点在哪里碰面。打完球，如果还有时间，也可以留下来喝点东西。

questions.en: Do young people do the same types of activity with their friends as older people do?
questions.zh: 年轻人和朋友一起做的活动，与老年人和朋友一起做的活动一样吗？
questions.sample: They share plenty of activities, particularly eating together and taking a walk. The difference may be in the timing. A group of students might meet for a late film, while retired friends could arrange the same outing in the afternoon.
questions.sampleZh: 有不少活动是共同的，特别是一起吃饭、散步。区别可能只是在时间上。一群学生可能会约着去看晚场电影，退休的朋友则可能把同样的活动安排在下午。

questions.en: Some people say that most people prefer to spend their free time with their friends rather than with their family. Do you think so?
