questions.zh: 有人说，大多数人有空时更喜欢和朋友待在一起，而非和家人待在一起。你觉得呢？
questions.sample: That varies with the person and the week. Teenagers may choose friends because they share the same school worries. Someone who works far from home might use every free weekend to have dinner with their parents.
questions.sampleZh: 这要看是什么人，也要看那一周的情况。十几岁的孩子可能会选朋友，因为大家都在担心类似的学校问题。在外地工作的人，则可能会利用每一个有空的周末回去和父母吃饭。

questions.en: How important is it for people to spend time with their extended family? [e.g. cousins]
questions.zh: 花时间和堂表亲等大家庭成员相处，有多重要？
questions.sample: It can be valuable because cousins and older relatives often know parts of the family story you haven't heard. Even an occasional visit can give you someone to call for advice when your parents are busy.
questions.sampleZh: 这可能很有意义，因为表亲和家里的长辈往往知道一些你从没听过的家族往事。哪怕只是偶尔去拜访，也能让你在父母忙的时候，多一个可以打电话请教的人。

questions.en: What impact does today's lifestyle have on how much time families spend together?
questions.zh: 如今的生活方式对一家人相处的时间长短有什么影响？
questions.sample: Long working hours and commuting can turn an evening together into a quick meal before bed. On the other hand, a family group chat lets relatives keep in touch during the day, even if they're in different cities.
questions.sampleZh: 工作时间长，通勤又耗时，原本可以和家人共度的一个晚上，可能只剩下睡前匆匆吃顿饭。不过，家庭群聊也能让大家白天随时联系，哪怕亲人们住在不同的城市。

questions.en: Do you think technology brings people together more than it keeps them apart?
questions.zh: 你觉得科技拉近人们距离的作用，大于它让人们疏远的作用吗？
questions.sample: Overall, I'd say it brings people closer when distance is a real problem. A video call lets grandparents watch a child open a present. At the dinner table, though, a phone can easily take attention away from the person beside you.
questions.sampleZh: 总体来说，当距离确实是个问题时，我觉得科技让人更亲近。通过视频电话，爷爷奶奶也能看着孩子拆礼物。但到了饭桌上，手机也很容易把人们的注意力从坐在旁边的人身上移走。

questions.en: Some people say that governments should spend money on large public events to bring people together. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，政府应该花钱举办大型公共活动，让人们聚在一起。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Yes, when the event is open to ordinary residents and easy to reach. A local sports day can bring neighbours onto the same team. I'd spend less on an expensive ceremony that people can only watch from a distance.
questions.sampleZh: 我同意，前提是活动向普通居民开放，而且去参加也方便。一次社区运动会，就能让邻居成为队友。至于那种耗资很大、大家只能远远看着的仪式，我觉得可以少花些钱。

questions.en: Do you think it's becoming increasingly important to encourage a sense of community in today's world?
questions.zh: 你觉得在当今世界，培养人们对社区的归属感是不是越来越重要了？
questions.sample: I think it is, particularly in cities where people often move for work. If neighbours know each other's names, asking someone to collect a parcel or check on an older resident becomes a much smaller step.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得是，尤其是在那些人们经常为了工作搬来搬去的城市里。如果邻居们连彼此的名字都叫得出来，请人代收一个包裹，或者去看看一位年长的居民，就容易开口多了。

questions.en: Why do people need friends?
questions.zh: 人们为什么需要朋友？
questions.sample: A friend gives you someone who understands your everyday life and can listen without immediately trying to solve everything. On a difficult day, even a short walk and an honest conversation can change how the evening feels.
questions.sampleZh: 朋友了解你的日常生活，也愿意听你说话，不会一听就急着替你把所有问题都解决。遇到不顺心的一天，哪怕只是一起走一小段路，坦诚地聊一聊，整个晚上的心情都可能不一样。

questions.en: Do older people prefer spending time with family or with friends?
questions.zh: 老年人更喜欢和家人还是朋友共度时光？
questions.sample: I think many older people enjoy both for different reasons. Being with family gives them time with grandchildren. Meeting an old friend lets them talk about memories and interests their younger relatives may not share.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得很多年长者都喜欢，只是原因不同。和家人在一起，他们可以多陪陪孙辈。和老朋友见面，则能聊一聊年轻亲戚未必了解的回忆和兴趣。

questions.en: Do young people prefer spending time with family or with friends?
questions.zh: 年轻人更喜欢和家人还是朋友共度时光？
questions.sample: Many young people choose friends for day-to-day activities because they're at a similar stage of life. They can discuss exams or work without explaining all the background. Important festivals are often when they make more time for family.
questions.sampleZh: 很多年轻人平时会选择和朋友一起活动，因为彼此正处在人生相似的阶段。他们讨论考试或工作时，不用先解释一大堆背景。遇到重要节日，他们往往会多留些时间给家人。

questions.en: How do people get along in a big family?
questions.zh: 人们在一个大家庭里是怎样相处的？
questions.sample: It helps if people agree about small things, like who cooks and when everyone needs quiet. In a big family, a misunderstanding over the bathroom can grow quickly. Talking about routines early saves a lot of arguments.
questions.sampleZh: 大家先在小事上商量好会有帮助，比如谁做饭、什么时候需要保持安静。大家庭里，连谁先用卫生间这样的小误会都可能越闹越大。提前聊清楚生活习惯，能少很多争执。

questions.en: Some people say that protecting a country's environment is more important than building a country's economy. Do you think so?
questions.zh: 有人认为，对一个国家来说，保护环境比发展经济更重要。你同意吗？
questions.sample: When growth would cause lasting damage, I'd put the environment first. A factory may create jobs, but families also need clean water. Helping the factory produce less waste could protect both the river and those jobs.
questions.sampleZh: 如果经济增长会给环境留下长期的损害，我会优先考虑环境。工厂可以创造就业机会，可附近的家庭也需要干净的水。如果能帮助工厂减少废物，就可能既保护河流，也保住那些工作岗位。

questions.en: Do people's feelings change when they spend time in nature?
questions.zh: 在大自然中待一会儿会改变人的心情吗？
questions.sample: Often they do. After a morning of screens and traffic, people may feel calmer when they hear birds or walk by water. The change of pace gives them a chance to think about something other than the next task.
questions.sampleZh: 常常会。花了一上午盯屏幕、穿梭在车流里之后，听到鸟叫或沿着水边走走，人可能会平静下来。节奏慢一点，就有机会想想眼前下一项任务以外的事。

questions.en: Some people say that every city should have places where people can easily spend time in nature. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，每座城市都应该有方便人们亲近自然的地方。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Yes, and the space should be easy to reach on foot. A small park near a block of flats gives children somewhere to play and older residents somewhere to sit, even when nobody has time for a long outing.
questions.sampleZh: 应该，而且这样的地方最好走路就能到。住宅楼附近有个小公园，孩子们就有地方玩，年长的居民也有地方坐。哪怕大家都没空专门出一趟远门，也能用得上。

questions.en: What kinds of places do people go to, to spend time in nature?
questions.zh: 人们会去什么样的地方亲近自然？
questions.sample: City residents often choose riverside paths and public parks because they can get there after work. At weekends they may travel a little farther to a forest, a lake or a hill with a walking trail.
questions.sampleZh: 城市居民常去河边的步道和公共公园，因为下班后就能到。周末时间多一些，他们可能会去稍远的森林、湖边，或者找一座有徒步小径的小山。

questions.en: Do you think people nowadays spend enough time in nature?
questions.zh: 你觉得现在人们亲近大自然的时间够吗？
questions.sample: Some do, especially if a green space is on their route to work. Many others spend weekdays indoors and go straight home afterwards. For them, a short walk at lunchtime may be the easiest chance to get outside.
variants: Do you think people should spend more time in nature?
questions.sampleZh: 有些人花在户外的时间够多，尤其是上班路上就有绿地的人。也有很多人工作日一直待在室内，下班又直接回家。对他们来说，午休时走一小圈可能是最容易抓住的户外时间。

questions.en: Do you think spending time in nature makes people care more about plants and animals?
questions.zh: 你觉得花时间亲近大自然，会让人更关心动植物吗？
questions.sample: It can. A child who watches a bird build a nest may understand why cutting down that tree matters. Reading a rule about protecting wildlife is easier to forget when the animals feel distant and unfamiliar.
questions.sampleZh: 会有这种作用。亲眼看过小鸟在树上筑巢的孩子，可能更明白为什么砍掉那棵树会有影响。如果动物始终显得遥远又陌生，读到过的野生动物保护规定也更容易忘记。

questions.en: If people do not spend time in nature, how might that affect people's health and wellbeing?
questions.zh: 如果人们平时不接触大自然，健康和幸福感可能会受到什么影响？
questions.sample: They might miss an easy reason to move around or take a break from screens. You can relax indoors too, of course. A nearby green space simply makes it easier to fit a pleasant walk into an ordinary day.
questions.sampleZh: 他们可能会少了一个很自然的理由，起来活动一下，或者让眼睛离开屏幕一会儿。当然，在室内也能放松。只不过附近有一块绿地的话，在平常的一天里安排一次令人愉快的散步就容易多了。

questions.en: Is restricting public access the best way to protect the natural environment?
questions.zh: 限制公众进入自然区域，是保护自然环境的最好办法吗？
questions.sample: Sometimes it is necessary, especially during a nesting season or when a path is badly damaged. In other places, marked trails and clear signs can protect wildlife while still letting visitors see what they're being asked to protect.
questions.sampleZh: 有时候确实有必要，比如鸟类正在筑巢，或者一条小径已经严重受损的时候。在其他地方，标出游览路线、把提示牌写清楚，也能保护野生动植物，同时让游客亲眼看看自己要保护的究竟是什么。

questions.en: Do you think advances in science and technology might be able to reverse the existing damage to the environment?
questions.zh: 你觉得科学技术的进步有可能逆转已经造成的环境破坏吗？
questions.sample: Technology could help with some damage, for example by finding polluted areas and helping people clean up a river. Other losses are much harder to undo. Once a species disappears, a new machine can't simply bring it back.
questions.sampleZh: 技术可能帮助修复一部分损害，比如配合人们找到受污染的区域，再清理一条河流。另一些损失就很难挽回。一个物种一旦消失，并不能靠一台新机器轻易让它重现。

questions.en: What can governments do to encourage people to spend more time in nature?
questions.zh: 政府可以怎样鼓励人们多花些时间亲近自然？
questions.sample: They could improve ordinary parks first, with safe paths, public toilets and benches in the shade. A cheap bus to a country park would also give families without a car somewhere new to go at the weekend.
questions.sampleZh: 政府可以先把大家日常去的公园打理好，修安全的小路，设置公共厕所，在树荫下放些长椅。再开通一趟开往郊野公园、票价便宜的公交车，没有汽车的家庭周末也就多了一个新的去处。

questions.en: What kind of people do you think enjoy being in nature?
questions.zh: 哪些人会特别喜欢待在大自然里？
questions.sample: People who like a slower pace often enjoy it, but nature attracts very different groups. A runner may want a long trail, a photographer may look for birds, and a tired office worker may just want a quiet bench.
questions.sampleZh: 喜欢慢节奏的人常常很享受待在大自然里，但大自然吸引的人其实各不相同。跑步的人可能想找一条长步道，摄影爱好者可能在寻鸟，而累了一天的上班族也许只想找一张安静的长椅。

questions.en: What problems happen when many people travel to work at the same time?
questions.zh: 许多人同时出门上班时会出现哪些问题？
questions.sample: Roads fill up, buses move more slowly and passengers may have to wait for the next train. Even a small delay can spread because so many people need the same station or junction at almost the same time.
questions.sampleZh: 道路变得拥挤，公交车开得更慢，乘客还可能要等下一班地铁。因为那么多人差不多同时要经过同一座车站或同一个路口，哪怕一处只有小小的延误，也可能影响到其他地方。

questions.en: What are the benefits of taking holidays in another country?
questions.zh: 去国外度假有哪些好处？
questions.sample: A holiday abroad can teach you how people handle ordinary things, from ordering lunch to greeting a stranger. Those small experiences often make a bigger impression than a famous building, and they give you stories to share afterwards.
questions.sampleZh: 去国外度假，可以让人了解当地人怎样处理普通的小事，从点午饭到跟陌生人打招呼都有。这些小经历往往比一座著名建筑更令人印象深刻，回来后也多了些可以跟人分享的故事。

questions.en: Why do people need to travel to other countries?
questions.zh: 人们为什么需要去其他国家旅行？
questions.sample: There are practical reasons as well as holidays. Someone might study a subject that's taught abroad, visit family or meet colleagues in person. A short visit can also clear up misunderstandings that are difficult to explain by email.
questions.sampleZh: 除了度假，还有一些很实际的原因。有的人去国外学一门在那里开设的课程，探望家人，或者和同事当面交流。一次短暂的见面，有时也能说清那些在邮件里很难解释的误会。

questions.en: What are common ways of travelling to work in your country?
questions.zh: 在你的国家，人们通常怎样通勤？
questions.sample: In large Chinese cities, many people take the metro or a bus, and some ride an electric bike for the last part. In smaller towns, a bicycle or a short walk may be enough to get to work.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国的大城市里，很多人坐地铁或公交，还有人会骑电动车走完最后一段路。在小城镇，骑一段自行车，或者步行一小会儿，可能就能到上班的地方。

questions.en: Why do more people travel longer distances to work now than in the past?
questions.zh: 为什么现在比过去有更多人要长距离通勤？
questions.sample: Jobs and reasonably priced homes aren't always in the same area. Someone might work in the city centre but rent farther out. A new train line can make that distance manageable, even though the journey is still long.
questions.sampleZh: 工作机会和租金负担得起的住房，并不总在同一片区域。有些人可能在市中心工作，却住在更远的地方。新开通的一条轨道交通线路可以让这段路变得能接受，虽然通勤距离还是很长。

questions.en: Is travelling to another country different from just reading about it?
questions.zh: 亲自去另一个国家旅行，和只从书面材料中了解它，有什么不同吗？
questions.sample: Yes. A book can explain the history of a market, but it can't fully show how it sounds at breakfast time. Travelling also forces you to make choices, like asking for directions when you take the wrong bus.
questions.sampleZh: 不一样。书能解释一座市场的历史，却很难让你真正听到那里早餐时的热闹声音。旅行时你还得自己做决定，比如坐错了公交车以后，要开口问别人怎么走。

questions.en: Some people say that to protect the environment, people will have to travel less. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，为了保护环境，人们将不得不减少出游。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Some trips could be avoided, especially short business visits that work just as well online. I think how people travel matters too. Choosing a train for a nearby city is another way to reduce the impact.
questions.sampleZh: 有些出行确实可以省掉，尤其是那些在线上就能办妥的短期出差。我觉得出行方式也很重要。去附近城市时选择坐火车，也是一种减轻环境影响的办法。

questions.en: What steps could be taken to reduce the environmental impact of international travel?
questions.zh: 可以采取哪些措施来减少国际旅行对环境的影响？
questions.sample: For busy routes, better rail links could give people a real alternative to a short flight. Travellers could also stay longer in one place instead of flying between several cities in the same week.
questions.sampleZh: 在客流量大的线路上，改善铁路连接，可以让大家在短途飞机之外有切实可行的选择。旅行者也可以在一个地方多待几天，而不必在同一周里坐飞机辗转好几座城市。

questions.en: How could space tourism affect the environment?
questions.zh: 太空旅游可能怎样影响环境？
questions.sample: Rocket launches use a great deal of fuel, and more launches could mean more pollution and noise near launch sites. Since the experience is mainly for a few visitors, I'd want its wider costs looked at carefully.
questions.sampleZh: 火箭发射要消耗大量燃料，发射次数增加，也可能让发射场附近的污染和噪声变得更严重。由于主要是少数游客能够享受这种体验，我希望人们能仔细考虑它对更多人和环境造成的代价。

questions.en: Which is better for knowing more about a country? Travelling or reading books about it?
questions.zh: 要深入了解一个国家，亲自去旅行和读介绍它的书，哪种方式更好？
questions.sample: I'd choose travel for getting to know daily life because you can talk to people and notice things you didn't expect. Books are better for background. Reading a little before a trip makes the places you see more meaningful.
questions.sampleZh: 如果是想了解日常生活，我会选旅行，因为你能跟当地人聊天，也会留意到一些意料之外的事情。了解背景知识时，书更有优势。出发前读一点，能让亲眼看见的那些地方更有意义。

questions.en: How much time do you think people should spend on a trip abroad?
questions.zh: 你觉得一次出国旅行多长时间比较合适？
questions.sample: A week or two seems reasonable if it's a first visit. It gives you time to find your way around and spend an ordinary day somewhere. A shorter trip can still be lovely if you focus on one city.
questions.sampleZh: 如果是第一次去，我觉得一两周比较合适。这段时间足够你熟悉路线，也能在某个地方过上普普通通的一天。如果只专心游览一座城市，时间再短一点也照样可以很愉快。

questions.en: Who prefers travelling abroad? The young or the old?
questions.zh: 年轻人和老年人，谁更喜欢出国旅行？
questions.sample: Younger people may be more willing to plan an unfamiliar trip on their own, while retired people may have more time for a long holiday. In the end, money, health and family plans probably matter more than age.
questions.sampleZh: 年轻人可能更愿意自己安排一趟去陌生地方的旅行，而退休的人也许有更多时间度长假。说到底，能花多少钱、身体怎么样、家里有什么安排，可能都比年龄更重要。

questions.en: Do Chinese people like travelling abroad?
questions.zh: 中国人喜欢出国旅行吗？
questions.sample: Many do, especially when they want to try different food or see a place they've heard about for years. Others choose trips within China because planning is simpler and they can still find very different scenery.
questions.sampleZh: 很多人喜欢，尤其是想尝尝不同的食物，或者亲眼看看一个听说了很多年的地方时。也有人选在中国境内旅行，因为更容易安排，而且一样可以看到差别很大的风景。

questions.en: Why do tourists often take a lot of photos?
questions.zh: 为什么游客常常会拍很多照片？
questions.sample: Photos help tourists remember small details that fade quickly, like the name of a street or something funny a friend did. They're also a simple way to show family members what a place actually looked like.
questions.sampleZh: 照片能帮游客记住那些很快会忘的小细节，比如一条街的名字，或朋友做过的一件有趣的事。想让家里人看看某个地方究竟是什么样子，照片也是最简单的方法之一。

questions.en: What things do people often take photos of in their daily lives?
questions.zh: 人们在日常生活中经常拍些什么？
questions.sample: Meals, pets and friends turn up in lots of everyday pictures. People also photograph useful things. A picture of a bus timetable or the floor where you parked can save a surprising amount of time later.
variants: What kind of photos do people often take?
questions.sampleZh: 许多日常照片拍的都是饭菜、宠物和朋友。人们还会拍一些有实际用处的东西。拍下公交时刻表或自己停车的楼层，之后往往能省下意想不到的时间。

questions.en: Why do many people like to share their photos of daily life online?
questions.zh: 为什么很多人喜欢在网上分享自己的日常照片？
questions.sample: It's a quick way to include people who aren't there. A student living away from home might post a picture of dinner, and a parent can reply with a joke or a suggestion for tomorrow's meal.
questions.sampleZh: 这能很快让没在现场的人也参与到你的生活里。比如一个离家读书的学生发一张晚饭的照片，父母就能在下面开句玩笑，或者给孩子出主意，说说明天可以吃什么。

questions.en: Some people take photos of things that are not very interesting. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人觉得，有些人拍的东西其实没什么意思。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Yes, a picture of a cup of tea may look ordinary to a stranger. The person who took it might remember an important conversation at that table, though. A photo can have a private meaning that viewers don't see.
questions.sampleZh: 同意。一杯茶的照片在陌生人眼里可能很平常，但拍照的人也许记得，自己曾在那张桌子旁有过一次重要的谈话。照片有时有很私人的意义，旁人看不出来。

questions.en: Do you think tourists should be allowed to take photos everywhere they go?
questions.zh: 你觉得游客应该可以在他们去的任何地方拍照吗？
questions.sample: I don't think so. Visitors should respect a place that asks for quiet or privacy, such as a hospital ward or a religious ceremony. If a particular person is the main subject, asking first is a simple courtesy.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得不应该。游客应该尊重那些需要安静或保护隐私的场合，比如医院病房或宗教仪式。如果打算让某个人成为照片的主角，拍之前先问一声是基本的礼貌。

questions.en: Do tourists spend so much time taking photos that they don't enjoy their experiences?
questions.zh: 游客会不会花太多时间拍照，以至于没能好好享受旅行本身？
questions.sample: Some do, especially when they take the same picture again and again. Taking one or two photos can help you notice details. After that, putting the phone away gives you a chance to enjoy the view itself.
questions.sampleZh: 有些人确实会，尤其是反反复复拍同一个画面的时候。拍一两张照片可以帮你留意到更多细节。拍完就把手机收起来，才能有机会好好欣赏眼前的风景。

questions.en: To what extent can people be sure that what they see in a photo is real?
questions.zh: 人们能在多大程度上确定照片里的内容是真实的？
questions.sample: A photo can show that something was there, but it rarely gives the whole story. Cutting out the edge of a picture can make a small crowd look huge. I'd check who took it and whether other pictures agree.
questions.sampleZh: 照片可以证明某个东西出现在那里，但往往说不清事情的全貌。只要裁掉画面边缘，就可以让一小群人看起来像是一大群。我会看是谁拍的，也会看看其他照片是否呈现了相同的情况。

questions.en: Some people say there should be stricter rules about which photos can be shown in the news. Do you think so?
questions.zh: 有人说，哪些照片可以刊登在新闻里，应该有更严格的规定。你觉得呢？
questions.sample: I'd support clearer rules about privacy and misleading edits. A news photo can inform people without showing an injured person's face. If an editor has changed something important in the image, readers should be told clearly.
questions.sampleZh: 我支持把保护隐私和防止误导性修图的规定说得更清楚。新闻照片即使不露出伤者的脸，也能让公众了解事情经过。如果编辑改动了画面中的重要内容，就应该明确告诉读者。

questions.en: Do you think a single photo might have the power to change society's views?
questions.zh: 你觉得一张照片就有可能改变社会大众的看法吗？
questions.sample: Yes, especially if it makes a distant problem feel personal. A picture of one family carrying their belongings through a flood may stay in people's minds longer than a page of figures and lead them to ask questions.
questions.sampleZh: 可以，尤其是当一张照片让遥远的问题变得和人切身相关时。一张全家人拿着财物穿过洪水的照片，可能比一整页统计数字更让人难忘，也更能促使大家追问发生了什么。

questions.en: Some people don't mind others walking into their shot when they're taking photos. What do you think about this?
questions.zh: 有些人拍照时并不介意别人走进镜头。你怎么看？
questions.sample: On a busy street, I think it's fair enough. Other people have to get where they're going, and a passer-by can even make a photo feel more natural. For a family portrait, I'd wait for a quieter moment.
questions.sampleZh: 如果是在繁忙的街道上，我觉得路人走进镜头也很正常。别人也需要赶路，而且有时正是经过的行人让照片看起来更自然。如果要拍家庭合照，我就等人少一点再拍。

questions.en: Do you think it's ok to take photos everywhere?
questions.zh: 你觉得在任何地方都可以拍照吗？
questions.sample: No. There's a difference between taking a landscape photo and pointing a camera at someone having a private moment. In places like changing rooms, people should be able to go about their day without being photographed.
questions.sampleZh: 不是到处都可以。拍一张风景照，和把镜头对准一个正在经历私人时刻的人，是两回事。比如在更衣室，人们理应能安心做自己的事，不用担心被拍。

questions.en: Why are some people keen on taking photos?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人特别喜欢拍照？
questions.sample: For some people, photography is a way of noticing details. Waiting for the light to change on a building makes an ordinary street feel interesting. Others mainly enjoy keeping a record they can look back on with friends.
questions.sampleZh: 对一些人来说，摄影是一种观察细节的方式。等着一栋楼上的光线发生变化，会让原本普通的街道变得有意思。还有些人主要是想留个记录，以后可以和朋友一起回顾。

questions.en: When do people like taking photos?
questions.zh: 人们喜欢在什么时候拍照？
questions.sample: People reach for a camera at weddings, graduations and family reunions because the group may not meet again soon. They also take pictures on ordinary days when they notice an unusual sky or a meal they've cooked well.
questions.sampleZh: 遇到婚礼、毕业或家庭团聚，人们往往会拿起相机，因为这一群人可能短时间内不会再聚齐。平常日子里，要是看到特别的天空，或者自己把一道菜做得很成功，他们也会拍照。

questions.en: What things make people feel stressed in everyday life?
questions.zh: 日常生活中的哪些事情会让人觉得有压力？
questions.sample: Tight deadlines, noisy surroundings and unexpected costs can all put people under pressure. Sometimes several small problems arrive together. Missing a bus feels much worse when you're already late and still thinking about a bill.
questions.sampleZh: 紧迫的截止日期、嘈杂的环境和计划外的开销，都会让人有压力。有时是好几件小麻烦一下子凑到了一起。比如，你本来就迟到了，还一直惦记着一张账单，这时再错过公交车，感觉会糟得多。

questions.en: How important is it to have a daily routine?
questions.zh: 有规律的日常作息有多重要？
questions.sample: A routine is useful because it saves you from making the same small decisions every morning. Packing your bag the night before, for instance, makes leaving home easier. There should still be room for something unexpected.
questions.sampleZh: 有规律的日常安排很有用，因为你不必每天早上都重新做同样的琐碎决定。比如前一天晚上收好包，第二天出门就会轻松些。不过，日程里还是应该给突发情况留点余地。

questions.en: Some people say that a certain amount of stress can be beneficial. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，一定程度的压力对人有好处。你同意吗？
questions.sample: A little pressure can get someone started. Knowing a presentation is due on Friday may encourage a team to practise on Wednesday. If the pressure continues for weeks without a break, though, it becomes much less useful.
questions.sampleZh: 一点压力能促使人开始行动。比如，知道周五要做汇报，一个团队可能周三就开始排练了。但如果压力一连持续好几周，中间又没有休息，它能带来的好处就小得多了。

questions.en: What types of activities do people have to do every day?
questions.zh: 人们每天都必须做哪些事情？
questions.sample: Most people have to wash, eat and keep their living space reasonably tidy. Work or study adds another set of tasks, like checking messages. Even on a free day, something simple usually needs doing at home.
questions.sampleZh: 多数人每天都要洗漱、吃饭，把自己住的地方收拾得大致整洁。工作和学习还会带来另一批任务，比如查看消息。即使到了休息日，家里通常也总有一两件小事需要做。

questions.en: How can people make routine activities less boring? [e.g. cleaning, ironing]
questions.zh: 怎样能让打扫、熨衣服这类例行事务不那么无聊？
questions.sample: I like the idea of pairing a dull job with something enjoyable. You can put on a short podcast while folding clothes, or cook with a housemate. The job still gets done, but it takes up less of your attention.
questions.sampleZh: 我喜欢把无聊的活儿和自己喜欢的事凑在一起。比如，叠衣服的时候听一期短播客，或者和室友一起做饭。事情一样能做完，却不用把注意力全放在那件琐事上。

questions.en: What would make people feel less stressed - having more time or more money?
questions.zh: 更多的时间和更多的钱，哪一样更能缓解人的压力？
questions.sample: It depends on what's causing the stress. Extra money helps if someone is worried about rent. A person who earns enough but works every evening might benefit much more from one free afternoon with their family.
questions.sampleZh: 得看压力是从哪里来的。如果有人在为房租发愁，多一点钱会有帮助。而对于一个收入足够、却每天晚上都得工作的人来说，腾出一个下午陪陪家人，可能更有用。

questions.en: How easy is it to achieve a balanced lifestyle?
questions.zh: 想让生活的各个方面保持平衡，容易吗？
questions.sample: It can be difficult when your timetable changes without warning. Someone who can finish work at a regular time has more choice about cooking or exercising. I think a flexible plan is easier to keep than a perfect one.
questions.sampleZh: 如果时间表常常突然变动，想过得平衡就挺难。一个能按时下班的人，更能自己决定是做饭还是运动。我觉得，一个可以灵活调整的计划，比一个看似完美的计划更容易坚持。

questions.en: Some people say that many people might have the wrong priorities in life. Do you think so?
questions.zh: 有人说，很多人可能没有分清生活中什么更重要。你觉得呢？
questions.sample: Sometimes people put so much effort into earning a little more that they miss the things they wanted the money for. Still, priorities depend on circumstances. Paying the rent first makes complete sense if money is tight.
questions.sampleZh: 有时候，人们一心想多赚一点，却错过了自己当初想挣钱去做的事。不过，每个人的轻重缓急要看所处的情况。如果手头紧，先顾着交房租完全说得通。

questions.en: Some people say it's impossible to achieve a balanced lifestyle, so there's no point in trying. What do you think?
questions.zh: 有人说，既然不可能让生活的各个方面都保持平衡，就没必要去尝试。你怎么看？
questions.sample: I don't agree. Even if a perfect balance is impossible, a small change can improve a week. Finishing one evening on time to see a friend is worthwhile even during a busy month.
questions.sampleZh: 我不同意。即使无法达到完美的平衡，小小的调整也能让一周过得更好。哪怕这个月很忙，有一个晚上能按时收工去见朋友，也是值得的。

questions.en: Why do some people refuse to abide by rules?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人不愿意遵守规则？
questions.sample: Some people don't understand what a rule is meant to achieve, while others think following it will cost them time. Someone may skip a queue when they're late. A clear explanation and fair treatment can reduce that attitude.
questions.sampleZh: 有些人不明白制定一条规则究竟是为了什么，也有人觉得遵守它会浪费时间。比如，有人迟到了，就可能去插队。讲清楚原因、对大家一视同仁，有助于减少这种心态。

questions.en: Will you continue doing something when you are aware that it's a waste of time?
questions.zh: 如果你知道做某件事很浪费时间，你还会继续做吗？
questions.sample: Sometimes I do, especially if I'm watching short videos and the next one looks interesting. Once I notice, I try to finish the current video and put my phone down. A clear stopping point usually helps.
questions.sampleZh: 有时还是会，尤其是我正在刷短视频，下一个看起来又挺有意思的时候。一旦意识到这一点，我就尽量看完当前这条，把手机放下。给自己定一个明确的停止点，一般有帮助。

questions.en: How do you balance life and work?
questions.zh: 你怎样平衡生活和工作？
questions.sample: I pick a finishing time before I start work and write down tomorrow's first task before I log off. If a friend asks me out for a walk after that, I can go without spending the whole evening wondering whether I've forgotten something.
questions.sampleZh: 我会在开工前先定好几点收工，关电脑前再写下明天要做的第一件事。这样，要是之后有朋友约我去散步，我就能放心出门，不用一整个晚上都在想自己是不是忘了什么。

questions.en: Do you think stress is important in people's lives?
questions.zh: 你觉得压力在人们的生活中起着重要作用吗？
questions.sample: A small amount can tell people that something needs their attention, like an approaching exam. I don't think everyone needs to feel stressed to do good work, though. Curiosity and clear goals can motivate people as well.
questions.sampleZh: 少许压力能提醒人们，有件事该重视了，比如一场快要到来的考试。不过，我不觉得每个人都非得有压力才能把事情做好。好奇心和清楚的目标同样可以给人动力。

questions.en: What are young people interested in talking to each other about?
questions.zh: 年轻人在一起时喜欢聊些什么？
questions.sample: Young people often talk about things happening right now, like a difficult class, a job interview or a funny video. With close friends, the conversation may turn to money or future plans because they face similar decisions.
questions.sampleZh: 年轻人常常会聊眼下发生的事，比如一门很难的课、一次工作面试，或者一个好笑的视频。和亲近的朋友在一起时，话题也可能转向钱或未来的打算，因为他们面临类似的选择。

questions.en: What problems occur when someone doesn't listen carefully?
questions.zh: 如果一个人没有认真听，会出现哪些问题？
questions.sample: They can miss one small detail that changes the whole task. If a teammate hears the meeting time but misses the new location, everyone loses time. The speaker may also feel that their effort was wasted.
questions.sampleZh: 一个没听到的小细节，可能会改变整个任务。比如队友听到了开会时间，却没听说地点换了，大家的时间都会被耽误。说话的人也可能会觉得自己白费了一番力气。

questions.en: How can someone who is talking know if the other person is really listening?
questions.zh: 说话的人怎样才能知道对方是否真的在听？
questions.sample: A useful sign is a follow-up question that connects to something specific. If I mention a difficult journey and the other person asks how I got home, I know they've followed the story more closely than a simple nod suggests.
questions.sampleZh: 一个很有用的信号，是对方能针对某个具体细节接着问。比如我说路上不太顺利，对方问我最后是怎么回到家的，我就知道他比仅仅点点头的人听得更认真。

questions.en: Do you think most young people are interested in talking to older people?
questions.zh: 你觉得大多数年轻人都对跟老年人交谈感兴趣吗？
questions.sample: I think many are interested when the conversation has a clear connection to their own lives. A grandparent's story about choosing a first job can be fascinating. A long talk full of names they've never heard is harder to follow.
questions.sampleZh: 如果话题和他们自己的生活有关，我觉得很多年轻人都会感兴趣。听爷爷奶奶讲当年怎么选第一份工作，可能很有意思。可如果对方讲了很久，提到的又全是他们没听过的人名，就很难一直听下去。

questions.en: Some people say that conversations are more interesting when people don't agree with each other. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，大家意见不一致时，聊天反而更有意思。你同意吗？
questions.sample: A friendly disagreement can make a conversation more interesting because both people have a reason to explain their thinking. It stops being enjoyable if someone treats it as a competition and refuses to listen to the other side.
questions.sampleZh: 友善的分歧能让谈话更有意思，因为双方都有理由把自己的想法说清楚。如果有一方把聊天当成比赛，又不肯听对方的意见，那就不好玩了。

questions.en: Some people say that people who talk about themselves a lot are not good listeners. Do you think so?
questions.zh: 有人说，总在谈自己的人往往不善于倾听。你觉得呢？
questions.sample: Not always. Some people tell a story about themselves because they're trying to show they understand. The real test is whether they return to the other person's experience afterwards or keep the attention on themselves.
questions.sampleZh: 不一定。有些人讲自己的经历，其实是想表示自己理解对方。要看的，是他们讲完之后会不会再问起对方的感受，还是始终把注意力留在自己身上。

questions.en: How do you think the use of computers and phones have changed personal communication?
questions.zh: 你觉得电脑和手机的使用改变了人与人之间交流的哪些方面？
questions.sample: Phones and computers make it easy to talk across cities and to reply when both people are free. Written messages can also hide tone. A short reply that means “I'm busy” might sound unfriendly to the person reading it.
questions.sampleZh: 手机和电脑让住在不同城市的人也能轻松聊天，双方有空的时候再回消息就行。不过，文字有时看不出语气。本意只是“我现在很忙”的一句简短回复，在收到的人看来可能并不友好。

questions.en: Do you think technology has had different impacts on language used by younger people and by older people?
questions.zh: 你觉得科技对年轻人和老年人日常用语的影响有所不同吗？
questions.sample: Young people may pick up new expressions from videos and use them in group chats. Older people can use the same tools differently, perhaps sending voice messages instead of typing. Both groups change their language depending on who they're talking to.
questions.sampleZh: 年轻人可能从视频里学到新的表达，然后用在群聊里。年纪大些的人用同样的工具时，也许更喜欢发语音而不是打字。无论哪个年龄段，都会根据谈话对象调整自己的表达。

questions.en: Do you think face-to-face communication is a basic human need?
questions.zh: 你觉得面对面交流是人类的一项基本需求吗？
questions.sample: I think most people need some face-to-face contact, even if they enjoy chatting online. Sitting beside someone makes it easier to notice a pause or a smile, which can matter a lot during a difficult conversation.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得多数人还是需要一些面对面的接触，即使他们也喜欢在网上聊天。坐在一个人身旁，更容易注意到他突然停顿了一下，或是笑了笑。在一场难开口的谈话里，这些细节可能很重要。

questions.en: How can a teacher tell if students are listening in class?
questions.zh: 老师怎么知道学生上课有没有在听？
questions.sample: Rather than looking only for eye contact, a teacher can ask students to explain an idea in their own words. If they can give a fresh example, it shows they followed the lesson, even if they were quiet.
questions.sampleZh: 老师不必只看学生有没有眼神交流，也可以让他们用自己的话解释一个概念。一个学生哪怕课堂上很安静，只要能自己举一个新例子，就说明他跟上了这堂课。

questions.en: What do you think about talking with people who have different opinions?
questions.zh: 你怎么看待与自己观点不同的人交谈这件事？
questions.sample: I enjoy it when both people have time to explain themselves. A different opinion can reveal something I hadn't considered, such as how a new rule affects a neighbour. I don't have to change my mind to learn something.
questions.sampleZh: 只要双方都有时间把自己的想法说完，我就挺喜欢这样的交谈。不同的意见可能让我留意到原先没想到的事，比如一条新规定会怎样影响邻居。就算我最后没有改变主意，也能从中学到东西。

questions.en: Some people say it's always better to save historic buildings than to build new ones. Do you think so?
questions.zh: 有人说，保留历史建筑总比盖新楼好。你同意吗？
questions.sample: I would save buildings that tell an important local story, especially ones people can still use. But keeping every old building isn't realistic. Sometimes a new home or clinic is what the neighbourhood needs most.
questions.sampleZh: 我愿意保留那些能讲述当地重要历史的建筑，特别是人们现在还能继续使用的。不过，要保住每一栋老建筑并不现实。有时候，附近居民当下真正需要的是新住房或一家诊所。

questions.en: Some people say it's better for most people to live in flats than in houses. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，对大多数人来说，住公寓比住独立住宅更好。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Flats suit many city residents because shops and transport are often nearby, and there is less to look after. A house may suit a large family who want a garden. The better choice depends on space, cost and location.
questions.sampleZh: 公寓适合许多城市居民，因为附近常有商店和公共交通，需要自己打理的地方也少些。对一个想有花园的大家庭来说，独栋房屋可能更合适。哪种更好，还得看需要的空间、花销和所在位置。

questions.en: Why do some people choose to live in the countryside?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人会选择住在乡下？
questions.sample: Some people want more room and a quieter daily routine. Others have family in a village and enjoy knowing their neighbours. The countryside is especially attractive if they can keep their job without making a long daily journey.
questions.sampleZh: 有些人希望空间大一点，日常生活安静一些。还有些人的家人在村里，他们也喜欢和邻里相熟的感觉。如果既可以保住现有的工作，又不用天天跑很远的路，乡村生活就尤其有吸引力。

questions.en: What kinds of things make a building a nice place to live in?
questions.zh: 哪些因素会让一栋楼住起来舒服？
questions.sample: Natural light, good airflow and some protection from noise make a real difference. A building also needs practical details, like a lift that works and somewhere to leave a bike. Those things matter every single day.
questions.sampleZh: 自然光充足、通风良好、能隔绝一部分噪声，住起来真的会舒服很多。楼里还得有些实用的设计，比如能正常使用的电梯，以及停自行车的地方。这些都是每天都用得上的东西。

questions.en: What things make historic buildings worth saving?
questions.zh: 哪些特点让历史建筑值得保护？
questions.sample: A historic building might show a building skill people rarely use now, or it may hold memories for a whole community. An old theatre, for example, tells you something about how people once spent their evenings together.
questions.sampleZh: 一栋历史建筑也许展现了如今很少有人使用的建造工艺，也可能承载着整个社区的回忆。比如一座老剧院，就能告诉我们，以前人们是怎样一起度过夜晚的。

questions.en: Who should pay the costs of saving historic buildings?
questions.zh: 应该由谁承担保护历史建筑的费用？
questions.sample: If a building is privately owned and earns money, the owner should cover some of the cost. Public support makes sense when the whole community benefits, especially if visitors or school groups can go inside.
questions.sampleZh: 如果建筑归私人所有，而且能够带来收入，业主就应该承担一部分费用。如果整个社区都能从保护中受益，花些公共资金也有道理，特别是游客或学生团体还能进到建筑里参观的时候。

questions.en: Do you think an architect's only responsibility is to design buildings that are beautiful?
questions.zh: 你觉得建筑师的职责仅仅是设计美观的建筑吗？
questions.sample: No. An architect also has to think about how people move, work and feel inside the building. A beautiful clinic with confusing doors and nowhere for patients to sit would still be a poor design.
questions.sampleZh: 不是。建筑师还要考虑人们在建筑里怎样走动、怎样工作，以及待在里面是什么感受。一家诊所即使很漂亮，要是门的位置让人摸不着头脑，病人也找不到地方坐，它的设计仍然不好。

questions.en: How valuable is impressive architecture to a city's image and status?
questions.zh: 令人印象深刻的建筑，对一座城市的形象和地位有多大价值？
questions.sample: A striking building can help people recognise a city immediately and give visitors a reason to come. Its value lasts longer when residents use it too. An attractive concert hall earns more affection if local families can afford tickets.
questions.sampleZh: 一栋引人注目的建筑能让人一眼认出这座城市，也能吸引游客前来。如果本地居民也会使用它，它的价值就更持久。比如一座美观的音乐厅，如果普通家庭也买得起门票，就更容易得到大家的喜爱。

questions.en: Do you think environmental considerations will be the priority in building design in the future?
questions.zh: 你觉得未来建筑设计会把环境因素放在首位吗？
questions.sample: I think they will become a bigger priority because heating and cooling a building can cost a lot over time. Designers may pay more attention to shade and natural light, although price and useful space will still matter.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得环境因素会更受重视，因为从长远看，建筑里的供暖和制冷都可能花很多钱。设计师也许会更关注遮阳和自然采光，但价格和可用空间仍然很重要。

questions.en: Why do people visit historic buildings?
questions.zh: 人们为什么会去参观历史建筑？
questions.sample: Some visitors are interested in the history, while others enjoy seeing details that newer buildings rarely have. Walking through an old courtyard makes it easier to imagine how a family lived than simply reading a date on a sign.
questions.sampleZh: 有些游客对历史感兴趣，另一些人喜欢看新建筑里很少有的细节。走进一座老院子，比单单读一读标牌上的年份，更容易想象当年一家人在里面过着怎样的日子。

questions.en: Why is it hard to protect historic buildings?
questions.zh: 保护历史建筑为什么这么难？
questions.sample: Repairs can be expensive because old materials and skilled workers may be hard to find. A building also needs a reason to stay in use. If it sits empty for years, small problems can grow much worse.
questions.sampleZh: 修缮费用可能很高，因为适合老建筑的材料和有相应手艺的工人未必好找。建筑还得有能让人继续使用它的用途。要是常年闲置，原本的小问题也可能越来越严重。

questions.en: What kinds of places are often noisy where you live?
questions.zh: 在你住的地方，哪些场所经常很吵？
questions.sample: Where I live, the bus station gets noisy just before school and work start. Several buses pull in at once, and drivers call out the route numbers so people know which one to catch. A few streets away, the smaller roads are much quieter.
questions.sampleZh: 我住的地方，上班上学前那段时间公交站很吵。好几辆公交同时进站，司机会喊出线路号，好让乘客知道该坐哪辆车。走出几个街区，旁边的小路就安静多了。

questions.en: Is a silent environment essential for concentration?
questions.zh: 安静无声的环境是集中注意力的必要条件吗？
questions.sample: Not for everyone. Some people work well with the low sound of a café, but a clear conversation nearby can pull their attention away. I think the type of noise matters more than complete silence.
questions.sampleZh: 并不是每个人都需要绝对安静。有些人在咖啡馆低低的背景声里也能工作得很好，但旁边若有一段听得一清二楚的谈话，他们就容易分神。我觉得声音的种类，比是否完全安静更重要。

questions.en: Whose responsibility should it be to regulate noise levels?
questions.zh: 控制噪声的音量应该由谁负责？
questions.sample: Local authorities should set clear limits, particularly at night, and businesses should manage the noise they create. Residents have a part to play too. Turning down a speaker can solve a problem before anyone needs to complain.
questions.sampleZh: 地方管理部门应该设定清楚的噪声限制，夜间尤其需要，商家也该管好自己产生的噪声。居民同样能出一份力。比如主动把音箱音量调低，往往在别人需要投诉之前，问题就解决了。

questions.en: In what public places do people not want to hear much noise?
questions.zh: 在哪些公共场所，人们不希望听到太多噪声？
questions.sample: Libraries and reading rooms are obvious examples because people go there to concentrate. Quiet also matters in hospital waiting areas, where patients may be tired or worried. A loud video from one phone can disturb the whole room.
questions.sampleZh: 图书馆和阅览室是很明显的例子，因为人们去那里是为了专心。医院候诊区也需要安静，患者也许正感到疲倦或担心。哪怕只有一个人的手机在大声播放视频，都可能打扰整间屋子的人。

questions.en: Some people say that noisy places are usually more exciting than quiet places. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，吵闹的地方通常比安静的地方更让人兴奋。你同意吗？
questions.sample: They can be, particularly during a street performance or a sports match. But noise on its own doesn't create excitement. Watching the sun come up from a quiet hill can be much more memorable than standing beside a busy road.
questions.sampleZh: 有时会，尤其是看街头表演或体育比赛的时候。但光有噪声不一定就让人兴奋。在安静的山坡上看太阳升起，可能比站在繁忙的道路旁更令人难忘。

questions.en: Why do some people not like noisy places?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人不喜欢吵闹的地方？
questions.sample: Loud noise can make a simple conversation tiring. People have to raise their voices or keep asking others to repeat themselves. Someone who has already spent the day in a busy workplace may especially want a quieter evening.
questions.sampleZh: 声音太大，连普通的聊天都容易让人觉得累。说话的人得提高嗓门，或者不停请对方重复。尤其是已经在忙乱的工作场所待了一整天的人，晚上可能更想找个安静的地方。

questions.en: What can people do when noise is annoying them?
questions.zh: 受到噪声困扰时，人们可以怎么做？
questions.sample: If the noise comes from one person, a calm request is a good first step. For example, a neighbour might not realise how far music travels at night. If it keeps happening, the building manager could help.
questions.sampleZh: 如果噪声来自某个具体的人，可以先平静地跟对方说一声。比如，邻居可能根本没意识到夜里音乐声能传那么远。如果情况一再发生，就可以请物业管理人员帮忙。

questions.en: Some people say that noise pollution is as harmful as water and air pollution. Do you think so?
questions.zh: 有人说，噪声污染的危害不亚于水污染和空气污染。你觉得呢？
questions.sample: They cause different problems, so I wouldn't give them one simple ranking. Dirty water can make daily life unsafe, while constant night-time noise can stop a whole street from sleeping. People need practical ways to report both.
questions.sampleZh: 它们带来的问题不同，我不会简单给危害程度排个名次。水不干净可能影响日常生活的安全，而夜里持续不断的噪声，可能会让整条街的人都睡不着。两种情况都需要有切实可用的反映渠道。

questions.en: Do you think noise pollution will become more of an issue for societies in the future?
questions.zh: 你觉得未来噪声污染会成为更严重的社会问题吗？
questions.sample: It could, particularly where new homes, shops and busy roads are built close together. Better public transport and quieter equipment might help. The result will depend partly on whether planners think about noise before people move in.
questions.sampleZh: 可能会，尤其是在新住宅、商店和繁忙道路都离得很近的地方。更好的公共交通和噪声更小的设备可能有帮助。最后情况怎样，部分取决于规划者有没有在居民搬进来之前就考虑噪声问题。

questions.en: How can people consider others' feelings when chatting in public?
questions.zh: 在公共场合聊天时，人们如何考虑他人的感受？
questions.sample: A quick look around often tells you what volume is right. In a busy park, a normal conversation is fine. On a quiet train, people can lower their voices or move a phone call away from sleeping passengers.
questions.sampleZh: 看一眼周围，通常就知道多大的音量合适。在热闹的公园里，正常音量聊天就可以。在安静的列车上，人们可以把声音放低，或者走到离睡着的乘客远一点的地方再打电话。

questions.en: How would people usually respond to noises in your country?
questions.zh: 在你们国家，人们通常如何应对噪音？
questions.sample: It depends on the time and place. People may accept loud music during a daytime festival but ask a neighbour to turn it down late at night. Some will speak directly, while others ask the building manager first.
questions.sampleZh: 这得看时间和场合。人们也许能接受白天节庆活动的响亮音乐，但到了深夜就可能请邻居把音量调低。有些人会直接去说，也有人会先找物业管理人员。

questions.en: Which area is exposed to noise more, the city or the countryside?
questions.zh: 哪个地方更容易受到噪音影响，城市还是乡村？
questions.sample: Cities are usually noisier because more traffic, building work and people share a small area. The countryside has noisy moments too, such as a tractor passing early in the morning. Those sounds are often less constant.
questions.sampleZh: 城里通常更吵，因为更多车辆、工地和行人挤在有限的空间里。乡下也有吵闹的时候，比如一大早有拖拉机经过，但这种声音往往不会持续那么久。

questions.en: What kinds of noises are there in our life?
questions.zh: 我们生活中有哪些类型的噪音？
questions.sample: At home we hear voices, kitchen sounds and sometimes music from next door. Outside there are traffic lights, engines, birds and people talking. The same sound can feel pleasant during the day and irritating late at night.
questions.sampleZh: 在家里，我们会听到说话声、厨房里的声音，有时还有隔壁传来的音乐。出门后，则能听见交通信号的提示音、发动机声、鸟叫和行人的交谈声。同一种声音白天听着也许挺舒服，到了深夜却可能让人心烦。

questions.en: Should children not be allowed to make noise under any circumstances?
questions.zh: 是否应该完全禁止孩子发出噪音？
questions.sample: No. Children need places where they can laugh, run and shout, such as a playground. What matters is learning that different places have different rules. A library calls for a much softer voice than a football field.
questions.sampleZh: 不应该。孩子需要有能笑、能跑、能大喊大叫的地方，比如游乐场。重要的是学会不同场所有不同的规矩。在图书馆里，说话声自然该比在足球场上轻得多。

questions.en: Do you think it is good for children to make noise?
questions.zh: 你觉得孩子吵闹一些对他们来说是件好事吗？
questions.sample: Yes, in the right setting. Singing or cheering with other children can help a shy child join a game. Adults can let them enjoy that while teaching them to notice when someone nearby needs quiet.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得可以，前提是场合合适。跟着其他孩子一起唱歌或欢呼，可能会帮助一个害羞的孩子加入游戏。大人可以让他们享受其中，同时也教他们留意身边什么时候有人需要安静。

questions.en: What impact can the creative arts have on society as a whole? [e.g. music, theatre]
questions.zh: 音乐、戏剧等艺术形式能对整个社会产生哪些影响？
questions.sample: Music and theatre can bring people with different backgrounds into the same room and give them something to discuss. A play about a family's daily problems, for instance, might help the audience understand neighbours they rarely speak to.
questions.sampleZh: 音乐和戏剧能把不同背景的人带进同一个空间，也让他们有了共同的话题。比如，一部讲述某个家庭日常难处的戏，可能会让观众更理解那些平常很少交谈的邻居。

questions.en: At work, to what extent might teams benefit from having creative people?
questions.zh: 工作团队里有富于创造力的人，能在多大程度上让团队受益？
questions.sample: They can benefit a lot when a project gets stuck. A creative teammate may suggest drawing a simple picture instead of adding another page to a report. The idea works best when colleagues have time to try it.
questions.sampleZh: 项目遇到瓶颈时，有这样的人特别有帮助。一位有创意的队友可能会建议，画一张简单的图，而不用给报告再添一页文字。如果同事们有时间把想法试一下，就更能看出效果。

questions.en: Do you think creative talents are natural and cannot be learned?
questions.zh: 你觉得创作才能是天生的，后天学不来吗？
questions.sample: People may start with different strengths, but creativity can grow with practice. A child making a paper bridge learns by changing one fold and trying again. A teacher who welcomes several possible answers gives that child room to improve.
questions.sampleZh: 每个人起初擅长的东西可能不同，但创造力是可以通过练习培养的。一个做纸桥的孩子，每次改变一道折痕再试一次，就会慢慢学到东西。老师如果欢迎不同的答案，孩子就有了继续尝试和进步的空间。

questions.en: What kinds of things do children like to make?
questions.zh: 孩子喜欢动手做哪些东西？
questions.sample: Many children enjoy making things they can use immediately, like paper planes, toy animals or cards for a friend. Simple materials work well because the child can choose the colours and quickly see the result.
questions.sampleZh: 很多孩子喜欢做马上能用的东西，比如纸飞机、玩具小动物，或者送朋友的卡片。简单的材料就很合适，因为孩子可以自己选颜色，而且很快就能看到成品。

questions.en: Some people say that all children should have lessons in art and craft at school. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，所有孩子都应该在学校上美术和手工课。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Yes, I think everyone should have the chance to try them. A short craft lesson gives children a different way to show an idea. Someone who rarely speaks in class might proudly explain a small model they've made.
questions.sampleZh: 是的，我觉得每个孩子都应该有机会尝试美术和手工。一节短短的手工课，就能让孩子换一种方式表达想法。一个平时在课堂上很少说话的学生，也可能很自豪地介绍自己做的小模型。

questions.en: Why do many parents keep the things that their children have made?
questions.zh: 为什么许多家长会把孩子亲手做的东西留下来？
questions.sample: The object reminds parents of a stage that passes quickly. A birthday card with uneven writing may mean more to a family than an expensive gift because they remember the child trying so hard to make it.
questions.sampleZh: 孩子的作品会让父母想起那个很快就会过去的成长阶段。一张字写得歪歪扭扭的生日卡片，对一家人来说可能比昂贵的礼物更有意义，因为他们还记得孩子当时做得有多认真。

questions.en: How important is it for creative people to have quiet time alone?
questions.zh: 对有创造力的人来说，能安静地独处一会儿有多重要？
questions.sample: Quiet time can help them follow an idea before anyone comments on it. A musician might need an hour alone to try a tune. Later, playing it for someone else can show which parts really work.
questions.sampleZh: 安静独处的时间，让他们能在别人发表意见之前，先顺着自己的想法试一试。音乐人也许需要独处一个小时，试奏一段曲调。之后再弹给别人听，就更容易发现哪些地方确实打动人。

questions.en: What challenges do creative people often face?
questions.zh: 有创造力的人常常面临哪些挑战？
questions.sample: They may have plenty of ideas but little time, money or equipment to test them. There's also the problem of explaining an unfamiliar idea. A rough model can sometimes communicate more clearly than a long speech.
questions.sampleZh: 他们可能想法很多，却缺少把它们付诸尝试的时间、经费或设备。另一个困难是如何向人解释一个陌生的构想。有时候，一个粗略的模型就比一段很长的说明讲得更清楚。

questions.en: Do you think the development of new technology will ultimately inspire or limit creativity?
questions.zh: 你觉得新技术的发展最终会激发还是限制创造力？
questions.sample: I expect it to inspire more people by making creative tools cheaper and easier to try. A student can edit a short film on a phone. The risk is that everyone copies the same popular style without experimenting.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得新技术会激发更多人的创造力，因为创作工具变得更便宜，也更容易上手。学生用手机就能剪一部短片。风险是大家都模仿同一种流行风格，不再自己动手尝试。

questions.en: What impact can artistic buildings have on society?
questions.zh: 具有艺术特色的建筑会给社会带来哪些影响？
questions.sample: An unusual building can become a meeting place and give a neighbourhood a recognisable identity. If people can enter and use it, its design may also make art part of an ordinary afternoon, not just a special museum visit.
questions.sampleZh: 一栋造型特别的建筑可以成为人们碰面的地点，也能让整个街区更有辨识度。如果人们还能进去使用它，这样的设计就让艺术成了普通一个下午的一部分，而不必特意安排一次博物馆之行。

questions.en: Do children these days still like doing arts and crafts?
questions.zh: 现在的孩子还喜欢做手工吗？
questions.sample: Many do, especially when the activity gives them a real choice. Making a gift for a friend feels different from copying a perfect model. Screens compete for attention, but children still enjoy having something they can hold.
questions.sampleZh: 现在仍有许多孩子喜欢，尤其是活动中能自己做决定的时候。亲手给朋友做礼物，和照着完美的范本复制，感觉大不相同。虽然电子屏幕也很吸引人，但孩子们依然喜欢那种成品能拿在手上的感觉。

questions.en: Why do some children enjoy making things by hand?
questions.zh: 为什么有些孩子喜欢动手做东西？
questions.sample: They can watch an idea turn into a real object through their own effort. If two children start with the same piece of paper, they might finish with completely different animals. That freedom makes the process fun.
questions.sampleZh: 因为他们能看着脑海中的想法，通过自己的努力变成一个实物。两个孩子即使拿到相同的一张纸，最后也可能做出完全不同的小动物。这种自由正是过程有趣的地方。

questions.en: Do you think art classes are important for children?
questions.zh: 你觉得美术课对孩子重要吗？
questions.sample: Yes. Art classes let children practise noticing details and making choices that don't have one correct answer. They can also share an idea through a drawing when they haven't yet found the words to explain it.
questions.sampleZh: 重要。美术课能让孩子练习观察细节，也能让他们在没有唯一正确答案的事情上自己作选择。一个想法暂时找不到合适的话来解释时，他们还可以把它画出来和人分享。

questions.en: What can people do to become fit and healthy?
questions.zh: 人们可以做些什么来增强体能、改善健康？
questions.sample: For most people, a practical start is moving more in ways they actually enjoy, eating regular meals and making time to sleep. Walking with a friend after dinner can be easier to keep up than buying expensive equipment.
questions.sampleZh: 对多数人来说，可以先从实际的小事做起，选自己真正喜欢的方式多活动，按时吃饭，也给睡眠留足时间。晚饭后和朋友一起散步，可能比花钱买昂贵的健身器材更容易坚持。

questions.en: Do you think a healthy community is one where people feel a sense of belonging?
questions.zh: 你觉得一个健康的社区应该是让居民有归属感的地方吗？
questions.sample: Belonging is part of it, because people are more likely to ask for help if they know their neighbours. A healthy community needs practical things too, such as safe paths and clean shared spaces where residents can meet.
questions.sampleZh: 归属感是其中的一部分，因为认识邻居的人更愿意在需要时开口求助。健康的社区也需要实际的条件，比如安全的步道，以及干净、方便居民相聚的公共空间。

questions.en: How can stress affect a person's physical and mental health?
questions.zh: 压力会怎样影响一个人的身体和心理健康？
questions.sample: Stress can make it difficult to switch off at night or focus on a familiar task. Someone facing several deadlines may also skip meals or become impatient with friends. A lighter workload and a chance to talk can make a difference.
questions.sampleZh: 压力可能让人晚上很难放松，也会让人做熟悉的事情时仍然无法集中注意力。一个人如果同时面对好几个截止日期，可能还会顾不上吃饭，或者对朋友不耐烦。减轻些工作量，有机会找人聊聊，都可能有帮助。

questions.en: Do you think young people now are fitter and healthier than young people in the past?
questions.zh: 你觉得现在的年轻人比过去的年轻人体能更好、也更健康吗？
questions.sample: I don't think age groups from different periods can be compared with one simple answer. Young people today may have better access to sports facilities, but some also spend much more of the day sitting in front of screens.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得不能用一个简单的答案比较不同时代的年轻人。现在的年轻人或许更方便使用各种运动设施，但也有些人一天中坐在屏幕前的时间，比以前长得多。

questions.en: Why do people often find it hard to improve their health and fitness?
questions.zh: 为什么人们常常觉得很难改善健康状况、增强体能？
questions.sample: Time and cost often get in the way. Someone who finishes work late may find the nearest gym closed or too expensive. A simple activity near home is easier to continue than a plan that requires a long journey.
questions.sampleZh: 时间和花销往往是阻碍。下班晚的人可能会发现，最近的健身房已经打烊，或者价格太高。一项在家附近就能做的简单运动，往往比需要长途往返的计划更容易坚持。

questions.en: How important is it to stay physically and mentally active throughout life?
questions.zh: 人的一生都保持身体和头脑活跃，有多重要？
questions.sample: I think both matter because they help people enjoy ordinary tasks and interests as they get older. A walk to the market gives someone a reason to move, while planning a new recipe keeps their mind busy too.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得身体和头脑都保持活跃很重要，这能帮助人们在变老的过程中，仍然享受日常事务和自己的兴趣。步行去市场，给了人活动身体的理由；琢磨一道新菜该怎么做，也能让脑子动起来。

questions.en: Some people say that having social connections contributes to a person's physical and mental wellbeing. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，和他人保持联系有益于一个人的身心健康。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Yes. A friend can listen after a difficult day and invite you out when you'd otherwise stay home. Even a regular walk together gives both people something to look forward to and a reason to be active.
questions.sampleZh: 同意。在一天过得很艰难的时候，朋友可以听你说说话，也能在你原本打算一个人待在家里时约你出门。哪怕只是固定一起散步，也会给两个人带来期待，让双方都有理由多活动一下。

questions.en: What role can governments play in promoting a healthy society?
questions.zh: 政府可以在促进全社会健康方面发挥什么作用？
questions.sample: They can make healthy choices easier by providing safe parks, clean drinking water and affordable local sports facilities. Those changes reach people who can't pay for a private gym or travel far for a place to exercise.
questions.sampleZh: 政府可以通过建设安全的公园、提供干净的饮用水和收费合理的社区体育设施，让健康的生活选择更容易实现。这些改变也能惠及无力负担私人健身房、或不能跑很远去运动的人。

questions.en: Do you think societies in the future will prioritise happiness over wealth?
questions.zh: 你觉得未来社会会把幸福看得比财富更重要吗？
questions.sample: I think people may ask more often what extra money is actually buying them. Once families can cover basic needs, a shorter journey to work or more time with their children may matter more than a small pay rise.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得人们可能会更常问自己，多挣一些钱究竟给生活带来了什么。当一个家庭的基本需要已经有保障，缩短通勤时间，或者多陪陪孩子，也许会比小幅加薪更重要。

questions.en: What things do people often need to save money to buy?
questions.zh: 哪些东西通常需要人们先攒钱才能买？
questions.sample: A home is a major example, but people also save for a laptop, a bicycle or a holiday. What counts as a big purchase depends on income. For a student, even replacing a broken phone can require several months of saving.
questions.sampleZh: 买房是一个很典型的例子，但人们也会为笔记本电脑、自行车或一次度假存钱。什么算得上一笔大支出，要看个人收入。对学生来说，哪怕只是把坏掉的手机换掉，也可能得攒上好几个月。

questions.en: Do you think schools should teach children how to manage money?
questions.zh: 你觉得学校应该教孩子如何理财吗？
questions.sample: Yes, especially if the lessons use everyday examples. Students could plan a week's lunches with a small budget and see what happens when prices change. That's much easier to remember than a list of money terms.
questions.sampleZh: 应该，尤其是课程里能用到日常例子的时候。比如，让学生拿一笔很小的预算来安排一周的午饭，再看看价格变化会带来什么影响。这比记一串跟理财有关的术语好记多了。

questions.en: Why are some people not very good at saving money?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人不太擅长存钱？
questions.sample: Some people spend a little at a time and don't notice the total until the end of the month. Others have little left after rent and food. The first problem is about habits, while the second is about income.
questions.sampleZh: 有些人每次只花一点，直到月底才意识到总共花了多少。还有些人交完房租、买完吃的，本来就剩不下多少钱。前一种情况是习惯问题，后一种则跟收入有关。

questions.en: Do most people prefer to save money or spend money?
questions.zh: 大多数人更喜欢存钱还是花钱？
questions.sample: Most people do some of both. Someone saving for a home may enjoy buying a coffee on the way to work. I'd say habits change when people have a clear goal or suddenly face a large expense.
questions.sampleZh: 多数人两件事都会做。一个正在攒钱买房的人，也可能喜欢上班路上买杯咖啡。我觉得当人们有了明确目标，或是突然有一笔大额开销，花钱和存钱的习惯就可能随之改变。

questions.en: Some people say that parents should teach children to be generous. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，父母应该教孩子为人大方。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Yes, and parents can show that generosity doesn't require much money. A child could share a favourite book or help a neighbour carry a bag. Seeing the other person's reaction makes the idea easier to understand.
questions.sampleZh: 应该，父母还可以用实际行动让孩子知道，大方不一定得花很多钱。孩子可以把喜欢的书借给别人读，也可以帮邻居提个袋子。亲眼看到对方的反应，比听道理更容易明白慷慨的意义。

questions.en: Do you think children might understand more about money today than children did in the past?
questions.zh: 你觉得今天的孩子有可能比过去的孩子更懂得钱是什么、该怎么用吗？
questions.sample: They may see more prices online, but that doesn't always mean they understand money better. Paying by phone hides the feeling of handing over cash. Giving a child a small budget can make the cost of each choice clearer.
questions.sampleZh: 现在的孩子也许能在网上看到更多商品的价格，但这不总意味着他们更懂钱。用手机支付，少了把现金亲手递出去的感受。给孩子一小笔预算，可能让他们更清楚每个选择意味着花多少钱。

questions.en: Why are there so many different attitudes to money in society?
questions.zh: 为什么社会上人们对钱的态度有这么多差异？
questions.sample: Family experience makes a difference. Someone who grew up with uncertain income may feel safer with savings, while someone whose bills were always covered may spend more freely. People also value different things, such as travel or a home.
questions.sampleZh: 家庭经历会起作用。一个在收入不稳定的家庭里长大的人，手里有些存款可能才觉得安心；一个从小不用担心账单的人，花钱也许就更自在。大家看重的东西也不同，有人重视旅行，有人更想拥有自己的家。

questions.en: Do you think society might value leisure time more highly than money in the future?
questions.zh: 你觉得未来社会有可能把休闲时间看得比金钱更重要吗？
questions.sample: It could, especially if working hours become more flexible. Someone who already earns enough might choose an extra day off to see family. For people struggling to cover basic costs, a higher income will still be the immediate priority.
questions.sampleZh: 有可能，尤其是当工作时间变得更灵活的时候。一个收入已经足够的人，可能更愿意多休一天，去陪陪家人。但对还在为基本开支发愁的人来说，更高的收入仍是眼前最需要的。

questions.en: Do you think society could ever function without money?
questions.zh: 你觉得社会有没有可能在没有货币的情况下正常运转？
questions.sample: A small group can exchange favours, but a large society would find it difficult. A baker who needs a bus ride can't rely on the driver wanting bread each morning. Money gives strangers a common way to trade.
questions.sampleZh: 小范围内，人们可以互相帮忙、交换服务，但一个庞大的社会很难完全这样运转。比如，面包师要坐公交车，不能指望司机每天早上都正好想要面包。货币让互不相识的人也有了共同的交易方式。

questions.en: Should people spend time on charity, or just money?
questions.zh: 做慈善时，人们应该投入时间，还是只捐钱就够了？
questions.sample: Both kinds of help matter. A food bank needs money to buy supplies and people to sort and deliver them. Someone with a free Saturday might give time, while a busy worker could cover the cost of several meals.
questions.sampleZh: 两种帮助都重要。食物救助机构既需要钱采购物资，也需要人手来整理、分发。周六有空的人可以捐出时间，而工作很忙的人则可以出钱，承担几份饭的费用。

questions.en: Is it easier to spend money or save money?
questions.zh: 花钱和攒钱，哪一个更容易？
questions.sample: Spending is usually easier because it gives an immediate reward, and phone payments take only a moment. Saving becomes easier when the goal feels real. A picture of the trip you're saving for can help you pause before buying something.
questions.sampleZh: 花钱往往更容易，因为能马上得到回报，用手机付款更是一瞬间的事。存钱的目标足够具体时，就比较好坚持。比如，把正攒钱要去的旅行目的地的照片放在眼前，买东西前可能就会多想一想。

questions.en: Do you think it is easier to teach teenagers how to manage money when they are around 16 or 17 years old?
questions.zh: 在青少年十六七岁时教他们理财会更容易吗？
questions.sample: Yes, around that age teenagers often start paying for meals, travel or outings on their own. A lesson about budgeting then connects to decisions they already make. Younger children can still learn the basics with a small amount of pocket money.
questions.sampleZh: 我觉得是。到了十六七岁，很多孩子已经开始自己支付吃饭、出行或跟朋友出去玩的费用。这时候学怎么做预算，能直接和已有的选择联系起来。年龄更小的孩子也可以通过少量零花钱学习基础理财。

questions.en: Should parents teach their children to spend money freely or to save money?
questions.zh: 父母应该教孩子自在地花钱，还是把钱存起来？
questions.sample: I'd teach both, starting with a small amount the child can divide. Saving part for a bigger goal builds patience, while choosing what to do with the rest gives them practice making decisions without risking very much.
questions.sampleZh: 我会两样都教，先给孩子一小笔可以自己分配的钱。拿出一部分为大目标存起来，能培养耐心；剩下一部分让他们自己决定怎么用，也能练习作选择，而且即使出错，代价也不大。

questions.en: Do you think companies should offer training for all staff who deal with the public?
questions.zh: 你觉得公司应该为所有需要跟公众打交道的员工提供培训吗？
questions.sample: Yes. Everyone who meets customers should know how to answer common questions and who to call when a problem is more serious. Practising a difficult conversation before it happens can help a new employee stay calm and polite.
questions.sampleZh: 应该。所有需要接触顾客的员工，都该知道怎样回答常见问题，也要知道碰到更严重的问题时找谁。事先练习一次难应对的对话，能帮助新员工在真正遇到时保持冷静和礼貌。

questions.en: In what kinds of jobs do people need to deal with the public?
questions.zh: 从事哪些工作的人需要和公众打交道？
questions.sample: Shop assistants, receptionists, bus drivers and library staff all deal with the public, although the contact varies. A driver may give quick directions, while a receptionist may need to sit with someone and explain a longer process.
questions.sampleZh: 店员、前台接待、公交司机和图书馆工作人员都需要和公众打交道，只是接触方式不同。司机可能只需要简单指个路，而前台接待有时得坐下来，向人解释一套比较长的流程。

questions.en: What personal qualities are needed to deal with the public?
questions.zh: 与公众打交道需要具备哪些个人品质？
questions.sample: Patience and clear communication matter most. Someone who is upset may explain the problem badly, so staff need to listen before offering an answer. It also helps to admit when they need to ask a colleague.
questions.sampleZh: 最重要的是耐心，还有把事情说清楚的能力。一个情绪激动的人，可能说不清自己碰到了什么问题，所以工作人员要先听完，再给答复。如果需要请教同事，坦率地告诉对方也会有帮助。

questions.en: Some people say that most companies respond quickly to problems reported by customers. Do you agree?
questions.zh: 有人说，大多数企业都会迅速回应顾客反映的问题。你同意吗？
questions.sample: Some reply quickly, especially to simple questions like where a parcel is. Getting a useful solution can take longer. An automatic message is easy to send, but customers usually want a person who can actually make a decision.
questions.sampleZh: 有些公司回复得很快，特别是碰到“我的包裹到哪儿了”这种简单问题时。不过，要等到真正有用的解决办法，可能就没这么快。发一条自动回复很容易，但顾客想找的，通常是一个真正能作决定的人。

questions.en: What should companies do if a product is faulty or has problems?
questions.zh: 如果产品有缺陷或出了问题，企业应该怎么做？
questions.sample: First, they should listen and check what went wrong. Then they can offer a clear choice, such as repairing the item, replacing it or returning the money. The customer shouldn't have to explain the same problem to four different people.
questions.sampleZh: 首先，他们应该听顾客把情况说完，核实是什么地方出了问题。然后可以给出清楚的选项，比如维修、更换或退款。顾客不应该为了同一件事，先后对四个人重复说明情况。

questions.en: How can companies avoid having problems with their products or services?
questions.zh: 企业可以怎样防止自己的产品或服务出问题？
questions.sample: Testing a product with the people who will actually use it can catch problems early. Companies should also read repeated complaints carefully. If ten customers misunderstand the same instruction, rewriting it may prevent a hundred more calls.
questions.sampleZh: 让真正会用到产品的人先试一试，可以及早发现问题。公司也应该认真看看反复出现的投诉。如果有十位顾客都误解了同一条说明，把它重新写清楚，也许就能省下之后的一百通电话。

questions.en: What challenges can big companies face when operating in different countries?
questions.zh: 大企业在不同国家经营时可能遇到哪些挑战？
questions.sample: The same product or message may be understood differently in another country. Delivery systems, local rules and customer habits can vary too. Hiring people who know the local market can prevent expensive mistakes over small details.
questions.sampleZh: 同一件产品或同一句宣传语，在另一个国家可能会被理解成不同的意思。当地的配送体系、规章和顾客习惯也可能不一样。聘用了解当地市场的人，有助于避免因为小细节犯下代价高昂的错误。

questions.en: How important are happy staff to the success of a company?
questions.zh: 员工工作得开心，对一家企业的成功有多重要？
questions.sample: They're very important, particularly in services. Staff who feel respected are more likely to notice a problem and speak up before it gets worse. A friendly team can also make customers want to return.
questions.sampleZh: 很重要，尤其是在服务行业。员工如果觉得自己受到尊重，发现问题时就更可能在情况恶化之前主动说出来。一个亲切的团队，也会让顾客愿意再来。

questions.en: Some people say that a successful company must be innovative. Do you think so?
questions.zh: 有人说，成功的企业必须有创新精神。你觉得呢？
questions.sample: A company doesn't always need a completely new product. A neighbourhood bakery can succeed by making good bread every morning and treating customers well. It still needs to change when people's tastes or shopping habits change.
questions.sampleZh: 企业并不总要拿出一种全新的产品。社区面包店每天早上把面包做好，待客亲切，也能经营成功。不过，人们的口味或购物习惯发生变化时，它仍然需要跟着调整。

questions.en: Can consumption drive economic growth?
questions.zh: 消费能推动经济增长吗？
questions.sample: Yes. When people buy more from a local café, the owner may order more ingredients or hire another worker. The benefit lasts longer if the business has steady customers instead of depending on one short shopping rush.
questions.sampleZh: 能。如果人们在一家社区咖啡馆里增加消费，店主可能会采购更多原料，或者再雇一名员工。要是店里有稳定的客源，而不只是靠短暂的一波购物热潮，这样的好处就会更持久。

questions.en: What are the advantages and disadvantages of shopping online?
questions.zh: 网购有哪些优点和缺点？
questions.sample: Online shopping makes it easy to compare prices and order something at any time. The downside is that a picture can't tell you how a pair of shoes feels. Returning the wrong size can take more effort than visiting a shop.
questions.sampleZh: 网购的好处是方便比价，什么时候都能下单。缺点是，单凭照片没法知道一双鞋穿着是什么感觉。要是买错了尺码，退换花的工夫，可能比直接去一趟店里还多。

questions.en: What are the differences between online shopping and in-store shopping?
questions.zh: 网购和实体店购物有什么区别？
questions.sample: In a shop, you can touch the material, ask a question and take the item home at once. Online, you usually have a wider choice and can read other buyers' comments, but you have to wait for delivery.
questions.sampleZh: 在实体店里，可以摸一摸材质、当场提问，然后马上把东西带回家。网上的选择一般更多，也能看看其他买家怎么说，但买完之后得等送货。

questions.en: Why do some people not like shopping in small shops?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人不喜欢在小商店购物？
questions.sample: Some people want a wider choice of sizes or prices than a small shop can offer. Others prefer to look around without talking. In a tiny space, a helpful owner can sometimes make a shy customer feel watched.
questions.sampleZh: 有些人希望尺寸选择更多，或者想比较更宽的价格范围，而小店未必能提供。也有人逛街时就想自己看看，不想聊天。店面很小时，即便店主只是热心帮忙，也可能让害羞的顾客觉得一直有人盯着。

questions.en: What are the advantages and disadvantages of shopping in small shops?
questions.zh: 在小商店购物有哪些优点和缺点？
questions.sample: The owner may remember what you like and give personal advice that a large store can't offer. On the other hand, a small shop may run out of your size quickly or close earlier in the evening.
questions.sampleZh: 店主可能记得你的喜好，能给出大型商店不一定能提供的个人化建议。另一方面，小店里你要的尺码也可能很快卖完，而且晚上的打烊时间可能更早。

questions.en: Why are shopping malls so popular in China?
questions.zh: 为什么大型购物中心在中国这么受欢迎？
questions.sample: Shopping malls are popular in China partly because people can get several things done in one visit. A family might pick up groceries, have lunch and take a child to an indoor play area. That saves them the trouble of making three separate trips.
questions.sampleZh: 商场在中国受欢迎，一个原因是人们去一趟就能办好几件事。一家人可以买菜、吃午饭，还能带孩子去室内游乐区玩，省得为了三件事分别跑三趟。

questions.en: Is it important for everyone to have a specialized skill?
questions.zh: 每个人拥有一项专业技能重要吗？
questions.sample: A specialist skill can help someone stand out at work, but not everyone needs to choose one very early. Broad skills like listening and organising time are useful almost everywhere. A person can specialise after discovering what they enjoy.
questions.sampleZh: 一项专长有助于一个人在工作中脱颖而出，但没必要每个人很早就选定一门专长。倾听、安排时间之类的通用能力，几乎在哪儿都派得上用场。等弄清自己喜欢什么以后，再深入学习某个方向也可以。

questions.en: Can a child learn skills from another child?
questions.zh: 孩子可以从另一个孩子身上学到技能吗？
questions.sample: Absolutely. Children often copy each other during games without feeling they're having a formal lesson. A child who has just learned to tie a knot may remember exactly which step was confusing and explain it clearly to a friend.
questions.sampleZh: 当然可以。孩子们玩游戏时常常会模仿彼此，又不会觉得像是在上正式的课。一个刚学会打结的孩子，也许还清楚地记得哪一步最容易卡住，所以反而能给朋友解释得很明白。

questions.en: What are the differences between the way adults learn and the way children learn?
questions.zh: 成年人和儿童的学习方式有什么不同？
questions.sample: Children often learn by copying a movement or turning a task into a game. Adults may ask why a step matters before trying it. An adult learning a new computer program might prefer a short guide they can check afterwards.
questions.sampleZh: 孩子往往通过模仿一个动作，或者把任务变成游戏来学习。成年人也许会先问清楚某个步骤为什么重要，再开始动手。比如，成人学习一款新的电脑软件时，可能会更喜欢有一份之后还能翻看的简短指南。

questions.en: What are the differences between learning in a group and learning by yourself?
questions.zh: 小组学习和自己独立学习有什么区别？
questions.sample: A group gives you people to ask and a reason to practise regularly. Working alone lets you repeat a difficult step without holding anyone back. For speaking practice, I think the two approaches can fit together quite well.
questions.sampleZh: 在小组里学习，有问题时可以问人，也有了定期练习的理由。自己学的时候，可以把一个困难的步骤多练几遍，也不用担心耽误别人。拿口语练习来说，我觉得这两种方式完全可以搭配使用。

questions.en: Do you think creativity is important for everyone?
questions.zh: 创造力对每个人都重要吗？
questions.sample: Yes, because ordinary problems don't always come with instructions. A teacher may need a new way to explain a word, or a cook may replace a missing ingredient. Neither has to be an artist to use a creative idea.
questions.sampleZh: 重要，因为日常遇到的问题并不总有现成的说明。老师也许得换一种方式解释一个词，做饭的人也许得想办法替换一种缺少的食材。两个人都用到了有创意的想法，却都不一定是艺术家。

questions.en: Do you think there are too many advertisements on TV in your country?
questions.zh: 你觉得你们国家电视上的广告太多了吗？
questions.sample: Sometimes there are, especially when a long break interrupts an exciting part of a programme. A few adverts are understandable because they help pay for the show. Repeating the same one several times is what bothers people most.
questions.sampleZh: 有时候是多了点，尤其是一段很长的广告把节目最精彩的地方打断时。播一些广告可以理解，因为广告收入能帮节目支付制作费用。真正让人烦的，是同一条广告来回放好几遍。

questions.en: Do you have a favourite advertisement?
questions.zh: 你有特别喜欢的一则广告吗？
questions.sample: I like adverts that show a real problem being solved. A short demonstration of a housework tool is more memorable to me than a famous face simply holding a box. I can decide whether I'd actually use the product.
questions.sampleZh: 我喜欢能展示怎样解决实际问题的广告。对我来说，一个家务小工具的简短演示，比一位名人只拿着个盒子的画面更好记。我也能自己判断，这个产品我究竟用不用得上。

questions.en: Have you ever bought something because of an advertisement?
questions.zh: 你曾因为看了广告而买某样东西吗？
questions.sample: Yes, small things like snacks can catch my attention that way. If an advert shows a flavour I haven't tried, I might pick it up on my next shopping trip. For anything expensive, I'd compare reviews and prices first.
questions.sampleZh: 买过，像零食这样的小东西，很容易通过广告引起我的注意。如果广告里出现了一种我没尝过的口味，下次购物时我可能就会顺手买来试试。东西价格高的话，我会先比较评价和价格。

questions.en: Does the government play an important role in promoting healthy lifestyles in a community?
questions.zh: 政府在社区推广健康生活方式方面起着重要作用吗？
questions.sample: Yes, especially when a whole neighbourhood needs a safe place to be active. A local government can improve lighting on walking paths or open a sports ground to residents. Individual families usually can't arrange those things on their own.
questions.sampleZh: 很重要，尤其是整个社区都需要安全的活动场所时。地方政府可以改善步行道的照明，或者把体育场地向居民开放。这些事通常不是一个家庭单靠自己就能安排好的。

questions.en: Do you think it is important to live in a community where people have healthy lifestyles?
questions.zh: 住在大家都注重健康生活的社区里重要吗？
questions.sample: It helps because good habits are easier to keep when people around you share them. Seeing neighbours walk after dinner might encourage you to join. Still, someone should feel welcome even if their interests or abilities are different.
questions.sampleZh: 有帮助，因为周围的人都有相似的健康习惯，自己也更容易坚持。比如，看见邻居晚饭后出去散步，你也许就愿意加入。不过，即使有人的兴趣或身体能力和别人不同，也应该让对方觉得自己同样受欢迎。

questions.en: How can people relieve stress in daily life?
questions.zh: 人们可以怎样缓解日常生活中的压力？
questions.sample: A short break can give people a little distance from whatever is worrying them. Some prefer a walk, while others call a friend or write down the next small task. The best choice depends on what caused the pressure.
questions.sampleZh: 休息一小会儿，可以暂时从让自己担心的事里抽出来。有人喜欢散散步，有人会给朋友打电话，也有人会把接下来能做的一件小事写下来。怎么做最合适，还得看压力从何而来。

questions.en: Which group pays more attention to health, young people or old people?
questions.zh: 年轻人和老年人，哪一群体更注重健康？
questions.sample: Older people often pay closer attention to regular meals and daily exercise because staying independent matters to them. Young people may care just as much about sleep or sport. Their idea of looking after themselves can look different.
questions.sampleZh: 年长者常常会更留心按时吃饭、日常锻炼，因为保持独立生活的能力对他们很重要。年轻人对睡眠或运动的重视程度也可能不低。只是不同年龄段的人，照顾自己的方式看起来不太一样。

questions.en: What is the most popular sport in your country?
questions.zh: 你们国家最受欢迎的运动是什么？
questions.sample: I'd probably say table tennis is one of the most popular in China. It gets plenty of attention during big tournaments, and people can play a quick game at school or in a neighbourhood sports area.
questions.sampleZh: 我大概会说，乒乓球是中国最受欢迎的运动之一。大型比赛期间，它会吸引很多人关注。平时在学校或社区运动场地里，人们也能方便地打一小会儿。

questions.en: Is it easy to identify children's talents?
questions.zh: 孩子的天赋容易发现吗？
questions.sample: It isn't always easy because a child may never have tried the activity they're good at. Offering several games or subjects helps. Watching what they keep practising voluntarily may tell adults more than one result in a competition.
questions.sampleZh: 不一定容易，因为孩子也许从来都没试过自己真正擅长的那件事。给他们机会尝试好几种游戏或科目，会有帮助。比起一次比赛的成绩，观察孩子自愿反复练习什么，可能更能让大人看出他们的天赋。

questions.en: Is talent important in sports?
questions.zh: 天赋在体育运动中重要吗？
questions.sample: Talent can make the first steps easier, for example if someone naturally has good balance. Over time, training and the ability to learn from mistakes matter a great deal. A talented player who never practises may stop improving.
questions.sampleZh: 天赋能让人起步时轻松一些，比如有的人天生平衡感好。但从长远看，训练以及从错误中学习的能力都非常重要。即使运动员天赋很好，如果从不练习，也可能不再进步。

questions.en: Should students have physical education and do sports at school?
questions.zh: 学生应该在学校上体育课、参加体育运动吗？
questions.sample: Yes, because school gives everyone access to exercise, including children who can't join a private club. I would offer a variety of activities. A student who dislikes football might enjoy swimming, dance or a simple walking challenge.
questions.sampleZh: 应该，因为在学校运动意味着每个人都有锻炼的机会，包括那些上不起私人运动俱乐部的孩子。我会提供多种活动供大家选择。不喜欢足球的学生，说不定会喜欢游泳、跳舞或参加简单的步行挑战。

questions.en: What kinds of books are popular in China?
questions.zh: 哪些类型的书在中国比较受欢迎？
questions.sample: Detective stories, books about personal growth and practical guides all seem popular with different readers in China. Young adults may choose a short novel for the metro, while a parent might look for a book to share with a child.
questions.sampleZh: 在中国，不同的读者似乎各有所好，比如推理小说、个人成长类书籍和实用指南都有人喜欢。年轻人可能会找一本短篇小说，方便在地铁上读；家长可能会想找一本能跟孩子一起读的书。

questions.en: Are success books useful to everyone?
questions.zh: 讲述如何获得成功的书对每个人都有用吗？
questions.sample: They help some readers by offering examples or a habit they can try. But a successful person's story comes from particular circumstances. Copying their exact routine may make little sense for someone with different work hours or family responsibilities.
questions.sampleZh: 这类书能给一些读者提供例子，或者介绍一个值得试试的习惯。但一个成功人士的故事，有他自己特定的背景。如果自己的工作时间或家庭责任不同，原样照搬对方的生活安排可能没什么意义。

questions.en: Do you think people today read less than before? Why?
questions.zh: 你觉得现在的人比以前读书少了吗？为什么？
questions.sample: People may spend less time reading printed books, but that doesn't tell the whole story. Someone can read articles or a novel on a phone during a commute. What seems harder today is finding time to read without interruption.
questions.sampleZh: 人们读纸质书的时间也许少了，但这并不能说明全部情况。有人在通勤途中也可以用手机读文章或小说。我觉得如今真正更难的，是找到一段不会被打断的阅读时间。

questions.en: Why do some people prefer watching movies to reading books?
questions.zh: 为什么有些人更喜欢看电影而不是读书？
questions.sample: A film gives people the voices, music and images straight away, so it's easier to enjoy after a tiring day. It also fits into one evening. A book often asks for more time and a little more imagination.
questions.sampleZh: 电影能直接把人声、音乐和画面呈现出来，所以累了一天以后，看电影比较容易放松。一部电影一个晚上就能看完。读一本书往往要花更多时间，也需要多发挥一点想象力。

questions.en: How can parents help children develop a love of reading?
questions.zh: 家长怎样才能帮孩子爱上阅读？
questions.sample: Letting children choose a book is a good start, even if they keep choosing the same funny story. Parents can read a few pages with them before bed. Enjoying that time together makes reading feel like a treat.
questions.sampleZh: 可以先让孩子自己选书，即使他们老是选同一个好笑的故事也没关系。家长每天睡觉前可以陪着读上几页。如果孩子喜欢这段相处的时间，就更容易觉得读书是一件让人期待的事。

questions.en: Do you think it is good to change one's daily routine?
questions.zh: 你觉得改变日常作息是好事吗？
questions.sample: Yes, a small change can make daily life more pleasant. Trying a different route home might lead you past a park or a new food shop. I'd still keep routines that already work well, like a sensible bedtime.
questions.sampleZh: 挺好的，小小的调整就能让日常生活多一点乐趣。比如回家时换一条路，你也许会经过一个公园，或发现一家新开的食品店。不过，原来就有用的习惯我还是会保留，比如在合理的时间睡觉。

questions.en: Do you think it is good to change jobs?
questions.zh: 你觉得换工作是好事吗？
questions.sample: It can be good if the new role offers a chance to learn or a schedule that suits someone's life better. Changing just because of one bad week may be risky. I'd first ask what would actually improve in the next job.
questions.sampleZh: 要是新工作能提供学习机会，或者工作时间更适合自己的生活，换工作可能是好事。只因为某一周过得不好就跳槽，可能有些冒险。我会先问自己，新工作究竟能改善什么。

questions.en: Is it good for people to get a job promotion?
questions.zh: 获得职位晋升对人们来说是好事吗？
questions.sample: A promotion can bring a better salary and more influence over a project. It may also mean spending less time doing work you enjoy and more time managing people. I'd want to know what the new role involves before saying yes.
questions.sampleZh: 升职可能意味着收入更高，在项目里也更有发言权。但也可能意味着你要少做自己喜欢的具体工作，多花时间管理别人。答应之前，我会先了解新职位究竟要做些什么。

questions.en: Do people often make plans around their regular routines?
questions.zh: 人们经常围绕自己平时的作息来安排事情吗？
questions.sample: Yes, routines are usually the starting point. A student might arrange exercise after their last class, while parents often plan shopping around school pickup. Building a new activity into an existing routine makes it easier to remember.
questions.sampleZh: 人们一般是以已有的日常安排为起点。比如学生可以把锻炼放在最后一节课之后，家长也经常要围绕放学接孩子的时间来安排购物。把新活动接在原本就有的习惯上，会更容易记得去做。

questions.en: Who tends to change their daily routine more often, younger people or older people?
questions.zh: 年轻人和老年人，谁更常改变自己的日常作息？
questions.sample: Younger people may change theirs more often when they move, start university or take a new job. Older people can have more settled schedules, although retirement can also change the shape of a whole week quite suddenly.
questions.sampleZh: 年轻人在搬家、上大学或换工作的时候，可能会更经常调整日常安排。年长者的生活节奏往往比较稳定，不过退休这件事，也可能一下子改变一整周的时间安排。

questions.en: Do you think children sometimes have to make important decisions?
questions.zh: 孩子有时也必须做重要决定吗？
questions.sample: Yes, although the decisions look different from adult ones. Choosing whether to tell a teacher about bullying, for example, can feel very important to a child. An adult can explain the choices without taking every decision away.
questions.sampleZh: 有的，只是孩子面对的决定和成年人面对的不太一样。比如要不要把同学受欺负的事告诉老师，对孩子来说可能是个很重要的决定。大人可以帮助他们弄清有哪些选择，而不必把每一个决定都替他们做了。

questions.en: What important decisions do teenagers need to make after graduation?
questions.zh: 青少年毕业后需要做哪些重要决定？
questions.sample: They may need to choose between further study, training or a first job, and sometimes decide whether to move city. Looking at costs and talking to someone who's tried each path can make the choice feel less frightening.
questions.sampleZh: 他们可能需要在继续读书、接受职业培训和找第一份工作之间作出选择，有时候还要决定要不要搬到另一座城市。先算算费用，再和亲自走过这些路的人聊聊，做选择时就可能没那么害怕。

questions.en: Who can children turn to for help when making a decision?
questions.zh: 孩子在做决定时可以向谁求助？
questions.sample: Parents and teachers are useful starting points because they often know the child well. For a specific decision, another person may help more. An older student who joined the school team can explain what training is really like.
questions.sampleZh: 父母和老师是很合适的求助对象，因为他们一般比较了解孩子。碰到某个具体决定时，其他人也许更能帮上忙。比如，一位已经加入校队的学长或学姐，能告诉孩子训练究竟是什么样的。

questions.en: Do you think advertisements can influence our decisions when shopping?
questions.zh: 广告会影响我们的购物决定吗？
questions.sample: Yes, particularly when several products look similar. A familiar picture or a short demonstration may make one brand come to mind first. Before buying something expensive, I think people are more likely to check other information too.
questions.sampleZh: 会，尤其是几样商品看起来很相似的时候。看到熟悉的图片或一个简短的演示，某个品牌可能会最先浮现在脑海里。不过在买贵重物品之前，我觉得人们通常还会查查其他信息。

questions.en: Do you think the influence of advertising is good?
questions.zh: 你觉得广告给人带来的影响是好的吗？
